names.short_meaning: He whose manifestation is the whole universe of forms: the virāṭ-puruṣa
names.commentary:
He whose manifestation is the whole universe of forms: the virāṭ-puruṣa. The cause is always present in the effects and as such That Form from which the whole universe has emerged out can only be its own manifestation. The whole cosmos of gross forms is His own expression, and therefore, He is called as virāṭpuruṣa. 'sa eva sarva-bhūtātmā viśvarūpo yato 'vyayaḥ'. The Sanskrit term viśvam comes from the root √viś, to enter: Thus it means He who has created and entered into the entire universe, as the All — Pervading Reality. It can also mean: That into which the entire universe has entered to remain therein established. In the Upaniṣads also we have assertions of similar ideas. It is only when intellectually, we view the Lord that we come to recognise Him as the 'cause' for the universe. When viewed through contemplation, since the effect is nothing other than the cause, there can be no world other than Him. In fact, there is nothing other than the Supreme. In the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad we read 'oṃkāra evedam sarvam'. In Gītā 'oṃ ity ekākṣaraṃ brahma'.

sa eva sarva-bhūtātmā viśvarūpo yato 'vyayaḥ. — Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.2.69.

सर्वभूतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभूतानि चात्मनि । ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः ॥ — Gītā 6.29.

brahmaivedaṃ viśvam idaṃ variṣṭhaṃ puruṣa evedaṃ viśvam.
names.simple_meaning: He whose manifestation is the whole universe of forms: the virāṭ-puruṣa

names.short_meaning: The term Viṣṇu is dissolved as veveṣṭi vyāpnoti iti viṣṇuḥ — That which pervades everywhere is Viṣṇu
names.commentary:
The term Viṣṇu is dissolved as veveṣṭi vyāpnoti iti viṣṇuḥ — That which pervades everywhere is Viṣṇu. That which has the nature of pervasiveness is Viṣṇu. He is the one who pervades all and nothing ever pervades Him.

'īśāvāsyam idaṃ sarvam'-All this is indwelt, pervaded by the Lord. This very same idea is described in the typical style of the Purāṇas, in the incarnation of the Lord as Vāmana, the short-boy, who, with His three feet, measured the entire universe. Because of this act, the Lord got the name Viṣṇu, says Mahābhārata. Viṣṇu Purāṇa (3-1) says: यस्माद्विष्टमिदं सर्वं तस्य शक्त्या महात्मनः। तस्मादेवोच्यते विष्णविशेर्धातोः प्रवेशनात ।।

The root √viś means 'to enter' (प्रवेशनं). The entire world of things and beings is pervaded by Him and the Upaniṣad emphatically insists in its mantra 'whatever that is there is the world of change' (यत्किञ्च जगत्यां जगत्… Īśa). Hence it means that He is not limited by space (deśa), time (kāla) or substance (vastu).

Because this whole world has been pervaded by the glory of the Great Self, He is named Viṣṇu, from the root √viś, to enter, to pervade.

names.simple_meaning: The all-pervading one

names.short_meaning: In the ritualistic portion of the Vedas we find many mantras ending with 'vaṣaṭ' and they are used in pouring devoted and dedicated oblations
names.commentary:
In the ritualistic portion of the Vedas we find many mantras ending with 'vaṣaṭ' and they are used in pouring devoted and dedicated oblations. Thus the term vaṣaṭkāra means: He who is invoked, and for propitiating whom, the oblations are poured in Vedic ritualism, using mantras ending with vaṣaṭ.

Also vaṣaṭkāra can mean yajña in its association and thus the term in its suggestion can signify 'He who is of the form of the yajña'. In the Upaniṣads also we find this meaning endorsed when the Upaniṣad mantra says: "yajño vai Viṣṇuḥ"—yajña itself is Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The sacred vaṣaṭ call through which offerings are made

names.short_meaning: He who is the Lord (Prabhu) of the Past (bhūta), the Future (Bhavya) and the Present (Bhavat)
names.commentary:
He who is the Lord (Prabhu) of the Past (bhūta), the Future (Bhavya) and the Present (Bhavat). Time is the concept of the intellect; it expresses itself in the interval between experiences. Experiences are registered as thoughts and thoughts are ever-changing. This very change is known and experienced by us. The knower of the change must be something other than the change. Thus, He who is the Illuminator of all changes, meaning the Consciousness (ātman) is the Lord Viṣṇu.

He is the One who is not conditioned by time.
names.simple_meaning: He who is the Lord (Prabhu) of the Past (bhūta), the Future (Bhavya) and the Present (Bhavat)

names.short_meaning: The Creator (kṛt) of all creatures (bhūta)
names.commentary:
The Creator (kṛt) of all creatures (bhūta). This word can be dissolved in two ways: (a) One who creates the creatures (bhūtāni karoti iti bhūta-kṛt) or (b) One who annihilates all creatures (bhūtāni kṛntati iti bhūtakṛt). In both these cases, Brahman, the Supreme, is the One Reality that seems to function as the Creator, Sustainer or Destroyer, when He functions through different guṇas in the Total — Mind. Functioning through a preponderance in rajoguṇa, He becomes the 'Creator'; through sattvaguṇa the 'Sustainer', and through tamoguṇa, He Himself expresses as the 'Destroyer'.

Subjectively, the Atman functioning through my own mind and intellect is I, the individuality. My personality entirely depends upon the quality and texture of my own thoughts. I myself become according to the moods of my mind the creator, sustainer and annihilator of my world of experiences. He who manifests and functions, in these three aspects, is the Supreme Viṣṇu.

"Tvam kartā sarva-bhūtānām." — Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.4.15.
ocr_notes: Scan pages 21–22: removed the name-2 footnote spliced into the middle of the sentence and joined the page-break continuation.
names.simple_meaning: The Creator (kṛt) of all creatures (bhūta)

names.short_meaning: One who nurtures and nourishes all beings (living creatures) in all their attitudes is this Great Reality and, therefore, He is called as the bhūta Bhrit
names.commentary: One who nurtures and nourishes all beings (living creatures) in all their attitudes is this Great Reality and, therefore, He is called as the bhūta Bhrit. In Gītā there is an elaborate description of this idea in the 15th Chapter where the Lord points out how, He, as the light in the sun, fertility in the earth, growth in the plants, nourishment in food, heat in fire,—becomes Himself the 'eater', and, therefore, how He Himself presides over all the functions of the body and mind, and apparently nurtures and nourishes the creatures, who are in fact nothing other than Himself.
names.simple_meaning: The sustainer and nourisher of all beings

names.short_meaning: One who 'becomes' (Bhavati iti bhāvaḥ) Himself into the movable and the Immovable beings and things in the world
names.commentary:
One who 'becomes' (Bhavati iti bhāvaḥ) Himself into the movable and the Immovable beings and things in the world. He is the Pure Existence in all the sentient organisms and the insentient objects in the universe.

Hence He is indicated by the term bhāvaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: Existence becoming all moving and unmoving beings

names.short_meaning: He is the ātman of all the beings: The very 'Be' in all the living beings
names.commentary: He is the ātman of all the beings: The very 'Be' in all the living beings. Just as the same universal space plays in all rooms as the room-space, or in all pots as the pot-space, so the Infinite Life playing through any given vehicle is called the ātman of the vehicle. It is well known that space everywhere is one and the same; so too, the One Reality sports as though different ātmans. This One Universal Soul is called in Vedānta the Supreme Brahman (Para — Brahman). In Bhāgavata, the Lord is addressed as "You are the One Self in all living creatures ever illumining all their experiences." In Kaṭhopaniṣad: "The One enchanting Truth that revels in every form manifesting in plurality''-(एको वशी सर्व- भृतान्तरात्मा रूपं रूपं प्रतिरूपो बहिश्च).
names.simple_meaning: He is the ātman of all the beings: The very 'Be' in all the living beings

names.short_meaning: One who creates and multiplies the creatures; meaning the One, who is the cause for the birth and who is responsible for the growth of all living creatures
names.commentary: One who creates and multiplies the creatures; meaning the One, who is the cause for the birth and who is responsible for the growth of all living creatures.
names.simple_meaning: The creator and nourisher of all beings

names.short_meaning: One with an extremely Pure (pūtam) Essence: One who is not affected the least by the impurities of māyā
names.commentary: One with an extremely Pure (pūtam) Essence: One who is not affected the least by the impurities of māyā. The Self is beyond all vāsanās and, therefore, He cannot be affected by any one of the manifestations of māyā such as thoughts of the intellect, emotions of the mind or the perceptions of the body. Immaculate is ever the Self, and so He is termed as the Pure Self (pūta-ātmā).
names.simple_meaning: The supremely pure Self

names.short_meaning: The Supreme, meaning that which transcends all limitations and imperfections of matter: in short, the Transcendental Reality
names.commentary:
The Supreme, meaning that which transcends all limitations and imperfections of matter: in short, the Transcendental Reality. The Spirit is other than matter, and that in its presence, the vestures of matter, borrowing their dynamism from Him, play their parts rhythmically at all times. This has been the assertion found chorusly repeated in all the Upaniṣads and in the entire Vedantic literature. Śaṅkara in ātma Bodha points out that the Self is other than the three bodies and that He functions in the microcosm as a king in the nation. It was also said therein that matter borrows its energy from the Spirit and continues its activity "as the world from the Sun". Kaṭhopaniṣad and the Gītā guide us from the outer levels of our personality, stage by stage, into the inner-most sanctum, and there, the teachers declare, is He the Infinite, transcending all, reigning in His own glory. "In short, that which remains other than the cause and effect-māyā and matter-is He, the Parama ātman. In Viṣṇu Purāṇa this Supreme is glorified as Maha Viṣṇu (paramātmā)"—Viṣṇu Purāṇa 6.4.10.

Dehendriya-mano-buddhi-prakṛtibhyo vilakṣaṇam.

Tat-vṛtti-sākṣiṇam vidyād ātmānaṃ rājavat sadā.

As the world from the Sun (sūryālokamayā janāḥ). — Ātma Bodha 20.

इन्द्रियाणि पराण्याहुरिन्द्रियेभ्यः परं मनः । मनसस्तु परा बुद्धिर्यो बुद्धेः परतस्तु सः ॥ — Gītā 3.42.

परमात्मा च सर्वेषामाधारः परमेश्वरः । विष्णुर्नाम सर्ववेदेषु वेदान्तेषु च गीयते ॥ — Viṣṇu Purāṇa 6.4.10.
names.simple_meaning: The supreme self beyond all material limitations

names.short_meaning: He who is the final Goal, that is reached by all the liberated souls
names.commentary:
He who is the final Goal, that is reached by all the liberated souls. The limitations and bondages lived through by man are in fact the destiny of the matter vestures. Through delusion of un-understanding, we identify with them and come to suffer the consequent sense of imperfections. To liberate ourselves from the thraldom of matter is to realize the Self. Hence the Truth is defined as the Supreme Goal of the emancipated.

This 'Goal' to be attained is called as 'Gati' in Sanskrit. "The Supreme Goal" (Paramaa Gatih) would necessarily be then that Goal, having reached which, there is no return: "There where having gone, men never return. That sacred place is My seat''--( यदगत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम )--- Gītā Ch. 15. St. 6.

In Gītā. (Ch. 8. St. 16) even more explicitly the same idea has been asserted by Śrī Kṛṣṇa when He says: "O Son of Kunti, having reached Me, there shall be no more any re-birth" -( मामपेत्य तू कौन्तेय पूनर्जन्म न विद्यते ) Again, He defines the final Goal as "That having reached no return again"-(यस्मिन गता न निवर्तन्ति भ्यः)-Gītā Ch. 15, St. 4.
names.simple_meaning: He who is the final Goal, that is reached by all the liberated souls

names.short_meaning: "Vyaya" means destruction: destruction cannot be without change; therefore, that which is "without destruction" (avyayaḥ) is the changeless
names.commentary: "Vyaya" means destruction: destruction cannot be without change; therefore, that which is "without destruction" (avyayaḥ) is the changeless. The Indestructible, and therefore, changeless, can never have any modifications (Parinaama). For, modification is but the death of a previous condition and the birth of a new condition. The Eternal and the Immutable (avyayaḥ) is the Supreme sat-cit-ānanda, and every other thing and being come under the hammer of change. The medium in which all these changes are sustained is Brahman, the Immutable. The Upaniṣads glorify Him as "Ajaro Amaro avyayaḥ"—without old age, death or change.
names.simple_meaning: The changeless and imperishable one

names.short_meaning: One who dwells in the Fort-city
names.commentary:
One who dwells in the Fort-city (Puri sete iti puruṣaḥ) ( पुरि शेते इति पुरुष: ). Herein metaphorically the ṛṣis conceive our body as a fortress with nine gate-ways-"Nava Dvaare Pure Dehee"-(Gītā Ch. 5, St. 13) —and declare the One who rules within it, like a king, is the Self.

This term can also be dissolved in two more different ways giving more and more suggestions to the nature of the Self. Thus, puruṣa can mean "That which was before all creatures" -Puraa Aaseet iti puruṣaḥ (प्रा आसीत् इति प्रव:) or it can be "One who completes and fulfils the Existence everywhere", meaning, without whom Existence is impossible (Poorayati iti puruṣaḥ) (परयति इति पुरुष:).

This ātman remains in the bodies of living creatures as their individuality (jīva) and in all the activities, physical, mental and intellectual, ātman is not in fact involved but He is therein only an observer of all that is happening. This will become clear in the following discussion.
names.simple_meaning: One who dwells in the Fort-city

names.short_meaning: Witness
names.commentary:
Witness. In every day life he is a witness who without any mental reservation or personal interest observes and watches what is happening in a given field of experience. "Saakshaad Drashtari sākṣī syaad — Amarakosa.

"The 'Knower' in every bosom is the same Supreme Self", says Lord Kṛṣṇa (Gītā Ch. 13, St. 3). Though thus Consciousness illumines everything, It is only a Witness, as It knows no change. Just as the sun illumines every thing in the world and yet the Sun is not affected by the condition of the things it is illumining, so too Viṣṇu, the Supreme, illumines all, without Itself undergoing any change.

According to Paanini Sutras the word sākṣī is derived from "Sa+akshi", meaning "direct perceiver".
names.simple_meaning: Witness

names.short_meaning: One who knows the body and all the experiences from within the body, is the Knower-of-the-field, kṣetrajñaḥ
names.commentary: One who knows the body and all the experiences from within the body, is the Knower-of-the-field, kṣetrajñaḥ. As Brahmapurana would put it: Bodies are 'fields' and the Atman illumines them all without an effort, and therefore, is called Knower-of-the-field, kṣetrajñaḥ".
names.simple_meaning: One who knows the body and all the experiences from within the body, is the Knower-of-the-field, kṣetrajñaḥ

names.short_meaning: Indestructible: things which are finite are necessarily conditioned by time and space; the Infinite is unconditioned, and so It is akṣaraḥ
names.commentary:
Indestructible: things which are finite are necessarily conditioned by time and space; the Infinite is unconditioned, and so It is akṣaraḥ. Since It is Indestructible. It cannot come under the methods of universal destruction arising from nature or through the wilful actions of man. "It, cannot be cleaved by instruments of destruction, nor can fire burn It, nor water drench It, nor air dry It"-(Gītā Ch. 2, St. 23). It is also indicated that the Supreme Brahman is the Akshara—"akṣaram Brahma Paramam"—(Gītā Ch. 8, St. 3).

Please note that in the stanza there is the extra word 'only' (Eva) used, indicating that kṣetrajñaḥ is the akṣaraḥ; there is no difference between them both: the "Knower-of-the-field" and the "field".
names.simple_meaning: Indestructible

names.short_meaning: The one who is to be known or realized through yoga
names.commentary:
The one who is to be known or realized through yoga. By withdrawing the sense-organs from their objects of preoccupation, when the mind of the seeker becomes quietened, he is lifted to a higher plane-of-consciousness, wherein he attains "yoga", meaning wherein he realizes the Reality. At such moments of equanimity and mental quiet "yoga" is gained: Samatvam yoga uchvate—(Gītā Ch. 2, St. 48).

Since He is experienced through Yoga He is known as yogaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The one who is to be known or realized through yoga

names.short_meaning: One who guides all the activities of all men 'who knows yoga' (Yogavit)
names.commentary:
One who guides all the activities of all men 'who knows yoga' (Yogavit). To all men of realization, He who is the Ideal, is the Supreme Lord. Just as our activities are today ordered by our selfishness and individuality, the Ideal that commands and orders all activities in the bosom of a Man of Realization is his God — Consciousness. This realm of experience is Mahaa Viṣṇu. In the Gītā also we find the same idea expressed, in the language of emotion, when the Lord says: "Those who contemplate upon Me with total dedication, their daily welfare and spiritual progress I shall bear".

अनन्याश्चिन्तयन्तो मां ये जनाः पर्युपासते । तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम् ॥ — Gītā 9.22.
names.simple_meaning: One who guides all the activities of all men 'who knows yoga' (Yogavit)

names.short_meaning: Lord of both pradhāna and puruṣa
names.commentary:
Lord of both pradhāna and puruṣa. The term pradhāna means 'māyā'—the total cause for the entire universe of forms. puruṣa indicates the individuality in each one of us—the jīva.

Lord Īśvara means the Master (Eeshte iti Īśvaraḥ). The Lord of māyā and jīva means the one who makes both these possible to exist and function. The One Infinite Reality which Itself manifests as māyā, jīva and Īśvara is the Essence in Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: Lord of both pradhāna and puruṣa

names.short_meaning: One whose form is half human and half lion
names.commentary: One whose form is half human and half lion. This is the famous fourth incarnation of Lord Viṣṇu which He took in order to destroy the atheistic tyrant Hiraṇyakaśipu and bless his devotee, Prahlāda.
names.simple_meaning: One whose form is half human and half lion

names.short_meaning: One who is always with Śrī
names.commentary: One who is always with Śrī. Mother Śrī is Mother Lakṣmī. In the Puranic terminology Lakṣmī stands for all powers, all faculties. The total manifested power potential in the Omnipotent is Lakṣmī. These powers are ever in Him and therefore, He is the śrīmān.
names.simple_meaning: One who is always with Śrī

names.short_meaning: He who has beautiful and graceful locks of hair
names.commentary:
He who has beautiful and graceful (Va) locks of hair (keśa) is familiar as in Lord Kṛṣṇa's form. Or, it can also mean, one who destroyed the demon Kesin who was sent to destroy the child — Kṛṣṇa by his uncle Kamsa. This interpretation is endorsed by the Viṣṇu Purāṇa, 5.16.23.

प्रशस्ताः केशाः सन्त्यस्येति केशवः।

यस्मात् त्वयैव दुष्टात्मा हतः केशी जनार्दन । तस्मात् केशव नाम्ना त्वं लोके ज्ञेयो भविष्यसि ॥ — Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.16.23.
names.simple_meaning: He who has beautiful and graceful locks of hair

names.short_meaning: The constitution of the individuality, jīva, when analysed, we find that it is made up of both the perishable-matter and the Imperishable — Spirit
names.commentary:
The constitution of the individuality, jīva, when analysed, we find that it is made up of both the perishable-matter and the Imperishable — Spirit. The Spirit expressing through matter is the individuality, jīva.

Reflected moon is the moon of the heavens dancing on the surface of water. Just as the moon is something different from its reflections and the water surfaces, so too the Self is, in its transcendental nature, something different from both matter, the perishable, and Spirit, the Imperishable, ever playing in matter. This Transcendental Truth is indicated by the term the Supreme puruṣa (Purushottama).
names.simple_meaning: The supreme person, beyond the perishable and imperishable

names.short_meaning: He who is the all
names.commentary: He who is the all. He being the One cause from which have sprung forth all things and beings. He himself is the all. In Mahābhārata Udvoga Parva (70-12) we read: "As He is the origin and end of all, whether existent or otherwise, and as He, at all times, cognises all, He is called "Sarva". All waves rise from the same ocean and, therefore, the ocean is the very essence in all waves.
names.simple_meaning: He who is the all

names.short_meaning: The Auspicious One: meaning, the One who gives auspiciousness to those who hear of Him, to those who have a vision of Him, and to those who meditate upon Him
names.commentary: The Auspicious One: meaning, the One who gives auspiciousness to those who hear of Him, to those who have a vision of Him, and to those who meditate upon Him.
names.simple_meaning: The auspicious one who bestows auspiciousness

names.short_meaning: The One who is Eternally Pure
names.commentary: The One who is Eternally Pure. In Him can never be any contamination of the imperfection of Rajas and Tamas. 'Non-apprehension of Reality' is Tamas and 'mis-apprehensions of Reality' constitute the Rajas. In the Reality Itself there can be neither of them 'He is Brahman; He is Siva', (स ब्रह्म स: शिव:), so the Upaniṣad declares of the Absolute Oneness, which is Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The One who is Eternally Pure

names.short_meaning: Generally this term sthāṇuḥ is used for the permanent pillars that mark the frontiers of a country
names.commentary:
Generally this term sthāṇuḥ is used for the permanent pillars that mark the frontiers of a country. They are permanent, immovable, fixed. The Truth, that remains thus firm and motionless, without movement, permanently established in Its own Realm of Purity, is called by the term sthāṇuḥ—the Pillar, "Eternal, All — Pervading, the Pillar, Motionless (is) this Ancient One," so says Gītā Ch. 2, 24.

नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणुरचलोऽयं सनातनः ॥ — Gītā 2.24.
names.simple_meaning: The firm and immovable one

names.short_meaning: The very cause for the five great elements: Space, Air, Fire, Water and Earth
names.commentary: The very cause for the five great elements: Space, Air, Fire, Water and Earth.
names.simple_meaning: The very cause for the five great elements: Space, Air, Fire, Water and Earth

names.short_meaning: The Imperishable treasure
names.commentary: The Imperishable treasure. The term Nidhi means 'that in which precious things are stored away or preserved secretly': (Nidheeyate Asmin iti Nidhih). Therefore, He who is the substratum—container—for the entire universe is the Nidhi. During the dissolution (sleep) the One into Whom all things go to lie merged therein temporarily, till the next projection or creation (waking), as this Immutable Treasure Chest—the Viṣṇu. Here 'unchangeable' (Avyaya) is qualifying 'Nidhi'.
names.simple_meaning: The Imperishable treasure

names.short_meaning: One who takes up by his own free-will various incarnations for the glory of the world is saṃbhavaḥ
names.commentary:
One who takes up by his own free-will various incarnations for the glory of the world is saṃbhavaḥ. In fact, He alone is the source of all that is created. In Harivaṃśa we read the assertion: "I am the Nārāyaṇa, the Source from which all creatures and things spring forth". To uphold dharma I shall manifest again and again, declares the Lord in His Gītā: "संभवामि युगे युगे".

अहं नारायणो ब्रह्म सम्भवः सर्वदेहिनाम्, सर्वभूतोद्भवकरः। — Harivaṃśa.
names.simple_meaning: One who takes up by his own free-will various incarnations for the glory of the world is saṃbhavaḥ

names.short_meaning: To do bhāvanā is to give: One who gives everything to His devotees is bhāvanaḥ
names.commentary: To do bhāvanā is to give: One who gives everything to His devotees is bhāvanaḥ. The Lord is One who gives both joy and sorrow to each one according to his deserts. In the case of humanity it is He again who destroys the evil and blesses the good.
names.simple_meaning: To do bhāvanā is to give: One who gives everything to His devotees is bhāvanaḥ

names.short_meaning: The One who 'Governs' the entire living world
names.commentary: The One who 'Governs' the entire living world. Governing includes protecting the world from all harms and serving it positively with progress and joy. One who does these to all creatures at all times is Viṣṇu—the great bhartā.
names.simple_meaning: The One who 'Governs' the entire living world

names.short_meaning: The One who is the very womb of all the Five Great Elements
names.commentary: The One who is the very womb of all the Five Great Elements. It is That from which even the very concepts of time and space have sprung from.
names.simple_meaning: The One who is the very womb of all the Five Great Elements

names.short_meaning: The Almighty Lord
names.commentary: The Almighty Lord. He who is the All — Powerful. He who has the supreme freedom to do (Kartum), not to do (Akartum), or to do quite differently from what He had already done (Anyathaa Kartum) is considered as the prabhuḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The Almighty Lord

names.short_meaning: One who has the ability to do anything without the help of other beings or things is called īśvaraḥ
names.commentary: One who has the ability to do anything without the help of other beings or things is called īśvaraḥ (ईष्टे इति ईश्वर:).
names.simple_meaning: The independent lord whose power needs no aid

names.short_meaning: The one who manifests Himself from Himself is considered as self-made
names.commentary: The one who manifests Himself from Himself is considered as self-made. Everything born or produced must have a cause. The Supreme is the cause from which all effects arise, and Itself has no cause. This uncaused Cause-of-all, this Ultimate Cause, with reference to which every thing else is considered as 'effects' is in itself the Absolute Cause. This idea is indicated by the term Self-made (svayambhūḥ).
names.simple_meaning: The one who manifests Himself from Himself is considered as self-made

names.short_meaning: He who brings Auspiciousness— both inner goodness and outer prosperity to His devotees
names.commentary: He who brings Auspiciousness— both inner goodness and outer prosperity to His devotees. śambhuḥ is one of the famous names of Lord Siva. By using this term in invoking Viṣṇu, by its suggestion, it declares that Viṣṇu and Siva are not two Divine Entities, but they are both manifestations of the One Essential Reality.
names.simple_meaning: He who brings Auspiciousness— both inner goodness and outer prosperity to His devotees

names.short_meaning: The Truth (puruṣa) that glows with a golden splendour in the solar orb is called ādityaḥ
names.commentary:
The Truth (puruṣa) that glows with a golden splendour in the solar orb is called ādityaḥ. There are twelve Ādityas and of them One is called Viṣṇu. Kṛṣṇa Himself declares, 'I am Viṣṇu among the Ādityas' -ādityānām Aham Viṣṇuḥ-(Gītā Ch. 10, St. 21). The word Āditya can mean 'Son of Aditi'—signifying the one who was born as the son of Aditi in His Vāmana incarnation.

The term ādityaḥ can also mean in Sanskrit 'One who is like the sun'. The Sun is the one who illumines all, and every living creature draws its nurture and nourishment directly or indirectly always from the sun alone. In the same way Brahman is the one Sun in the universe of living creatures illumining all experiences of all creatures.

अरुणः — Aruṇaḥ; सूर्यः — Sūryaḥ; भानुः — Bhānuḥ; तपनः — Tapanaḥ; चन्द्रमस् — Chandramas; मित्रः — Mitraḥ; हिरण्यवीर्यः — Hiraṇya-vīryaḥ; रविः — Raviḥ; अर्यमा — Aryamā; गभस्तिः — Gabhastiḥ; दिवाकरः — Divākaraḥ; विष्णुः — Viṣṇuḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The golden person shining within the sun

names.short_meaning: One who has eyes like the lotus
names.commentary: One who has eyes like the lotus. Joy and Peace in the bosom of an individual are expressed in the world outside at no other point so vividly as in the eyes. The One, whose inner peace and joy, beaming out through His eyes, bring into the devoted hearts all the aesthetic beauty and romantic thrills of seeing a lotus dancing in the breeze, In short, the term indicates the Lord who with His beautiful looks, magically lifts all the sorrows in the devotee's heart and fills it with Peace, Joy and Perfection.
names.simple_meaning: One who has eyes like the lotus

names.short_meaning: One who possesses thundering voice of compulsion: Svana means 'sound'
names.commentary: One who possesses thundering voice of compulsion: Svana means 'sound'. One whose 'call' is thundered in all hearts, familiarly known as the 'compelling whisper' of the Higher. Or, Svanam can also mean 'breath'; and so, the term can mean, 'He whose great breath is the very Vedas'. "Thus, O Maitreyee, this has been breathed forth from this great Being what we have as Rigveda, Yajurveda" — Brihadaaranyaka Upaniṣad (4.4.10). In the Spiritual literature of India we often read Vedas described as His breath; He breathed out the Vedas (Nih-svasitam).
names.simple_meaning: The one whose commanding voice is thunderous

names.short_meaning: One who has neither birth (ādi) nor death (Nidhanam)
names.commentary: One who has neither birth (ādi) nor death (Nidhanam). Thus One who is changeless is Anaadi — Nidhanam; for, any change should include the death of an old condition and the birth of a newer condition. To the Immortal and the Immutable, change is impossible.
names.simple_meaning: One who has neither birth (ādi) nor death (Nidhanam)

names.short_meaning: One who is the Substratum for the world of names and forms, and who supports all fields of experiences in all
names.commentary: One who is the Substratum for the world of names and forms, and who supports all fields of experiences in all. He who is the 'screen' for the 'cinema of empirical experiences' (Visvam).
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Substratum for the world of names and forms, and who supports all fields of experiences in all

names.short_meaning: The One who is the Dispenser of all 'fruits-of-actions'
names.commentary: The One who is the Dispenser of all 'fruits-of-actions'. In the Karma-kaanda portion of the Vedas, Īśvara is described as the Dispenser of fruit (Karmaphala-daataa Īśvaraḥ). He is the Lord who is behind this universe of scientific truths and rhythm. He is the One who has not only ordered the Laws of Nature, but He is the One, afraid of whom, the phenomena dare not disobey His Laws anywhere at any time. The light of the sun, the heat in the fire, the sweetness in the sugar, the pains in sin and the joys in goodness, are all their 'nature' and none dare ever disobey these laws. The One who is thus the unquestionable Law behind the entire universe of Laws is vidhātā.
names.simple_meaning: The One who is the Dispenser of all 'fruits-of-actions'

names.short_meaning: The fundamentals that form the reinforcement on any existent thing are called dhātu
names.commentary:
The fundamentals that form the reinforcement on any existent thing are called dhātu. In the science of life, as explored by the ṛṣis, all corporal forms have risen from and exist as composed of some definite 'elemental factors' called the dhātus. Of the endless varieties of dhātus available in existence, the subtlest dhātu. without which no existence, is ever possible, is the Chit dhātu, and this is dhātu-ruttamah.

Though very rarely, we do find some commentators splitting this word into two as dhātu and Uttama. But in the majority of cases we find it taken to form one term and explained as 'the subtlest of the dhātus'.

For example: The body is made up of seven dhātus: marrow, bone, fat, flesh, blood, lower-skin and upper-skin; all metals are dhātus—similarly everywhere.
names.simple_meaning: The supreme essence underlying every existent thing

names.short_meaning: He, who cannot be defined and explained in terms of any logical terms of reference with other things, should necessarily be inexpressible
names.commentary: He, who cannot be defined and explained in terms of any logical terms of reference with other things, should necessarily be inexpressible. A thing that can be directly perceived (Pratyaksha) can be described, certain other things, which we may not directly perceive, but can infer (anumaana) them from data available. And there are yet things which can be brought home to the listener by describing them in terms of similar other objects (Upamaa). Since the Infinite has no 'Properties' It cannot be perceived, nor can It be "understood through inference," nor even explained in terms of similar or dissimilar things." Hence the Supreme Reality, Viṣṇu, is called as aprameyaḥ. We can experience Him only by ending all sense of 'separativeness' and becoming one with Him.
names.simple_meaning: The one beyond definition and comparison

names.short_meaning: In the Puranic literature the meaning for this term is 'close-cropped' or 'One who has coiled up his locks of hair' (Hris+keśa)
names.commentary:
In the Puranic literature the meaning for this term is 'close-cropped' or 'One who has coiled up his locks of hair' (Hris+keśa). It can also be interpreted as the Lord of the senses (Hrisheeka+Eesa). The term 'Hrisheeka' is an obsolete one now, and it means the "sense-organs". The ātman, the Self, as Consciousness is the One who gives light to all the sense-organs and, therefore, It is the Lord of the sense-organs. This Lord is Viṣṇu.

The obsolete word Hrisheeka also means the 'rays' or 'that which gives joy'. Thus the term hṛṣīkeśaḥ can mean "The Lord of the rays": the Sun and the Moon. This way interpreted, commentators point out that the term hṛṣīkeśaḥ means He who has Himself become the Sun and the Moon.

In His manifestation as the Sun and the Moon, the Lord Himself whips the world to wakeful activities and sends the world to sleep and rest. Thus Hrisheekesa in its deeper significance, is, to all contemplative hearts, the Lord, who becomes Himself the world, exhausts Himself in His activities, and ultimately packs His toys and goes to rest at the time of dissolution.
names.simple_meaning: The lord of the senses

names.short_meaning: One from whose navel springs the Lotus, which is the seat of the four-faced Creator
names.commentary:
One from whose navel springs the Lotus, which is the seat of the four-faced Creator. Brahmājī. Lotus in Hinduism represents the seat of either Truth or any of Its manifested powers. The creative faculties in man flow from the navel area (centre), and manifest as the 'four-faced' inner equipment (Antahkarana) constituted of the mind, intellect, Chit and ego.

In the Yoga-sastras, we find a lot of details regarding this concept. According to them every "idea" springs from Him (parā), and then at the navel area, each of them comes to be 'perceived' (Pasyantee). Thereafter they play in the bosom as thoughts (Madhyamaa), and at last they are expressed (Vaikharee) in the outer fields-of-activity. In this discussion—upon the evolutionary stages through which every "idea" becomes an "action"—we gather a clearer insight into the meaning of the symbolism of "the Creator seated on the lotus", which springs forth from the navel of the Lord, the Supreme Viṣṇu.
ocr_notes: Scan locus corrected from [34] to [33] by complete-text replay against the PDF page OCR.
names.simple_meaning: One from whose navel springs the Lotus, which is the seat of the four-faced Creator

names.short_meaning: The Lord of the Immortals, the Devas
names.commentary: The Lord of the Immortals, the Devas. The Denizens of the Heavens, including all the office bearers therein (Dikpaalakas etc.) along with Indra, are called 'Devas', and they enjoy in their heavenly state a relative immortality. They live and continue functioning till the great dissolution—the Sleep of the Creator. Compared with the short span of the existence of man on this globe, the aeons through which the Devas live can be considered as endless or immortal. One who serves them with His might, giving protection and security to all creatures, is called, therefore, amara-prabhuḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of the Immortals, the Devas

names.short_meaning: The very creator—of the world-of-objects, of all equipments-of-experiences, and of all experiences in all bosoms is called the Visva — Karmaa
names.commentary: The very creator—of the world-of-objects, of all equipments-of-experiences, and of all experiences in all bosoms is called the Visva — Karmaa. Herein the Infinite Lord is but a Witness of all that is happening and though the experienced world is sustained in Him, He is not involved in the imperfections or mortality, that are happening all around at all times in the Visvam. "They are in Me, I am not in them"-Gītā.
names.simple_meaning: The maker of the universe and all experience

names.short_meaning: The term means One who has the ability to reflect upon the Higher (Mananaseelah manuḥ)
names.commentary: The term means One who has the ability to reflect upon the Higher (Mananaseelah manuḥ). Manu also means mantra and so, as applied to the Lord, it can mean as the One who has manifested Himself in the form of the Vedic mantras.
names.simple_meaning: The reflective thinker who contemplates the highest

names.short_meaning: One who makes gross things of huge dimensions into minutest particles
names.commentary: One who makes gross things of huge dimensions into minutest particles. At the time of the world's dissolution, the entire gross-world folds back into its subtler elements until at last pure objectless space alone comes to remain.
names.simple_meaning: One who makes gross things of huge dimensions into minutest particles

names.short_meaning: It is the superlative degree of gross (sthoola) and thus 'the Supremely gross' is the subtlest Reality
names.commentary:
It is the superlative degree of gross (sthoola) and thus 'the Supremely gross' is the subtlest Reality. The contradiction that it contains is itself its vigour and beauty. The Infinite as the subtlest is All — Pervading in Its own nature. It is this Maha — Viṣṇu who has Himself become the entire universe of gross things and beings. Just as all waves are the ocean, the total world of gross things is itself the form of Viṣṇu.

In His cosmic form, Nārāyaṇa had manifested to Arjuna in the Gītā. There the words of Arjuna's chant will clearly bring home to us that the entire gross world is ever His own Divine form.
names.simple_meaning: The greatest and most substantial

names.short_meaning: The Ancient (Sthavirah) and the Motionless or firm (Dhruvah)
names.commentary: The Ancient (Sthavirah) and the Motionless or firm (Dhruvah). He is called the 'Ancient' because the very first 'unit of time' itself had risen from Him. He was the progenitor of the very concept of Time in us. Therefore, 'Time' cannot condition Him. Thus He becomes the most Ancient. He is the 'Firm Truth'; nothing that happens in the phenomenal world can affect Him at any time.
names.simple_meaning: The Ancient (Sthavirah) and the Motionless or firm (Dhruvah)

names.short_meaning: That which cannot be perceived through the play of the sense-organs; in short, that which is not an 'object' of perception, but which is the very 'subject'—who is the Perceiver in all that is perceived
names.commentary:
That which cannot be perceived through the play of the sense-organs; in short, that which is not an 'object' of perception, but which is the very 'subject'—who is the Perceiver in all that is perceived. The 'Subject' can never become the 'object', and hence Truth is something that the sense-organs cannot apprehend, as they do any other sense-objects. He is the one 'Subject' ever-perceiving all objects, through all sense-organs of all living creatures, everywhere, at all times. The Lord is the 'Subject', not only in the sense-organs, but He is the "feeler" in the mind and the "thinker" in the intellect.

And thus the sense-organs cannot perceive It, nor the mind feel It, nor the intellect apprehend It; says the Upaniṣad. "That from which words retire unapproached along with the mind" is the Supreme. Hence He is Agraahya—Imperceptible and Incomprehensible. Kenopaniṣad is very clear and emphatic: "That which the eyes cannot perceive, but because of which eyes are perceiving, understand That to be Brahman (Maha Viṣṇu) and not that which you here worship."

यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते अप्राप्य मनसा सह।

यच्चक्षुषा न पश्यति येन चक्षूंषि पश्यन्ति तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते।
names.simple_meaning: The ungraspable subject, never an object of perception

names.short_meaning: That which remains at all times the same is the Permanent
names.commentary:
That which remains at all times the same is the Permanent, ( शक्बत् भवतीति शाक्वत: ). That which is permanent, should remain Changeless in all the three periods of time. In short, He is unconditioned by time. The Supreme Consciousness Itself is the very Illuminator of Time, and the Illuminator can never be affected by what It illumines.

This changeless reality is Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: That which remains at all times the same is the Permanent

names.short_meaning: The word Kṛṣṇa means in Sanskrit 'the dark'
names.commentary:
The word Kṛṣṇa means in Sanskrit 'the dark'. The Truth that is intellectually appreciated, but spiritually not apprehended, is considered as 'veiled behind some darkness' The root Krish means Existence (sattā) and na means Bliss (ānanda). So says Vyasa in Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva 70, 5. Therefore Kṛṣṇa (Krish+na) means Existence — Bliss (sattā — ānanda). Thus, the very name divine, 'Kṛṣṇa', represents the Supreme paramātman. Or, because of His dark-blue complexion He is called as Kṛṣṇa. Mahābhārata Santi Parva 343 says, "As My colour is dark-blue, I am called Kṛṣṇa, O Arjuna." In Mahābhārata, we find Kṛṣṇa explaining Himself to Arjuna 'when the earth becomes shelled in by its hard crux I shall turn myself into an iron plough-share and shall plough the earth. Apart from the above meaning Kṛṣṇa also means the Enchanter of all His devotees (Aakarshana). Truth is One which irresistibly attracts everybody towards Itself. Commentators have interpreted this significance in a more attractive context.

They conclude that Kṛṣṇa means One who sweeps away the sins in the heart of those who meditate upon Him. Truth has got a magnetism to attract to Itself all the ego and ego-centric passions of the individual. In this sense viewed, we need not consider Kṛṣṇa as a deity of the farm-yard in the agricultural estates. The Lord ploughs the hard stupidities in us and prepares the heart-field, weeding out all the poisonous growths of sin, and cultivates therein pure Bliss which is of the nature of Reality.

कृषिर्भूवाचकः शब्दो णश्च निर्वृतिवाचकः । तयोरैक्यं परं ब्रह्म कृष्ण इत्यभिधीयते ॥

कर्षामि पृथिवीं भूत्वा कर्षणाय अयसो हलः।
names.simple_meaning: The dark-hued one

names.short_meaning: Red-eyed
names.commentary: Red-eyed. Very often we find descriptions in the Purāṇas, where the Lord is explained as having eyes like the red-lotus (Hibiscus). Generally the ruddy eyes represent anger and the incarnations are taken for the purpose of destroying the evil and so His anger is towards the evil-minded materialists who live ignoring the higher values of life.
names.simple_meaning: Red-eyed

names.short_meaning: The root Tarda means "destruction" and with the prefix Pra the root (Pra-tarda) means "supreme destruction"
names.commentary: The root Tarda (तर्द) means "destruction" ( तर्द हिसायां ) and with the prefix Pra the root (Pra-tarda) means "supreme destruction". One who does this total destruction (pratardanaḥ) is the Lord in the form of Rudra at the time of the great dissolution (Pralaya).
names.simple_meaning: The supreme destroyer

names.short_meaning: The term means 'born full' or 'ever-full'
names.commentary: The term means 'born full' or 'ever-full' (परिपूर्ण:). He is ever-full and perfect in His Essential Nature, as the Transcendental Reality, or even when He manifests in the form of His various incarnations. Especially in His chief and glorious incarnation as Lord Kṛṣṇa, He proved Himself to be ever full with His Omnipotency and Omnisciency.
names.simple_meaning: The ever-full and abundant one

names.short_meaning: One who is the very foundation or support (dhāma) of the three quarters (Kakubh)
names.commentary:
One who is the very foundation or support (dhāma) of the three quarters (Kakubh). We find this is generally commented upon and described as "all quarters, in the three realms above, below and middle."

Viewing this from the platform of Vedānta, He must be considered by us as the three Planes-of — Consciousness—the waking (Jaagrat), the dream (Svapna) and the deep-sleep (Sushupti) conditions. The fourth Plane-of — Consciousness (Tureeya) is indeed the Substratum for all the other three planes.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the very foundation or support (dhāma) of the three quarters (Kakubh)

names.short_meaning: One who gives purity to the heart
names.commentary:
One who gives purity to the heart. To the seekers who are meditating upon Him, He gives inner purity, and hence He is known as pavitraṃ. Or, the term Pavi means the weapon vajra (thunderbolt).

One who saves ( त्रायते ) his devotees from the thunderbolt of Indra (पनि) is pavitraṃ. The thunderbolt is described as an instrument in cross bones-made out of the bone of sage Dadheechi. Indra is the Lord of the Indriyas (इन्द्रियाणां राजा-इन्द्रः).

In Vedānta Indra signifies the mind. Mind's cross purposes, confusions, intellectual compromises and the consequent self-cancellation of our mental powers (saṅkalpa — Vikalpa) can be the great thunderbolt of the mind with which Indra (mind) can destroy in no time all the acquired tapas of the saadhaka.

Deep devotion, ardent meditation and firm faith in the Lord Viṣṇu save the saadhaka from all such mental storms and, therefore, the Lord acquires the significant name pavitraṃ.
names.simple_meaning: One who gives purity to the heart

names.short_meaning: Mangalam is that which not only removes the dark pains of evil, but brings the bright joys of merit
names.commentary:
Mangalam is that which not only removes the dark pains of evil, but brings the bright joys of merit. maṅgalaṃ param is Supreme Mangalam, and It can be none other than He, by whose mere remembrance all inauspiciousness gets lifted up and all Auspiciousness comes to flood our hearts. The Upaniṣad declares: "May That Brahman—who removes all inauspiciousness in man and gives man all auspiciousness, by a mere remembrance of Him -give us all auspiciousness.

अशुभानि निराचष्टे तनोति शुभसन्ततिम् । स्मृतिमात्रेण यत्पुंसां ब्रह्म तन्मङ्गलं विदुः ॥
names.simple_meaning: Mangalam is that which not only removes the dark pains of evil, but brings the bright joys of merit

names.short_meaning: "The Controller of all the five Great Elements"
names.commentary: "The Controller of all the five Great Elements". When this term is used, Īśvara becomes the Administrator of His own Law in the phenomenal world of plurality. The executive function of His Infinite Will, when manifested through Him, the Lord, Īśvara, is said to function as īśānaḥ. Or, the term can also mean One who is the Supreme Īśvara—the Paramesvara.
names.simple_meaning: "The Controller of all the five Great Elements"

names.short_meaning: One who gives (dadāti) the Pragnas to all
names.commentary: One who gives (dadāti) the prāṇas to all. The term prāṇas used in philosophy indicates "all manifestations of Life in a living body". The Source of Life from which all dynamic activities in the living organisms of the world flow out, meaning, That from which all activities emerge out is prāṇadaḥ. Taittirīya Upaniṣad (2-7) exclaims: "Who could then live, who could breath" if He be not everywhere."
names.simple_meaning: One who gives (dadāti) the Pragnas to all

names.short_meaning: That which sustains is prāṇa, and that which has got prāṇa functioning in it is called a Praanee
names.commentary: That which sustains is prāṇa (प्राणिति इति प्राणः) and that which has got prāṇa functioning in it is called a prāṇī. Since the Lord is termed as this very same prāṇa, it means by its suggestion that He is One who ever lives. The Immortal and the Eternal is prāṇaḥ The term can also mean that which gives Life-impulse even to the air; the capacity to sustain life in the atmosphere flows from Him alone. In the Kenopaniṣad we read the Supreme 'Defined' as the "prāṇa of prāṇas" (prāṇasya prāṇaḥ).
names.simple_meaning: The life-breath that sustains all

names.short_meaning: Older than all
names.commentary:
Older than all. The Infinite is That which was even before the very concept of space (Aakaasa) came into existence. The term is the superlative degree of the Aged. In short, the import of this term is the same as the more familiar term used in our sastras, the Ancient (sanātanaḥ).

Vṛddhaḥ—aged; jyāyān—more aged; jyeṣṭhaḥ—most aged.
names.simple_meaning: Older than all

names.short_meaning: The most Glorious One: Here again it is the superlative degree of glorious, Sreyah
names.commentary:
The most Glorious One: Here again it is the superlative degree of glorious, Sreyah.

Śreyān—glorious; śreyaḥ—more glorious; śreṣṭhaḥ—most glorious.
names.simple_meaning: The most excellent and glorious one

names.short_meaning: The Lord (Pati) of all living creatures (prajāḥ)
names.commentary: The Lord (Pati) of all living creatures (prajāḥ). The term Prajas means 'Children'. Therefore Prajaapati means the Great Father, to whom all beings in the living kingdom are His own children. In this sense, the term connotes One, who, as the Creator, creates all creatures.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord (Pati) of all living creatures (prajāḥ)

names.short_meaning: One who dwells in the womb (garbha) of the world (hiraṇya)
names.commentary:
One who dwells in the womb (garbha) of the world (hiraṇya). The Upaniṣad declares: "All these are in-dwelt by the Lord." The "Golden Universe" is an idiom in Sanskrit where 'gold' means "objects of fulfilment and joy". One who dwells in them all is hiraṇyagarbhaḥ. The term can also mean as He who, having become first the Creator, has come to be considered as the womb of all objects.

īśāvāsyam idaṃ sarvam.

हिरण्यगर्भः समवर्तताग्रे।
names.simple_meaning: One who dwells in the womb (garbha) of the world (hiraṇya)

names.short_meaning: One who is the very womb of the world (bhūḥ)
names.commentary:
One who is the very womb of the world (bhūḥ). The One from whom the world has emerged out. In the Cosmic Form of the Lord, this world occupies an insignificant though sacred portion, just as the foetus in the womb, constantly and lovingly nurtured and nourished by the very Essence in the mother. Or, bhūḥ = the earth: the divine consort of Hari: Garbha = Protector.

The Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 3.1.2 says: "The Divine Earth, the wife of Viṣṇu."
names.simple_meaning: One who is the very womb of the world (bhūḥ)

names.short_meaning: The Lord of māyā, Spouse of Mahālakṣmī
names.commentary:
The Lord of māyā, Spouse of Mahālakṣmī. Or, the term can signify the One who is ultimately experienced through a diligent practice of "Madhu-technique": the very famous Madhu vidyā of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad. The term mādhavaḥ can also mean One who is the Silent (Mauni); who is ever the Non-interfering Observer, the Silent Witness of the physical, mental and intellectual activities in the realm of change. To put it in one word, He is the One whom the seeker experiences when he has stilled his mind which has been purified by Yoga practices.

Expounding the significance of the name Mādhava, Vyāsa says in the Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva:

मधुविद्यावबोधत्वाद् धवत्वाद्वा श्रियोऽनिशम् । मौनाद् ध्यानाच्च योगाच्च विद्धि भारत माधवम् ॥

"O Bhārata, know Mādhava by mauna, by meditation and by yoga."
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of māyā, Spouse of Mahālakṣmī

names.short_meaning: One who destroyed the great demon Madhu
names.commentary: One who destroyed the great demon Madhu. The story of Viṣṇu destroying these two demons, Madhu and Kaitabha, is a story of secret suggestions in Mahābhārata. Madhu also means in Veda (Madhu - honey) as the fruits of actions (Karma-phala). Actions leave impressions and these sensuous vāsanās are destroyed by meditations on the Reality and so the Supreme gathers to Itself the name madhusūdanaḥ: "the Destrover of vāsanās."
names.simple_meaning: One who destroyed the great demon Madhu

names.short_meaning: One who is Omnipotent, and so has all powers in Him to the full
names.commentary: One who is Omnipotent, and so has all powers in Him to the full. The manifested powers of Life express themselves in every intelligent man as the power of action in the body (Krivaa śakti), the power of desire in the mind (Icchaa śakti) and the power of knowledge in the intellect (Inaana śakti). All these three powers are manifestations of Him, and since He is the One everywhere, He is the total mighty power—the Great Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: One who is Omnipotent, and so has all powers in Him to the full

names.short_meaning: One full of prowess (Vikrama), courage, daring
names.commentary: One full of prowess (Vikrama), courage, daring. Or, it can be One who has "Special foot steps". This term commemorates how the Lord, as Vamana, measured with His tiny three steps all the three worlds.
ocr_notes: Scan locus corrected from [41] to [40, 41] by complete-text replay against the PDF page OCR.
names.simple_meaning: One full of prowess (Vikrama), courage, daring

names.short_meaning: Lord Viṣṇu's Divine Bow is called 'Śārṅga' and it is described as the mightiest among the weapons
names.commentary: Lord Viṣṇu's Divine Bow is called 'Śārṅga' and it is described as the mightiest among the weapons. One who is having this Mighty Bow at all times is dhanvī. It can also remind us of His incarnation as Śrī Ramachandraji, when, in order to protect the world from the mighty rākṣasas of Lanka, He had to dedicate a substantial part of His life almost constantly wielding his bow: hence Śrī, Rama came to be known as Dhanushpaani; in His attitude of protection He is known as Kodandaraama. Thus, the term dhanvī, the Wielder of the bow, is quite appropriate for Viṣṇu. "I am Śrī Rama among the Wielders of the bow" —Gītā Ch. 10, St. 31.
names.simple_meaning: The wielder of the divine bow Śārṅga

names.short_meaning: Supremely intelligent; One who is capable of understanding everything
names.commentary: Supremely intelligent; One who is capable of understanding everything. One who has the capacity to comprehend intellectually all that is happening around is called medhāvī. Since Consciousness is the One Light in all living creatures, which illumines all intellects, and since Viṣṇu is this Infinite Consciousness, He is the One Knower, knowing all things, at all times, at once. Hence Sarasvati, the Goddess of Learning and Knowledge is described as the very tongue of Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: Supremely intelligent; One who is capable of understanding everything

names.short_meaning: While describing the term Vikramee (75) we had already explained the meaning contents of Vikrama, and thus Vikrama is an appellation that had come to Viṣṇu as a result of His Supernatural Act of measuring the universe with three steps
names.commentary:
While describing the term Vikramee (75) we had already explained the meaning contents of Vikrama, and thus Vikrama is an appellation that had come to Viṣṇu as a result of His Supernatural Act of measuring the universe with three steps.

Also, Vi means the "king-of-birds", the white-necked eagle; Krama means steps and, therefore, 'movement or travel'. In this sense Vikrama can mean: "One who rides on the white-eagle (mind) is Viṣṇu"—who is described as having Garuda for His vehicle (Vaahanam).
names.simple_meaning: The one of mighty stride who measured the universe

names.short_meaning: He who is All — Pervading is kramaḥ
names.commentary: He who is All — Pervading is kramaḥ. Because of His All — Pervasiveness, the Infinite is called as Viṣṇu. That which goes beyond the frontiers of the known is the Supreme, and, therefore, in the description of Him, who has manifested as the Cosmos, we have in Purushasookta an indication that He not only pervades all that is known but "extends even beyond by ten digits" (Atyatishthat Dasaangulam).
names.simple_meaning: He who is All — Pervading is kramaḥ

names.short_meaning: One who is 'incomparably Great' in glory-anuttamaḥ
names.commentary:
One who is 'incomparably Great' in glory-anuttamaḥ. In the Sanskrit construction of the word, it means something more than what we have said; it means: 'He is one, beyond whom there exists none who is greater than He (अविद्यमानः उत्तमो यस्मात्=unexcelled).

The Upaniṣad itself describes Him: "अविद्यमानः परं नापरमस्ति किञ्चित". In Gītā (XI-43) we read: "For Thy equal exists not, whence another superior to Thee?" In Śrī Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad (12) we again read, "There is nothing above or below, equal to Him".
names.simple_meaning: One who is 'incomparably Great' in glory-anuttamaḥ

names.short_meaning: One who cannot be attacked, stormed or beleaguered successfully
names.commentary: One who cannot be attacked, stormed or beleaguered successfully. In short, He is All — Powerful. In the Purāṇas, we find Daityas and Asuras and others, mighty and powerful ones, become themselves helpless victims of His Power and come under His sway. To one who has realized the Infinite, the lower nature of the mind (Daityas) and the enchantments of the senses (rākṣasas), are all helpless to overwhelm Him. "Rasopyasya Param Drishtvaa Nivartate" — (रसोऽप्यस्य परं दृष्ट्वा निवर्तते ) — Gītā Ch. 2, St. 59.
names.simple_meaning: One who cannot be attacked, stormed or beleaguered successfully

names.short_meaning: He who knows all that is done by all: the One Knower who knows all physical activities, all emotional feelings, and all intellectual thoughts and motives
names.commentary:
He who knows all that is done by all: the One Knower who knows all physical activities, all emotional feelings, and all intellectual thoughts and motives. He illumines them all, in all, at all times. Hence He is called Kritajna. Viṣṇu is the One who knows clearly the exact depth of sincerity, the true ardency of devotion, the real amount of purity in the bosom of all his devotees, and, accordingly, brings joy and bliss to their hearts.

In modern society this word is used to mean 'gratitude' (Kritajnataa prakathanam) and in the context of the earlier explanations gratitude is not so much in the formal words but it is in the constant awareness of what all others have done to us and an alertness to pay back the debt in terms of similar services to others. Gratitude in Bharat is not expressed with a couple of dry words "Thank you".
names.simple_meaning: The knower of all deeds

names.short_meaning: The One, who is the very dynamism behind all activities
names.commentary: The One, who is the very dynamism behind all activities. He is the Inevitability behind the result of actions. He is called kṛtiḥ because it is He who visits to bless the good and to punish the evil; in short; He is the One who rewards all our actions.
names.simple_meaning: The One, who is the very dynamism behind all activities

names.short_meaning: One who is the Self in all beings
names.commentary: One who is the Self in all beings. In the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (7.24.1) when the disciple asks, "Where does the Lord, the Infinite, stand established?" the Sruti answers, "In Its own glory established ever is the Self"—(Sve Mahimni Pratishthitah).
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Self in all beings

names.short_meaning: The denizens of the Heavens are called in the Purāṇas as Suras
names.commentary:
The denizens of the Heavens are called in the Purāṇas as Suras. Eesa means the Lord; Suresa, therefore, indicates the God of gods, the Lord of the Suras. The gods are called as Suras because they are capable of blessing their devotees with a fulfilment of their desires. Therefore, sureśaḥ means One who is the best among those who fulfil all the demands of their devotees (Suras). In short, He is the One who gives the Supreme State of Beatitude and the consequent total liberation from all desires of the ego.

And their opposites are called Asuras.

सु ष्ठु राति ददाति इति सुरः।
names.simple_meaning: The lord of the gods

names.short_meaning: The Refuge for all who are suffering from the thraldom of imperfection in life
names.commentary:
The Refuge for all who are suffering from the thraldom of imperfection in life. According to the Sanskrit Lexicon (Amarakosa), the term śaraṇaṃ means 'Protector' and also 'home'. Since the Lord is the Ultimate Goal, śaraṇaṃ, He is also the "Destination", the 'Harbour'.

The One who realizes Him comes to live in Him. He is the Home to which the Prodigal Son (jīva) ultimately returns. Not only for the Men of Realization is He the Home, but for all creatures, movables and immovables. He is the Home, to which they all disappear to rest and to revive during Pralava (Sleep).

निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः।
names.simple_meaning: The Refuge for all who are suffering from the thraldom of imperfection in life

names.short_meaning: One who is Himself the Infinite Bliss
names.commentary: One who is Himself the Infinite Bliss. Transcending the mind lie the shores of Bliss, beyond the waters of agitations. The Infinite is described in our Upaniṣads as the "Sacchidaananda", ever of the same nature—"Saantam Sivam Sundaram".
names.simple_meaning: One who is Himself the Infinite Bliss

names.short_meaning: Retas means 'seed'; the term connotes that He is the seed from which the tree of life has sprung forth
names.commentary: Retas means 'seed'; the term connotes that He is the seed from which the tree of life has sprung forth. He who is the very cause for the entire play of experience in the world of pluralistic objects (Sarva — Prapancha — Kaaranabhootah) is called viśvaretāḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The seed from which the universe arises

names.short_meaning: He from whom all living creatures (prajā) spring forth (Bhava) is known as prajābhavaḥ
names.commentary: He from whom all living creatures (prajā) spring forth (Bhava) is known as prajābhavaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: He from whom all living creatures (prajā) spring forth (Bhava) is known as prajābhavaḥ

names.short_meaning: Ahan has got two meanings: the 24-hour-day or the 12-hour day-time
names.commentary: Ahan has got two meanings: the 24-hour-day or the 12-hour day-time. He is of the nature of 'day-time' means "He is the One, ever effulgent and bright"; as bright as the daylight that illumines all objects around. In case we accept the other meaning, "the 24-hour-day", then, a day being a unit of time, the term Ahan can also mean, "One who is of the nature of Time itself". Also He is one who does not (a) ever destroy (han) the devotees who have surrendered themselves to Him.
names.simple_meaning: Ahan has got two meanings: the 24-hour-day or the 12-hour day-time

names.short_meaning: One who is of the nature of year-meaning One who is the Lord of Time; He, from whom the very 'concept of Time' rises
names.commentary: One who is of the nature of year-meaning One who is the Lord of Time; He, from whom the very 'concept of Time' rises.
names.simple_meaning: Time itself, the source of the year

names.short_meaning: One who is unapproachable
names.commentary: One who is unapproachable. 'Vyaala' also means 'Serpent'; to those who have no devotion or understanding, God or Truth is as horrible and terrible as a 'serpent'. Moreover, it is so difficult to grasp in our understanding that It is like a serpent: ever eluding, always slippery.
names.simple_meaning: One who is unapproachable

names.short_meaning: One whose very nature is Knowledge
names.commentary:
One whose very nature is Knowledge. That the Supreme is Knowledge Absolute is very well known. It is in the light of Consciousness that all 'knowledges' are possible. 'Knowledge of a thing' is the Awareness of its nature. Awareness is Knowledge. Since the Supreme is the One Awareness everywhere, all 'Knowledges' spring from the Self. Hence, He is called "the Pure Knowledge". "Consciousness is Brahman" is one of the mahāvākyas.

"Prajñānam brahma." — Aitareya Upaniṣad 3.3.
names.simple_meaning: One whose very nature is Knowledge

names.short_meaning: This term, "All-seeing", is very appropriate
names.commentary:
This term, "All-seeing", is very appropriate inasmuch as the Supreme Consciousness has been defined and indicated in the Kenopaniṣad as, "That which the eyes cannot see, but because of which the eyes see." It is the Seer in the eyes, the Hearer in the ears, the Speaker, the Feeler and the Thinker. And since this Principle of Consciousness is One everywhere, as expressed through the equipments, It is indeed the One Seer in all 'seeing', by everyone, everywhere. The Upaniṣad says, "विश्वतश्चक्षुर्विश्वाक्षः", and the Gītā indicates Him as "One who has eyes and heads everywhere"—"सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्".

Sarvadarśanaḥ: omnispective.
names.simple_meaning: The all-seeing one

names.short_meaning: Unborn
names.commentary:
Unborn. Birth implies a modification; birth cannot be without the death of its previous condition. Since the Eternal and the Infinite is ever Changeless, there can be in It neither birth nor death. That which is born must necessarily die (जातस्य हि ध्रुवो मृत्युः — Gītā 2.27), and so that which is unborn should be deathless (amṛta).

Ṛg Veda 1.81.5: "He was neither born nor is He going to be born."

न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचिन्नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः ।
अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे ॥ — Gītā 2.20.

In the Mahābhārata (Śānti Parva 343) we read, "I am not born, nor am I to be born, nor have I any possibility of future birth; I am the Kṣetrajña in all beings; hence I am called 'Unborn'."
names.simple_meaning: Unborn

names.short_meaning: God of all gods or the Supreme Controller of all
names.commentary: God of all gods or the Supreme Controller of all. In a sense it means the Almighty, the All-powerful. "He is the Lord of all," says Brihad Upaniṣad (6-4-2).
names.simple_meaning: God of all gods or the Supreme Controller of all

names.short_meaning: One who has achieved all that has to be achieved, as He Himself is the Final Goal for all
names.commentary: One who has achieved all that has to be achieved, as He Himself is the Final Goal for all. Or the term can also mean "the most famous" (प्रसिद्धः).
names.simple_meaning: One who has achieved all that has to be achieved, as He Himself is the Final Goal for all

names.short_meaning: He who is available for recognition (Siddha) everywhere at all points in His nature as Pure Consciousness
names.commentary:
He who is available for recognition (Siddha) everywhere at all points in His nature as Pure Consciousness. Again, Siddhi also means the 'fruit of action', and in the context here this would mean, "He who gives the Infinite fruit of Kaivalya, mokṣa." All other karmas can acquire for us only relative joys of the heavens, but in realizing the Self the seeker gains an 'Infinite State from which there is no return', so describes the Gītā.

यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम । — Gītā 15.6.
names.simple_meaning: He who is available for recognition (Siddha) everywhere at all points in His nature as Pure Consciousness

names.short_meaning: One who is the very beginning (ādi) of all; One who was in existence earlier than everything else
names.commentary: One who is the very beginning (ādi) of all; One who was in existence earlier than everything else. Even before the effects arise, the Cause. The Infinite which was before creation and from which the created beings had emerged out, as an effect, is naturally the Primary Cause (Moola-kāraṇa).
names.simple_meaning: The beginning of all

names.short_meaning: Chyutah= Fallen; acyutaḥ: One who has never fallen: the Ever — Pure Reality which is never fallen into the mis-conceptions of Samsar: the Pure Knowledge in which ignorance has never come to pollute Its purity
names.commentary: Chyutah= Fallen; acyutaḥ: One who has never fallen: the Ever — Pure Reality which is never fallen into the mis-conceptions of Samsar: the Pure Knowledge in which ignorance has never come to pollute Its purity. Lord Himself says in Bhagavata, "I have never ever before fallen from my Real Nature; therefore, I am acyutaḥ", ("यस्मान्न च्यतपूर्वोऽहं अच्यतस्तेन कर्मणा")
names.simple_meaning: The unfallen and ever-pure one

names.short_meaning: There is a lot of controversy among pundits upon the exact meaning of this term
names.commentary:
There is a lot of controversy among pundits upon the exact meaning of this term. But all controversies become meaningless when we read Bhagavān's own words, "Since Kapi has a meaning the 'boar', and since vṛṣa has the meaning of 'dharma', the great Kaśyapa Prajāpati says I am vṛṣākapiḥ."

कपिर्वराहः श्रेष्ठश्च धर्मश्च वृष उच्यते ।
तस्माद् वृषाकपिं प्राह कश्यपो मां प्रजापतिः ॥

In Sanskrit the term Kapi has a meaning: 'that which saves one from drowning'. Lord in the form of the Great Boar (Varāha), in that incarnation, had lifted the world from the waters at the end of the deluge; the term vṛṣa means 'dharma'. One who thus lifts the world drowned in Adharma to the sunny fields of dharma is vṛṣākapiḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The Boar who raises the world from adharma to dharma

names.short_meaning: One who has His manifestations (ātmā) in Infinite varieties, almost unaccountable (Ameya)
names.commentary: One who has His manifestations (ātmā) in Infinite varieties, almost unaccountable (Ameya). The virāṭ puruṣa of the Form of All — Lord of the Cosmic Form is suggested here. As all forms have risen from Him, exist in Him, and dissolve into Him alone, all forms are His own different forms.
names.simple_meaning: One who has His manifestations (ātmā) in Infinite varieties, almost unaccountable (Ameya)

names.short_meaning: Yoga is from Yuj 'to join'; 'to attach'
names.commentary:
Yoga is from Yuj 'to join'; 'to attach'. One who is totally free (vinissritah) from all contacts or attachments. Attachment to a thing is possible only when the object-of-attachment is other than the subject. In the One Infinite Reality there cannot be any attachment with anything, mainly because there is nothing here that is not the Infinite Itself. The Infinite is a Mass of Love; there is no attachment in It; for, attachment is Love with possessiveness and desire for gratification. "This puruṣa is, indeed, unattached", roars Brihad Upaniṣad (6-3-15).

Lastly, the term, Sarva — Yoga — Vinissritah can also mean that He is beyond the reach of the various systems of Yogas taught in the śāstras. These systems are to quieten the mind, to end the misapprehensions-of — Truth, to annihilate the māyā. What is there left over in the seeker's bosom is the Self—the Great Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The one free from every bond and attachment

names.short_meaning: The One who is the very support of all elements, and the One who Himself is the very Essence of the elements
names.commentary: The One who is the very support of all elements, and the One who Himself is the very Essence of the elements. This is something like the dream made up of our own mind; and the very same dream-world plays itself out, all the time sustained in the very same mind. Similarly, the Self indwells all and all dwell in the Self. In the Gītā we are told by the Lord, "I am among the Vasus the Paavakah"—"वसना पावकरचास्मि"—(Gītā. Ch. 10, St. 23). Therefore, the Self exists like air—allowing everything to remain in it and sustaining everything by it.
names.simple_meaning: The One who is the very support of all elements, and the One who Himself is the very Essence of the elements

names.short_meaning: One who has a mind which is Supremely Pure; meaning a mind that has none of the sins of passions and pains; none of the storms of desires and jealousies; none of the quakes of likes and dislikes
names.commentary: One who has a mind which is Supremely Pure; meaning a mind that has none of the sins of passions and pains; none of the storms of desires and jealousies; none of the quakes of likes and dislikes.
names.simple_meaning: The one whose mind is supremely pure

names.short_meaning: He is the Real
names.commentary:
He is the Real. The term Satyam used in philosophy has a special connotation. That which remains the same in all the three periods of time is called Satvam. That which seemingly exists, but which never was nor shall ever be, is considered as a false delusion, A-satva. He who remains the same, before the creation, during the existence and even after the dissolution, is the Infinite Truth, satyaḥ. The Taittirīya Upaniṣad thunders that the Eternal Truth is "Truth, Knowledge, Bliss": "Satyam, jñānam, Anantam Brahma" ("सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं ब्रह्म") — Taittirīya Upaniṣad: 2-1.

We may here mention a couple of other meanings that are generally given to this term "The best among good people is Satyam (सत्स साथ: सत्य:). Again, the word Satyam is made up of three sounds — Sat-ti-yam — and, herein, according to the Upaniṣad itself, "Sat means prāṇa, ti means food, Yam means sun;" therefore, Satyam is the Law which orders the food to sustain the prāṇa when both are blessed by the sources of all gross energies in the cosmos, the Sun.
names.simple_meaning: He is the Real

names.short_meaning: He who is equally in all
names.commentary:
He who is equally in all. In Kaṭhopaniṣad we read the declaration of Lord Death to Nachiketas how the same Truth has come to express itself differently from form to form (एको वशी सर्वभूतान्तरात्मा एक बहुधा यः करोति तमात्मस्थं यऽनुपत्रयन्ति धीरास्तेषां सूखं…).

रूपं To visualize the Paramesvara who revels equally in all, among the perishables and imperishables, is the Vision Divine. Kauseshika Upaniṣad (3-9) says, "One should understand that the Self is the same-in-all". In the Gītā also is the declaration "I am the Seer in all the fields-of-experiences everywhere" (“क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत”—Gītā Ch. 13, St. 3).
names.simple_meaning: He who is equally in all

names.short_meaning: The term Sammatam means 'acceptable'
names.commentary: The term Sammatam means 'acceptable'. The One Truth, which has been proved and accepted by the ṛṣis in the Upaniṣads through subtle logic and philosophical reasoning, is called Sammatah. This is the most direct and very appealing meaning: But there are some who would interpret this portion of the Thousand Names of Lord Viṣṇu by combining samātmā (107) and sammitaḥ (108) to form together a single 'Name', wherein the compound word would read Samaatma-asammitah. Here the term Asammitah then would come to mean "One who is incomparable, Inimitable (Atulya) who has none to equal Him".
names.simple_meaning: The acceptable one, equal to all

names.short_meaning: Equal; the same
names.commentary: Equal; the same. Truth remains the same. One Infinite Reality plays the game of plurality. As has been said in the Kaṭhopaniṣad, "The One Principle of Fire having entered this world burns itself out differently according to the equipments upon which it is manifested", so the One Truth manifests as the many jīvas. Hence He is called the samaḥ. Also it can mean as One who is ever united, with (Sa) Lakṣmī' (Maa).
names.simple_meaning: Equal; the same

names.short_meaning: Moghah means "useless fellow" (Nishphalah), "a disappointing power"
names.commentary: Moghah means "useless fellow" (Nishphalah), "a disappointing power". Amogha is the opposite of it: "Ever Useful", "Ever the Ful-filler" of all the wishes and demands of His devotees. Chāndogya Upaniṣad (8-1-5) declares: "Truthful is His wish, and Truth is His resolve".
names.simple_meaning: The unfailing one whose acts are never futile

names.short_meaning: One who can be contacted and fully experienced in the Heart Space (Pundareekam)
names.commentary: One who can be contacted and fully experienced in the Heart Space (Pundareekam). In the Nārāyaṇa Upaniṣad (10) we find the same term employed: "In the core of the body, in the Heart Space, dwells the Supreme." In the 'Heart', the meditator can experience the Reality more readily and very clearly, and so the All — Pervading Reality is described as "dwelling in the Heart-cave".
names.simple_meaning: The one realized in the lotus of the heart

names.short_meaning: vṛṣa means dharma
names.commentary: vṛṣa means dharma. One whose every activity is righteous and who acts only to establish righteousness. "For the sake of establishing dharma, I am born in every age", says Lord—(Gītā Ch. 4, St. 8).
names.simple_meaning: The one whose actions are dharma

names.short_meaning: One who is of the form (ākṛti) of dharma (vṛṣa)
names.commentary: One who is of the form (ākṛti) of dharma (vṛṣa). It is not only that His actions are righteous but He is Himself Righteousness. It can also mean as One who takes different forms during His Divine Incarnations—all for maintaining the Rule of dharma in the world.
names.simple_meaning: One who is of the form (ākṛti) of dharma (vṛṣa)

names.short_meaning: One who makes all people weep
names.commentary: One who makes all people weep, ( रोदयतीति रुद्र: ). At the time of death or during the total dissolution, the One who makes all weep is rudraḥ. From a devotee's standpoint the same term is interpreted as the One who liquidated (द्रवयति ) all sorrows ( हत ) is rudraḥ. Bhagavān declares Himself to be "Among the Rudras, I am Śaṅkara "रुद्राणां शंकरश्चास्मि"—(Gītā Ch. 10, St. 23). According to the Vedic terminology there are 11 Rudras; this eleventh "Rudra" is called as Śaṅkara: Sam-karoti-iti = Sankarah — "One who blesses all with Auspiciousness (Sam)."
names.simple_meaning: One who makes all people weep

names.short_meaning: One who has many heads
names.commentary:
One who has many heads. The Purushasooktam of the Rig Veda describes the Cosmic Form of the Lord with a narration, "The puruṣa of thousand heads, thousand eyes and thousand feet…" In Gītā a similar description of the Universal Form of the Lord is found in Chapter XI. Again in the Gītā Chapter XIII when the Lord was describing the Infinite Goal to be known (Jñeyam), He describes It as "Everywhere legs, everywhere hands, everywhere eyes, everywhere His face".

Thus, He whose personal manifestations constitute the universe is known as "One who has many heads."
names.simple_meaning: One who has many heads

names.short_meaning: One who rules over the worlds
names.commentary: One who rules over the worlds. "Like a King" — (राजवत् सदा) — Atmabodham gives this analogy. He in whose presence all the instruments of perception, feeling and knowing continue their co-ordinated activity is the Self, the Atman, who is Great Lord Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: One who rules over the worlds

names.short_meaning: One who is the Total Cause from which alone the entire world of experiences has emerged out
names.commentary: One who is the Total Cause from which alone the entire world of experiences (visvam) has emerged out (विश्वस्य योनि: विश्वयोनि:). The womb (yoni) from which thoughts and actions had risen is called Visvavonih.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Total Cause from which alone the entire world of experiences has emerged out

names.short_meaning: One who has beautiful and efficient ears
