names.commentary: One who has beautiful and efficient ears (Sravas): "Everywhere are His ears" (सर्वतः श्रुतिमत्) — (Gītā Ch. 13, St. 13) meaning thereby He is the Hearer in all ears. The term Sravas not only means ears, but it also means "names" - so Suchisravas can mean 'One who has Divine and Sacred names'. Thus, the devotee can invoke Him with thousands of His names when He can readily listen in and rightly understand the exact purity and the real depth of devotion in the devotee. Also the term can be used to indicate the One whose "names" are worthy of being heard by seekers.
names.simple_meaning: One who has beautiful and efficient ears

names.short_meaning: One who is Immortal and Immutable
names.commentary: One who is Immortal and Immutable. Mritam = dead. The Infinite is Ajarah, Amarah and avyayaḥ. It can also mean as One who is of the nature of Nectar (Amritam) — a sure cure for those who are suffering from malady of ignorance. amṛtaḥ also means mokṣa; and thus it is indicated. He is the ever-liberated—the Pure State of Being.
names.simple_meaning: One who is Immortal and Immutable

names.short_meaning: One who is both permanent (śāśvataḥ) and irremovable (sthāṇuḥ)
names.commentary: One who is both permanent (śāśvataḥ) and irremovable (sthāṇuḥ). He is the One who remains Changeless, because Immortal; who remains the same in all periods of time, because permanent (śāśvataḥ): and who remains changeless in His nature of Consciousness (sthāṇuḥ). This is a single term (śāśvata-sthāṇuḥ) and, therefore, we must add the meanings together - Permanent and Changeless; Permanently Changeless Factor in life is Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: One who is both permanent (śāśvataḥ) and irremovable (sthāṇuḥ)

names.short_meaning: He who is the most Glorious (Vara) Destination (āroha)
names.commentary: He who is the most Glorious (Vara) Destination (āroha). The Seat of the Self is the most Glorious because the imperfections of the world-of-matter (Prakriti) are not there in the Spirit (puruṣa). Liberation from the thraldom of matter is the arrival of the Infinitude of the Self. "He never returns" (न च निवर्तते), thunders the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (8-15-1) three times in one and the same breath, assuring us that one who has reached the Seat of Viṣṇu, beyond the frontiers of the intellect, there is for him no more any return ever into the ego-centric life of tensions of sorrows.
names.simple_meaning: He who is the most Glorious (Vara) Destination (āroha)

names.short_meaning: One of great Tapas
names.commentary: One of great Tapas. The term tapas in Sanskrit has three meanings: 'Knowledge' (Inaana), 'Prosperity' (Aisvarya) and also 'Might' (Prataapa). It is in the presence of Consciousness that we come to know all our experiences. 'Conscious of' a thing or an idea is the 'Knowledge of' the thing or the idea. That about which I am not conscious of, I have really no knowledge of it. All knowledges, of all bosoms, in all living creatures, everywhere, at all times, cannot be without the play of Consciousness upon the respective objects of knowledge, and hence this Consciousness is indicated in the Upaniṣads as Pure Knowledge, in the light of which alone all knowledges are possible. All achievements and prosperity (Aisvarva), all might and power of the living creatures can express themselves through them only when they are alive. This great truth is Maha Viṣṇu. "Whose Tapas is of the nature of Knowledge" (Mundaka — Upaniṣad. 1-1-9).
names.simple_meaning: One of great Tapas

names.short_meaning: "He who has gone everywhere", meaning "One who pervades everything"
names.commentary: "He who has gone everywhere", meaning "One who pervades everything". The cause pervades its effect: gold in all ornaments; ocean in all waves; cotton in all cloth. The Infinite Consciousness Itself expresses as both world-of-matter (kṣetra) and the Knower-of-the-field (kṣetrajña). Viṣṇu, the Infinite is beyond these two (Uttamah puruṣaḥ) in whom there is no expression of matter and, therefore, no 'Knower'-hood. He is the All — Pervading Self. Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The all-pervading one who has gone everywhere

names.short_meaning: One who is All- Knowing (Sarvavit) and Effulgent (bhānuḥ)
names.commentary: One who is All- Knowing (Sarvavit) and Effulgent (bhānuḥ). The Light of Consciousness is the "Light that illumines all lights" and it is again Consciousness that "illumines even darkness" ("ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिः तमसः परमुच्यते )”-Gītā Ch. 13, St. 17. In the Mundaka Upaniṣad (4.10) also we read: "तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति": "By its Light alone it illumines all other experiences." Sarvavit — bhānuḥ is one term: meaning that all Knowing Effulgent Consciousness.
names.simple_meaning: One who is All- Knowing (Sarvavit) and Effulgent (bhānuḥ)

names.short_meaning: He, while facing whom, even the mighty army of the gods retreat and scatter away, is called as viṣvaksenaḥ
names.commentary: He, while facing whom, even the mighty army of the gods retreat and scatter away, is called as viṣvaksenaḥ. He is the Almighty and All — Powerful. and no army can stand against Him.
names.simple_meaning: The one before whom hostile armies scatter

names.short_meaning: The term Ardayati is a verb meaning both 'giving sorrow' or 'giving joy'
names.commentary: The term Ardayati (अर्दयति) is a verb meaning both 'giving sorrow' or 'giving joy'. Thus, One who gives sorrow and disaster to the vicious, and who blesses with joy and peace to the good people is called janārdanaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The one who brings both discipline and joy to beings

names.short_meaning: The term Veda comes from the root vid: 'to know'
names.commentary: The term Veda comes from the root vid: 'to know'. Since Veda gives knowledge, the Lord is termed as vedaḥ, in the sense, that He is the One who gives the Knowledge of the Reality, because He is the very Reality. In Mahābhārata, Vyasa says: "Kṛṣṇa alone is All-vedas, All-sciences, All-techniques and All-dedicated Actions"— "सर्वे वेदा: सर्वेविद्या: संशास्त्राः सर्वयज्ञाः सर्वज्ञञ्च कृष्णः". In the Bhagavad Gītā (Ch. 10, St. 2) Lord says: "Out of mere compassion for them, I, abiding in their Self, destroy the darkness born of ignorance, by the luminous lamp of wisdom".
names.simple_meaning: The Veda; knowledge itself

names.short_meaning: 'One who knows the veda'
names.commentary:
'One who knows the veda'. The Lord alone is the One Experience without which the Vedas cannot be fully realized. The surest and the most exhaustive commentary of the Vedas is to be found only in a stilled mind, which is in communion with Viṣṇu, the Supreme Reality.

Gītā (Ch. 15, St. 15) says, "I am the author of the Vedānta, as well as the Knower of the Vedas."
names.simple_meaning: 'One who knows the veda'

names.short_meaning: He who has no imperfections (Vyanga) anywhere in him—The All — Perfect
names.commentary: He who has no imperfections (Vyanga) anywhere in him—The All — Perfect. The term Vyanga also means person, and so Avyanga means One who cannot be known by anyone in any 'personal-form'. Gītā plainly says "This great Reality is Imperceptible, Unthinkable, without any modifications". —"अव्यक्तोऽयमचिन्त्योऽयमविकार्योऽयम्चिकार्योऽयम्चिकार्योऽयम्चिकार्योऽयम्चिकार्योऽयम्चिकार्योऽयम्चिकार्योऽयम्चिकार्योऽयम्चिकार्योऽयम्चिकार्योऽय Ch. 2, St. 25.
ocr_notes: Scan locus corrected from [53] to [53, 54] by complete-text replay against the PDF page OCR.
names.simple_meaning: He who has no imperfections (Vyanga) anywhere in him—The All — Perfect

names.short_meaning: One whose very limbs are the Vedas
names.commentary: One whose very limbs are the Vedas. In Kenopaniṣad in the closing stanzas, the teacher insists that all knowledges are Its limbs —“वेदाः सर्वाङ्गानि…”
names.simple_meaning: One whose very limbs are the Vedas

names.short_meaning: ‘One who contemplates upon the Veda is vedavit’: (Vedam Vichaarayati = vedavit)
names.commentary:
‘One who contemplates upon the Veda is vedavit’: (Vedam Vichaarayati = vedavit). Mere word meaning cannot give us the true concept of the subtle theme discussed in the Vedas. Continuous reflection upon their declarations alone can reach us to the peaks of their imports. In the Gītā, Bhagavān Himself declares that He is not only the very Revealer of Vedas but He is at once the Knower of the Veda-"वेदान्तकृद्वेदिवदेव चाहम"-Gītā Ch. 15, St. 15.

It is absolutely necessary that the student of the Vedas should try to understand the meaning of their declaration. To repeat the mantras parrot-like is not of any consequence: 'He who has studied the Vedas but has not understood the meaning, but carries a load, as the 'road-rest' on the roadside.' Thus He who constantly reflects upon the Veda, and naturally lives upto it, is the Great Lord.

स्थाणुरयं भारहारः किलाभूदधीत्य वेदं न विजानाति योऽर्थम्।
names.simple_meaning: The knower and contemplator of the Veda

names.short_meaning: The term Kavi in the Vedas means the 'Seer'
names.commentary:
The term Kavi in the Vedas means the 'Seer'. One who experiences something more than the ordinary is called a Kavi. In the Īśāvāsyopaniṣad (8) we read: "कविर्मनीषी परिभः स्वयंभूः"—"The Seer, the Intelligent…"

In the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (5-7-23) we read: "There is no Seer except Him." In the Glory of the Lord, He confesses, in the Gītā, "among the Poets, I am Usanas, Sukra — Aachaarya" (कवीनामश्राना कवि:).
names.simple_meaning: The seer

names.short_meaning: One who presides over all fields of experiences — all lokas
names.commentary:
One who presides over all fields of experiences — all lokas. President is one who is responsible for the conduct of the assembly; he guides the discussion in a disciplined manner, and ultimately at the end of it all, he dissolves the meeting. All through the discussions he never interferes with the freedom of speech and action of the members, if they act within the agenda of the day. Similarly, the Lord presides over all the fields of activities, never interfering with the freedom of the individuals to act. "The Supreme puruṣa in this body is also called the spectator, the permitter, the supporter, the enjoyer, the great Lord, and the Supreme Self." From the Puranic standpoint the Lord in His Vāmana manifestation was installed as the king of the three worlds and, therefore, this name, say the Pauraanikas.

उपद्रष्टानुमन्ता च भर्ता भोक्ता महेश्वरः । परमात्मेति चाप्युक्तो देहेऽस्मिन् पुरुषः परः ॥ — Gītā 13.22.
names.simple_meaning: One who presides over all fields of experiences — all lokas

names.short_meaning: The President of the Heavens to whom the Devas run for protection when they are threatened by their constant enemies - the Daityas and the Asuras
names.commentary: The President of the Heavens to whom the Devas run for protection when they are threatened by their constant enemies - the Daityas and the Asuras. When in the Heaven of our bosom, the thought-angels are threatened by the negative tendencies and criminal purposes, He to whom the good in us surrender totally for sure protection and safety is Viṣṇu, the President within the bosom.
names.simple_meaning: The lord of the gods

names.short_meaning: Presiding over the activities of the living organisms, Consciousness revels, illumining both the good and the evil therein
names.commentary: Presiding over the activities of the living organisms, Consciousness revels, illumining both the good and the evil therein. The One Sacred factor that constantly thus illumines all the nature and functions (dharma) of the body, mind and intellect is the dharmādhyakṣaḥ, Lord Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: Presiding over the activities of the living organisms, Consciousness revels, illumining both the good and the evil therein

names.short_meaning: kṛtam = that which is done = that which is manifested or created
names.commentary:
kṛtam = that which is done = that which is manifested or created. Akritam, therefore, is that which has not manifested or become. The former (kṛtam) indicates all the "effects" manifested out of the Creator's activities, and the latter (Akritam) is the "cause" from which no manifestation has yet emerged — it is still unmanifest.

The Self, the Atman, is the 'Post' — in the ghost-in-the-post example — upon which the cause and the effect, the unmanifest and the manifest, like the "ghost" apparently come to play (kṛtam = Vvaktam, A-kṛtam = A-Vvaktam).
names.simple_meaning: The one who is both cause and manifested effect

names.short_meaning: The Self is described as four-fold when we consider the Atman as the Glory (vibhūti) of the Self
names.commentary: The Self is described as four-fold when we consider the Atman as the Glory (vibhūti) of the Self. Thus, the Essential factors, with which alone the endless play of creation, sustenance and destruction can continue, are the glories of the Self (ātma-vibhūti). In Viṣṇu Purāṇa, four distinct vibhooties of the Lord — when He functions as the creator, sustainer and destroyer — are found enumerated. From the standpoint of a Vedantic student, since in the Non-dual Reality there cannot be anything other than Itself, all the plays of the gross, the subtle and causal bodies, in the microcosm and in the macrocosm, are the glories (vibhooties) of the One Self. In the Absolute, in the Eternal, all these are transcended; these - the waker, dreamer, deep-sleeper, the Tureeva — are all Its Glories. The Possessor of these Glories is the One that transcends even "Tureeya": He is called as the Tureevaateetah.
names.simple_meaning: The fourfold self

names.short_meaning: One who manifests into the four mighty powers (vyūha)
names.commentary:
One who manifests into the four mighty powers (vyūha). The Truth, that plays thus Himself in these four levels having apparently created the world of experiences, is Viṣṇu, the All — Pervading. According to the Vaishnava literature, for the purpose of creation, Maha Viṣṇu Himself became four mighty powers (vyūha) and they were called Vāsudeva, Samkarshana, Pradyumna and Aniruddha.

One who has Himself these four mighty powers, necessary for the conduct of plurality, is the Great Self, Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: One who manifests into the four mighty powers (vyūha)

names.short_meaning: The canine teeth fully developed in the upper and the lower rows, as in the case of carnivorous animals, are called in Sanskrit as daṃṣṭrā
names.commentary:
The canine teeth fully developed in the upper and the lower rows, as in the case of carnivorous animals, are called in Sanskrit as daṃṣṭrā. This is reminiscent of the Powerful daṃṣṭrā of the Lord when He took the form of Nara — Simha to protect Prahlāda.

Also in the Purāṇas we find that the Great white Elephant of Indra, "Airaavata," has four tusks — He whose glory is the four-tusked Airaavata is Maha — Viṣṇu. To the student of the Upaniṣad, it is indeed very clear that these four 'tusks' or 'teeth' are nothing other than the four paadas which Māṇḍūkya thunders — "Chatushpaada". The manifestation of the Might and Glory of the Supreme are the play of the waking, dream and deep-sleep conditions. With reference to these three. transcending them all, is the fourth plane-of-consciousness the Spring board for all these three. He, whose Glory are all these four grinding, crushing, fearful experiences of duality, is the One Non-dual Self, the Great Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The four-tusked one

names.short_meaning: "One who has four hands" It is famous that Maha Viṣṇu has four hands and they carry the Conch, the Discus, the Mace, and the Lotus
names.commentary:
"One who has four hands" It is famous that Maha Viṣṇu has four hands and they carry the Conch, the Discus, the Mace, and the Lotus. According to the Purāṇas, these four are used by the Lord in maintaining dharma among mankind. The 'Conch' calls man to the righteous path that directly leads to Peace and Perfection, the Divine Vishnupada. Very many of us in the enchantment of the imme diate sense-joys refuse to listen to the small inner voice of conscience, the sound of the Pāñcajanya-conch, and so He wields the 'Mace' and we come to suffer small calamities and tragic jerks in our smooth existence - communal, social or national. If still the individual is not listening to the call of the 'Conch', the wheel-of-time, Chakra annihilates the entire. The call and the punishment are all only to take man towards his Ultimate Goal, represented by the "Lotus" in His hand.

Subjectively Viṣṇu is the Self within, who manifests as the four-armed 'subtle-body' to serve as the Eesa of the gross physical structure, in all its actions and protect it with existence.

The "Subtle-body" as the inner-equipment (Antah — Karana) functions as four mighty powers - mind, intellect, chit and ego. Chit is the 'Lotus', intellect is the 'Conch', ego is the 'Mace', and mind is the 'Discus'. All these four are wielded by the One Infinite Blue-bodied Nārāyaṇa, clothed in His 'yellow garb', manifesting to maintain and sustain the world of good and evil. Since the Self functions thus in a four-fold pattern, Viṣṇu has the appellation, "the four-armed Lord."
names.simple_meaning: "One who has four hands" It is famous that Maha Viṣṇu has four hands and they carry the Conch, the Discus, the Mace, and the Lotus

names.short_meaning: Self — Effulgent Consciousness illumines everything; and it is not borrowing Its Light from any other source
names.commentary:
Self — Effulgent Consciousness illumines everything; and it is not borrowing Its Light from any other source. "It is the Light of lights that illumines even darkness"—(Gītā Ch. 13, St. 18). And the Upaniṣad is equally vehement and declares: "There the sun has no light nor the stars nor these lightnings; how little then can this fire!

By its Light alone all these are illumined.

न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः । तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ॥
names.simple_meaning: Self — Effulgent Consciousness illumines everything; and it is not borrowing Its Light from any other source

names.short_meaning: The immediate meaning of the term is food, viz
names.commentary: The immediate meaning of the term is food, viz. eatables. In philosophy it has a wider implication and the term "food" cannotes the entire field-of-objects experienced or enjoyed by the sense-organs. The world-of-objects projected by the sense-organs, the inner psychological play and this world-of-matter constituting the field-of-plurality, all together is comprehended by the term māyā. Thus orthodox commentators reduce this term 'bhojanam' to the contents and functions of māyā. Taittirīya Upaniṣad (2-7) says: "He is indeed the Essence (Rasa)" (रसो वै स:).
names.simple_meaning: Food; all that is experienced

names.short_meaning: The "Experiencer"
names.commentary:
The "Experiencer". Not only the world-of-objects is essentially nothing but the Spirit, Lord Viṣṇu, but even the very instruments-of-experiences and their ultimate joys and sorrows, are all illumined for us by the Lord-of — Lakṣmī. The Pure Self, expressing through the gross, the subtle and the causal bodies, becomes the waker, dreamer and deep-sleeper, experiencing all happenings, good and bad, as the individuality in that living person. Consciousness, puruṣa, identifying with and functioning through matter (Prakriti), comes to experience the endless modifications that are born out of Prakriti. The Self in Its Infinite nature is actionless and yet in māyā seems to function and becomes the Enjoyer or Sufferer of the actions of matter.

पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान् गुणान् ॥ — Gītā 13.21.
names.simple_meaning: The "Experiencer"

names.short_meaning: One who is capable of patiently suffering, in his perfect detachment, all that is happening around, is a sahishnuh
names.commentary:
One who is capable of patiently suffering, in his perfect detachment, all that is happening around, is a sahishnuh. Whatever happens to the reflections of the Sun, the Sun in the cosmos is unaffected by them, and with reference to his reflections we can call him a sahiṣṇuḥ: the Sun is a mere "witness" of his own endless reflections.

The term has also got two more meanings in Sanskrit as 'Forgiver' or 'Conqueror'. Viṣṇu is one who forgives us readily all our trespasses, and conquers for us all the inimical forces in our inner personality.
names.simple_meaning: One who is capable of patiently suffering, in his perfect detachment, all that is happening around, is a sahishnuh

names.short_meaning: One who had born (Jah) in the very beginning (aadi) of the world (jagat) is called jagadādijaḥ
names.commentary:
One who had born (Jah) in the very beginning (aadi) of the world (jagat) is called jagadādijaḥ. At the time of dissolution (Pralaya) when the entire gross and subtle bodies go to lie absorbed in the Total Causal-body, the world, in Pralaya, lies merged in Īśvara. Before the gross world-of-plurality emerges out there should be a condition of subtle manifestation of it in the form of thoughts.

Thoughts constitute the mind-intellect; when the Infinite functions through this Total Mind-intellect, It is called as hiraṇyagarbha — the womb of all objects, it is from the Hiranvagarbha-state, the manifestation of the gross world emerges out. when the Lord comes to play as the virāṭ ātmā. Maha Viṣṇu is the One who was born before the world of gross bodies, therefore, it is indicated here that He is the "Womb-of-all-objects" in the world, the Hiranvagarbha—the very Creator.

समष्टिकारणशरीराभिमानी आत्मा ईश्वरः।

समष्टिसूक्ष्मशरीराभिमानी आत्मा हिरण्यगर्भः।
names.simple_meaning: The one born at the very beginning of the world

names.short_meaning: Agham means sin (pāpa), impurities (mala); and therefore, anaghaḥ means One who has no imperfections and who is not affected by the good and bad vāsanās left over in the personality as a result of the wilful actions
names.commentary:
Agham means sin (pāpa), impurities (mala); and therefore, anaghaḥ means One who has no imperfections and who is not affected by the good and bad vāsanās left over in the personality as a result of the wilful actions. He is the Un-contaminated (Aliptah). The Light of Consciousness is the Illuminator of the mind, and so the peace of virtue or the agitations of the sin cannot affect the Illuminator — the Illuminator being always different from the illuminated.

Chāndogya Upaniṣad (8-1-5) says: "He is free from Sin".
names.simple_meaning: The sinless and faultless one

names.short_meaning: "The Victorious"
names.commentary:
"The Victorious". One who realizes the Self can thereafter stand apart from the thraldom of matter, Victorious over the tyrannies of the flesh, feelings or facts. Thus, the Seat of Self is the Seat of Victory over matter.

The Peace and harmony of the Self can never be assailed by the noisy hordes of the world of plurality. Vijaya is the name also of Arjuna and the Lord Himself says, "Among the Pandavas, I am Arjuna" ("पाण्डवानां धनजय:")— Gītā Ch. 10, St. 37.
names.simple_meaning: "The Victorious"

names.short_meaning: "Ever Successful"
names.commentary: "Ever Successful". In all undertakings He alone wins; One who never knows any defeat or failure. Upaniṣad says: "Truth alone wins, never falsehood" (सत्यमेव जयते नानतं).
names.simple_meaning: "Ever Successful"

names.short_meaning: It can be interpreted in two ways as (a) He who is the Cause of the universe or (b) He who has the world as His Cause
names.commentary: It can be interpreted in two ways as (a) He who is the Cause of the universe or (b) He who has the world as His Cause. The former is clear to those who have so far followed the commentary, and to them the latter may be a very confusing statement. From the standpoint of the Purāṇas, it is logical. The Self has manifested as the various incarnations from time to time because of the condition of the world, and therefore, Visvam is the cause for His manifestations.
names.simple_meaning: The source of the universe, or he whose source is the universe

names.short_meaning: One who comes to live again and again in various equipments of living organisms is punarvasuḥ
names.commentary: One who comes to live again and again in various equipments of living organisms is punarvasuḥ: (वसति इति वस:).
names.simple_meaning: One who comes to live again and again in various equipments of living organisms is punarvasuḥ

names.short_meaning: The younger brother of Indra
names.commentary:
The younger brother of Indra. In His Incarnation as Vāmana, He was born to Aditi, who was the mother of Indra, and hence, the Lord is known as the "Younger brother of Indra". In Sanskrit the prefix upa denotes 'Above' in the sense of 'superior to'; therefore, Upendra may also mean "One who is superior to Indra", the king of gods. Such an explanation we find in the Harivaṃśa (76-47).

Indra, the king of the sense-organs, is the mind and the Consciousness, which is the Self, is the One factor that dynamises the mind. Since life is that which controls even the mind. certainly It is superior to the mind and this Self is the Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The younger brother of Indra

names.short_meaning: Of the ten great incarnations, the fifth one is Vāmana; and the very name indicates 'One who has a small body'
names.commentary:
Of the ten great incarnations, the fifth one is Vāmana; and the very name indicates 'One who has a small body'. It was in the form of a child (vatuh=A child student in a gurukula) that Vāmana approached the divinely righteous Emperor Mahaabali to beg of him a little land, of the length of his tiny three steps—and the Lord measured in His three steps all the three worlds and thus conquered Mahaabali. He checked (Vamayati) the rising pride of possession in Bali, hence He, in that incarnation as a Vatu, is called Vāmana.

The term Vāmana also means 'worshipful'. "मध्ये वामन- मासीनं विश्वेदेवा उपासते": "Him, the Dwarf, sitting in the middle of the heart, all gods adore", so we read in the Kaṭhopaniṣad (5-3). However, here the emphasis should be upon the meaning "short statured" because of the contrast it makes with the following name.
names.simple_meaning: The small-bodied Vāmana incarnation

names.short_meaning: One whose body is vast is called prāṃśuḥ
names.commentary:
One whose body is vast is called prāṃśuḥ. Vāmana, when He got the promise from the righteous King, and when He started measuring, the Lord took His Cosmic Form, and with each step measured the earth, the interspace, and the heaven. In Harivaṃśa (262-263) there is a beautiful description of the little Vāmana growing into His Total Form. The rate of His expansion is described with reference to two fixed factors the Sun and the Moon. When He took the form, the Sun and the Moon were His eyes; as He measured the earth, they came to His bosom; as He was measuring the space, the Sun was at His navel and as He lifted His feet to measure the Heaven, the Sun and the Moon were just below His knees.

अनण्वस्थूलमह्रस्वदीर्घमजमव्ययम् । अरूपगुणवर्णाख्यं तद्ब्रह्मेति अवधारयेत् ॥
names.simple_meaning: The tall one whose body fills the sky

names.short_meaning: One whose activities are ever a fulfilment of some great purpose
names.commentary: One whose activities are ever a fulfilment of some great purpose. Even insignificant actions, which, ordinarily, people would think are empty and purposeless, are never really so, when they spring from Him. Even when He punishes, it is only for inaugurating a greater evolutionary blessing.
names.simple_meaning: One whose activities are ever a fulfilment of some great purpose

names.short_meaning: One who is spotlessly 'clean', and therefore, Ever — Pure
names.commentary: One who is spotlessly 'clean', and therefore, Ever — Pure. Impurities in a substance are things other than itself; when dust is on the cloth, the cloth is impure, (अ-शचि:), unclean. Since the Self, the ātman, is the Non- Dual Reality, having nothing other than Itself in It, Ever-pure alone must It always be. And śuciḥ is One who gives this purity to those who contemplate upon Him constantly.
names.simple_meaning: One who is spotlessly 'clean', and therefore, Ever — Pure

names.short_meaning: One who has infinite strength and vitality
names.commentary: One who has infinite strength and vitality. Wherever, in the organism, we meet with any strength and vitality they are all the strength and vitality of the Self. The Infinite Viṣṇu is the One All — Pervading Self, and therefore, He is the very spring-head for all strength.
names.simple_meaning: One who has infinite strength and vitality

names.short_meaning: One who is beyond Indra in knowledge, glory and strength
names.commentary: One who is beyond Indra in knowledge, glory and strength. Since Indra represents the 'mind-intellect' equipment, ātman, the Self is denoted here as that which transcends the mind.
names.simple_meaning: One who is beyond Indra in knowledge, glory and strength

names.short_meaning: One who holds the entire world of beings-and-things together in an indissoluble embrace unto Himself
names.commentary:
One who holds the entire world of beings-and-things together in an indissoluble embrace unto Himself. Just as the hub of a wheel holds the rim unto itself by its endless spokes, so too the ātman, the Self within, lends Its vitality to every cell in the body and to every thought in the inner-equipments.

In none can anything happen which is not a glory borrowed from Him. And, the Self, being the same everywhere, in all existence, in both the movables and immovables, gross and subtle — in the manifest as well as in the unmanifest — He certainly is the One who holds the world of phenomena unto Himself in a vast embrace of Love and Oneness.
names.simple_meaning: One who holds the entire world of beings-and-things together in an indissoluble embrace unto Himself

names.short_meaning: One who has created out of Himself the whole world
names.commentary: One who has created out of Himself the whole world. It therefore must also connote One, who has the whole created world as His own form, since the creation is His own manifestation as the Subtle and the Gross.
names.simple_meaning: One who has created out of Himself the whole world

names.short_meaning: One who supports Himself by Himself
names.commentary:
One who supports Himself by Himself. In the previous epithet Samgrahah, He was shown as the Cohesion of Love in the world of matter and energy. and in Sargah, He, as the One material and efficient cause of creation, was shown as also the very supporter of the manifested world. But who supports Him? He is dhṛtātmā — He is established in Himself.

धृत आत्मा येन सः = धृतात्मा।
names.simple_meaning: One who supports Himself by Himself

names.short_meaning: The Appointing Authority: It is He, who orders all the mighty forces of nature and prescribes for each the Laws of their conduct, the ways of their behaviour and the methods of their functions
names.commentary:
The Appointing Authority: It is He, who orders all the mighty forces of nature and prescribes for each the Laws of their conduct, the ways of their behaviour and the methods of their functions. The Sun, Moon.

Air, Waters, Dik — Paalakas, Death etc. are all appointed and ordered by the Lord.
names.simple_meaning: The appointing authority who orders the laws of nature

names.short_meaning: One who is the mighty Power that administers all the forces of Nature under His Law
names.commentary: One who is the mighty Power that administers all the forces of Nature under His Law. Everything in nature strictly obeys ever all His Laws.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the mighty Power that administers all the forces of Nature under His Law

names.short_meaning: That which is to be known; in the language of the Gītā, it is Ineyam
names.commentary:
That which is to be known; in the language of the Gītā, it is Jñeyam. That final knowledge, knowing which every-thing becomes known. "Kasmin nu bhagavo vijnaate sarvamidam vijnaatam bhavati iti"— "कस्मिन्न भगवो विज्ञाते सर्वमिदं विज्ञातं भवतीति" —(Mundaka. 1-3).

All sciences are investigations into Truth. After observing the nature and behaviour of things and beings when the investigator moves ahead seeking the ONE Harmonious Chord of Reality that holds all phenomena in its inescapable love-web, the scientist of Truth—comes to reject first the gross, and soon thereafter the subtle realms, and ultimately even the causal factors, and thus—comes to apprehend this harmony, which he is seeking as the very subjective core of his own Self. This final Goal to be realized, "having known which everything else becomes known," the One Consummate Knowledge to be gained (vedyaḥ), is the Self, the Great Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: That which is to be known; in the language of the Gītā, it is Ineyam

names.short_meaning: The One Supreme Doctor who alone can minister to the world suffering from ego and egocentric misconceptions
names.commentary: The One Supreme Doctor who alone can minister to the world suffering from ego and egocentric misconceptions. One who is a master of all knowledge (vidyā) is also termed as vaidyaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The One Supreme Doctor who alone can minister to the world suffering from ego and egocentric misconceptions

names.short_meaning: To the confused and the deluded to detach themselves from the false vestures-of-matter and to seek their identity with the ETERNAL Self is called Yoga
names.commentary: To the confused and the deluded to detach themselves from the false vestures-of-matter and to seek their identity with the ETERNAL Self is called Yoga. All attempts in attaining an at-one-ment with the Self is called Yoga. The Goal, the Self, therefore, in the language of the seeker must be Sadaayoga-ever in yoga.
names.simple_meaning: The one always united in yoga

names.short_meaning: "He who destroys the mighty heroes"
names.commentary: "He who destroys the mighty heroes". The powerful men of strength and valour when they grow in their audacity to become tyrants, the Lord manifests to destroy such rākṣasas and thus protects the dharma and the Good.
names.simple_meaning: "He who destroys the mighty heroes"

names.short_meaning: Earlier this term was used (72) where we interpreted the term as the "Lord of Lakṣmī."
names.commentary:
Earlier this term was used (72) where we interpreted the term as the "Lord of Lakṣmī." Maa means not only "Lakṣmī," but she is also "vidyā" (Knowledge). The Lord (Dhava) of all Knowledge (Maa) is Mādhava. He who helps introspection and meditation in the seeker is Mādhava. "To become conscious of the existence of a thing" is called the knowledge of the thing. The ātman, the Self is Existence (Sat) and Consciousness (Sphurana) and, therefore, Lord Viṣṇu, the Self is the source of all knowledge and as such the Master of all Vidvaas: (Maa-dhava). Harivaṃśa says: "O Hari, You are the Lord (Dhava) of Knowledge (Maa). and hence You are called as Mādhava, the Master of Maa."

This term is also interpreted in this way: Mā = meditation; dha = introspection; va = uniting.
names.simple_meaning: The lord of Lakṣmī

names.short_meaning: The term madhuḥ familiarly stands for "honey"
names.commentary: The term madhuḥ familiarly stands for "honey". It is also a term to indicate "nectar." One who generates Nectarine Bliss in the hearts of His devotees is called madhuḥ. The spring time in India is called as Madhumaasa since spring is the season of flowers; full of honey for the bees, and joy for man. The month called Madhu (March — April) is the Chaitra month which is considered specially auspicious for prayers, and meditation. One who is of the nature of the Mādhava-maasa, the month of Mādhava (April — May) can also be the suggestion in this term. Vaisaakha (April — May) is considered as the most auspicious time of the year for the worship of Viṣṇu by all Vaishnavites.
names.simple_meaning: The one sweet as honey to his devotees

names.short_meaning: One who is beyond the sense-organs not only in the sense, that the sense-organs cannot perceive Him as their 'object' but also in the sense that He is other than the sense-organs and their functions
names.commentary:
One who is beyond the sense-organs not only in the sense, that the sense-organs cannot perceive Him as their 'object' but also in the sense that He is other than the sense-organs and their functions.

Lending to them, all their very vitality, is His mere presence! He is the very 'subject' in the perceiver, and, therefore, the instruments of perceptions, emotions, and thoughts cannot experience Him: this Source of All-life is Maha Viṣṇu.

Kaṭhopaniṣad (3-15) says: "He is soundless, untouched, formless, immutable, so without taste, eternal, smell-less.
names.simple_meaning: The one beyond the senses and their functions

names.short_meaning: One who is the Supreme Master of all māyā
names.commentary:
One who is the Supreme Master of all māyā. He is the very Substratum upon which all the plurality springs up and plays their infinite enchantments. constantly basking in the Light of the Supreme Consciousness.

ātman, the Self, is untouched by the play of māyā, and yet the māyā-play is sustained only by the exuberant warmth of His Divine presence. The Sun is the Master of all clouds. inasmuch as, in its presence, borrowing its heat, water by its own nature gets evaporated, and the water, vapour again. because of its own nature of a lesser density than the atmospheric air, rises to the higher altitudes and gathers there as clouds. It is, again, the nature of the atmosphere that at higher altitudes it is cooler and the water-vapour so cooled becomes water again, and due to the higher density of water it descends as rain. In this example the Sun can be called as the "Creator" of all clouds and the "Cause for the rains," and consequently the sun is also the "Master of the Seasons." And yet, the Sun is uncontaminated by all these phenomena that are happening in its presence.

In the same fashion the Infinite Reality, Viṣṇu, is indicated here as the Great Magician, who has the magic of māyā at His command. Kṛṣṇa Himself confesses in the Gītā: "Very difficult indeed it is to cross over My māyā"—"मम माया दरत्यया"—(Gītā Ch. 7 St. 14).
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Supreme Master of all māyā

names.short_meaning: The Great Enthusiast: the Ever — Dynamic Accomplisher
names.commentary: The Great Enthusiast: the Ever — Dynamic Accomplisher. The Powers of creation, of sustenance and of annihilation—in their totality is the world of birth and death that we live in. This wonderful world cannot be sustained without the endless enthusiasm of this Mighty Power. Looking at the ocean, through the waves, we come to recognise the ocean as the "Sleepless Agitator"; similarly, looking at Viṣṇu, through the ephimeral kaleidoscopic changes in the patterns of life available to us in our experience today, we call Him as the "Dynamic accomplisher" (mahotsāhaḥ). The term employed here, the Enthusiastic Accomplisher, is indeed one of the most appropriate names for Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The Great Enthusiast: the Ever — Dynamic Accomplisher

names.short_meaning: One who has Supreme Strength
names.commentary: One who has Supreme Strength. He, being Omnipotent, is the Source of all Strength that we see in each individual organism in life. His Vitality reflected in each of us, is our individual strength; naturally He is the Infinitely Strong, mahābalaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: One who has Supreme Strength

names.short_meaning: In the previous term, we were told He is Omnipotent
names.commentary: In the previous term, we were told He is Omnipotent. Here He is indicated as Omniscient. The Supreme, functioning through the intellect, is the intelligence. The quality and quantity of the intelligence will depend upon the condition of the "intellect' through which the Infinite comes to play. The intelligence in a mathematician, poet or an artist, scientist or politician—all are the different play-patterns of energies invoked from the one Supreme Intelligence, and therefore, Mahavishnu, the Self, is called here as mahābuddhiḥ, the Reservoir of all Intelligence.
names.simple_meaning: The one of great intelligence

names.short_meaning: One who is the Supreme Essence
names.commentary: One who is the Supreme Essence. "vīrya" is the Essence behind all the creative urges. Since the Divine is the very source, from which alone the dynamism for creation can manifest, the Supreme Divinity is termed here as the Mahaaveerva.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Supreme Essence

names.short_meaning: All — Powerful
names.commentary: All — Powerful. Power (शिक्त) here means efficiency (सामर्थ्यम्). He—whose manifestations are the power-of-action, the power-of-desire and the power-of-knowledge (किया-काम-ज्ञान) śaktis—must necessarily be the most powerful, inasmuch as a play of these three powers is the total play of the world.
names.simple_meaning: All — Powerful

names.short_meaning: Of Splendorous Light
names.commentary: Of Splendorous Light. Dyuti means 'Glow', Sobhaa. The Pure Consciousness is the illuminator of all, including all other material sources of light in the world—Sun, Moon, stars, fire etc.—but this is not all; He is also the One, who is Himself Self — Effulgent. This is Mahavishnu—the Supreme Self. In the Muṇḍakopaniṣad (4-9) Lord is described as the "Light of lights". Brihadaaranyakopanishad (6-3-9) declares: "He is Self-effulgent".
names.simple_meaning: Of Splendorous Light

names.short_meaning: One whose form is indefinable, indescribable, inexplicable
names.commentary:
One whose form (वव्) is indefinable, indescribable, inexplicable (Anirdesyam). Ordinary things can be defined, described or explained because they come within our experience. Our objective experiences can be satisfactorily expressed in words. Viṣṇu is that Truth which is the Subjective Essence in all of us; He is that 'Knowledge', in the light of which, all other knowledges are rendered possible.

As such no "sources of knowledge" (Pramaanas such as Direct perception, Inference etc.) can be employed successfully in exploring the realm of the Self. Subjective experiences of 'Be', the Maha Viṣṇu, is possible; but It can never become an 'idea' to express, nor can It become an 'emotion' to feel, nor can It ever become an 'object' to be described.
names.simple_meaning: One whose form is indefinable, indescribable, inexplicable

names.short_meaning: Śrī means Glory (Aisvarya)
names.commentary: Śrī means Glory (Aisvarya). Viṣṇu is permanently wedded to Mother Glory; He, who is constantly courted by all glories, is śrīmān, Lord Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The possessor of glory

names.short_meaning: He whose Essence (ātmā) is inestimable and immeasurable (Ameya)
names.commentary: He whose Essence (ātmā) is inestimable and immeasurable (Ameya). As ātman (Kshetrajna) He, the One, expresses Himself everywhere in every equipment (kṣetra), as the 'knower' in each 'field'. Since these equipments are infinite in number, as the individuality (jeeva) in each one of the created beings, His own Glory expresses in endless manifestations.
names.simple_meaning: He whose Essence (ātmā) is inestimable and immeasurable (Ameya)

names.short_meaning: One who supports the great Mountain
names.commentary:
One who supports the great Mountain. In the Purāṇas, we find two instances, wherein the Lord has been described as the uplifter of or as having lifted and supported the mountains. While churning the milky ocean with the Mandara (मन्दर) mountain we are told that the "churning-stick" sunk into the bottom and the Lord had to manifest in the form of the Great Tortoise (Koorma) and support it, while the Gods and Demons continued the churning, until they gathered the nectar (Amritam).

Again, the Supreme, as Lord Kṛṣṇa, in order to protect the cows had to lift the Govardhana Mountain. Because of these two stories in the Purāṇas, Lord, the Protector of the mind in Saadhanaa, is called as mahādridhṛk.

Viṣṇu is the Divine, that supports the mind-intellect of the sādhaka while he is churning, through study (sravana) and reflection (manana), his own Milk-like pure heart-of devotion in order to gain the experience of Immortality (Amritam).
names.simple_meaning: One who supports the great Mountain

names.short_meaning: One who wears or wields the Great Bow called Śārṅga
names.commentary: One who wears or wields the Great Bow called Śārṅga (शार्ड).
names.simple_meaning: The wielder of the great bow Śārṅga

names.short_meaning: The husband of Mother Farth
names.commentary: The husband of Mother Farth. The Sanskrit term for husband is bhartā and the term denotes 'Supporter'. In the Puranic language we have the description of how the Lord, as the Great Boar (बराह) uplifted the earth from the "waters of Deluge." Viewed from the platform of philosophy, just as gold is the supporter of all things made of gold, the Infinite Consciousness is the Essence from which everything has risen. Hence He is the Lord, the Supporter, the Husband (bhartā) of Mother Earth and everything that exists in her.
names.simple_meaning: The husband of Mother Farth

names.short_meaning: The permanent abode of Śrī
names.commentary: The permanent abode of Śrī. Mother Śrī connotes "all Glory and power, faculties and strength, to be good and to perform creative acts of righteousness". She is found to remain never permanently in any bosom. Even saints and sages, in recorded history, have come to compromise the perfections in them. The only place, where imperfections never enter to molest the serene essence, is the seat of Eternal Perfection, which is the bosom of Nārāyaṇa. Hence Maha Viṣṇu is indicated as Sreenivaasa—"the Permanent Abode of Lakṣmī".
names.simple_meaning: The permanent abode of Śrī

names.short_meaning: For the truly virtuous and for all spiritual seekers (Sat — People) He who is the final Goal
names.commentary: For the truly virtuous and for all spiritual seekers (Sat — People) He who is the final Goal. In the language of the Gītā He is the "parā gatih". The term gati is used to denote not only the goal, but the very movement, as well as the direction and the way. Nārāyaṇa is the very Direction, Path, Progress and the Goal for his devotees.
names.simple_meaning: For the truly virtuous and for all spiritual seekers (Sat — People) He who is the final Goal

names.short_meaning: One who cannot be obstructed or resisted by anyone
names.commentary: One who cannot be obstructed or resisted by anyone. Irresistibly, the will of the Lord functions in the world of created things-and-beings. Just as in the world of matter, the laws of nature are irresistible, the Rhythm and Harmony of Truth ever march in their Eternal Logic of objectless Love and immaculate perfection. Time and tide wait for none. When the sun rises, the living creatures absorb energy and nothing can obstruct this process. In the presence of the Self, the worlds of matter must get thrilled into their own independent activities, and in all these welter of efforts and exertions, achievements and failures, joys and sorrows, the Self is not involved by the Irresistible Enchantment of His presence, the Gopis seek their own fulfilment in their own dances. In the Purāṇas, we find Bhagavān Viṣṇu taking up in His various Incarnations different manifested forms and in all of them He was victorious: ever irresistible (aniruddhaḥ) is His Might.
names.simple_meaning: One who cannot be obstructed or resisted by anyone

names.short_meaning: The One who doles out happiness (ānanda) even for the Denizens-of-the Heavens (Suras)
names.commentary: The One who doles out happiness (ānanda) even for the Denizens-of-the Heavens (Suras). In the Upaniṣad we have the declaration, that the Infinite Perfection, the Lord is of the very nature of Absolute Bliss—“आनन्दं ब्रह्मोति व्यजानात्”. In the Aanandavallee of Taittirīya Upaniṣad we find the arithmetics of Bliss. The ṛṣi concludes that all joys of the world and heavens-mental and supramental—are all but flickerings of the Infinite Bliss, which is the Lord Mahavishnu.
names.simple_meaning: The One who doles out happiness (ānanda) even for the Denizens-of-the Heavens (Suras)

names.short_meaning: The word Go in Sanskrit has four meanings: 'Earth', 'Cows', 'Speech' and 'Vedas'
names.commentary:
The word Go in Sanskrit has four meanings: 'Earth', 'Cows', 'Speech' and 'Vedas'. As the earth is the supporter of everything that is existing, He, who is the supporter of everything within the individual, is called Govinda; He, who is the Protector of the Cows and played the part of Gopaala in Gokula, is the very controller of the animal instincts and passions in the bosom of man; "One, without whom, no speech can ever emerge out of any throat—He being the very Life in all Creatures" says Kenopaniṣad; and the Highest Speech is the declaration of Truth in the Vedas. The Lord Himself is the very Theme and the Author of the Vedas.

This great Self is Mahavishnu.

यद्वाचा अनभ्युदितं येन वागभ्युद्यते । तदेव ब्रह्म त्वं विद्धि नेदं यदिदमुपासते ॥ — Kena Upaniṣad 1.4.
names.simple_meaning: The protector of cows and restorer of the earth

names.short_meaning: One, who is the Lord of all 'seers' and "Men of Wisdom"
names.commentary: One, who is the Lord of all 'seers' and "Men of Wisdom". We have already indicated that Go means Vedas. Govit — Vedavit-those, who have realized the Theme indicated in the Vedic declaration as the Essential Reality in their Own subjective bosom. They are called the Seers or Sages. To such Men-of — Wisdom the Self alone is the Lord and the Master.
names.simple_meaning: One, who is the Lord of all 'seers' and "Men of Wisdom"

names.short_meaning: The term marīciḥ means 'Effulgence'
names.commentary: The term marīciḥ means 'Effulgence'. Consciousness illumines objects and therefore in terms of worldly knowledge the Upaniṣads declare that the Supreme is the Light — Infinite. In the Gītā we read Bhagavān Vāsudeva declaring: "I am the Light in all effulgents"— "तेजस्तेजस्वनामहम"—(Gītā Ch. 10, St. 36).
names.simple_meaning: The ray of light in all that shines

names.short_meaning: One who restrains and controls every rākṣasic impulse within the bosom
names.commentary: One who restrains and controls every rākṣasic impulse within the bosom. In the forms of the ten incarnations. He had controlled the irresistible tyrannies of the vicious against the good. In the form of pain and agitation, sorrow and death, it is He, who is the Controller, damanaḥ, of all negative tendencies in everyone's Heart.
names.simple_meaning: One who restrains and controls every rākṣasic impulse within the bosom

names.short_meaning: One of the great declarations of the Vedas is: "I am Brahman" (ahaṃ brahmāsmi)
names.commentary: One of the great declarations of the Vedas is: "I am Brahman" (ahaṃ brahmāsmi). Here the term I, the first person singular used, denotes the Supreme Self "functioning through the conditionings." This individual concept is called jīva. Thus I, the jīva (Aham), once detached from the conditionings, is essentially nothing other than He, the Lord (Sah). This experience that Aham is Sah is the very God-consciousness and therefore, Viṣṇu, the Supreme State of Realization is declared as haṃsaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The divine swan expressing the identity of self and Brahman

names.short_meaning: Parna means wings; Suparna means that which has beautiful wings-bird
names.commentary:
Parna means wings; Suparna means that which has beautiful wings-bird. "A pair of white-winged birds extremely friendly sit on one and the same tree; one cats the fruits, the other eats not and gazes on". Thus traditionally in the Upaniṣads, the Suparnas suggest the jīvātmā and the paramātmā sitting on the same tree (body): one (jīva) eats the fruits (of actions) and the other (the Self) merely gazes on (sākṣī). Viṣṇu is this All-experiencing Principle of consciousness.

द्वा सुपर्णा सयुजा सखाया समानं वृक्षं परिषस्वजाते । तयोरन्यः पिप्पलं स्वाद्वत्त्यनश्नन्नन्यो अभिचाकशीति ॥ — Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.1.
names.simple_meaning: The beautiful-winged one

names.short_meaning: The sacred serpent named in the puranas as Ananta
names.commentary: The sacred serpent named in the puranas as Ananta. "Among the serpents I am Ananta," says Kṛṣṇa: "अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानाम"—(Gītā Ch. 10, St. 29).
names.simple_meaning: The greatest serpent, Ananta

names.short_meaning: He, who supports at His navel, the creator, Hiranyagarbha
names.commentary: He, who supports at His navel, the creator, Hiranyagarbha. The meaning for this term as given by some is "the One who has the navel region beautiful in its golden hue" must fail, in the context of the thoughts in the stanza, to appeal to all seekers.
names.simple_meaning: He, who supports at His navel, the creator, Hiranyagarbha

names.short_meaning: One who has glorious Tapas
names.commentary: One who has glorious Tapas. Consistent creative thinking is called tapas. For this, mental concentration is unavoidable. Mind cannot have consistent concentration unless it can have a perfect control over the sense-organs. Even when the mind is withdrawn from the sense-organs, it must have a consistent intellectual ideal to concentrate upon. In the Upaniṣad, we read: "He thought and through thought, He created all this"—"स तपः तप्तवा इदमेतदस्जत्."
names.simple_meaning: One who has glorious Tapas

names.short_meaning: One who supports at His navel the very seat of all creative-power
names.commentary: One who supports at His navel the very seat of all creative-power. We have described this term earlier (48). According to Śaṅkara, here the term may mean one who has a navel region which in its rounded beauty, is as charming as the lotus flower.
names.simple_meaning: One who supports at His navel the very seat of all creative-power

names.short_meaning: The Lord of the creatures
names.commentary: The Lord of the creatures. Since all creatures have emerged from Him, the living creatures are His children (prajā) and He is their Pati. The term Pati has a direct meaning: 'father'. Thus Viṣṇu, as the only source from which all creatures have emerged out, is called as prajāpatiḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of the creatures

names.short_meaning: One who knows no decay
names.commentary: One who knows no decay. Birth, growth, decay, disease and death, are the five great modifications through which every finite object must necessarily pass. Everything born must perish. The one who has no birth has no death. The waves die but not the ocean. That which is Changeless in the changing whirls of matter is the Infinite Viṣṇu. In the Bhagavad Gītā, the Lord is emphatic: "He who sees the Changeless amidst the changing names and forms, He alone sees the meaning and purpose of life."—"विनश्यत्स्व- विनश्यन्तं यः पश्यति स पश्यति."
names.simple_meaning: One who knows no decay

names.short_meaning: The seer and knower of everything
names.commentary: The seer and knower of everything. The Consciousness that illumines all motives and intentions - and the manifested activities that spring from them - in each individual, at all times, is necessarily the Witness of all, the Seer of everything, Maha Viṣṇu.
ocr_notes: Scan locus corrected from [72] to [71] by complete-text replay against the PDF page OCR.
names.simple_meaning: The seer and knower of everything

names.short_meaning: One who destroys
names.commentary:
One who destroys. The Law behind all destruction and change in the māyā is the Mighty Lord. On transcending the Vehicles of the body, mind and intellect, at a time when all experiences of perceptions, emotions and thoughts are annihilated from us, the Experience left over is the Supreme. And in the Non-dual Supreme, there cannot be any object other than itself. Therefore, that "State" is called as the Total Destroyer. The State of Waking is the "destroyer" of the dream-world; the State of Sleep is the "destroyer" of the waking and the dream; the State of God Consciousness is the total "Annihilator" of all the known three planes of Consciousness. He is siṃhaḥ — a word that has been formed by the mutual transposition of the letters in Himsaa.

Even taking its obvious superficial meaning Viṣṇu is a Lion in our bosom, in as much as, He is the king of the forest of saṃsāra: at the roar of Nārāyaṇa all the animal-passions flee from the jungles of the mind. In the Gītā while describing His own Glory, the Lord says, "Among the animals, I am the King of animals, Lion."—" मगाणां च मगेन्द्रोऽहम" -Gītā Ch. 10, St. 30,
names.simple_meaning: One who destroys

names.short_meaning: The Co-relator, the Regulator, the One who co-relates the actions and their fruits
names.commentary: The Co-relator, the Regulator, the One who co-relates the actions and their fruits. In fact, the fruit of an action is nothing other than the action itself: the action itself presents as its fruit in a different period of time. maturing under its own Law. This Great Law is the Lord, whom the devotee accepts as "The Giver of all fruits of action" (कर्मफलदाता ईश्वरः).
names.simple_meaning: The Co-relator, the Regulator, the One who co-relates the actions and their fruits

names.short_meaning: The structural engineering of individuality is the mightiest of phenomenon available in nature
names.commentary: The structural engineering of individuality is the mightiest of phenomenon available in nature. The Supreme is the Law and the Law-giver; and the Light of Consciousness functioning in the mind and intellect Itself is the individuality (jīva), that comes to suffer the good and bad results of the actions. Thus not only that it is He, who is the Giver of the results but It is He, again, Who is the enjoyer or the sufferer of the results. Hence He is called as the One who is apparently conditioned by the actions that emanate from Him, sandhimān, enjoyer (conditioned). In fact, He is the One presiding over and illumining all actions: the very Law of reaction Itself; the ensuing experience in all ac tions, of all people, at all times. From the stand-point of our existence, with reference to our individual existence, the Divinity in us, for all appearances, seems to be conditioned; this sandhimān, the jīva in His own Pristine Purity is Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The structural engineering of individuality is the mightiest of phenomenon available in nature

names.short_meaning: Firm, consistent
names.commentary: Firm, consistent. One who is ever consistent in His nature and One who remains changeless, at all times
names.simple_meaning: Firm, consistent

names.short_meaning: Unborn
names.commentary: Unborn. ajaḥ is also a term denoting the Creator, Brahmājī; He who, in the form of Hiranyagarbha, apparently creates the delusory world of plurality is Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: Unborn

names.short_meaning: One who cannot be attacked and vanquished
names.commentary: One who cannot be attacked and vanquished. In the long run, everyone in his own maturity will have to come and accept and walk the path of Viṣṇu — He is the final Goal. In the lesser levels of evolution, the animal-man may deny himself the peace and joy of living the spiritual values, and deluded by the senses and enchanted by the flesh, he may live a life of sense-joys and temporary fulfilments. But soon enough irresistibly he will be seeking the "feet" of Viṣṇu for real happiness and true achievement. His also is the final victory and one can stand apart from Him in a victory over him.
names.simple_meaning: One who cannot be attacked and vanquished

names.short_meaning: One who rules over the universe
names.commentary: One who rules over the universe. Not only that He is the Administrator of the laws of the Phenomenon but also He is the śāstā. He is the One who, through śāstra, with firm hand, instructs and guides us through the righteous path, drives us along steadily to progress in cultural beauty and finally reaches us at the Great Goal of all evolutions: the Seat of Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: One who rules over the universe

names.short_meaning: The famous term ātmā, famous in all the Vedas, is Viṣṇu
names.commentary: The famous term ātmā, famous in all the Vedas, is Viṣṇu. This term clearly shows that all the thousand terms, used herein, though can be considered for the Saguna worship of Viṣṇu, represent nothing other than the Pure Self, which is the famous theme of the Hindu Scriptures. Through hundreds of suggestive definitions, this Great Self has been successfully pointed out through declarations of Its Transcendental Nature and through statements of negation indicating what He is not.
names.simple_meaning: The self celebrated throughout the Vedas

names.short_meaning: Sura="God of the Heaven", Ari="enemies", Ha="destroyer"
names.commentary: Sura="God of the Heaven", Ari="enemies", Ha="destroyer". The Supreme is the Destroyer of the enemies of the gods. The sensuous claims of the flesh, the mild assertions of the ego, the nocturnal devils of desires and passions, are the common enemies of the higher mind aspiring to evolve. When invoked with true devotion, He who drives away and destroys the inimical negative tendencies, and helps the devotee to master himself, is surārihā, Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: The destroyer of the enemies of the gods

names.short_meaning: The teacher, who initiates seekers into the secrets of the sacred scriptures is called the Guru
names.commentary: The teacher, who initiates seekers into the secrets of the sacred scriptures is called the Guru. Since the Lord, the infinite alone, is the very author and knower of the Vedas, He is the Teacher in all spiritual study. ātman being the Light, that illumines the knowledge in the teacher, his very capacity to speak and the very ability in the student to hear, understand and comprehend this great Truth. He alone is the Teacher wherever there is any transfer of knowledge.
names.simple_meaning: The teacher

names.short_meaning: The Greatest Teacher; One who had inspired with knowledge and initiated the very Creator Brahmājī into the knowledge of the four Vedas
names.commentary:
The Greatest Teacher; One who had inspired with knowledge and initiated the very Creator Brahmājī into the knowledge of the four Vedas. The creative mind of the very first Spiritual Master must have received this experience of the Transcendental, initiated by none other than the Supreme Itself. Later on, the Man of Realization might come to help other seekers, and to that extent the following generations of disciples, can, no doubt, psychologically believe that the teacher guided them to Truth.

But, in fact for all times to come, the final experience of the theme of the Vedas is arrived at only through the final revelation, which has nothing to do with the teacher or the text.

Svetaasvatara Upaniṣad (6-18) says, "He who first Created the Creator (Brahmaa) and imparted him the Vedas." The Guru and the scripture, devotion to God, meditation. moral conduct and the religious discipline are all necessary, in as much as, they prepare the bosom of the seeker for the dawn of realization. But the final unveiling is done by the Infinite alone, and hence, Viṣṇu, the Self, is the best among the Gurus. Heaviness is called by the same term (Gurutvam), and in this sense the Lord is indicated here as "that which is heavier than the heaviest."
names.simple_meaning: The greatest teacher

names.short_meaning: The Goal; the Sacred destination of a pilgrimage
names.commentary:
The Goal; the Sacred destination of a pilgrimage. The Supreme is the Param-dhaama, the 'Supreme Destination', having reached which, there is nothing more to reach beyond. This Absolute State of Perfection is called the "Peak" (dhāma). The Sanskrit term dhāma also means "Effulgence" (Tejas); the Pure Consciousness as the Illuminator of all experiences is considered and glorified as the Light of all Lights etc.

Nārāyaṇopaniṣad declares: "Nārāyaṇa is the Supreme Light."

Muṇḍakopaniṣad says: "Brahman is the Supreme Whole."
names.simple_meaning: The Goal; the Sacred destination of a pilgrimage

names.short_meaning: One who is Himself the Truth
names.commentary:
One who is Himself the Truth. The difference from the general connotation, we have for the term "That which remains without a change in the past, present and future" is called Satyam. "Truth, Knowledge, Infinite is Brahman", thunder the scriptures. Brihad Upaniṣad (4-1-20) says, "The prāṇas are the truth, and He is the Truth of them."

satyam jñānam anantam brahma.
names.simple_meaning: One who is Himself the Truth

names.short_meaning: Dynamic Truth
names.commentary: Dynamic Truth. Passive truthfulness is the harbour of the fools, the dark den of the cowards; although it is any day better than suicidal untruth and criminal dishonesty. The Lord, the Infinite is not only Himself the Truth but He is Dynamic in insisting that "Truth shall prevail, not untruth", (सत्यमेव जयते न अनुतं). Not only gravity is a law of nature, itself ever truthful, but it insists that none shall escape its influence or disobey its sway. So too, the Infinite Law of Harmony and Love is an Inevitable Truth persisting with insistence in life. The Lord is therefore indicated by the term "satyaparākramaḥ".
names.simple_meaning: Dynamic Truth

names.short_meaning: The condition of "the eyelids closed" is called nimiṣaḥ; the unwinking is called Animishah
names.commentary:
The condition of "the eyelids closed" is called nimiṣaḥ; the unwinking is called Animishah. When the eyes are open, the mind is extrovert; the condition of mental introvertedness is expressed in an unconscious closing of the eyes. When a man is deeply thinking, remembering, contemplating, we find him naturally closing his eyes.

In a state of intense contemplation, when the intellect is turned away from the objects-of-experiences, the bosom experiences the One Divine "Subject" both within and without. The Lord is described here as "with eyes closed", only to indicate that He is ever rooted in Himself; from Him viewed, there exists nothing other than Himself to constitute the world-of-objects.
names.simple_meaning: The one whose eyes close in inward contemplation

names.short_meaning: One who remains unwinking
names.commentary: One who remains unwinking. Whenever we wink both the eye-lids close together and what we are seeing is at least technically veiled from the seer in the eye. The Supreme is indicated here by the term "unwinking", in the sense that the consciousness is Ever — Knowing-(इन्ट: दन्टे: अविपरिलोपात पश्यन्नेव भवति). In Śaṅkara's words, in Chāndogya Bhaashya, "there is no cessation of knowing in the knower"
names.simple_meaning: One who remains unwinking

names.short_meaning: A garland is called Srak and, therefore, the term means One who is constantly wearing a garland of undecaying flowers
names.commentary: A garland is called Srak (स्रक्) and, therefore, the term means One who is constantly wearing a garland of undecaying flowers. The famous garland of Viṣṇu is called Vaijayantī.
names.simple_meaning: The wearer of an unfading garland

names.short_meaning: vācaspati is a term given to One who is eloquent in championing the Supreme law of life; and dhī means the power of intelligence; and udāradhīḥ one who has a "Large-hearted intelligence", One who is not puritanical in his viewpoints
names.commentary:
vācaspati is a term given to One who is eloquent in championing the Supreme law of life; and dhī means the power of intelligence; and udāradhīḥ one who has a "Large-hearted intelligence", One who is not puritanical in his viewpoints. God is not only the Declarer of the Law but He has a large-hearted tolerance to appreciate the weakness of the devotee's heart, suffering under the delusion of māyā, and hence, has a great sympathy for the weakness in us. This is expressed in God's Infinite kindness towards sinners in general.

The laws of spiritual fiving can be disobeyed for a long time without any tyrannical onslaught, unlike the law of physical nature, which is blind and uncompromising. Fire knows no mercy. But Nārāyaṇa, the Great Viṣṇu, is kind and considerate while He expresses the Truth of Life eloquently at all times around us. In His Large-heartedness, He has enough paternal kindness to overlook our trespasses.
names.simple_meaning: The lord of speech, endowed with generous intelligence

names.short_meaning: One who guides us to the end - the peak
names.commentary: One who guides us to the end - the peak. Also the One, who leads (Agra) the entire pilgrimage—the Guide. He moves ahead and following His footsteps, keeping Him in our gaze, faithfully following Him, we shall reach the Goal and thus He is called as the leader, Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: One who guides us to the end - the peak

names.short_meaning: One who controls, guides and leads the "Collection", the "flock" (grāma)
names.commentary: One who controls, guides and leads the "Collection", the "flock" (grāma). In Sanskrit grāma means "a collection of many number of things".
names.simple_meaning: One who controls, guides and leads the "Collection", the "flock" (grāma)

names.short_meaning: Śrī means Light, Effulgence or glory
names.commentary: Śrī means Light, Effulgence or glory. Consciousness has all these three, and therefore, śrīmān means the Self, the Lord.
names.simple_meaning: The radiant possessor of splendor

names.short_meaning: The word in its direct meaning is "Justice"
names.commentary: The word in its direct meaning is "Justice". In the spiritual world, it connotes logical arguments (Tarka) and lines of contemplation (Yukti) which help us in arriving at the absolute experience indicated in the Sruti, are together called Nyaava.
names.simple_meaning: Justice and right reasoning

names.short_meaning: The leader—one who protects, nurtures, nourishes and guides all living creatures in the world
names.commentary: The leader—one who protects, nurtures, nourishes and guides all living creatures in the world. One who is the Superintendent of the machinery of life --("Jagat — Yantra Nirvaahakah")--Śaṅkara.
names.simple_meaning: The leader—one who protects, nurtures, nourishes and guides all living creatures in the world

names.short_meaning: One who efficiently administers all movements of all living creatures
names.commentary: One who efficiently administers all movements of all living creatures. In the physical body. all physiological activities are controlled by the five 'Praanaas' and thus in the form of 'Praanaas' He who governs all movements of all living creatures in the universe is Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: One who efficiently administers all movements of all living creatures

names.short_meaning: One who has endless number of heads
names.commentary: One who has endless number of heads. All living creatures are His manifestations and He Himself is the One who has become the many. Therefore all heads are His, just as in a factory the proprietor considers all the employees as his own 'hands'. Here the term Sahasra means innumerable.
names.simple_meaning: One who has endless number of heads

names.short_meaning: The very Soul of the Universe; the very inner Essence in all living creatures
names.commentary: The very Soul of the Universe; the very inner Essence in all living creatures.
names.simple_meaning: The very Soul of the Universe; the very inner Essence in all living creatures

names.short_meaning: In describing the macrocosmic form of the Lord we have an endorsement of this declaration in the Bhagavad Gītā
names.commentary:
In describing the macrocosmic form of the Lord we have an endorsement of this declaration in the Bhagavad Gītā.

अनेकवक्त्रनयनमनेकाद्भुतदर्शनम् । — Gītā 11.10.

रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम् । — Gītā 11.23.
names.simple_meaning: The thousand-eyed cosmic form

names.short_meaning: The One Infinite Consciousness expresses everywhere, in all forms, at all times
names.commentary: In the Purushasookta of the Rig — Veda, the same terms are used in describing the Infinite Form of the Mighty Truth: "सहस्रशीर्षा पृरुष: सहस्राक्ष: सहस्रपात्।" ("The puruṣa is thousand-headed, thousand-eyed, and thousand-footed.") The "many heads" (224), "many eyes" (226), "many legs" (227), together indicate that, through all these equipments of thinking (head), of action (leg) and of perception (eyes), the Thinker, the Doer and the Seer, the One Infinite Consciousness expresses everywhere, in all forms, at all times, and He is Lord Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The One Infinite Consciousness expresses everywhere, in all forms, at all times

names.short_meaning: One who is the Unseen Dynamism behind the ever-whirling wheel-of time upon which play the endless drama of birth and death
names.commentary:
One who is the Unseen Dynamism behind the ever-whirling wheel-of time upon which play the endless drama of birth and death. The repetition (Aavartanam) of these changes is the experience of saṃsāra, and the One mighty Lord, in whose presence alone the factors of matter start their thrilled dance of decay, is indicated here (āvartanaḥ) as "the Great Power behind the continuity of change in the world of phenomena". In the Gītā, Bhagavān says, "O Arjuna, the Lord dwells in the heart of all, and spins. through His māyā, all layers of personal ties as though the universe is a complicated machinery."

ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति । भ्रामयन् सर्वभूतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥ — Gītā 18.61.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Unseen Dynamism behind the ever-whirling wheel-of time upon which play the endless drama of birth and death

names.short_meaning: The pure Self, which has retreated totally from all Its identifications with matter
names.commentary: The pure Self, which has retreated totally (Nivritta) from all Its identifications with matter. In short, Maha Viṣṇu is the Pure Self, ever Immaculate and totally Free from all the sorrows of the constant modifications taking place apparently in the Prakriti.
names.simple_meaning: The pure Self, which has retreated totally from all Its identifications with matter

names.short_meaning: One who is completely veiled from the recognition of the "Perceiving-feeling-thinking entity", the ego (jīva)
names.commentary:
One who is completely veiled from the recognition of the "Perceiving-feeling-thinking entity", the ego (jīva). The Self is veiled away from direct experience of all jīvas. This intellectual state of non-apprehension (Aavarana) creates the agitation (Vikshepa) which is the cause for the misapprehensions of Truth as the sad and sorrowful world of imperfections. Thus veiled, lies the Truth today to the seeker, and that Glorious spiritual Centre is Viṣṇu.

अज्ञानेनावृतं ज्ञानं तेन मुह्यन्ति जन्तवः ॥ — Gītā 5.15.
names.simple_meaning: One who is completely veiled from the recognition of the "Perceiving-feeling-thinking entity", the ego (jīva)

names.short_meaning: One who persecutes relentlessly men, who are sensuous, evil-minded, and so, fully extrovert in their personality (rākṣasas)
names.commentary: One who persecutes relentlessly men, who are sensuous, evil-minded, and so, fully extrovert in their personality (rākṣasas). In the form of disease, decay, disaster or death That which manifests to annihilate the pride, vanity and conceits of all "animal-men", as they live drowned in their flesh cravings, low emotions and materialistic values, is the Ultimate Reality—the Supreme Lord Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: One who persecutes relentlessly men, who are sensuous, evil-minded, and so, fully extrovert in their personality (rākṣasas)

names.short_meaning: One who thrills the day (Ahas) and makes it function vigorously (pravartakah)
names.commentary:
One who thrills the day (Ahas) and makes it function vigorously (pravartakah). The one who dynamises the day and lends the enchantment of joy to all living creatures is the Sun. The Mighty Truth, who, in the form of the Sun, gives life to all and lends this energy to them to act, is Viṣṇu. In the Gītā, Lord Kṛṣṇa says, "Please understand that I am the Light of the Sun that illumines all earth; and the light and heat in the moon and fire are all mine only."

यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम् । यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम् ॥ — Gītā 15.12.
names.simple_meaning: One who thrills the day (Ahas) and makes it function vigorously (pravartakah)

names.short_meaning: Fire
names.commentary:
Fire. One, who is worshipped at the altar as the God of gods, was Fire in the Vedic period. Invoking the various deities, oblations were poured into the Fire in Vedic ritualism and Lord Fire is entrusted with the duty of conveying (वह) the oblations to the appropriate deities invoked by the devotee.

In short, Viṣṇu is the Omniscient Lord, who conveys appropriate Karma-phala to the kartā (doer) and thus fulfils all actions of everybody, at all times.
names.simple_meaning: Fire

names.short_meaning: This term has four distinct meanings
names.commentary:
This term has four distinct meanings. All of them are appropriate here. (a) 'Air' (Vaayu); living creatures; (b) "Beginning-less" (ādi-rahitah); that Truth, from which the concept of time itself has born, must have been there even before time, manifested, and therefore, in terms of our intellectual concept of time, we can only say that He is "Beginningless"; (c) 'Eater' of food (Attaa); all experiences that satisfy the inner man is called the "food", and since all experiences are lived only when illumined by the consciousness, the Supreme, in terms of our experience is called the "Eater" and (d) "The Homeless" since He is All-pervading He is the shelter of all and He is not sheltered by anything.

Interval between any two successive experiences.

Consciousness functioning through the mind and intellect is the Enjoyer and Doer—the ego. — Gītā 18.61.
names.simple_meaning: The wind, needing no impulse from another

names.short_meaning: One who supports (Dharah) the earth (dharaṇī)
names.commentary: One who supports (Dharah) the earth (dharaṇī). The field of our experiences is the earth, and for all our earthly experiences, Consciousness is at once the very substratum and the very Illuminator. In the Light of Consciousness alone, the web of happenings around is held together to provide us with our experiences.
names.simple_meaning: One who supports (Dharah) the earth (dharaṇī)

names.short_meaning: One who is full of the Supreme Grace and who, so little, so easily, becomes so entirely satisfied
names.commentary:
One who is full of the Supreme Grace and who, so little, so easily, becomes so entirely satisfied. Even to those who can remember Him, even if it be in a spirit of constant and faithful antagonism, His Grace is readily available. In Bhāgavata we read Pootanaa, who tried to poison Him, Kamsa, who planned to murder Him, or Sisupaala, who falsely accused Him—all of them were ultimately rewarded by the Lord. In the Gītā, He confesses, "With a little am I satisfied. if it is given with sincerity, and with faithful consistency".

पत्रं पूष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति । तदहं भक्त्यपहतं अश्नामि प्रयतात्मन: 11 (Gītā Ch. 9 St. 26).
names.simple_meaning: One who is full of the Supreme Grace and who, so little, so easily, becomes so entirely satisfied

names.short_meaning: Ever — Pure and All- Blissful Self
names.commentary:
Ever — Pure and All- Blissful Self. The Supreme is ever-pure because, It is untouched by the sorrows lived by matter, when matter is ruled over by its guṇas. In Gītā we read that the cause for all the sorrows of the individuality (jīva) is the attachment with matter and its various imperfect conditions (guṇas). Since He is untouched by them He is Ever — Pure; and since no identification of matter is in Him. He is all — Bliss.

पुरुषः प्रकृतिस्थो हि भुङ्क्ते प्रकृतिजान् गुणान् ॥ — Gītā 13.21.
