names.simple_meaning: Ever — Pure and All- Blissful Self

names.short_meaning: As a Mighty Source of all existence in every thing and every being
names.commentary: As a Mighty Source of all existence in every thing and every being. He is the Supporter (Dhrik) of the total world of all perceptions, all emotions and all thoughts (Visva). Herein the Supporter and the supported being essentially one, no calamity comes to the Lord by the increase in population. Ocean, the supporter of the waves, can never feel bothered by the stormy surface and the consequent increase in the number of waves.
names.simple_meaning: As a Mighty Source of all existence in every thing and every being

names.short_meaning: The One who enjoys or swallows (Bhuk) all experiences (Visva)
names.commentary:
The One who enjoys or swallows (Bhuk) all experiences (Visva). The Supreme Consciousness, apparently conditioned by the mind and intellect is the experiencer of the joys and sorrows.

The term also means, "the One who absorbs unto Himself all names and forms" at the time of the dissolution (Pralaya). In the plane of God-consciousness all other experiences, gathered in fields of waking, dream and deep-sleep, are transcended and, therefore, the State of Perfection can be figuratively indicated as "viśvabhuk" the One who swallows all other experiences of plurality".
names.simple_meaning: The One who enjoys or swallows (Bhuk) all experiences (Visva)

names.short_meaning: One who manifests Himself in an endless variety of forms
names.commentary: One who manifests Himself in an endless variety of forms. Though essentially the Infinite is One, Non — Dual and All — Pervading, the Reality, when viewed through the equipments of mind-and-intellect (māyā) seems to have apparently become the pluralistic world. Muṇḍakopaniṣad (1-6) says, "He is Eternal and Multiform." Based upon this idea we have in the Purāṇas, the description of the Lord's incarnations and His play in the world of the many.
names.simple_meaning: One who manifests Himself in an endless variety of forms

names.short_meaning: One who revels and adores those who are good and wise
names.commentary: One who revels and adores those who are good and wise. His palace is ever lit up with His hospitality and He Himself presides over the loving reception of the righteous (सतकरोति इति सत्कर्ता).
names.simple_meaning: One who revels and adores those who are good and wise

names.short_meaning: One who is adored by all good people, not only is He adored and worshipped by great men of wisdom and devotion—as the Sanatkumaaras, Naarada and others—but He is invoked and worshipped consciously by all living creatures
names.commentary: One who is adored by all good people, not only is He adored and worshipped by great men of wisdom and devotion—as the Sanatkumaaras, Naarada and others—but He is invoked and worshipped consciously by all living creatures. The Upaniṣad describes every experience of all living creatures as a yajña in which the stimuli received are the 'Oblations' poured at which the inner Consciousness flares up into brilliancy.
names.simple_meaning: The one honored and worshiped by the good

names.short_meaning: One, who functions strictly according to the righteous code of living is a sādhuḥ
names.commentary: One, who functions strictly according to the righteous code of living is a sādhuḥ (साधयति इति साध:) Atman, the Self, is the Mighty Presence, which apparently lends intelligence and capacity to inert matter. The Supreme Saadhu is Viṣṇu Himself.
names.simple_meaning: One, who functions strictly according to the righteous code of living is a sādhuḥ

names.short_meaning: Leader of men; the One who leads all creatures along the path of an inexorable law—the law of action and reaction, the rhythm of Karma
names.commentary: Leader of men; the One who leads all creatures along the path of an inexorable law—the law of action and reaction, the rhythm of Karma. Irresistibly, the good is led, by his own subjective disharmony, dashes to reach a hell made by himself for himself.
names.simple_meaning: Leader of men; the One who leads all creatures along the path of an inexorable law—the law of action and reaction, the rhythm of Karma

names.short_meaning: This simple sacred word has an endless number of direct and indirect meanings, imports and suggestions, and Vyasa seems to have explored almost all its possibilities
names.commentary:
This simple sacred word has an endless number of direct and indirect meanings, imports and suggestions, and Vyasa seems to have explored almost all its possibilities. The Shelter (Ayanam) for man (Nara) is Naaraayana.

1. The term Nara implies the ego-centric individuality.

2. A large collection of them is called Naara and the One who is the sole refuge for the entire living creatures is called nārāyaṇaḥ.

3. Nara also means Īśvara and the elements (Tattvas) born out of Him are called Naara; and One who is the controller, the regulator, the very source of all Existence in these very Tattvas is called Nārāyaṇaḥ.

4. Naaraah also mean "waters". According to the picture painted in the Purāṇas of the Deluge, wherein the names, and forms devolve themselves into their elemental waters, the Lord is objectively described as lying alone upon the waters, the Eternal baby, floating upon a banyan leaf. "Holding in His Lotus-hand His own Lotus-feet, and sucking His own toe with His Lotus-lips, the Lotus child resting playfully upon a banyan leaf, floating up on the waters of the Deluge—I meditate." It is in this sense, we find Manu interpreting the word "Naaraayana". In the great devotional classic, Bhaagavatam, we find very many suggestions digged out of this sacred name; such as the 'Self of all bodies', "the Dynamic Force behind matter", "the Witness of all good and bad". All these indicate that Śrī Nārāyaṇa is nothing other than the Glory (Ayanam) of the Self.

नराज्जातानि तत्त्वानि नाराणीति विदुर्बुधाः । तान्येव चायनं तस्य तेन नारायणः स्मृतः ॥ — Mahābhārata.

करारविन्देन पदारविन्दं मुखारविन्दे विनिवेशयन्तम् । वटस्य पत्रस्य पुटे शयानं बालं मुकुन्दं मनसा स्मरामि ॥

Manu Smṛti 1.10 says: "The waters are called nāras which come out of Nara (God). As they are originally His abode, He is called Nārāyaṇa."
names.simple_meaning: The resting place of all beings

names.short_meaning: The Guide
names.commentary: The Guide: ("नयति इति नरः प्रोक्तः परमात्मा सनातनः"). One who guides all creatures strictly according to their actions is none other than the Ancient (sanātana) Self
names.simple_meaning: The Guide

names.short_meaning: Sankhyaa means number; Asankhya=numberless
names.commentary:
Sankhyaa means number; Asankhya=numberless. asaṅkhyeyaḥ is one who has numberless names and forms. The infinite variety of things and beings that constitute the manifested Universe are all His Own Form, and hence He is indeed numberless, whom He expresses Himself as the Universe. In the 11th Chapter of Gītā, we see through Arjuna's eyes the Cosmic Form of the Lord. Of boundless forms on everyside with numberless arms, stomachs, mouths and eyes-neither end nor middle, nor beginning do I see, O Lord of the Universe.

अनेकबाहूदरवक्त्रनेत्रं पश्यामि त्वां सर्वतोऽनन्तरूपम् । नान्तं न मध्यं न पुनस्तवादिं पश्यामि विश्वेश्वर विश्वरूप ॥ — Gītā 11.16.
names.simple_meaning: The one beyond all counting

names.short_meaning: Prameya=pramāṇa Vishaya—anything that can be known through any of the "Sources-of-knowledge"—direct or indirect
names.commentary: Prameya=pramāṇa Vishaya—anything that can be known through any of the "Sources-of-knowledge"—direct or indirect. Atman, the Self, cannot be apprehended by the intellect through any of the known "Sources-of — Knowledge" (pramāṇa) and so He is called as Aprameya. One who has this nature is the Self, aprameyātmā, Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: The one whose self cannot be measured by any proof

names.short_meaning: The One who transcends everything, in His Glory is the Supreme (viśiṣṭaḥ)
names.commentary: The One who transcends everything, in His Glory is the Supreme (viśiṣṭaḥ). Something that is other than the three bodies, something other than the five kosas, something definitely different from the finite world of perishable things is the Infinite Self-which cannot be defined in terms of either the waking or the dream or the sleep conditions. The Self is something other than all these: "एतत् विलक्षण विद्यात् आत्मानं राजवत् सदा” or “उपाधित्रितयादन्यं आत्मानमवधारयेत्।” —(Atma Bodh). This Supreme-most Truth is Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The One who transcends everything, in His Glory is the Supreme (viśiṣṭaḥ)

names.short_meaning: One who governs; One who is the Law Maker and the Law that governs the universe
names.commentary: One who governs; One who is the Law Maker and the Law that governs the universe. The goal of His administration is the protection of the good (śiṣṭaḥ). Maha Viṣṇu is the Governor of all, and the Protector of the good.
names.simple_meaning: One who governs; One who is the Law Maker and the Law that governs the universe

names.short_meaning: One who is Pure
names.commentary: One who is Pure. The immaculate Reality which is never contaminated by the māyā and its by-products is Maha Viṣṇu. When dirt (Mala) exists upon anything, it becomes unclean. In the Absolute Oneness there can be nothing other than itself and therefore the Fourth-plane-of — Consciousness (Tureeyam) is indicated in our Scriptures as the Transcendental Ever — Pure Self, Śrī Hari.
names.simple_meaning: One who is Pure

names.short_meaning: One who has gained all that has to be gained and achieved all that has to be achieved
names.commentary: One who has gained all that has to be gained and achieved all that has to be achieved. That which has to be achieved in life during an individual's existence has all been classified under four heads and they are called as the four "aims of life" (Purushaartha). They are Righteousness in conduct, (dharma), Wealth and Possession (Artha), desires and ambitions (kāma), liberation from imperfections (mokṣa). One who has gained all these "four" has nothing more to gain as there cannot be any sense of imperfection in Him. One who has gained (Siddhah) all that has to be gained (Arthah) is Siddhaartha, Lord Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: One who has gained all that has to be gained and achieved all that has to be achieved

names.short_meaning: saṅkalpa means "intellectual willing and wishing"
names.commentary: saṅkalpa means "intellectual willing and wishing". One who gains all that He wishes for, or One who immediately gains what He wills is called Siddha-sankalpah. Ordinarily we fail to gain what we demand because of the disintegration within ourselves. The Lord, the Perfect, is One who instantaneously gains all that He wishes; hence the Upaniṣads define Him as the Satya Sankalpavaan. This great Paramesvara of the Upaniṣads is the Maha Viṣṇu, the theme of the "Thousand Chants' (Sahasranāma).
names.simple_meaning: The one whose resolve is always fulfilled

names.short_meaning: One who is the Giver of the appropriate reward for all actions, for those who are doing spiritual practices
names.commentary: One who is the Giver of the appropriate reward for all actions, for those who are doing spiritual practices. Lord Nārāyaṇa is the great Universal Power that brings about the reward for all actions.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Giver of the appropriate reward for all actions, for those who are doing spiritual practices

names.short_meaning: One who is the very secret force which enables the seeker to diligently continue all efforts of his seeking
names.commentary: One who is the very secret force which enables the seeker to diligently continue all efforts of his seeking. Siddhi ordinarily means "fulfilment", here it means all efforts at a given fulfilment. It is also interpreted by some as the One Mighty Reality, to worship at whose altar is the very means (sādhana) for all achievements (Siddhi), and this is Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the very secret force which enables the seeker to diligently continue all efforts of his seeking

names.short_meaning: The term Vrishah is very familiar in the ritualistic portion of the Vedas and it connotes objectively the sacred "Left over" after the yajña functions
names.commentary: The term Vrishah is very familiar in the ritualistic portion of the Vedas and it connotes objectively the sacred "Left over" after the yajña functions. Subjectively, vṛṣa means the residual 'results' gathered in the personality after each devoted and dedicated act of offering, during all Self-less services (yajñas). Therefore, vṛṣāhī means "One who is a controller of all actions and the dispenser of all results", in all individual, conscious, intelligent creatures.
names.simple_meaning: The one whose days are devoted to dharma

names.short_meaning: The term vṛṣa though not very familiar now is used in the Vedic literature to indicate dharma—"the essential nature of a thing without which the thing cannot remain as the thing" is its dharma
names.commentary: The term vṛṣa though not very familiar now is used in the Vedic literature to indicate dharma—"the essential nature of a thing without which the thing cannot remain as the thing" is its dharma. One who showers all dharmas is called vṛṣabhaḥ. In short, one who showers glowing health, burning devotion and thrilling silence on all sincere seekers and faithful devotees is vṛṣabhaḥ; and He is Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: The embodiment of dharma who showers desired fruits

names.short_meaning: All — Pervading: Long — Strident
names.commentary:
All — Pervading: Long — Strident. We had already explained this term earlier (2). In Mahābhārata we also read the Lord Himself explaining to Arjuna, "Because I stand striding across the Universe (Kramanaat), O Partha.

I am known as Viṣṇu."—"क्रमणात चाप्यहं पार्थ विष्णरित्यभिसंज्ञित:।" -(Mahābhārata 12-350-43). In the Upaniṣad also we read, "Viṣṇu has spread Himself and conquered all these three worlds ("इदं विष्ण: विचक्रमे").
names.simple_meaning: All — Pervading: Long — Strident

names.short_meaning: We had already explained that vṛṣa means dharma
names.commentary:
We had already explained that vṛṣa means dharma. The term Parvam means "Ladder". "a flight of steps" that takes us to the Higher floors (Hence Parvata means mountain). Thus, here, the term is explained as a flight of steps on the ladder of life to take one to the Ultimate Reality, the Eternal (sanātana) dharma: "I am the way".

Viṣṇu is the One worship at whose altar will facilitate the devotee's steady evolution towards the experience of the Higher consciousness.
names.simple_meaning: The ladder whose steps are dharma

names.short_meaning: vṛṣa, that which rains; Udara=belly
names.commentary: vṛṣa, that which rains; Udara=belly. The idea here is the seat of all creative thinking is resting on a psychic centre, roughly indicated by the navel. and hence we find the description that the total Creator of the universe is sustained and held aloft at the navel of Maha Viṣṇu. During Pralaya (sleep) the "creative power" merges back to its source, and thereafter, upon waking, the creation again starts; the "creative power" manifests itself and continues its creative activities, from the same point of its merger, (Udara). This culminating point of all creation, during the time of the dissolution—which is also the same from wherein, during creation, the manifestations of names and forms spring forth (shower down = vṛṣa)— is Viṣṇu, the Supreme, and hence, He is called as vṛṣodaraḥ, "the Showering Belly."
names.simple_meaning: The one whose depths contain the source of creation

names.short_meaning: One who is the nurturer and nourisher everywhere, at all levels of life, both material and spiritual
names.commentary: One who is the nurturer and nourisher everywhere, at all levels of life, both material and spiritual. In short, from the standpoint of the student, who is studying with devotion these "Thousand names of the Lord", the term indicates that Viṣṇu is the Mighty Power that supplies all spiritual growth, provides all well-being and ultimately blesses all His devotees with the final Realization.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the nurturer and nourisher everywhere, at all levels of life, both material and spiritual

names.short_meaning: One who can grow Himself into any dimensions; ever-growing
names.commentary: One who can grow Himself into any dimensions; ever-growing. Since the names and forms of the universe are ever dynamic and the unseen movement of progressive evolution is everywhere, the Lord is indicated here as this very "dimensional movement of progress" (Vardhana). (The Pauraanikas attribute that this name came to Him because He in His Vāmana incarnation grew Himself to measure under His three steps the whole universe.)
names.simple_meaning: One who can grow Himself into any dimensions; ever-growing

names.short_meaning: Alone=solitary
names.commentary:
Alone=solitary. Ever standing apart from everything. With reference to the dream and the dreamer, the waker is, we know, indeed, separate. Similarly the world of names and forms and its joys and sorrows, passions and lusts, smiles and tears, though they all play in the Self, the Supreme is not affected by them.

The horrid "ghost" cannot affect the innocent "post". One who thus remains alone and apart, in His Own Majesty and Perfection, even when the world-of-māyā is heaving about is viviktaḥ. In the daily happenings of Samsar, in its births and deaths. He remains ever changeless and ever unaffected. This freedom is indicated in the Gītā and the Lord explains: "They are in me; I am not in them"-"मत्स्थानि सर्वभतानि न चाहं तेष्व- वस्थित: 1" —(Gītā ix, 4).
names.simple_meaning: The solitary and distinct one

names.short_meaning: The ocean for all the rivers of all scriptural thoughts
names.commentary: The ocean for all the rivers of all scriptural thoughts. All scriptures, irrespective of the age, language, tradition and beliefs, ultimately indicate a Theme which is ever the same. All scriptures are rivulets of thoughts, flowing through different terrains of national character and historical climates, gushing to reach forward the ocean of Perfection, which lies beyond the dark sorrows of mortality. That which is the goal of all Scriptures is the Immortal Bliss of God-consciousness, the Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The ocean for all the rivers of all scriptural thoughts

names.short_meaning: He who has graceful arms
names.commentary: He who has graceful arms. This need not be taken as a description of the physical beauty of the anatomical structure of the arms but since those arms are ever working in the service of His devotees on sheltering them (Abhaya) and in blessing them (Varada) they are full of grace and hence graceful.
names.simple_meaning: He who has graceful arms

names.short_meaning: One who cannot be comprehended even by Great yogīs, who spend long periods of time in meditation
names.commentary: One who cannot be comprehended even by Great yogīs, who spend long periods of time in meditation. Transcending the mind and intellect is the "experience" of the Supreme and, therefore, the mind and intellect can never comprehend It.
names.simple_meaning: One who cannot be comprehended even by Great yogīs, who spend long periods of time in meditation

names.short_meaning: One who is cloquent of His Glory
names.commentary: One who is cloquent of His Glory. The full sense of the term should embrace not only the eloquence in speech, but all physical capabilities in the world, all the Glories of the cosmos, all the beauties of the heart, the total might of the intellect—all are eloquent of His Glory. Through the scriptures of the world, it is again He, who speaks to us of our ultimate Harbour beyond the stormy seas of māyā, in the simple words of brilliant suggestions declared by the Saints, Sages, ṛṣis, Prophets and other Divine Men.
names.simple_meaning: One who is cloquent of His Glory

names.short_meaning: One who is Lord of even Indra, the Lord of gods
names.commentary: One who is Lord of even Indra, the Lord of gods. In philosophy the "Mind" is called Indra (Indriyaanaam rājā) and One who is the Lord of even the "mind" is the Self.
names.simple_meaning: One who is Lord of even Indra, the Lord of gods

names.short_meaning: Vasu means wealth and, therefore, vasudaḥ means One who enriches all, both in their outer prosperity and in their inner well-being
names.commentary: Vasu means wealth and, therefore, vasudaḥ means One who enriches all, both in their outer prosperity and in their inner well-being. Once surrendered unto Him, man learns to live ever in dynamic success, with all the glories of the loving heart, self-controlled mind, and contemplative intellect.
names.simple_meaning: The giver of wealth

names.short_meaning: The term Vasu has got three meanings: Wealth (Dhana), Veil (Aacchaadana) and Sun (Āditya); thus He is the One who manifests Himself in the form of the external wealth, for He, as the very sun, nurtures and nourishes the world
names.commentary:
The term Vasu has got three meanings: Wealth (Dhana), Veil (Aacchaadana) and Sun (Āditya); thus He is the One who manifests Himself in the form of the external wealth, for He, as the very sun, nurtures and nourishes the world. He is the One, who veils Himself from the comprehension and understanding of the unprepared men of evil temperaments who possess no true devotion.

The term Vasu also can mean "One who lives in" (Vasati iti) all things and beings of the universe; or it can also mean "One who allows all things and beings to exist in Himself" (Vaasayati iti). In Gītā and in the Upaniṣads we find the Infinite described as the very Indweller everywhere in His Īśvara status, and as the very substratum for the universe in the Pure Transcendental nature.

यस्त् सर्वाणि भृतानि आत्मन्येवानुपश्यति । सर्वभृतेषु चात्मानं ततो न विज्गुप्सते ।। —(Īśa.—6) Again in Gītā (VI, 29) we read: सर्वभतस्थमात्मानं सर्वभतानि चात्मनि। ईक्षते योगयुक्तात्मा सर्वत्र समदर्शनः।।
names.simple_meaning: The one manifest as wealth, the veil, and the nourishing sun

names.short_meaning: One who is of Infinite forms in His manifestations; the single waker's mind becomes itself variegated to serve as the endless items of the dream-world
names.commentary:
One who is of Infinite forms in His manifestations; the single waker's mind becomes itself variegated to serve as the endless items of the dream-world. The One Supreme "Cause" of the whole Universe is Viṣṇu; and all "effects" are but different expressions of their "cause".

In a very familiar chant, traditionally repeated by all devotees, this idea has been brought out beautifully. जलं विष्णु: स्थलं विष्णु: विष्णुराकाशमुच्यते । स्थावरं जंगमं विष्णुः सर्वं विष्णुमयं जगत्।।

Looking at Him through our distorting instruments of body-mind-intellect, we see the plurality, and only on trans cending this equipment can we "experience" the Oneness of the Absolute Reality.
names.simple_meaning: The one of infinite forms

names.short_meaning: Vast, of Infinite dimensions;Pervading all
names.commentary: Vast, of Infinite dimensions;Pervading all. One whose very form (roopa) is the totality of the universe and therefore as vast as the universe. In the description of the Supreme Person in the Rig Veda (Purushasookta) we read the ṛṣis declaring that Viṣṇu is not only of the total size and dimension of the Universe but He stands beyond it all by ten digits.—"Atyatishthat Dasaangulam".
names.simple_meaning: Vast, of Infinite dimensions;Pervading all

names.short_meaning: Sipi is the name given to the "Sacrificial cow"
names.commentary:
Sipi is the name given to the "Sacrificial cow". The term denotes the One who sanctified all dedicated offerings poured into all fields of selfless sacrifices (yajña). The root Si (शि) has also the meaning of waters; Sipi—'that which drinks water'—"The rays of the Sun".

Thus śipiviṣṭaḥ would indicate the Supreme, who is the Presiding deity in the Sun, giving it both its energy of heat and light. In Gītā, the Lord confesses: "Understand that the light and energy that expresses themselves through the sun and moon is the Light and Glory essentially belonging to Me".

यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगत् भासयतेऽखिलम् । यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम ।।
names.simple_meaning: Sipi is the name given to the "Sacrificial cow"

names.short_meaning: The One who illuminates; expressing Itself as the All-pervading Consciousness in every equipment
names.commentary:
The One who illuminates; expressing Itself as the All-pervading Consciousness in every equipment. He is the knower, knowing everything in each bosom (Sarvavit) and knowing all things that are happening in the universe at one and the same time in His omnisciency (Sarvajnah). He is the Illuminator of all experiences. Just as the One sun illumines everything in the world the Reality illumines both the fields of experiences and the knower-of-the-field यथा प्रकाशयत्येकः कृत्स्नं लोकिममं रविः।

क्षेत्रं क्षेत्री तथा कृत्स्न प्रकाशयति भारत ।। —(Gītā XIII—33)
names.simple_meaning: The One who illuminates; expressing Itself as the All-pervading Consciousness in every equipment

names.short_meaning: One who is the possessor (Dharah) of Perfect physical virility (Ojas), all brilliancy (Tejas) and every beauty (dyuti)
names.commentary:
One who is the possessor (Dharah) of Perfect physical virility (Ojas), all brilliancy (Tejas) and every beauty (dyuti). These three terms indicate perfection at three different levels of personality known to us at present. Ojas is glowing health (physical) due to perfect balance in the constituents (Tattvas) of the healthy body. This virility in us when conserved, disciplined and trained can, through meditation, be converted into intellectual "brilliancy" and perfect personality "integration".

The shine of an individual, who has thus sublimated Ojas, is termed in our śāstras as tejas. A Yogi, through intelligent living and through a devoted life of continued meditation. has thus gathered to himself ojas and Tejas sufficiently, he, in time, grows to become an experienced Saint of Divine Realization, a Buddha. The enchanting atmosphere of irresistible peace and compassion, love and perfection, knowledge and strength, such a man throws around him, is called the aura of Divinity (Dyuti). In the 10th Chapter of the Gītā, the Geetacharya autobiographically confesses, "I am the Might in all strength: I am the Brilliancy in all that is brilliant." Some commentators are found to take these three terms as separate names of the Lord. However, Śaṅkara interprets it as one single term.

बलं बलवतामस्मि तेजस्तेजस्विनामहम् । — Gītā 10.36.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the possessor (Dharah) of Perfect physical virility (Ojas), all brilliancy (Tejas) and every beauty (dyuti)

names.short_meaning: The Effulgent Self
names.commentary: The Effulgent Self. The One who is the Self in all hearts, who can be experienced as the Consciousness, which is the source of all illumination to shine upon all experiences in the three planes-of-consciousness, in all living creatures, at all times. This Universal and Absolute Self is Maha Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The Effulgent Self

names.short_meaning: The One who manifests Himself as the Essential Thermal Energy, that lends Life Potential to the very atmosphere around each living creature
names.commentary: The One who manifests Himself as the Essential Thermal Energy, that lends Life Potential to the very atmosphere around each living creature. In the words of the Geetacharya, we find a confirmation to this declaration when the Lord declares to Arjuna that He Himself is the Reality that manifests as the heat and light in the Sun and the Moon, and it is He again who warms up the crust of the earth and impregnates it with its fertility. (Gītā XV-12 & 13).
names.simple_meaning: The One who manifests Himself as the Essential Thermal Energy, that lends Life Potential to the very atmosphere around each living creature

names.short_meaning: One who is ever full of all prosperity
names.commentary: One who is ever full of all prosperity. As the very Lord of Lakṣmī, Viṣṇu should be one who has all glories (Aisvarya). When the entire universe of wealth, strength and beauty is itself a manifestation from Him. He Himself must be the Absolute Glory.
names.simple_meaning: One who is ever full of all prosperity

names.short_meaning: Spashtam=clear
names.commentary:
Spashtam=clear. One who is clearly indicated by the Supreme Sound (Akshara), the famous Sound — Symbol of the Eternal Lord Om. In Gītā we read: "One who chants my name Om and leaves his body at the time of death thus remembering Me, he shall go to the Supreme State" In Sanskrit, kṣara means the "perishable" and Akshara means the "imperishable." The world of plurality, the "perishable" is no doubt nothing other than the All — Perfect, the Immutable Truth, but due to the imperfections of the instruments-of-perception—body, mind and intellect—the perceiving ego can experience only this world constituted of a plurality—sense objects, emotions and thoughts—The ego peeping through the vehicles can never experience the One co-ordinating Reality, the Divine. When the mind is hushed and the ego thus sublimated, the Immutable Akshara-factor is experienced, wherein we gain the clearest (Spashta) understanding of the Absolute. Since it is thus clear (Spashta) only in Its Immutable nature (Akshara = Kootastha), Viṣṇu, the Supreme Self, is indicated here as Spashtaaksharah).

ओमित्येकाक्षरं ब्रह्म व्याहरन्मामनुस्मरन् । यः प्रयाति त्यजन्देहं स याति परमां गतिम् ॥ — Gītā 8.13.
names.simple_meaning: The one whose imperishable syllable is clear

names.short_meaning: One who is of the nature of the Mantras of the Vedas
names.commentary: One who is of the nature of the Mantras of the Vedas. The declarations of the Vedas the mantras are the vehicles that will take us straight into an experience of the Transcendental. The vehicles are often called by the name of their destination. Mantra means that which can save us on being properly meditated upon (मननात त्रायते इति मंत्र:). Only through the mantras of the Upaniṣads we ever come to experience the Supreme Nature of the Lord. and so He is named as mantraḥ.
names.simple_meaning: One who is of the nature of the Mantras of the Vedas

names.short_meaning: Rays of the moon
names.commentary:
Rays of the moon. That the moonlight has got an effect upon the herbs was known to India in the Vedic period. "As the rays of the moon (Soma) I fill the vegetable kingdom with nutrition", confesses Bhagavān Vāsudeva. Thus the Lord is One who nurtures and nourishes all living creatures instilling into each its particular vitality. Though this is the deep philosophical significance, superficially the beauty, calm and peace that the moon suggests to our mind is but a reflection of the Infinite Peace of Viṣṇu.

पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः । — Gītā 15.13.
names.simple_meaning: Rays of the moon

names.short_meaning: The Effulgence of the Sun
names.commentary: The Effulgence of the Sun. Sun is the centre of the solar system, an eternal exchequer of energy, ever distributing Life and Strength to all living upon the earth; life would have been impossible but for the Sun. At the same time, the Sun stays where he is and he never interferes with life; from afar he blesses life. The Lord who thus from afar blesses by His mere presence is the true Sun of Life, the Atman, the Self - Śrī Mahāviṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The Effulgence of the Sun

names.short_meaning: The moon who has consoling rays that gives the essential food-value (Rasa) to the plants and fruits is called in Sanskrit as Amritaamsuh
names.commentary: The moon who has consoling rays that gives the essential food-value (Rasa) to the plants and fruits is called in Sanskrit as Amritaamsuh. In the Purāṇas it is described that the moon was first born from the milky-ocean during its churning. Since Viṣṇu is described as ever reposing upon His Ananta-bed in Ksheerasaagara, the Lord is Himself termed here as the Begetter of the Moon. Subjectively Moon (Mati) is the Presiding Deity of the intellect, and the discriminating intellect itself arose when our bosom started churning the heart by the two forces, the positive — the good (Deva) — and the negative — Vicious (Asuras). If the Sun is the Presiding Deity of energy, moon represents the world of matter, and the very source from which the world-of-matter, kṣetra, has risen is amṛtāṃśūdbhavaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: The source of the nectar-rayed moon

names.short_meaning: Self — Effulgent; One who expresses Himself for the blessing of the world in the form of the Sun and presides over the entire solar system
names.commentary: Self — Effulgent; One who expresses Himself for the blessing of the world in the form of the Sun and presides over the entire solar system.
names.simple_meaning: Self — Effulgent; One who expresses Himself for the blessing of the world in the form of the Sun and presides over the entire solar system

names.short_meaning: The patch in the moon looks like the silhouette of a rabbit for the naked eye; that which has a "beauty-spot" (Bindu) in the shape of a rabbit (Sasa) is called Sasabindu — the moon
names.commentary:
The patch in the moon looks like the silhouette of a rabbit for the naked eye; that which has a "beauty-spot" (Bindu) in the shape of a rabbit (Sasa) is called Sasabindu — the moon. Since the Lord is the Nourisher of all and He is Himself the entire world of matter, He Himself is the Moon "that nourishes with essence all plant kingdom".

गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा । पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः ॥ — Gītā 15.13.
names.simple_meaning: The moon marked like a hare

names.short_meaning: Sura means Deva and so the term indicates "the God of all gods"
names.commentary: Sura means Deva and so the term indicates "the God of all gods". The word Sura also can be dissolved to mean Giver (Ra) of Plenty (Su); Sura therefore stands for a person of extreme charity. The Lord, Īśvara, who prompts and fulfils the loving kindness of all charitable men is sureśvaraḥ, Lord Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The lord of the shining gods

names.short_meaning: Medicine
names.commentary:
Medicine. Nārāyaṇa is the Divine Medicine for the immediate cure for all the burning sorrows of Samsar. Even to consider it more directly as the specific cure for all bodily ailments is not necessarily wrong, for ailments of the body are caused by mental disintegration, and when the inner man has surrendered in devotion to Him.

Lord Nārāyaṇa indeed becomes a specific cure for even all the physical diseases of His devotees.
names.simple_meaning: Medicine

names.short_meaning: A reclamation bund thrown across waters connecting distant islands to the main land is called Setu
names.commentary: A reclamation bund thrown across waters connecting distant islands to the main land is called Setu. Śrī Ramachandraji built one and reached Lanka. The term jagataḥ setuḥ, therefore, implies that the Lord is Himself the Bridge over which one can safely cross over the realm of egocentric imperfections and reach the joyous realms of the Infinite Perfection.
names.simple_meaning: The bridge across the world's waters

names.short_meaning: One who champions heroically for Truth (Satya) and Righteousness (dharma)
names.commentary: One who champions heroically for Truth (Satya) and Righteousness (dharma). It can also imply as One who has Truthfulness (Satyam), Righteousness (dharma) and Heroism (Paraakramah). In short, Lord is One, who fights constantly against the false and the unrighteous to establish Truth and Purity.
names.simple_meaning: One who champions heroically for Truth (Satya) and Righteousness (dharma)

names.short_meaning: The Lord of the three periods of time: the past, the present and the future
names.commentary: The Lord of the three periods of time: the past, the present and the future. Lord of Time is the One, in whose presence alone, time concept is possible. "Time" is the interval between "thoughts" and the Awareness that illumines the rise and fall of thoughts is the very Lord of Time. Objectively He is the Lord of all those, that exist in the three periods of time; or He to whom all creatures conditioned by time, pray for comforts, solace and protection.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of the three periods of time: the past, the present and the future

names.short_meaning: One who purifies everything
names.commentary: One who purifies everything. Or One who manifests as the life-giving atmosphere around the world and sustains the existence everywhere.
names.simple_meaning: One who purifies everything

names.short_meaning: In the earlier term "Pavanah" the Lord is indicated as the One who has, in the form of the atmospheric air, filled the universe
names.commentary:
In the earlier term "Pavanah" the Lord is indicated as the One who has, in the form of the atmospheric air, filled the universe. He is the One who sustains life in all living creatures as the life-giving atmospheric air. Here, the present term "pāvanaḥ" means the One who gives this life-sustaining power to the atmospheric air. It is very well-known that the moving air (Breeze) purifies more than any other known thing in the world. This purifying power is acquired by the atmosphere by His Grace. In short, He is the secret glory that lends the atmosphere, the very life-sustaining property and He is the dynamism that moves the air.

From fear of Him the wind blows. — Taittirīya Upaniṣad.
names.simple_meaning: The purifier who fills the universe as wind

names.short_meaning: The term itself means Fire
names.commentary:
The term itself means Fire. So He who is in the form of fire, and sustains life. A certain amount of minimum thermal heat is necessary for life to continue, be it in the human body or be it in the Earth itself. This warmth of life in the world around and in the organism itself, without which life cannot continue, that mighty warmth of life is none other than the Lord, and hence, He is called analaḥ. Also the term 'Ana' has the meaning of prāṇa, and 'La' means to receive.

Therefore, the term can also imply "One who is the very Self. the very Vital Factor, in the prāṇa".
names.simple_meaning: The sacred fire

names.short_meaning: One who destroys all desires
names.commentary:
One who destroys all desires. Desires spring forth from the vāsanās. We can experience the Self only on transcending the vāsanās. Just as the sun is the destroyer of night, similarly, the Pure consciousness, the Atman and the vāsanās cannot remain at the one and the same time. The vāsanās end when the Atman is experienced.

From the devotees' stand-point, He is the One who fulfils all his desires. Or He who is the father of kāma, Pradyumna, which again is one of the names of Viṣṇu. Desire is the source from which endless series of other sources of sorrows flow into the human life. When a desire arises in the mind, only two things are possible. Either we fulfil the desire or we do not. In case we get our desires fulfilled, it is natural for the human mind to crave for more and thus he becomes restless due to greed. If, on the other hand, the desire is not fulfilled, anger rises and when anger increases, it brings about delusion of the mind and makes the victim see things in others, in himself and the situation he is in, which are not in fact there around him. In such a deluded one, Wisdom slips away and, naturally, therefore, his discriminative power cannot function, since he cannot judge the present situation with reference to any standard ideal that he had in the past. When the rational discriminative power fades away that man falls completely off the dignity of man and becomes worse than a brute. Gītā charters thus, a steady psychological fall in a spiritual being, and this entire chain of self-destruction springs forth from desire. A devotee, or a meditator, when he approaches this Great Reality, existing in the subjective Core of his own personality, he transcends all the realms of his desires and passions and, therefore, this Great Inner Self is indicated here as the "Destroyer of all Desires". He is the One who fulfils all desires in His devotees, and thus brings about a calm fullness of joy within.
names.simple_meaning: One who destroys all desires

names.short_meaning: One who fulfils all desires
names.commentary: One who fulfils all desires. The implications have been indicated in the analysis of the previous term. It can also mean as the Very Creator of the Lord of Love—kāma Deva. Even though desires spring forth from the realm of the Causal Body, constituted of the vāsanās without the thrilling touch of the Self, even vāsanās cannot express all by themselves. In that sense of the term, the very agitations of desire, erupt from His Grace. Hence, He is called the kāmakṛt.
names.simple_meaning: One who fulfils all desires

names.short_meaning: One who is of enchanting form
names.commentary:
One who is of enchanting form. Infinite Beauty is the very nature of the Self, and the Upaniṣads define the Self as Saantam — Sivam — Sundaram. The aestheticism in man craves for harmony and where we experience the greatest of harmony, there we detect the presence of beauty. In front of beauty, the entire personality of an intelligent man becomes calm and peaceful, hushed in silence, transported to ecstasy. These are moments when the meditator has transcended his Sheaths and is in union with the Pure Self. Naturally therefore, the Pure personality of an intelligent man becomes calm and peaceful. Self is indicated here as kāntaḥ—Divine Auspicious form of Absolute Beauty.

शान्तं शिवं सुन्दरम् ।
names.simple_meaning: One who is of enchanting form

names.short_meaning: One who is the beloved
names.commentary:
One who is the beloved. Not only He is the beloved of the devotees, but every activity of all living creatures is an attempt at courting and winning bliss and happiness. The Blissful Self is the goal of all creatures in life. Even insignificant unicellular organisms revolt against pain, and they too seek happiness. Man is no exception. The Infinite Bliss which is experienced only on transcending the body, mind and intellect, is that which is constantly demanded by every organism that breathes in this universe. In the ignorance of this All Satisfying Goal, the world suffers. That Lord is the beloved of all devotees, and in fact, He is also the beloved of even those who deny Him and run after the senseobjects. The theist seeks Him through devotion or meditation.

The atheist too seeks Him only in and through all his diligent pursuits of the sense-stimuli.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the beloved

names.short_meaning: One who supplies the desired objects; One who fulfils all desires
names.commentary: One who supplies the desired objects; One who fulfils all desires. To the devotee, the Lord, is the giver of all desired objects, and to a man of meditation, the Lord is that state-of-mind where all desires are fulfilled— in the sense that no more can any desire linger in his heart after the Experience—Divine.
names.simple_meaning: One who supplies the desired objects; One who fulfils all desires

names.short_meaning: He is the Lord, the Master, the Owner, the proprietor
names.commentary:
He is the Lord, the Master, the Owner, the proprietor. One who has all powers to do. (कर्त्), not to do (अकर्त्) and to do otherwise (अन्ययाकर्त्) is called the Great Lord.

गतिभर्ता प्रभुः साक्षी।
names.simple_meaning: He is the Lord, the Master, the Owner, the proprietor

names.short_meaning: One who is the creator of the divisions of aeons, described in our Purāṇas, as Yugas
names.commentary: One who is the creator of the divisions of aeons, described in our Purāṇas, as Yugas. These Yugas are four in number. kṛtam, Tretaa, Dvaapara and Kali. In short, He is the Lord of Time. By the term ādi, it must be understood to indicate all other divisions of Time as Centuries, Years, Months, Weeks, Days, Hours, Minutes and Seconds. He is not only the Lord of the Yugas, but He is the Light of Consciousness that illumines the duration of each experience and the very interval between every pair of subjective experiences.
names.simple_meaning: The creator of the ages

names.short_meaning: In the previous term the Lord is indicated as the Creator of the Yugas, and here we are told that He is also the Power behind the wheel of time that goes on changing and repeating itself, i.e
names.commentary: In the previous term the Lord is indicated as the Creator of the Yugas, and here we are told that He is also the Power behind the wheel of time that goes on changing and repeating itself, i.e. not only He is the Lord of Time, but He is the Mighty Administrator of the performances of Time, the very Law behind the constant flow of the flood of time.
names.simple_meaning: The one who turns the wheel of the ages

names.short_meaning: One whose delusory forms are endless and variegated
names.commentary: One whose delusory forms are endless and variegated. According to Purāṇas, for the sake of sustaining the world and maintaining its order and rhythm, the Lord had taken different forms, each of His manifestations well-suited for the times of His arrival. Thus, we have ten incarnations. Also, in that mighty manifestations of the Lord, as Kṛṣṇa and Rama, we find descriptions of how one and the same entity generated different attitudes and emotions in different types of people. In short, one who has realised the Self, can thereafter freely play through all his existing vāsanās and none of them can ever entangle him, because he has grown to be the master of his own vāsanās. māyā, otherwise called as Avidvaa, is constituted of the vāsanās in us, forming our Causal Body. One who has transcended this is the One who has realised the Infinite. Lord is therefore, one who is without māyā in Him. An individual entity, like us, is one who is under the tyrannies of māyā. The Lord is one who can wield māyā for His purpose without Himself becoming involved in it.
names.simple_meaning: One whose delusory forms are endless and variegated

names.short_meaning: This word can be dissolved as He who eats up everything
names.commentary:
This word can be dissolved as He who eats up everything. One who swallows up all perceptions, emotions and thoughts, created by the vāsanās, at the various levels of personality, due to our own individual vāsanās. At the time of samādhi when the limited ego is ended and the Supreme is experienced all the expressions of vāsanās are, as it were, swallowed by that Infinite Experience, and therefore, this Great Viṣṇu is called as the "Consumer of Everything."

Mahat Asanam Yasya Sah—(महत् अशनं यस्य सः).
names.simple_meaning: The great devourer who consumes all at dissolution

names.short_meaning: Through the sense-organs, the mind-and intellect at this moment, we are aware of the outer objects and our subjective emotions and thoughts
names.commentary: Through the sense-organs, the mind-and intellect at this moment, we are aware of the outer objects and our subjective emotions and thoughts. The ultimate Reality is neither the objects perceived by us, nor the instruments of our perception. He is the Subjective Core, the Eternal Essence, wherein, the perceived and the instruments of perceptions are all totally absent. This Subjective Reality must necessarily be, by Its very nature, not an object-of-perception, and hence, It is called as the Imperceptible, meaning: He is the very Perceiver in all perceptions.
names.simple_meaning: The one unseen by senses, mind, or intellect

names.short_meaning: He who has a form— clearly perceptible to the meditator in his meditation
names.commentary: He who has a form— clearly perceptible to the meditator in his meditation. The contradiction is so smotheringly apparent because of the very placing of the term. It is only just-now, in the above term, that we are told that the Lord is imperceptible (Adrisyah) and the very following term declares that He is perceptible. Here it means that though He is not perceptible with the physical instruments of perceptions, yet on transcending the equipments. the Yogi intimately comes to experience the entire Divine Glory of the Self. Though, ordinarily it is not easy to see Him, in the devotee's heart, the Lord comes to play vividly and drives the devotee mad in his ecstasy.
names.simple_meaning: He who has a form— clearly perceptible to the meditator in his meditation

names.short_meaning: One who vanquishes thousands
names.commentary: One who vanquishes thousands. In all the Purāṇas everywhere, it is found that the Incarnations manifest to destroy the diabolically fallen (rākṣasas) who approach the good in endless hoards to annihilaté them. One who conquers over these diabolical forces is the Lord Viṣṇu Subjectively the hosts of passions and lusts, greeds and jealousies which invade the inner bosom, and loot away the seeker's tranquillity and peace, are all ultimately vanguished by this Higher Consciousness and therefore, the Self is indicated as the one who is ever victorious over all the hoards of our lower impulses.
names.simple_meaning: One who vanquishes thousands

names.short_meaning: Ever-victorious
names.commentary:
Ever-victorious. The victory of the Lord is endless; in every Incarnation, He alone wins in the end. The victory over negative forces becomes complete when once the Higher Consciousness is experienced, and hence, the Self is indicated here as Ananta-jit.

Upaniṣad declares: “Satyameva Jayate Na Anritam” (सत्यमेव जयते नानृतम्)—“Truth alone wins, never falsehood.”
names.simple_meaning: Ever-victorious

names.short_meaning: This term can be interpreted in two ways
names.commentary:
This term can be interpreted in two ways. One who is invoked through the different types of Vedic rituals (yajñas), is iṣṭaḥ. Or, it can also mean: One who is loved by all. The Lord being the very centre of all love in everyone. The Brihadaranyakopanishad very clearly indicates this idea in almost unvarnished words: "The man loves his wife not because of the wife, but because of himself… etc."

All love springs from our personal love for the Infinite which is the Self in us.

Due to being the source of all love (Sarva-prema-aaspadatvaat).
names.simple_meaning: The beloved one

names.short_meaning: One who is the noblest and the most sacred
names.commentary: One who is the noblest and the most sacred. Viṣṇu, the Lord, dwells in the heart of everyone. He is the sole essence presiding over every physical, mental and intellectual activity in every living creature and, therefore, He is indicated by this term.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the noblest and the most sacred

names.short_meaning: To all spiritually minded good people and therefore sincere seekers, the Lord is the greatest beloved
names.commentary:
To all spiritually minded good people and therefore sincere seekers, the Lord is the greatest beloved in-as-much as, He represents the Goal and the Destination of all devoted seekers. In short, He is the Supreme Beloved for all spiritually inclined divine hearts.

He can also mean that the Lord is one who Himself is sincere and ardent lover and courtier of all devotees, sincerely and diligently seeking Him. There are commentators who indicate that the term can also mean: One who is being constantly invoked and held in adoration by all true devotees with their physical, mental and intellectual activities.

Sishtaanaam Ishtah (शिष्टानां इष्ट:)—The Beloved of the good people.

śiṣṭa Ishtah Yasya Sah—(शिष्ट इष्ट: यस्य सः).
names.simple_meaning: To all spiritually minded good people and therefore sincere seekers, the Lord is the greatest beloved

names.short_meaning: One who wears śikhaṇḍa, meaning "the peacock feather"
names.commentary: One who wears 'śikhaṇḍa' ( शिखण्ड ) meaning "the peacock feather". Lord Kṛṣṇa is described in Bhāgavata as having been adorned with the 'eye' of the peacock feather, especially in his early child-and-boy-hood.
names.simple_meaning: The wearer of the peacock plume

names.short_meaning: The term Nahanam means bondage; therefore, the term stands for "One who is familiar with bondages."
names.commentary: The term' Nahanam' (नहनम्) means bondage, therefore, the term stands for "One who is familiar with bondages." In Vedānta, the word 'Īśvaraḥ' (ईव्वर:) is the Supreme Consciousness conditioned by the total Causal — Body (māyā); at the same time, Īśvara is One who has the māyā under His control. It can also be understood as "One who binds all creatures of the world with the cord of māyā." Those who are students of the Purāṇas interpret this word as One whose glory was expressed in the spectacular magnificence in nahuṣaḥ, who gained the Office of Indra.
names.simple_meaning: The one who binds beings through māyā

names.short_meaning: There is a famous statement in the Hindu tradition from which we can gather that the Lord is of the nature of dharma
names.commentary:
There is a famous statement in the Hindu tradition from which we can gather that the Lord is of the nature of dharma. dharma means the essential Law of Being, that because of which an individual is an individual, without which the individual cannot exist, is the dharma of the individual. In this sense, the essential dharma of one is the Self. Thus, vṛṣaḥ is but another name to suggest that the Lord Viṣṇu is none other than the Self in us. It can also mean “One who showers the fulfilment of all desires in all devotees." Desires arise when the existing vāsanās get impatient and explode into manifestation. As the desire arises, the mind plans out and the body acts towards its fulfilment. All these activities are possible only when the vehicles are thrilled by the Self in us. Thus, ultimately, one who fulfils all desires is the Lord of our heart, the Atman.

“वृषो हि भगवान् धर्मः।”
names.simple_meaning: The embodiment of dharma

names.short_meaning: One who destroys anger in all sincere seekers
names.commentary: One who destroys anger (क्रोध) in all sincere seekers. We have already found earlier that anger manifests when fulfilment of a deep desire is obstructed. On realising the Lord, all desires end and, therefore, there cannot be any anger on any occasion. Also, anger can come only when we recognise the world of plurality around us. For one who is experiencing the Self, there is nothing but the One Self everywhere and, therefore, there is no occasion to entertain this emotion of anger.
names.simple_meaning: One who destroys anger in all sincere seekers

names.short_meaning: One who generates in a sincere and serious seeker anger against the lower tendencies when they manifest
names.commentary: One who generates in a sincere and serious seeker anger against the lower tendencies when they manifest—“Krodha-krit” (क्रोधकृत्). Also He is the very creative impulse 'kartā' (कर्ता) behind the lower tendencies; because all things come out from Him alone. Some commentators consider this term as two different words, but the majority consider them as an integrated one.
names.simple_meaning: One who generates in a sincere and serious seeker anger against the lower tendencies when they manifest

names.short_meaning: One who has number of hands; whose hands are everywhere doing all activities in the universe
names.commentary: One who has number of hands; whose hands are everywhere doing all activities in the universe. The life in the bosom as long as it exists, so long alone the hands and the legs function. The hands can lift and do its job only when it is in contact with life. Life expressing through the hand is its function. All hands that are doing variegated activities all over the world are all His hands in-as-much as, where He is not, that lifeless hand can perform no more any activity. Since He is thus the dynamic One Principle that functions through all hands at work. He is called a viśvabāhuḥ (विश्वबाहु:)
names.simple_meaning: One who has number of hands; whose hands are everywhere doing all activities in the universe

names.short_meaning: One who is the Substratum and support for the Earth
names.commentary: One who is the Substratum and support for the Earth (मही). The Lord is the very material cause for the universe and as such, He supports the world—just as cotton supports the cloth, mud supports the pot, gold supports the ornament. Since the term mahī (मही) also means "the adorations sent up by the devotees," it can also mean 'One who receives all the worship of devoted hearts.'
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Substratum and support for the Earth

names.short_meaning: One who has not got any modifications—such as birth, growth, decay, disease, death etc
names.commentary:
One who has not got any modifications (Chyutam) (च्यत्) -- such as birth, growth, decay, disease, death etc. The Eternal and Immutable cannot have any change and the Self being the Eternal, it cannot have any of the changes that are natural to all mortal and finite things.

Upaniṣads themselves thunder this Truth-"Eternal, Auspicious and Changeless."

“Saasvatam Sivam Achyutam” — (शाश्वतं शिवम् अच्युतम्).
names.simple_meaning: One who has not got any modifications—such as birth, growth, decay, disease, death etc

names.short_meaning: One who exists pervading all; spreading Himself everywhere
names.commentary: One who exists pervading all; spreading Himself everywhere. It can also mean "One whose glory, as described in the Upaniṣads, has spread round the world everywhere."
names.simple_meaning: One who exists pervading all; spreading Himself everywhere

names.short_meaning: All manifested expressions of life are called as the prāṇa
names.commentary: All manifested expressions of life are called as the prāṇa. He is the prāṇa in all living creatures; meaning, it is His manifestations that we recognise as the endless activities in all living creatures in this dynamic world. Also it can mean that "He is the One who in the form of vital-air, sustains life in all creatures."
names.simple_meaning: The life manifest in every living being

names.short_meaning: One who gives strength (prāṇa) to everywhere
names.commentary: One who gives strength (prāṇa) to everywhere. The root 'da' has a meaning of destruction and, therefore, the term comprehends also the power of destruction everywhere. According to the Purāṇas, therefore, He is the One who gives the strength and glory for Devas, and again, He is the One who supplies special strength to them to win over the brutal forces of the diabolically wicked, the Asuras. Subjectively, it is the Self that supplies the mental strength for cultivating the higher values of life, and it is the same Source Divine that floods the seekers' heart with the courage to annihilate the lower impulses that come to destroy his peace and tranquillity within.
names.simple_meaning: One who gives strength (prāṇa) to everywhere

names.short_meaning: The Brother of Indra
names.commentary: The Brother of Indra. This name has been acquired by Lord Viṣṇu because of His incarnation as the Adorable Dwarf—(Vāmana). At that time, the Lord had to take birth in the womb of Aditi and manifest as the younger brother of Indra. In the subjective science of Vedānta, the king of the gods (Indra) is the Lord of the sense organs and so he is the Mind. The spiritual urge that dawns in us as a younger brother of the Mind, ultimately comes to measure away and win over the three worlds of waking, dream and deep-sleep, and thus comes to conquer over the entire kingdom of Indra in more sense than one.
names.simple_meaning: The Brother of Indra

names.short_meaning: Treasure of waters, meaning the ocean
names.commentary:
Treasure of waters, meaning the ocean. The very glory and might of the oceans are all but a reflection of Śrī Nārāyaṇa's own glory divine. In the Gītā, Bhagavān Himself says, "among the collections of waters, I am the Ocean."

“सरसामस्मि सागरः।”
names.simple_meaning: The ocean, treasury of the waters

names.short_meaning: The Substratum for the entire universe
names.commentary:
The Substratum for the entire universe. The delusory mis-conceptions can be projected only upon something that is real and this permanent 'post' is called the 'Substratum' for the delusory 'Ghost'-Vision.

“मत्स्थानि सर्वभूतानि।”
names.simple_meaning: The Substratum for the entire universe

names.short_meaning: One who has no pramāda, meaning, One who never commits a mistake in judgement
names.commentary:
One who has no pramāda, meaning, 'One who never commits a mistake in judgement." The Lord is the Law behind all happenings in the universe. The results of the actions are always strictly according to the quality of the actions. In administering this Law of Karma, One who never makes any mistake is apramattaḥ. We are full of pramāda—we make the mistake of mis-understanding ourselves to be the matter equipment around us and due to this pramāda, we project in ourselves the false concept of an Ego.

The Supreme is ever the Pure Consciousness and, therefore, He is without such wrong self-judgement.
names.simple_meaning: The unerring one who is never careless

names.short_meaning: Everything in the world depends upon something else to serve as its cause
names.commentary: Everything in the world depends upon something else to serve as its cause. Since all things that we perceive and experience in the world are all effects, they have their own causes, and the effects must necessarily depend upon the cause for their very existence. The Supreme Lord is the One uncaused Cause with reference to whom everything is only an effect. Since He is thus the ultimate Cause, He is not depending upon anything other than Himself. This self-established Reality is indicated by the term pratiṣṭhitaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: Everything in the world depends upon something else to serve as its cause

names.short_meaning: This is one of the names of the youngest son of Lord Siva, Subrahmanya, who is described in the Purāṇa as Commander-in — Chief of the righteous army
names.commentary: This is one of the names of the youngest son of Lord Siva, Subrahmanya, who is described in the Purāṇa as Commander-in — Chief of the righteous army. Therefore, Skanda means "the Lord, whose glory is expressed, through Subrahmanya". In order to realise the Self, it is a prerequisite condition that the different personality layers in the seeker should be completely integrated.
names.simple_meaning: Skanda, commander of the righteous host

names.short_meaning: "One who upholds the withering righteousness."
names.commentary: "One who upholds the withering righteousness." Or, "One who fathered Lord Subrahmanya", meaning One who is in the form of Paramesvara.
names.simple_meaning: "One who upholds the withering righteousness."

names.short_meaning: One who carries the Lord
names.commentary: One who carries the Lord. The Lord is the One who carries the responsibilities of creation, sustenance and annihilation of the entire world of plurality. One who carries out these functions systematically without any hitch round millenniums is Śrī Nārāyaṇa and He is therefore dhuryaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: One who carries the Lord

names.short_meaning: One who blesses all true devotees and fulfils their request for boons
names.commentary: One who blesses all true devotees and fulfils their request for boons. It can also mean "One who gives the best (Varam) in life to those who seek Him with perfect detachment and sharpened discrimination.
names.simple_meaning: One who blesses all true devotees and fulfils their request for boons

names.short_meaning: "The One who controls, regulates and moves the great winds"
names.commentary:
"The One who controls, regulates and moves the great winds". In the Sanskrit literature, the movement of air in the atmosphere has been classified under seven types and they are called the 'Sapta Marutah' (सप्त महतः).

In short, the inconceivable might and power of the winds and their life-sustaining abilities are all lent out to the air by His own munificence and, therefore, He is called as Vaavuvaahanah.

Avahana (अवहन), Pravahana (प्रवहन्), Vivahana (विवहन) Paramavahana (परमवहन), Udvahana (उद्वहन), Samvahana (संवहन) and Parivahana (परिवहन).
names.simple_meaning: "The One who controls, regulates and moves the great winds"

names.short_meaning: One who is at once both Vāsu and Deva
names.commentary:
"One who is at once both Vāsu (वास्) and Deva (देव). Vāsu means "One who dwells in the physical equipments of all living creatures as its indweller (jīva-जीव); Deva means "One who revels or One who illumines". Thus, Vaasudevah means "One who lives in the physical equipment as though conditioned by them, and yet, who is the Vital Consciousness in the light of which every experience is illumined. The Lord is the One who dwells in all things of the universe and He is at once the Supporter of the entire world. Also, directly, it can be taken to mean, One who is born as the Son of Śrī Vasudeva in the Jail of Kamsa, the Blue — Boy of Brindaavana. He is called Vāsu as He veils Himself with His own Masyaa; Deva means "He who sports, wishes to conquer, conducts, shines, creates and moves". In the Udyoga Parva of Mahābhārata, we read, "Like the Sun with his rays I am covering (Deva) in all beings and hence, I am called Vāsudeva".

Vishnupurana says, "As He resides everywhere in and through all things, He is termed Vaasudevah." All beings remain in the Supreme, and He in all being and hence, the Omnipresent is called the Vāsudeva.

“वसनात् सर्वभूतानां वस्त्वादेवयोनिषु। वासुदेवस्ततो ज्ञेयो योगिभिस्तत्त्वदर्शिभिः।”
names.simple_meaning: One who is at once both Vāsu and Deva

names.short_meaning: Possessed of endless rays, meaning "One who illumines the world with the rays of the Sun and the Moon."
names.commentary:
Possessed of endless rays, meaning "One who illumines the world with the rays of the Sun and the Moon." Mahābhārata says, "He whose great rays are in the Sun, Moon and others and He who illumines the universe through them is called the Possessor of great rays.

Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva 70-4.
names.simple_meaning: The vast light whose rays illumine sun and moon

names.short_meaning: "One who is the Primary source for everything," meaning the Lord
names.commentary: "One who is the Primary source for everything," meaning the Lord. He is the First Cause, and hence the first Deity.
names.simple_meaning: The first of the gods

names.short_meaning: "The destroyer of the cities."
names.commentary:
"The destroyer of the cities." City is the well-equipped field for gathering endless experiences. The three cities through which we generally move about gathering our experiences in this world are the waking, dream and deep-sleep. On transcending the Gross, Subtle and Causal Bodies, one experiences the Self, and at such a moment these three cities are burned down or pillaged or blasted. The same ideal is explained in the Shiva-purana also; accordingly, we can say that He is One who as Mahesvara, performed the destruction of the three cities.

See Tripurasaṃhāra.
names.simple_meaning: "The destroyer of the cities."

names.short_meaning: "One who has no sorrows."
names.commentary: "One who has no sorrows." Sorrow is a condition experienced when the mind is agitated and extremely disturbed. The agitations of the mind come from desires, greed, etc. Therefore, the term aśokaḥ indicates, "One who has none of these negative tendencies that create in their turn more and more mental disturbances". This is a true appellation, because, the Lord, as the Self, transcends the realm of the thought-disturbances constituted by the mind-intellect-equipment.
names.simple_meaning: "One who has no sorrows."

names.short_meaning: “One who enables others to cross.”
names.commentary:
“One who enables others to cross.” The ego suffering the constant agitations of the equipments is saved by the Self. The ego (jeeva), when it discovers its identity with the Self, automatically moves away from the sorrows of the vehicles. In short, as Vishnubhaagavata says, "Who is there other than You that can save us from the wheel of births and deaths."

“Who is there other than You that can save us from the wheel of births and deaths?” — Viṣṇubhāgavata 7-9-6.
names.simple_meaning: “One who enables others to cross.”

names.short_meaning: One who saves is called tāraḥ
names.commentary:
"One who saves is called tāraḥ. One who saves from the fear of re-birth and also One who is a constant protector of the devotees and, therefore, the devotees themselves call Him as the Saviour (tāraḥ).

These three terms indicate how Viṣṇu is the Absolute Protector of His devotees. He saves us from the afflictions (Asoka) of the body and so Subjective-sorrows (Adhyaatma). He enables us to cross the ocean of saṃsāra (Taaranah) and, therefore, He saves us from all Cosmic pains (Adhibhootah).

He saves us from the elements (tāraḥ), and so, He is the Saviour from all sorrows of birth and death; this indicates all trans — Cosmic tragedies (Aadhidaivika), meaning that Nārāyaṇa can save us from all sorrows contributed by the hand-of — God.

"तारयति इति तारः।"
names.simple_meaning: The savior from the fear of rebirth

names.short_meaning: "The Valiant"
names.commentary: "The Valiant". All sources of strength and courage spring from the Life in us and, therefore, the Lord of the universe is called here as the Valiant—capable of crushing all unrighteous forces, however well-trenched they may be in the world.
names.simple_meaning: "The Valiant"

names.short_meaning: Soorasena is the father of Vasudeva, and we have already found that Vasudeva's son is Vāsudeva
names.commentary:
Soorasena is the father of Vasudeva, and we have already found that Vasudeva's son is Vāsudeva (वासुदेव). Therefore, the Lord had taken His incarnation in the family of Soora (जूर) and so He is termed as Saurih.

“शूरस्य गोत्रापत्यं पुमान् शौरिः।”
names.simple_meaning: Kṛṣṇa, descendant of Śūrasena

names.short_meaning: The Lord of the people (jana)
names.commentary:
The Lord of the people (jana). Those who are born are called Jana (जन). Therefore, the term indicates that He is the Lord of all creatures born in the universe

“जननधर्मवान् जनः।”.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of the people (jana)

names.short_meaning: “A hearty well-wisher, or friend of everyone”
names.commentary: “A hearty well-wisher, or friend of everyone”. Since the Lord is the Essential Life in everyone, He is the friend and ally of every individual inasmuch as, nobody spends his life except in concurrence with his own subjective intentions and purposes. Thus, the Lord is a friend fulfilling the intentions of a murderer, and He is again the friend of another helping Him to serve the mankind, if thatbe his intention. Thus, He is a friend and a devoted ally to everyone since He is the mighty power behind all vāsanās expressing through all creatures.
names.simple_meaning: “A hearty well-wisher, or friend of everyone”

names.short_meaning: Sata means "hundred", and here it is used as "innumerable"
names.commentary: Sata means "hundred", and here it is used as "innumerable". Thus the term 'śatāvartaḥ' means "One who takes infinite varieties of forms". All forms in the universe are but His own, inasmuch as, His manifestation is the universe. Again, He takes innumerable incarnations in order to maintain the law of the cosmos and also the law of evolution. It can also mean "One who, as prāṇa, moves in the innumerable Naadees in the body".
names.simple_meaning: The one of innumerable manifestations

names.short_meaning: "One who has the lotus in his hand"
names.commentary:
"One who has the lotus in his hand". The lotus is the national flower in Bharat as it symbolises in our culture, the Goal of our Spiritual life. It is to offer this "Knowledge", that the Lord blows His conch, and if people are not listening to this silent call of the Higher from within.

He uses His gadā (mace) to give merciful knocks in life. Still, if an individual or a generation is not listening to His kindly warnings, He has the Discus (Chakra) in His hand. He annihilates totally the existing forms and re-creates.
names.simple_meaning: "One who has the lotus in his hand"

names.short_meaning: “One whose eyes are as beautiful as the Lotus."
names.commentary: “One whose eyes are as beautiful as the Lotus." In short, 'lotus-eyed.'
names.simple_meaning: “One whose eyes are as beautiful as the Lotus."

names.short_meaning: "One who has the lotus in his navel"
names.commentary:
"One who has the lotus in his navel". This is not to be taken literally. Navel (Naabhi) is the psychic centre where all un-manifest thoughts first spring forth into our recognition (Pasyantee). The seedless state of all thoughts is called in the Yoga śāstra, as parā. It therefore means "one in whose bosom lies, in potential, all the possibilities of the universe of expression." It can also mean "One who manifests Himself in the lotus of the heart of his devotee.

Some translate as "He who is seated in the pericarp of the lotus."

Parā (परा), Paśyantī (पश्यन्ती), Madhyamā (मध्यमा), and Vaikharī (वैखरी) are the stages in which an unmanifest thought with the Self emerges slowly to full expression as words in the outer world.
names.simple_meaning: "One who has the lotus in his navel"

names.short_meaning: “One who has eyes as beautiful as the lotus”
names.commentary: “One who has eyes as beautiful as the lotus”. The lotus opens at sun-rise and closes in the night. The Lord opens His beauty and grace in the presence of the devotees and the flood of His grace, as it were, dries up in the presence of the dark sensuality of the ignorant.
names.simple_meaning: “One who has eyes as beautiful as the lotus”

names.short_meaning: "One who is being meditated upon in the centre of the lotus-of-the-heart."
names.commentary: "One who is being meditated upon in the centre of the lotus-of-the-heart."
names.simple_meaning: "One who is being meditated upon in the centre of the lotus-of-the-heart."

names.short_meaning: "One who sustains or nourishes all bodies"
names.commentary: "One who sustains or nourishes all bodies". Or, it can mean "One who is the form of food and prāṇa, becomes the very cause for the sustenance of the body". It is a fact very well known that even though a body can continue existing without visibly decaying for 50 years, once Life has ebbed away, the deadbody cannot maintain its form and it does not exist even for 48 hours intact. He who while presiding over the body nourishes and maintains it, and in whose absence the body decays and perishes, He is the One who is the Sustainer of the body (Dehabhrit).
names.simple_meaning: "One who sustains or nourishes all bodies"

names.short_meaning: “One who has great riddhi, meaning, prosperity and power”
names.commentary: “One who has great riddhi, meaning, prosperity and power”. These two—prosperity and power—together is called glory (Aisvarva). Thus the term means, "One who has by His very nature glory ever with Him."
names.simple_meaning: The one of magnificent prosperity and power

names.short_meaning: “One who has expanded Himself to be the universe."
names.commentary: “One who has expanded Himself to be the universe." In short, "One who has manifested Himself as the entire world of plurality, constituted of the finite things of the Cosmos."
names.simple_meaning: “One who has expanded Himself to be the universe."

names.short_meaning: "The ancient Self."
names.commentary: "The ancient Self." In the Self there is no concept of Time, It being beyond the intellect. But here, by the term vṛddhātmā, it only means that He was the Self before all creation. It is only after the creation of Time that we are capable of saying and indicating Him as the Self of the various living creatures. He is the first Sclf, meaning: He is the Self whose manifestations are the world of plurality.
names.simple_meaning: "The ancient Self."

names.short_meaning: "The Great-eyed", meaning
names.commentary: "The Great-eyed", meaning: the eyes that can see not only the world-of-objects, but also X-ray through them and see all that are happening deep within the bosom of all creatures. He is the "Great Eye" seeing all, at all times, as He is the Consciousness that illumines everything at all times, in all bosoms.
names.simple_meaning: The great-eyed one

names.short_meaning: One who has the eagle (Garuda) as his insignia on his flag
names.commentary: "One who has the eagle (Garuda) as his insignia on his flag. The eagle is considered as the vehicle of the Lord; most probably because this bird ever soars high and from above sees even the minutest speck of dirt in the world. The eagle after spying the carrion, swoops down and takes it away, thus purifying the atmosphere. Similarly, the Lord never allows any negative thought to come into the heart of His devotees, and hence, the eagle is considered as His vehicle.
names.simple_meaning: One who has the eagle (Garuda) as his insignia on his flag

names.short_meaning: "Incomparable."
names.commentary:
"Incomparable." For him whose name is the glory of the universe, there is no licence." Again, Bhāgavata Gītā says, "For Thy equal exists not, where is another superior to Thee in the three worlds?" In short, there is nothing like Him, since He does not fall under the categories of the things perceived by the body or the emotions felt by the mind or the thoughts entertained by the intellect: nothing that we know of can be comparable with Him.

Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 4-19.

“न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कृतोऽन्यो लोकत्रयेऽप्यप्रतिमप्रभावः।”
names.simple_meaning: "Incomparable."

names.short_meaning: “One who dwells and shines forth through the bodies.”
names.commentary:
“One who dwells and shines forth through the bodies.” Bodies are called Sara because they are perishable. The life that presides over the perishable body, whose glory is the individuality, is the Self, the Lord. It can also mean, "Lord, who is of the nature of Paramesvara," for, Lord Siva had once taken the incarnation of Sarabha (शर्भ), a creature with eight legs, capable of killing even the lions.

“जीर्यमाणात् शरः” — (Jīryamāṇāt śaraḥ).
names.simple_meaning: “One who dwells and shines forth through the bodies.”

names.short_meaning: "The All-inspiring, the Terrible," meaning
names.commentary:
"The All-inspiring, the Terrible," meaning: One who is a mighty and terrible phenomenon to those who are cruel and sensuous in the world. To the bad, the Lord is always a frightful power of vengeance, to follow them relentlessly as their doom.

Some commentators, due to the position of this word in the stanza, read it as a-bheemah, meaning thereby, "He who is the shelter" to those who are good.
names.simple_meaning: The formidable and awe-inspiring one

names.short_meaning: “Knower of all six systems of philosophy," or it can mean "One who knows the exact time (samaya) for creation, preservation and destruction."
names.commentary:
“Knower of all six systems of philosophy," or it can mean "One who knows the exact time (samaya) for creation, preservation and destruction." Or, it can also mean "One whose worship (yajña) is nothing more than keeping an equal vision of the mind by the devotee." The great devotee Prahalada says, "To be equal in all conditions, is the worship of Achyuta."

“समत्वमाराधनमच्युतस्य।” — Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1-17-90.
names.simple_meaning: The knower of every philosophy and the right time for every act

names.short_meaning: "The receiver of all oblation."
names.commentary:
