"The receiver of all oblation." He is the Lord of all yajñas and as such, He is the One to whom the devotee offers his oblations, and He is the One who receives them in all dedicated activities. Bhāgavata Gītā says, "I am indeed the enjoyer and also the Lord of all sacrifices." The Lord is called Havis as He is worshipped through oblation.

Some commentators recognise in this term two different names of the Lord: 'Havih' and 'Harih'. In this case, the former term, 'Havih' means "He who is invoked by everyone who performs the yajñas." The term Harih means "One who loots away all vāsanās (pāpa)," and consequently, "One who wipes away all expressions of vāsanās."

“अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च।” — Gītā IX-24.
names.simple_meaning: "The receiver of all oblation."

names.short_meaning: “Known through all methods of proofs," meaning "He is the One Self that is ultimately proved by all scientific investiga-tions and philosophical enquiries."
names.commentary:
“Known through all methods of proofs," meaning "He is the One Self that is ultimately proved by all scientific investigations and philosophical enquiries." Whether it be through dualistic (dvaita) or through non-dualistic (advaita) philosophy, the Ultimate Truth experienced by the realised seeker.

is this Great Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: The one indicated by every valid mark and method of knowledge

names.short_meaning: The consort of Lakṣmī
names.commentary: ‘‘The consort of Lakṣmī." He is the Spirit (puruṣa) that thrills the entire world-of-matter (Prakriti). Matter thrilled with the spirit is the dynamic world that we see around. Thus, the manifested Lord is ever wedded to Lakṣmī. Lakṣmī also means Effulgent, and therefore, the Lord who is Ever-effulgent, meaning the Pure Consciousness, that illumines everything, is indeed lakṣmīvān
names.simple_meaning: The consort of Lakṣmī

names.short_meaning: "Ever — Victorious."
names.commentary: "Ever — Victorious." In the Purāṇas, we find the Lord ultimately wins in His battle with the unrighteous forces. He is the destroyer of all pains in the individuality of the devotees. Samiti as a word, has got the meaning—"Battle".
names.simple_meaning: "Ever — Victorious."

names.short_meaning: kṣaraḥ means "decaying," "that which is perishing", and so vikṣaraḥ means "Imperishable"
names.commentary: kṣaraḥ means "decaying," "that which is perishing", and so vikṣaraḥ means "Imperishable". Those who are meditating upon the Lord in His un-manifested State of Glory, this term is very often used. All material things are conditioned by time and all objects are, therefore, perishable. The Lord, the Self, is the Subject and is, therefore, ever Unchanging and always Imperishable.
names.simple_meaning: The imperishable one

names.short_meaning: The term 'Rohita' means fish, and this name has come to indicate Lord Viṣṇu because of His first incarnation as the Fish
names.commentary: The term 'Rohita' means fish, and this name has come to indicate Lord Viṣṇu because of His first incarnation as the Fish. When the entire world was submerged in the waters of the deluge, the only living creatures that were available at that time could only be fishes. Lord could incarnate at that time only in the form of the Fish. Therefore, here the term means "One who had manifested to serve the living creatures as the Fish among the fishes."
names.simple_meaning: The red-hued Fish incarnation

names.short_meaning: "The Path."
names.commentary: "The Path." In order to realise the Highest which is the Nameless and Formless, human mind will have to first hold on to a divine form, and that is Lord Viṣṇu. He is the Way and the Goal. In short, "He is the One whom seekers of the Highest meditate upon in order to reach the Supreme."
names.simple_meaning: "The Path."

names.short_meaning: "The Cause"
names.commentary: "The Cause". One who is the cause for the whole universe. He is at once the material-cause (Upa adaana kāraṇa), the instrumental-cause (Nimitta kāraṇa) and He who alone is also the efficient-cause in the creation of this universe. Hence, He is called The Cause.
names.simple_meaning: "The Cause"

names.short_meaning: This term has come to indicate the Lord because, He is One who is known through a mind which is purified (Udara) by means of self-control (dama) and such other qualities
names.commentary:
This term has come to indicate the Lord because, He is One who is known through a mind which is purified (Udara) by means of self-control (dama) and such other qualities. According to Mahābhārata, "We call Him as Daamodara as He is known by means of Dama." Brahmapurana re-capitulates the incident in the early childhood of the Lord when He was tied with a cord (daama) round His waste (udara). This term can also mean "One in whose bosom rests the whole universe."

“दमात् दामोदरं विदुः।”

“दमानि लोकनामानि तानि यस्य उदरान्तरे।” — Vyāsa.
names.simple_meaning: The one known through self-control and a purified mind

names.short_meaning: "All enduring"
names.commentary: "All enduring". The Lord is One who has patience at everything, and is One who readily forgives all the defaults of His sincere devotees.
names.simple_meaning: "All enduring"

names.short_meaning: "The Supporter or the Bearer of the Earth"
names.commentary: "The Supporter or the Bearer of the Earth". Since He is the very essence in the universe as its material-cause, He is the One who supports all forms in the universe. The Lord supports the world, just as gold 'supports' the ornaments, the cotton 'supports' the cloth, the ocean 'supports' the waves.
names.simple_meaning: "The Supporter or the Bearer of the Earth"

names.short_meaning: He who has extreme beauty in all His limbs, or He who is ever fortunate, or He who gets the greatest share (bhāga) in every yajña
names.commentary: He who has extreme beauty in all His limbs, or He who is ever fortunate, or He who gets the greatest share (bhāga) in every yajña.
names.simple_meaning: He who has extreme beauty in all His limbs, or He who is ever fortunate, or He who gets the greatest share (bhāga) in every yajña

names.short_meaning: "He who is swift"; One who is the fastest in reaching the devotee the moment his loving heart remembers Him
names.commentary:
"He who is swift"; One who is the fastest in reaching the devotee the moment his loving heart remembers Him. By import it means that He is All-pervading, therefore, He is the fastest, inasmuch as "nothing can ever overtake Him." In the Īśāvāsyopaniṣad He is indicated as swifter than the mind—(Manasojaveeyah).

“नैनत् देवाः आप्नवन् पूर्वमर्षत्।” — Īśa 4.
names.simple_meaning: "He who is swift"; One who is the fastest in reaching the devotee the moment his loving heart remembers Him

names.short_meaning: "Of endless appetite."
names.commentary: "Of endless appetite." This should not be taken literally, but it only means that the entire world of plurality projected by the mind, merges back when the mind is transcended at the time of the experience of the Self. Just as we can say that the waker swallows the dreamer, the Higher Consciousness, with an infinite appetite, as it were, swallows the Infinite Cosmos; hence figuratively, He is considered as 'the Great Consumer' of the whole world of plurality during involution (Pralaya).
names.simple_meaning: "Of endless appetite."

names.short_meaning: "The Originator"
names.commentary: "The Originator". The Lord is the material-cause from which the entire universe arises and, therefore, He is the origin for the Cosmos, or it can mean to indicate, "One who is again and again born as the endless jivas under the urge of their individual vāsanās".
names.simple_meaning: "The Originator"

names.short_meaning: "The Agitator"
names.commentary: "The Agitator". If the Self were not in the equipments, the equipments will not get agitated -will not pursue their functions. The Atman, the Pure Consciousness is that which thrills and agitates both the matter (Prakriti) and energy (puruṣa), and causes the manifestation of the living entities (jivas), who, with their actions, constitute the dynamic aspect of the world. If the Self is not there, there can be no movement or expression of life; everything would have remained completely inert and insentient. He is the Lord who thrills the world and makes it so beautifully palpitating with life. Hence, He is called as the Agitator (kṣobhaṇaḥ).
names.simple_meaning: "The Agitator"

names.short_meaning: One who revels is Deva
names.commentary:
"One who revels is Deva. This term 'Deevyati' (दीव्यित) in Sanskrit also means 'to conquer', 'to shine' and 'to praise'. Therefore, Lord Viṣṇu is rightly called as devaḥ because He sports through His play—the great Creation — Sustenance — Destruction-play. He functions in all Beings as He shines as the Universal Consciousness; and He is praised by all the devotees. Svetasvatura Upaniṣad indicates "there is only one Deva".

दीव्यति इति देवः (Dīvyati iti Devaḥ).
names.simple_meaning: One who revels is Deva

names.short_meaning: "Containing all glories within: One in whom are all glories (Aisvarya)"
names.commentary: "Containing all glories within: One in whom are all glories (Aisvarya)". The glory of the Lord is the universe and this universe resides in Him, and therefore, all powers and glories that are manifested in the universe are also ever in Him.
names.simple_meaning: "Containing all glories within: One in whom are all glories (Aisvarya)"

names.short_meaning: The Supreme (Parama) Lord (Īśvara)
names.commentary:
The Supreme (Parama) Lord (Īśvara). The fanatics generally interpret the word to mean as "the only Lord", in the sense that all other concepts of God are wrong. The large-hearted, tolerant ṛṣis of old, could have never meant such a meaning: It could only mean "that He is the Supreme Consciousness whose expressions are all the deities". The term Īśvara indicates both might and glory.

Therefore, Paramesvara means "One who is Omnipotent and All-glorious."
names.simple_meaning: The Supreme (Parama) Lord (Īśvara)

names.short_meaning: "The Instrument."
names.commentary:
"The Instrument." That which is most useful in fulfilling any piece of work is called the tool or the instrument. For the creation of the world He is the instrumental-cause (Nimitta kāraṇa).

The grammarians (Vaiyākaraṇas) define it as “साधनतमं करणम्” (Sādhanatamaṃ karaṇam).
names.simple_meaning: "The Instrument."

names.short_meaning: "The Cause."
names.commentary: "The Cause." By the earlier term it was indicated that He is the instrumental-cause (Nimitta kāraṇa) for the whole universe. Here now, by this term, it is indicated that He is the very material-cause (Upaadaana kāraṇa) of the universe. Since the term directly means only "the cause", it can mean not only the material cause, but also it can suggest the instrumental-cause. In the former case it would mean "He from whom the whole universe arises", and in the latter sense, the term is interpreted by some commentators as "He who causes the universe to emerge out".
names.simple_meaning: "The Cause."

names.short_meaning: "The Doer"
names.commentary:
"The Doer". He is the One in whose presence alone all activities are possible, and hence by a transferred epithet, though the doings all belong to the equipments, the Self is called as the "Doer". One who can freely perform all the functions of creation, sustenance and destruction, is the "Doer".

Pāṇini says: “स्वतन्त्रः कर्ता।”
names.simple_meaning: "The Doer"

names.short_meaning: “One who creates the infinite varieties that constitute the universe."
names.commentary: “One who creates the infinite varieties that constitute the universe." It can also mean, "One who has created out of Himself, the endless self-manifestations of incarnations.”
names.simple_meaning: “One who creates the infinite varieties that constitute the universe."

names.short_meaning: “The Un-knowable”
names.commentary: “The Un-knowable”. One who cannot be comprehended by any of the known instruments of knowledge; One who is not an object of perception, but is the very subject and the perceiver in all sense-organs.
names.simple_meaning: “The Un-knowable”

names.short_meaning: "One who dwells in the cave of the heart" meaning "One who is the very core of every living creature."
names.commentary:
"One who dwells in the cave of the heart" meaning "One who is the very core of every living creature." He is concealed within the equipments and hence, He is described in our Scriptures as "One who dwells in the cave of the heart". The Smriti describes Him as "This Lord, the Great puruṣa, the Witness who dwells in the cave most secretively." Muṇḍakopaniṣad describes the Self as 'Nihitam Guhaayaam'. Again, the Lord Himself says, "I am not readily perceivable by all as I am veiled by my own māyā".

“गूढो गुहाशयः साक्षी महापुरुष ईश्वरः।” — Viṣṇu Bhāgavata 10-37-11.

“नाहं प्रकाशः सर्वस्य योगमायासमावृतः।” — Gītā.
names.simple_meaning: The one hidden in the cave of the heart

names.short_meaning: "Resolute."
names.commentary:
"Resolute." Being of the nature of Pure Wisdom, there is no vacillation in Him; all irresolution is at the level of the doubting mind and the unprepared intellect. The term “Vyavasaaya” also means “Yoga.”

In this sense, the term is used in the Gītā, “The intellect of one who is practising Yoga is single-pointed without vacillation.” Again, in the same chapter criticising those who are running after enjoyment and power, Kṛṣṇa says, “Those who are revelling in sensuality and consequently disturbing the poise of their intellect, cannot have a steady mind and consistent pursuit of Yoga.” To work persistently until the Goal is reached is resolution. “To steadily apply ourselves in continuously withdrawing ourselves from our identifications with the not — Self, until we come to apprehend and experience the Self”, is Yoga. Hence, commentators interpret “Vyavasaaya” as “Yoga.”

“व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिरेकेह कुरुनन्दन।” — Gītā II-41.

“भोगैश्वर्यप्रसक्तानां तयापहृतचेतसाम्। व्यवसायात्मिका बुद्धिः समाधौ न विधीयते॥” — Gītā II-44.
names.simple_meaning: "Resolute."

names.short_meaning: "The Basis or the Substratum."
names.commentary: "The Basis or the Substratum." The one who is the very Substratum for the entire pluralistic world; the One who orders the laws of the cosmos and administers those laws.
names.simple_meaning: "The Basis or the Substratum."

names.short_meaning: "The Ultimate Authority, State or Goal."
names.commentary: "The Ultimate Authority, State or Goal." He who absorbs unto Himself all the multiplicities of names and forms during the time of deluge (प्रलय:). The One Source into which all perceptions, emotions and thoughts retire and merge at the time of deep-sleep. In short, it means "the One who integrates the plurality and absorbs it all unto Himself when the projections are ended at that time of transcendence."
names.simple_meaning: "The Ultimate Authority, State or Goal."

names.short_meaning: "One who confers the right abode."
names.commentary:
"One who confers the right abode." Each living organism, "according to his actions and thoughts" gathers to himself vāsanās and according to the vāsanās, each individual takes his birth. Thus, the One who gives (dada) the appropriate abode (sthāna) to each individual (jeeva) is called sthānadaḥ. In short, the Lord is the distributor of the fruits-of-actions.

“यथाकर्म यथाश्रुतम्।” — Kaṭhopaniṣad II-V-7.

“कर्मफलदाता ईश्वरो नारायणः।”
names.simple_meaning: "One who confers the right abode."

names.short_meaning: "The stable; the Firm."
names.commentary:
“The stable; the Firm.” That which remains “the Changeless in the midst of changes”, “that which is Imperishable in the midst of all perishing”. The body, the mind and the intellect and the worlds interpreted by them are all variables and changeable. The Consciousness, which illumines all of them and makes us aware of them is, indeed, the “Changeless.”

“नित्योऽनित्यानाम्।” — Kaṭhopaniṣad II-V-13.

“चेतनश्चेतनानाम्।” — Kaṭhopaniṣad II-V-13.
names.simple_meaning: "The stable; the Firm."

names.short_meaning: “One who has Supreme Manifestations (ṛddhi)”
names.commentary:
“One who has Supreme Manifestations (ṛddhi)”. The glory (vibhūti) of the Lord is expressed in His manifestations and these manifestations are indeed divine as the Gītā thunders, “The glories of the Self are indeed divine.”

“दिव्या ह्यात्मविभूतयः।” — Gītā, Chapter XI.
names.simple_meaning: “One who has Supreme Manifestations (ṛddhi)”

names.short_meaning: "The extremely vivid."
names.commentary: "The extremely vivid." He who is extremely clear to those who have conquered the agitations and all disturbing thought-currents of the mind through a successful pursuit of the practice of meditation. He being the very Self, nothing in fact is so 'clear', meaning, so self-evident, as the Pure Consciousness is in us. No experience in the outer world or in our subjective bosom would have been possible had it not been for the Light of the Self. Even the sense of individuality in us is but an image of this Awareness, which is the very Self in every living creature. It being thus the Absolute Subjective essence. It is described as "the most Vivid."
names.simple_meaning: "The extremely vivid."

names.short_meaning: "The ever — Contented," meaning "the One who is happy at the minimum offering of a devotee."
names.commentary:
"The ever — Contented," meaning "the One who is happy at the minimum offering of a devotee." "I accept even if you offer some leaf or flower, or fruit or spoon of water, happily, if it is offered in love," confesses Lord Kṛṣṇa in the Gītā.

The Self being beyond body, mind and intellect, it cannot have any of the sense of imperfections or incompleteness and as such, the All-full Self must be at all times, complete in Himself. Naturally therefore He is All — Blissful. Consequently, His Nature must ever be Supreme contentment.

“पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति। तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः॥” — Gītā IX-26.
names.simple_meaning: The ever-contented one

names.short_meaning: "One who is ever-full."
names.commentary:
"One who is ever-full." The Supreme Consciousness being All-pervading, He is Infinitely Full; nothing can we take out of It, nor can we add to It. It is Ever-full and, therefore, even when the manifestations emerge out from It. It is not less for it.

“पूर्णस्य पूर्णमादाय पूर्णमेवावशिष्यते।” “When Full is taken away from the Full, the Full alone remains.” — Īśāvāsyopaniṣad, Śānti Pāṭha.
names.simple_meaning: "One who is ever-full."

names.short_meaning: “All auspicious gaze.”
names.commentary: “All auspicious gaze.” One whose very gaze brings streams of auspiciousness to the devotee. The Self being beyond vāsanās, one who realises the Self, goes beyond all sins. A devotee walking the very path and moving towards the spiritual contents, purifies himself from all sins, since he will be living a life not identifying with his body, mind and intellect.
names.simple_meaning: “All auspicious gaze.”

names.short_meaning: That which revels in every form or that in which all yogins in their meditation revel
names.commentary:
"That which revels in every form or that in which all yogins in their meditation revel. In Padmapurana, it is clearly defined, "In Him, who is Eternal Bliss, Pure Consciousness, and Endless, the yogins revel."

Therefore, by the term 'rāmaḥ', the Supreme Self is indicated. The term can also mean "One who has a compelling charm about Himself. He who is the most Handsome."

“रमन्ते योगिनः अस्मिन् इति रामः।” (Ramante yoginaḥ asmin iti Rāmaḥ.)

“रमन्ते योगिनोऽनन्ते नित्यानन्दे चिदात्मनि।” — Padma Purāṇa.
names.simple_meaning: That which revels in every form or that in which all yogins in their meditation revel

names.short_meaning: “He in whom the creatures rest; The Abode of perfect rest”, having reached which, there is no return into the realms of experiences
names.commentary: “He in whom the creatures rest; The Abode of perfect rest”, having reached which, there is no return into the realms of experiences. That state is called Viraamah. Some commentators recognise in this term a meaning as, "He (Īśvara) in whom the world of plurality merges during the deluge."
names.simple_meaning: The abode of perfect rest

names.short_meaning: "Passionless."
names.commentary: "Passionless." "One who is not associated with the agitations (Rajas) of the mind." The mind gets agitated when it identifies with the sense-objects of the world outside. The Atman, the Self, in its Pure Nature, has no such identifications, and, therefore, He is recognised as 'passionless?
names.simple_meaning: "Passionless."

names.short_meaning: ‘The path.’
names.commentary: ‘The path.’ There is no other way to know Him. For complete liberation, there is no way other than realising the Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: ‘The path.’

names.short_meaning: "The Guide", the "Conductor."
names.commentary:
"The Guide", the "Conductor." He who guides and ultimately takes the seeker to the Reality is Lord Nārāyaṇa, the Saguna Brahman. Through surrender to Nārāyaṇa, the devotee develops the integration within and when fully integrated, he becomes the meditator and through meditation, the Highest is achieved. Therefore, Viṣṇu is indicated here as the "Conductor."

The term can also mean "One who is fit to be conducted to the Highest." The individual-ego is that which tries to realise its own real nature, the self. The very individuality (Jiva) who is fit to be led towards the gateway to the Higher Consciousness is the One that has removed its false attachments and is held in animated joy, in meditation. In essence, such a jiva is nothing other than the Supreme, and, therefore, the Supreme is thus called as the Jiva.

“ब्रह्मवित् ब्रह्मैव भवति।” — Upaniṣad.
names.simple_meaning: "The Guide", the "Conductor."

names.short_meaning: “One who leads.”
names.commentary: “One who leads.” When such a true devotee slowly and steadily gains his detachments from the outer world he moves himself more and more into the Higher and Subtler states of Consciousness. The one who leads such a seeker is again the grace of the same Self—Atmabala.
names.simple_meaning: “One who leads.”

names.short_meaning: If the ego is led by the Lord (as Naya) to the Highest, then when once the Supreme State is reached, It has none to lead or guide It
names.commentary: If the ego is led by the Lord (as Naya) to the Highest, then when once the Supreme State is reached, It has none to lead or guide It. The Lord guides all, but there is none to guide Him. This is because He is All-pervading and, therefore, He needs no guide to lead Him to Himself, as He is everywhere at all times.
names.simple_meaning: If the ego is led by the Lord (as Naya) to the Highest, then when once the Supreme State is reached, It has none to lead or guide It

names.short_meaning: "The Valiant."
names.commentary: "The Valiant." One who, by His prowess, creates the fear in the minds of the Rakshasas.
names.simple_meaning: "The Valiant."

names.short_meaning: "The best among those who have power."
names.commentary: "The best among those who have power." All powers that are available, have been classified under three types: the power-of — Knowledge (jñāna-śakti), the power-of — Desire (Icchaa-śakti) and the power-of — Action (Kriyaa-śakti). All these powers are expression of the Self in the intellect, in the sub-conscious mind and in the physical body, respectively. Naturally the Self is the best among all other kinds of powers inasmuch as, all powers are expressions of this Great Self.
names.simple_meaning: "The best among those who have power."

names.short_meaning: This term is used in Hinduism in thousands of different shades that, to the early student, the meaning of this term is lost in confusion
names.commentary:
This term is used in Hinduism in thousands of different shades that, to the early student, the meaning of this term is lost in confusion. dharma of a thing is that because of which the thing is, without which the thing is not." This term, dharma, has, therefore, been translated as "the Law of Being"—the dharma of the Sun is light; the dharma of the Fire is heat, the dharma of Sugar is sweetness.

What then is the dharma of the individual? The essential dharma of the individual can only be the Self, because, without which the individual cannot exist, and the individual's expressions, physical, mental and intellectual, are all expressions of the Self through the equipment in Him. Thus, "dharma" means the One Self in all individuals.

This essential dharma in anything is that which supports the things and, therefore, the Self which is the essence everywhere, is considered as the very One which supports everything.

“धारयति इति धर्मः।” “देवैरत्रापि विचिकित्सितं पुरा नहि सुविज्ञेयमणुरेष धर्मः।” — Kaṭhopaniṣad.
names.simple_meaning: Dharma itself, the law that upholds

names.short_meaning: “One who is the Highest among men of realisation.”
names.commentary: “One who is the Highest among men of realisation.” All those who know the Reality are knowers of this Self. Naturally, therefore, the Self is the best Knower among all knowers of the Self.
names.simple_meaning: “One who is the Highest among men of realisation.”

names.short_meaning: “One who prevents men from going astray into wrong paths (Vikunthah)."
names.commentary:
“One who prevents men from going astray into wrong paths (Vikunthah)." In Mahābhārata it is mentioned, "I united the Earth with water, Space with air, and Air with fire, hence, the name 'vaikuṇṭhaḥ' has come to Me.

“मया संश्लेषिता भूमिरद्भिर्व्योम च वायुना। वायुश्च तेजसा सार्धं वैकुण्ठत्वं ततो मम॥” — Mahābhārata.
names.simple_meaning: “One who prevents men from going astray into wrong paths (Vikunthah)."

names.short_meaning: "One who dwells in all bodies (Puris)."
names.commentary:
"One who dwells in all bodies (Puris)." In Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (3-4-1) it is said, "because He as the first (Poorva) of all of them consumed Aushad) by fire all sins, therefore, He is called puruṣaḥ." In short, He is the One Self which thrills all living creatures everywhere at all times.

Puri śayanāt Puruṣaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: "One who dwells in all bodies (Puris)."

names.short_meaning: One who in the form of 'prāṇa' exists in the body, propels all sense-organs to act in their appointed fields
names.commentary: "One who in the form of 'prāṇa' exists in the body, propels all sense-organs to act in their appointed fields. It is Lord Viṣṇu that activates the body as the 5 praanas, is found in the Vishnupurana. As prāṇa, He causes movements.
names.simple_meaning: One who in the form of 'prāṇa' exists in the body, propels all sense-organs to act in their appointed fields

names.short_meaning: This can mean "One who gives 'prāṇa' or as "One who takes away 'prāṇa', because, the root 'da' has both the meanings, 'to give' and 'to break.'
names.commentary: This can mean "One who gives 'prāṇa' or as "One who takes away 'prāṇa', because, the root 'da' has both the meanings, 'to give' and 'to break.' Therefore, Viṣṇu is the Supreme who gives prāṇa to all creatures in the beginning of creation, and He alone is again the One who destroys all Pragnas (movements) at the time of dissolution.
names.simple_meaning: The giver and withdrawer of life-breath

names.short_meaning: “That which is praised or adored by even the gods.”
names.commentary:
“That which is praised or adored by even the gods.” There is a declaration of Sanatkumara, "Because it is being worshipped and adored by the gods, the Self is called as praṇavaḥ. This great Reality is indicated in the Vedas by the symbol Om and, therefore, 'oṃkāra' is called as praṇava. Thus the Supreme Self, 'oṃkāra' is Viṣṇu.

“प्रणवन्ति ह्ययं देवास्तस्मात् प्रणव उच्यते।”
names.simple_meaning: “That which is praised or adored by even the gods.”

names.short_meaning: “The expanded.”
names.commentary:
“The expanded.” He whose expanse is expressed as the world of infinite forms. In short, “He who is All-pervasive." Looking at the world, through Purāṇas, it suggests, "The One who is born as king pṛthuḥ, the son of king Vena (वेन:)—for bringing prosperity to the country, is Lord Nārāyaṇa."

“अत्र तु प्रथमो राज्ञां पुमान् प्रथयिता यशः। पृथुर्नाम महाराजो भविष्यति पृथुश्रवाः॥”
names.simple_meaning: “The expanded.”

names.short_meaning: It is a term used in Vedānta for the "Creator."
names.commentary: It is a term used in Vedānta for the "Creator." He is the expression of the creative urge of the Lord Nārāyaṇa. "The Golden-egg" means here that from which all the objective world had emerged out, indicating the Creator. So, the term means "He who is in Himself the very Creator." The term thereby suggests that the entire creative power of the Creator is but the expression of the Self, Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: The golden womb, the cosmic creator

names.short_meaning: "The destroyer of the enemies."
names.commentary: "The destroyer of the enemies." The Lord is the One who annihilates all the enemies of the gods, meaning, He is the One who destroys all the negative tendencies in all serious seekers totally devoted to Him.
names.simple_meaning: "The destroyer of the enemies."

names.short_meaning: "The Pervader."
names.commentary: "The Pervader." The effects can never remain without the Cause; the Cause is concurrent and inherent in its effects. And thus, the world that has risen from the Infinite, should be pervaded by the Infinite. He who thus pervades everything is Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "The Pervader."

names.short_meaning: “One who in the form of the atmospheric air, sustains all life everywhere."
names.commentary: “One who in the form of the atmospheric air, sustains all life everywhere." He is not the air, but He is the life-giving power in the air.
names.simple_meaning: “One who in the form of the atmospheric air, sustains all life everywhere."

names.short_meaning: One who is not available for the powers of the sense organs to perceive
names.commentary:
Mahābhārata says, "At no time My vitality flows downwards, and hence, I am called 'adhokṣajaḥ'. The term can also mean, "One who is not available for the powers of the sense organs to perceive." Or, it can also mean, "He who remains under both the atmosphere and the earth as the Supporter of the entire universe."

“अधो न क्षीयते जातु यस्मात् तस्मादधोक्षजः।” — Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva 71-10.
names.simple_meaning: One who is not available for the powers of the sense organs to perceive

names.short_meaning: "Seasons"—Here it means, the Lord of Time, who governs the seasons
names.commentary: "Seasons"—Here it means, the Lord of Time, who governs the seasons.
names.simple_meaning: Time as the ordered cycle of seasons

names.short_meaning: “One who is easy to be perceived if the seeker has sufficient devotion,” or “He whose meeting is auspicious inasmuch as it removes the seeker's worldly worries."
names.commentary: “One who is easy to be perceived if the seeker has sufficient devotion,” or “He whose meeting is auspicious inasmuch as it removes the seeker's worldly worries."
names.simple_meaning: The one whose auspicious vision is readily gained through devotion

names.short_meaning: "One who measures the merits and defects in each individual, and who doles out the appropriate results."
names.commentary:
"One who measures the merits and defects in each individual, and who doles out the appropriate results." Bhāgavata Gītā says, "I am the Time of counting." kālaḥ is also the name of Lord Death, and in this sense, it can mean "the Lord, who is Death or Annihilationpersonified to all His enemies."

कलयति इति कालः (Kalayati iti Kālaḥ).

“कालः कलयतामहम्।” — Gītā X-30.
names.simple_meaning: "One who measures the merits and defects in each individual, and who doles out the appropriate results."

names.short_meaning: "One who is centred in His own infinite glory."
names.commentary:
"One who is centred in His own infinite glory." Or, it can also mean "One who is readily available for experience in the Supreme cave of the heart."

In the Kaṭhopaniṣad, the seat of the Self within is described as: “परमे व्योम्नि प्रतिष्ठितः।”
names.simple_meaning: "One who is centred in His own infinite glory."

names.short_meaning: "The Receiver."
names.commentary:
"The Receiver." He who receives from His devotees even insignificant things as a leaf or a flower, with all satisfaction. Some commentators stretch the suggestion of the word and find a meaning in this term as "One who has been accepted as the Sole Refuge by all devotees "

“पत्रं पुष्पं फलं तोयं यो मे भक्त्या प्रयच्छति। तदहं भक्त्युपहृतमश्नामि प्रयतात्मनः॥” — Gītā IX-26.
names.simple_meaning: "The Receiver."

names.short_meaning: "The Terrible."
names.commentary:
"The Terrible." The One who gives fear to those who are diabolically evil", or, as the Upaniṣad declares, "For fear of Him the fire burns; for fear of Him shines the sun; For fear of Him Indra, Vaayu and Death proceed with their respective functions," -therefore He is the Terrible.

“भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सूर्यः। भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः॥” — Kaṭhopaniṣad II-VI-3.
names.simple_meaning: "The Terrible."

names.short_meaning: “The Year,” which is the abode of all living creatures
names.commentary:
“The Year,” which is the abode of all living creatures. Time is spread in which creatures exist and gather their experiences.

“सम्यक् वसन्ति भूतानि यस्मिन् इति संवत्सरः।”
names.simple_meaning: “The Year,” which is the abode of all living creatures

names.short_meaning: "The Smart."
names.commentary: "The Smart." One who undertakes the creation, sustenance and destruction of the Whole Cosmos with ease and efficiency, diligence and promptitude.
names.simple_meaning: "The Smart."

names.short_meaning: "The resting place;" "the Quiet."
names.commentary: "The resting place;" "the Quiet." That State wherein people who suffer in Samsar, can discover a perfect rest and quietude is the consciousness Supreme, Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "The resting place;" "the Quiet."

names.short_meaning: “The most skilful and efficient.”
names.commentary: “The most skilful and efficient.” All efficiency and skill that we find in the universe among the dynamic living creatures are all His expressions alone, and, therefore, He is the source of all skill and efficiency. Again. He is the One who is the very Creator and Preserver of the whole universe and He must be the most efficient Manager and Administrator among the living creatures.
names.simple_meaning: “The most skilful and efficient.”

names.short_meaning: The extension
names.commentary: The extension. The Lord is named thus because in the time of Pralaya, in Him the entire universe of names and forms comes to reside with ample accommodation for all of them. The term vistāraḥ can also mean "manifestation;" since the Lord manifests in Himself all the universe.
names.simple_meaning: The extension

names.short_meaning: "The firm and the motionless."
names.commentary:
"The firm and the motionless." The Firm (achanchala) indicates that He has no movements, because He is All-pervading. sthāṇuḥ (motionless) means that He is fixed like "the pillars that denote the frontiers of a country" (sthāṇuḥ). The terms here used are as one-word because the Lord is both these at one and the same time.

He is not only All-pervading, and, therefore, no movements in Him (Sthaavarah), but he is also without any locomotion (sthāṇuḥ). Both these terms indicate the All-pervasiveness of Lord Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: "The firm and the motionless."

names.short_meaning: The proof
names.commentary: The proof. He is the underlying principle of all intellectual arguments and for all scientific methodology, since He is the very Consciousness behind all discussions. Lord Nārāyaṇa is the very authority behind all dharmas and hence He becomes the essential Reality behind all (pramaana).
names.simple_meaning: The proof

names.short_meaning: “The Immutable Seed."
names.commentary:
“The Immutable Seed." Since the whole world has sprung from Him, He is the indestructible and changeless cause of the world. It can also mean "that without which the world can never be."

Hence He is the undecaying root of all things.
names.simple_meaning: “The Immutable Seed."

names.short_meaning: One who is worshipped by all; invoked by everyone
names.commentary: One who is worshipped by all; invoked by everyone. Lord Nārāyaṇa is desired by all as He is the paramātman who is of the nature of bliss. Even the sensuous man running after the sense-objects is seeking the Lord in as much as he is searching for bliss which is the nature of the Self.
ocr_notes: Scan locus corrected from [126] to [126, 127] by complete-text replay against the PDF page OCR.
names.simple_meaning: One who is worshipped by all; invoked by everyone

names.short_meaning: One to whom there is nothing that is yet to be fulfilled
names.commentary: One to whom there is nothing that is yet to be fulfilled. This means one who has no desires, as He has fulfilled all His desires. So long as vāsanās exist desires manifest. Where vāsanās have ended there cannot be any desires and that state is the State of Self-realization.
names.simple_meaning: One to whom there is nothing that is yet to be fulfilled

names.short_meaning: One who has got around him great sheaths
names.commentary: One who has got around him great sheaths. The Self in us functions through the fivesheaths such as the food-sheath, etc. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is one who, as the Lord of the universe (Jagadeesvarah), is conditioned by the macrocosmic sheaths of the universe, and therefore, the great Īśvara is here indicated as mahākośaḥ.
names.simple_meaning: One who has got around him great sheaths

names.short_meaning: One who is of the nature of enjoyment (bhogah), He being of the nature of bliss
names.commentary: One who is of the nature of enjoyment (bhogah), He being of the nature of bliss. Also He is the one from whom the greatest bliss (bhogah) can be gained by the seekers. In short, the term indicates Him as one who gives the greatest happiness to all those who are devoted to Him.
names.simple_meaning: One who is of the nature of enjoyment (bhogah), He being of the nature of bliss

names.short_meaning: One who is supremely rich with the wealth of bliss which he can give to His devotees
names.commentary: One who is supremely rich with the wealth of bliss which he can give to His devotees. Viṣṇu is one from whom His devotees gain great wealth.
names.simple_meaning: One who is supremely rich with the wealth of bliss which he can give to His devotees

names.short_meaning: One who has no nirveda
names.commentary: One who has no nirveda (निवंद). This term nirvedu means "the sense of disinterestedness that comes to the bosom of one who could not fulfil his passionate desires in life." The Lord is one who is griefless as He has no desires to fulfil. In His fullness and perfection, He has no more any desires to fulfil, and therefore, Śrī Hari has no occasion to suffer from the sense of nirveda.
names.simple_meaning: One who has no nirveda

names.short_meaning: One who is supremely gross
names.commentary:
One who is supremely gross. The entire cosmos being His form, He Himself is the universe, and as such in His total manifestation, He is supremely gross. Gītā says (Chapter XI-20) that the Lord spreads Himself covering the whole world and the atmosphere. The Upaniṣad (Mundaka 1-4) also says how "the sky forms His head, the sun and the moon are His eyes."

“द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः।” “This space between earth and the heavens and all the quarters are filled by You alone.” — Gītā XI-20.

“अग्निर्मूर्धा चक्षुषी चन्द्रसूर्यौ। दिशः श्रोत्रे वाग् विवृताश्च वेदाः।” Heaven is His head; His eyes the sun and moon; the four quarters His ears; His speech, the Vedas. — Muṇḍakopaniṣad II-1-4.
names.simple_meaning: One who is supremely gross

names.short_meaning: One who has no birth, or the one, having realised whom, the seeker will no more have births
names.commentary: One who has no birth, or the one, having realised whom, the seeker will no more have births. Some people dissolve the line Sthavishthah + bhūḥ. In that case instead of abhūḥ they give the Lord the name, 'bhūḥ', meaning 'earth.' Just as the earth is the stage upon which the entire drama of life is being played, Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the substratum upon which the entire world of experiences is playing about.
names.simple_meaning: One who has no birth, or the one, having realised whom, the seeker will no more have births

names.short_meaning: yūpaḥ is the name given to the post to which the sacrificial animal is tied in a vaaga
names.commentary: yūpaḥ is the name given to the post to which the sacrificial animal is tied in a vaaga. The Lord is the very Post to which all dharmas (righteousness) are tied. This means He is the very essence behind all righteousness.
names.simple_meaning: yūpaḥ is the name given to the post to which the sacrificial animal is tied in a vaaga

names.short_meaning: The Great Sacrificer
names.commentary:
The Great Sacrificer. Because the sacrifices dedicated to Him confer total liberation -(Nirvaana). Also in the Gītā we were told, "offer is Brahman, what is offered is Brahman, the fire is Brahman, the offerer is Brahman and the goal reached is also Brahman."

“ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हविर्ब्रह्माग्नौ ब्रह्मणा हुतम्। ब्रह्मैव तेन गन्तव्यं ब्रह्मकर्मसमाधिना॥” — Gītā IV-24.
names.simple_meaning: The Great Sacrificer

names.short_meaning: The Nave of the stars
names.commentary: The Nave of the stars. One who is the nave around which all the stars and the planets including the sun, moon and other planets always move around. For this brilliant glowing wheel of Light, Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the very Axle.
names.simple_meaning: The Nave of the stars

names.short_meaning: One who is the Lord of the stars
names.commentary:
One who is the Lord of the stars. Lord of the stars is the moon. Gītā says, “among the stars I am the moon.”

“आदित्यानामहं विष्णुर्ज्योतिषां रविरंशुमान्। मरीचिर्मरुतामस्मि नक्षत्राणामहं शशी॥” — Gītā X-21.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Lord of the stars

names.short_meaning: One who is supremely efficient in all undertakings
names.commentary: One who is supremely efficient in all undertakings. One who has extreme patience with all the stupidities of his devotees.
names.simple_meaning: One who is supremely efficient in all undertakings

names.short_meaning: One who ever remains without any scarcity—(kṣāma)
names.commentary: One who ever remains without any scarcity—(kṣāma). During the final deluge all things in the world dissolve and perish away but even then the Lord remains untouched by all distinction and hence He is called kshaamah.
names.simple_meaning: One who ever remains without any scarcity—(kṣāma)

names.short_meaning: One whose desires are auspicious
names.commentary:
One whose desires are auspicious. The Lord is considered as “Well-desiring” in as much as he desires the well-being of all His creatures at all times. He knows how to control and regulate His power of desiring (Icchaa-sakti) and thus He is extremely efficient in His creative activity.

सम्यगीहत इति समीहनः—“Wishing well.”
names.simple_meaning: One whose desires are auspicious

names.short_meaning: One who is of the nature of yajña
names.commentary: One who is of the nature of yajña. All sacrifices are His own forms. He exists as sacrifice in order to satisfy men and gods. Sruti says that all yajnas are of the nature of Viṣṇu (yajño Vai Viṣṇuḥ).
names.simple_meaning: One who is of the nature of yajña

names.short_meaning: One who is fit to be invoked through vainas
names.commentary: One who is fit to be invoked through vainas. Lord Nārāyaṇa is the only one who is being invoked in all vajnas, even when the devotee particularly invokes any other deity. He, being the Infinite, all gods are expressions of His own glory and therefore, irrespective of the deity invoked, all vainas are worship of Viṣṇu. In Harivaṃśa we read a declaration which openly reveals this truth: "They who worship through holy sacrifices, the devas or the pitris, they worship indeed the Viṣṇu, the Self, through the Self."
names.simple_meaning: One who is fit to be invoked through vainas

names.short_meaning: One who is to be most worshipped
names.commentary: One who is to be most worshipped. One who most certainly is to be invoked in every ritual because all other devataas invoked during the yajnas can each fulfil the seeker's desires; but to invoke Śrī Nārāyaṇa is to invoke the only Power that can supply complete liberation for the devotee. Therefore, He is the object of great sacrifice.
names.simple_meaning: One who is to be most worshipped

names.short_meaning: It is a kind of yāga wherein there is a pillar to which the sacrificial animal is tied
names.commentary: It is a kind of yāga wherein there is a pillar to which the sacrificial animal is tied. Since all sacrifices are offered to Him—the Lord, even kratuḥ, a sacrifice with violence inherent in it, is also Viṣṇu.
names.simple_meaning: It is a kind of yāga wherein there is a pillar to which the sacrificial animal is tied

names.short_meaning: The Lord who protects the good (Sat)
names.commentary:
The Lord who protects the good (Sat). In continuation with the previous Kratuh, when we read this it can also be considered as indicating a particular kind of yaina described as satraṃ in our Vedic literature.

The word is dissolved as “सतः त्रायते इति सत्रम्” (Sataḥ trāyate iti satram).
names.simple_meaning: The Lord who protects the good (Sat)

names.short_meaning: One who is the refuge (for the good people)
names.commentary: One who is the refuge (for the good people). One who is worshipped and invoked by those who wish to liberate themselves from all limitations in life. Gatih in Sanskrit means both the path and the goal. Thus, through surrendering to the Nārāyaṇa alone does one reach Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the refuge (for the good people)

names.short_meaning: “All-knower.”
names.commentary: “All-knower.” As He is the pure Consciousness in all living creatures, all knowledge in all beings is illumined by Him. Just as the sun is "the eye of the universe," so the Consciousness is the Illuminator of everything.
names.simple_meaning: “All-knower.”

names.short_meaning: “The ever-liberated Self."
names.commentary:
“The ever-liberated Self." The Supreme, though He expresses Himself through the equipments, He is never conditioned by the matter envelopments through which He apparently expresses Himself. Just as the waves rise, exist and dissolve in the ocean, the equipments of experiences rise, play and dissolve themselves in Him.

He is ever-liberated, never-shackled by gross matter. This great principle of Paraatmaa is Śrī Nārāyaṇa.-Sruti says (Kaṭhopaniṣad 5-1).

“पुरमेकादशद्वारमजस्यावक्रचेतसः। अनुष्ठाय न शोचति विमुक्तश्च विमुच्यते॥” — Kaṭhopaniṣad 5-1.
names.simple_meaning: “The ever-liberated Self."

names.short_meaning: "Omniscient."
names.commentary: "Omniscient." He is the Principle of Consciousness and, therefore, He is the Illuminator of all thoughts, all intentions, motives, emotions and all sense perceptions in an individual. The meaning is the same as in Sarvadarsee.
names.simple_meaning: "Omniscient."

names.short_meaning: “The Supreme Knowledge of all other knowledges.”
names.commentary: “The Supreme Knowledge of all other knowledges.” The Self is the Supreme Knowledge, for, without the Consciousness, no knowledge is possible. Taittireeyopanishad indicates the Self as: "Satyam jñānam, Anantam Brahma."
names.simple_meaning: “The Supreme Knowledge of all other knowledges.”

names.short_meaning: "The one who is ever performing the pure vow."
names.commentary: "The one who is ever performing the pure vow." It is a sacred vow of the Lord that He has to give shelter and protection to all those who totally surrender themselves into him—says Śrī Ramachandraji ("अभयं सर्वभूतेभ्यो ददाम्येतत् व्रतं मम।"): "To give shelter to all living creatures—this is my vow." This term can also refer to Him who had done tapas for a long number of years on the mount of Nara — Nārāyaṇa in Badrinath.
names.simple_meaning: "The one who is ever performing the pure vow."

names.short_meaning: One who has an enchanting face
names.commentary: One who has an enchanting face. Truth is beauty and Beauty truth. In all conditions the Lord is ever cheerful and brings to His face the dignified beauty of calm repose. When the devotees come and surrender at His sacred feet Nārāyaṇa is the one of Infinite mercy who beams with joy at the devotion of the surrender.
names.simple_meaning: One who has an enchanting face

names.short_meaning: One who is subtler than the subtlest
names.commentary: One who is subtler than the subtlest. In Vedānta terminology subtlety indicates Pervasiveness. Therefore, the term means All — Pervasive. The Upaniṣad says the Lord is All — Pervading, subtler than the subtlest (Sarvagatam susookshmam).
names.simple_meaning: One who is subtler than the subtlest

names.short_meaning: “Of auspicious sound.”
names.commentary: “Of auspicious sound.” This is the name of the conch that Kṛṣṇa blew in the opening of the Mahābhārata war. The sound of Viṣṇu is the essence of all Vedas as all the four Vedas have come from Him, the Supreme. Hence the term "of auspicious sound."
names.simple_meaning: “Of auspicious sound.”

names.short_meaning: "One who confers happiness."
names.commentary: "One who confers happiness." It can also mean in Sanskrit one who is the destroyer of joy (Da-to destroy). Here, of course, it means that One who gives joy to His devotees and takes away joy from those who are undivine.
names.simple_meaning: "One who confers happiness."

names.short_meaning: “The friend of all living creatures.”
names.commentary: “The friend of all living creatures.” A true friend is one who gives all that he possesses without expecting any return.
names.simple_meaning: “The friend of all living creatures.”

names.short_meaning: One who is the looter of the mind; or charming
names.commentary: One who is the looter of the mind; or charming. Not only is the Lord Beauty Incarnate, but He compels the attention of the devotee to come away from all other sense objects to dwell upon His enchanting form. Thus Viṣṇu is one who generates an irresistible joy in the mind of His devotees and compels them to spend their time in constant worship.
names.simple_meaning: One who is the looter of the mind; or charming

names.short_meaning: One who has conquered anger
names.commentary: One who has conquered anger. By the one term here, anger, we should consider all the six inner enemies kāma, Krodha, Lobha, Moha, Mada and Maatsarya. These six constitute the types of thoughts in man; the six categories into which all his mental activities fall. One who has conquered all these means one who is beyond the mind-the Self.
names.simple_meaning: One who has conquered anger

names.short_meaning: One having mighty, valiant arms
names.commentary: One having mighty, valiant arms. From time to time He has to incarnate in order to put down the wicked and thereby protect the good.
names.simple_meaning: One having mighty, valiant arms

names.short_meaning: One who splits asunder; destroys
names.commentary:
One who splits asunder; destroys. In the man-lion form, Narasimha, Lord Viṣṇu appears to tear open and kill Hiraṇyakaśipu. Again, in order to destroy Hiraṇyākṣa and to lift the earth from the ocean.

Śrī Nārāyaṇa had to take the form of the great boar (Varaaha). Accordingly in the Sanskrit vocabulary, bhoo-duarah (भदार:) is a synonym for boar (Varaaha). Dara means to split or to tear open. Thus the meaning of the divine Boar can be squeezed out from the term vidāraṇaḥ used here.
names.simple_meaning: One who splits asunder; destroys

names.short_meaning: One who puts people to sleep; stupefying
names.commentary:
One who puts people to sleep; stupefying. Lord Viṣṇu as Īśvara has for Himself the total vāsanā (māyā) as an equipment for His self-expression as Īśvara (Nārāyaṇa). He, through His māyā, veils each individual and renders them ignorant of their own divine nature.

This "veiling-power" (Aavarana śakti) creates many agitations (Vikshepa), due to which individuals rush out for sense-gratification. Since Īśvara, thus, with His māyā-power deludes everybody, He gathers to Himself this epithet svāpanaḥ, meaning "the mighty stupefying force."
names.simple_meaning: One who puts people to sleep; stupefying

names.short_meaning: The One who has everything under His own personal control; the totally independent
names.commentary:
The One who has everything under His own personal control; the totally independent. Since He is the Supreme Consciousness, all living creatures and phenomenal powers are functioning by His grace, drawing their capacities to exist and act from Him only. If He withdraws His patronage everything in this Universe must stop functioning immediately. He is supremely independent inasmuch as, though the world-of-objects needs Him, He is entirely self-sufficient and needs no world for His Existence. Thus He is totally free.

The waves need the ocean, but the ocean is totally independent of the waves' existence.
names.simple_meaning: The One who has everything under His own personal control; the totally independent

names.short_meaning: All-pervading
names.commentary:
All-pervading. Pervasiveness in philosophy indicates subtlety. Thus All-pervading means that which is "subtler than the subtlest." This concept is again sustained by the physical observations in the world. The cause always pervades all the effects; the gold pervades all ornaments.

The entire universe is an effect and He being the Cause, He pervades all and everything at all times. Thus the All-pervading, in its suggestion, indicates that He is the Ultimate-cause and Himself in His pervasiveness is ever-present everywhere and in everything, presiding over all behaviours, actions and work. everywhere in the universe.
names.simple_meaning: All-pervading

names.short_meaning: Many-souled
names.commentary: Many-souled. Lord, the Infinite, though ever the one, expresses Himself as the many, while manifesting Himself, in the form of the universe. It is He, the One Great Consciousness, that expresses Himself as the creator, sustainer and destroyer-in order to maintain the play of the eternal dance, among the phenomenal things and deeds. He who becomes the Trinity is the great Viṣṇu Tattva.
names.simple_meaning: Many-souled

names.short_meaning: The One who does many actions, as He is the One Lord of all evolution, preservation, and involution of the universe
names.commentary: The One who does many actions, as He is the One Lord of all evolution, preservation, and involution of the universe. Where He is not presiding over, no activity can ever take place.
names.simple_meaning: The One who does many actions, as He is the One Lord of all evolution, preservation, and involution of the universe

names.short_meaning: The Abode of Lord
names.commentary:
The Abode of Lord. Not only Lord is living in each one of us as our inner — Soul (Antarvaamee) but He is at once, the All-pervading Essence in which, the entire universe exists, and as such, He alone is the Abode in which we live, breathe and act. Thus, as the Abode of the creatures, He is the endless 'time' and the infinite 'space' at once. For, in time-space field alone do things exist. The term "Vatsa," in Sanskrit, also means "calf." The word under discussion, therefore, can also mean "one who gives away calves." This has reference to Kṛṣṇa who returned to the Gopas all the calves, when they were taken away by the enemy.

Here the term is dissolved as Vatsān Rāti Iti—“Vatsaraḥ.”
names.simple_meaning: The Abode of Lord

names.short_meaning: The Supremely affectionate
names.commentary: The Supremely affectionate. One who loves His devotees extremely. Nārāyaṇa is one who has got more affection towards His devotees than all the paternal and maternal love in the world put together. Supreme Love is the meaning of the word 'vatsalaḥ;' Lord Nārāyaṇa is Love — Incarnate
names.simple_meaning: The Supremely affectionate

names.short_meaning: The Father
names.commentary: The Father. One who has infinite number of children; Lord considers the entire living kingdom as His own children; and nurses and nourishes them. It can also be interpreted as one who trains and protects the calves in the herd.
names.simple_meaning: The Father

names.short_meaning: The Jewel-wombed
names.commentary:
The Jewel-wombed. Like the ocean, One who has rich wealth concealed in Himself. ‘‘सरसामस्मि सागरः।’’ (“Sarasaamasmi sāgaraḥ.”)—Gītā X—24.

On the whole, the term Ratna-garbhah only means that the Lord is quick in His bestowing all the desired objects on His devotees.
names.simple_meaning: The Jewel-wombed

names.short_meaning: The Lord of wealth
names.commentary: The Lord of wealth. Here the term "Wealth" means all the good things in the universe—all objects of happiness. He is described in the Purāṇas as the Lord of the Goddess Lakṣmī (Lakshmipati) and as such He is ever the Master-of-all-wealth. The greatest of wealth is, of course, the liberation, and Lord Nārāyaṇa is the Īśvara of this great wealth. He blesses the true devotees with the experience of complete liberation from the entanglements and sorrows of the vestures of matter around us.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of wealth

names.short_meaning: One who protects the dharma
names.commentary:
One who protects the dharma. In the Bhagavad Gītā the Lord says: "In every cycle I shall manifest for re-establishing dharma."

“परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम्। धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे॥” — Gītā IV-8.
names.simple_meaning: One who protects the dharma

names.short_meaning: One who acts dharma
names.commentary: One who acts dharma. Though He, as the Absolute Consciousness that illuminates everything, is beyond all dharma and Adharma, Śrī Nārāyaṇa exemplifies what is the righteousness by His own conduct. He is, therefore, called as dharma — Pravartaka. In the various incarnations, the Lord has exemplified how the generation should live under the ever-changing kaleidoscopic pattern of circumstances that play around us at all times.
names.simple_meaning: One who acts dharma

names.short_meaning: The Supporter of dharma; meaning the very Seat of all dharma
names.commentary:
The Supporter of dharma; meaning the very Seat of all dharma. Just as the waves exist in the ocean; just as the cotton supports the cloth; just as all the ornaments exist in gold—so Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Infinite Truth is the very essence and support of the entire universe. Nārāyaṇa is the Throne at which all righteousness take their refuge.

Without direct reference to Him and His Glory, righteousness ‘‘परित्राणाय साधूनां विनाशाय च दुष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ।।" --Gītā IV--8. has no meaning; just as law books of a country are empty pages when the Government falls.
names.simple_meaning: The upholder in whom dharma rests

names.short_meaning: The Existence in all things and beings is the same ever, and it is All-pervading
names.commentary:
The Existence in all things and beings is the same ever, and it is All-pervading. The sun exists; the space between the sun and the earth exists; the ocean and the creatures therein exist; the physiological organs and their functions, mind and its activities, the intellect and its agitations -all exist. This Ever-present Principle of Existence is Śrī Nārāyaṇa. That which remains the same without any change in and through all changes, unaffected ever, same in the past, present and the future is called in Vedānta as 'Satya.' One who has all these natures is called sat-puruṣa. In the Upaniṣads, the Supreme Brahman is indicated as 'Satya'-"This, O Child, indeed was sat." In the Gītā while describing the Changeless Factor behind the eternally changing matter, Bhagavān says: "That which is the All-pervading in this world, that alone is indestructible and no one can destroy it."

“सदेव सौम्येदमग्र आसीत्।” — Chāndogya Upaniṣad VI-2.

“अविनाशि तु तद्विद्धि येन सर्वमिदं ततम्।” — Gītā II-17.
names.simple_meaning: The Existence in all things and beings is the same ever, and it is All-pervading

names.short_meaning: The Conditioned; Limited; the One who appears at this moment as the limited, conditioned, and therefore confined only to the world of plurality
names.commentary:
The Conditioned; Limited; the One who appears at this moment as the limited, conditioned, and therefore confined only to the world of plurality. That which actually is not, but apparently seems to be there, is called a delusion and this is indicated by the word "asat." In the Vedantic terminology, higher — Self (Param) is ever Immutable and Eternal, while the lower — Self (A-param) constituted of all the universe of manifested things and beings, is mutable and ephemeral. Śrī Nārāyaṇa Himself is, in His Apara nature, expressing as the world of the many that we today recognise around us. Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa confesses to Arjuna in the Bhagavad Gītā: "Arjuna, I am at once immortality and mortality. I am both existence and non-existence."

“अमृतं चैव मृत्युश्च सदसच्चाहमर्जुन।” — Gītā IX-19.
names.simple_meaning: The conditioned one

names.short_meaning: The Perishing
names.commentary: The Perishing. One who is the very Immutable Self in all things, that appears to suffer from constant mutation: The changeless-core in the midst of all the changes. All the changeable and variable things and beings of the Universe play in Him who is the only Substratum and, therefore, the Immutable Eternal Reality is called here as the Mutable; the changing and the dying waves are all ever nothing but the changeless ocean indeed.
names.simple_meaning: The Perishing

names.short_meaning: Imperishable
names.commentary:
Imperishable. In order to recognize the change, there must be a changeless entity knowing it. If one ornament is to become another, there must be indeed the changeless consistent gold permanently supporting it all the time. In the same way, there must be a Changeless Factor which must be the essential core, that holds together the pattern of the constant changes, which together constitute the play of the universe. This Changeless Factor is called Nārāyaṇa. Kṛṣṇa says in Bhāgavata Gītā: "all creatures together constitute the kṣara-purusha and the Changeless in all creatures is the A-kshara-purusha."

“क्षरः सर्वाणि भूतानि कूटस्थोऽक्षर उच्यते।” — Gītā XV-16.
names.simple_meaning: Imperishable

names.short_meaning: The Non-knower
names.commentary:
The Non-knower. Here we must carefully understand the term 'knower.' The "knower" of the emotions and thoughts is the Self, imprisoned in the body, mind and the intellect, and, therefore, functioning as the perceiver, feeler, thinker-called in the Vedānta śāstra as the "jīva," This individualised personality is the 'doer' and the 'enjoyer', in the calamitous world of activities. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the Pure — Self, who has not been contaminated by the mattervestures and their agitated-nature, and the consequent sorrows.

Therefore, 'Viṣṇu,' the Pure — Self, is indicated here as Non — Knower (A-vijnaataa), meaning the "jīva."
names.simple_meaning: The Non-knower

names.short_meaning: The thousand-rayed
names.commentary:
The thousand-rayed. As the Pure Consciousness, He is effulgent, and in the Upaniṣads we read that even the sun, moon and stars gain their effulgence from Him alone. In fact the Upaniṣads conclude that all living creatures are resplendent after His effulgence alone. Or, we can say that it means Śrī Nārāyaṇa, in the form of the Sun, illumines and nourishes the world of living creatures; because the name of the Sun in Sanskrit is 'Sahasraamsuh.' In praising the Lord Sun it is usual to sing of him as Sooryanaaraayana.

“तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति।” — Muṇḍakopaniṣad II-ii-10.
names.simple_meaning: The thousand-rayed

names.short_meaning: All-supporter
names.commentary: All-supporter. As the final substratum for everything, the Lord supports the entire universe of living creatures, and nobody supports Him, He alone is His own support. The Lord is at once the material, instrumental and the efficient causes for the universe of forms.
names.simple_meaning: All-supporter

names.short_meaning: One who is famous because of six qualities, such as glory, righteousness, fame, wealth, knowledge and detachment
names.commentary:
One who is famous because of six qualities, such as glory, righteousness, fame, wealth, knowledge and detachment. Again following the Puranic literature. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the one who made on His own bosom the great mark of the feet of maharṣi Bhrigu.

In fact from the standpoint of pure Vedānta, the term indicates the Ever-existing Pure Consciousness which is the very goal (lakṣaṇa) to be ultimately achieved for liberation. lakṣaṇa also means the scriptural textbooks and, therefore, the term also can mean He who is the author (kṛta) of the Scriptures (lakṣaṇa).

“ऐश्वर्यं धर्मः यशश्च श्रीर्ज्ञानं वैराग्यम्।” (Aiśvaryaṃ dharmaḥ yaśaśca śrīr jñānaṃ vairāgyam.)
names.simple_meaning: One who is famous because of six qualities, such as glory, righteousness, fame, wealth, knowledge and detachment

names.short_meaning: The Centre of the Supreme planetary system
names.commentary: The Centre of the Supreme planetary system. The Sanskrit term 'Gabhasti' means 'rays', and the term 'nemih' means the 'spokes.' Therefore, the term indicates "One who is the hub of the wheel-of-light in which the spokes are His own rays of brilliancy." Astronomically, we can consider this as the sun, the centre of the planetary system. Subjectively, He is the Atman, the Self-the Effulgent Consciousness—beaming out Himself to the whirls of matter (the five koshas).
names.simple_meaning: The Centre of the Supreme planetary system

names.short_meaning: Abiding in Sattva
names.commentary:
Abiding in Sattva. māyā is constituted of the three guṇas: unactivity (sattva), activity (rajas) and inactivity (tamas). When the māyā is predominantly constituted of Sattva, it becomes the vehicle for the Supreme Brahman to express as God, Śrī Nārāyaṇa. The Lord is essentially constituted of the "Sattva guṇa" and, therefore, He is pure truthfulness in nature (Suddha Satya Svaroopa). It can also mean He who remains (Stha) in all beings (Sattva).

“The Rise and Fall of Man.” — Kenopaniṣad, Introduction.
names.simple_meaning: Abiding in Sattva

names.short_meaning: The Lion
names.commentary:
The Lion. Due to His great exploits in fighting the negative forces during His various incarnations, He is indicated as the Lion among beings in the universe. Also in Sanskrit "any part of a name can indicate the full name."

Thus Bhīma means 'Bhīma Sena' or 'Bhaamaa' means 'Satya — Bhaamaa'. Similarly, 'Simha' here might mean a part of the Lord's name as 'Narasimha'; Nārāyaṇa had taken the form of the Man — Lion in order to end the tyranny of Hiraṇyakaśipu, and bless his God-devoted son Prahlāda.
names.simple_meaning: The Lion

names.short_meaning: The Great Lord of Beings
names.commentary: The Great Lord of Beings. One who is the Lord who orders, commands, regulates and presides over all activities of all living creatures, and hence is ever the Ruler of All creatures.
names.simple_meaning: The Great Lord of Beings

names.short_meaning: The first Deity
names.commentary:
The first Deity. Or it can also mean one who is First (ādi) and one who is resplendent (Deva); further we can also take it to mean that He is the First Deva, meaning, He is the God of all gods. The term 'ādi' also means "one who eats;" the term 'Deva' can mean 'one who evolves': thus the term can mean "one who evolves in eating up," by consuming the names and forms. This implies that to the extent one withdraws himself from his false occupations with the perceived names and forms, he moves deeper and deeper into the experiences of the divine Lord in himself; with this idea in mind, Lord is described by this term.

"One who evolves in consuming the names and forms."
names.simple_meaning: The first Deity

names.short_meaning: The Great Deity
names.commentary: The Great Deity. He is the Source of all Consciousness, and from Him have risen all further deities and beings, therefore, it is right to consider Him as the Supreme Lord.
names.simple_meaning: The Great Deity

names.short_meaning: The Lord of all Devas
names.commentary: The Lord of all Devas. He is the very Consciousness in the gods themselves; therefore, in His unquestionable prominence, He is addressed here as "God of all gods."
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of all Devas

names.short_meaning: “One who is the king of gods”—Indra—(Deva Bhrit) and one who is the teacher (Guruh)
names.commentary: “One who is the king of gods”—Indra—(Deva Bhrit) and one who is the teacher (Guruh). In short, He is the protector and advisor of the very Indra, who is the king of gods.
names.simple_meaning: “One who is the king of gods”—Indra—(Deva Bhrit) and one who is the teacher (Guruh)

names.short_meaning: One who helps to lift us from (uttaraḥ) the ocean of Samsar
names.commentary:
One who helps to lift us from (uttaraḥ) the ocean of Samsar. It also conveys the most excellent meaning of "One who is greater and nobler than all other deities." Rigveda declares: "He is the most excellent of all."

“विश्वस्मादिन्द्र उत्तरः।” — Ṛg Veda 10-86-1.
names.simple_meaning: One who helps to lift us from (uttaraḥ) the ocean of Samsar

names.short_meaning: The shepherd—As one who played the part of a cow-herd in His Kṛṣṇa-incarnation
names.commentary: The shepherd—As one who played the part of a cow-herd in His Kṛṣṇa-incarnation. The term 'Go' in Sanskrit has got four meanings: the cattle, the earth, the speech and the vedas. In all these meanings He is the Lord (Pati): Lord of the cattle; Lord of Earth; Lord of speech; the Lord about whom all the Vedas speak of as the very Goal.
names.simple_meaning: The shepherd—As one who played the part of a cow-herd in His Kṛṣṇa-incarnation

names.short_meaning: The protector
names.commentary: The protector. He is the Protector of all living creatures in as much as, if He were not there, the creatures could not exist. He is the very Existence in the living Kingdom.
names.simple_meaning: The protector

names.short_meaning: The One who is to be attained only through the subtle perception of jñāna
names.commentary: The One who is to be attained only through the subtle perception of jñāna. He is not attained either by actions, or by progeny or by wealth. Only through a ("Inaana Prasaadena") pure 'knowledge' alone He is experienced. Here the word knowledge does not mean the ordinary knowledge-of-things. The experience of Truth is gained only on transcending the intellect. Thus crossing the barriers of non-apprehension (Avidyaa) the meditator comes to apprehend the Reality; this subjective first-hand apprehension is called True Knowledge (Inaana); by this one process alone can one attain the Infinite: hence this term.
names.simple_meaning: The One who is to be attained only through the subtle perception of jñāna

names.short_meaning: He who was even before Time
names.commentary: He who was even before Time. That from which even the concept-of — Time itself rose up is the Infinite Truth and, therefore, Truth cannot be measured in terms of Time. Therefore, He is called the Ancient, for, He transcends Time.
names.simple_meaning: He who was even before Time

names.short_meaning: One who nurses and nourishes the very element from which the bodies are constituted
names.commentary: One who nurses and nourishes the very element from which the bodies are constituted. The Lord is the controller of the very five elements.
names.simple_meaning: One who nurses and nourishes the very element from which the bodies are constituted

names.short_meaning: The Enjoyer or the Protector
names.commentary:
The Enjoyer or the Protector. The term "bhoktā" can be dissolved in two ways. In (a) it would mean the 'Protector' and in (b) it would mean as the 'Enjoyer'. According to Vedānta, Lord in His transcendental glory, as the Atman, is neither the 'Doer' nor the 'Enjoyer' and yet, here, the Lord is taken as the 'Enjoyer' only in the sense that the experiencer 'ego,' the jīva, is also nothing other than the Supreme in Its final Essence.

Bhunakti iti Bhoktā—“Protector.”

Bhunkte iti Bhoktā—“Enjoyer.”
names.simple_meaning: The Enjoyer or the Protector

names.short_meaning: One who is the Lord of the Monkeys-Śrī Ramachandraji
names.commentary:
One who is the Lord of the Monkeys-Śrī Ramachandraji. 'Kapih' also can mean the Boar-incarnation (Varaaha).

“कपिर्वराह इन्द्रश्च वराहवपरास्थितः।”
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Lord of the Monkeys-Śrī Ramachandraji

names.short_meaning: He who gives away large gifts (dakṣiṇā), as presents distributed at the end of the Sacrifices
names.commentary: He who gives away large gifts (dakṣiṇā), as presents distributed at the end of the Sacrifices. When the body, mind and the intellect of man make sacrifices, man does Karmas. Lord Nārāyaṇa is the One who gives the results for all actions: (Karma Phala Daataa); hence this term to indicate the Lord.
names.simple_meaning: He who gives away large gifts (dakṣiṇā), as presents distributed at the end of the Sacrifices

names.short_meaning: One who drinks the Soma-juice in the yajñas, in the form of the deity that has been invoked by the householder
names.commentary: One who drinks the Soma-juice in the yajñas, in the form of the deity that has been invoked by the householder. In short, Nārāyaṇa is the Lord that receives all the offerings, in all rituals, which we may offer, because He is the One invoked, who plays as the various hierarchy of deities.
names.simple_meaning: One who drinks the Soma-juice in the yajñas, in the form of the deity that has been invoked by the householder

names.short_meaning: One who drinks the nectar
names.commentary: One who drinks the nectar. As the Infinite Truth He at all times enjoys the blissful immortality (Amritatvam). Also, it may have the echo of the puranic story of the churning of the Ocean-of-milk (Ksheeraabdhi) until they got the Nectar, which was confiscated by the Asuras, and when they ran away, it was Śrī Nārāyaṇa, who, in the form of the irresistible Mohinee, a beautiful enchanting damsel, recovered the Nectar from them and distributed it to the gods. He had partaken the Nectar along with the gods.
names.simple_meaning: One who drinks the nectar

names.short_meaning: One who in the form of the moonlight (Soma) nourishes all the plant-kingdom with their respective essential sap
names.commentary:
One who in the form of the moonlight (Soma) nourishes all the plant-kingdom with their respective essential sap. It is very well known in the Hindu literature that the moonlight is that which enriches the food value in the fruits and grains. In the Gītā, Bhagavān says: "I in the form of the moon-light, enrich all the plant-kingdom," The term can also mean Siva, in which case it would mean as "One who is ever consorted by Umaa."

“पुष्णामि चौषधीः सर्वाः सोमो भूत्वा रसात्मकः।”

उमया सह वर्तते इति सोमः।
names.simple_meaning: One who in the form of the moonlight (Soma) nourishes all the plant-kingdom with their respective essential sap

names.short_meaning: One who has won over numerous enemies
names.commentary: One who has won over numerous enemies. The word Puru means 'many'.
names.simple_meaning: One who has won over numerous enemies

names.short_meaning: One who is Greater among the great
names.commentary: One who is Greater among the great. Here the word Puru means 'great'. In some readings we find instead of this term "purusattamaḥ" the term "Purushottamah" is used, in which case the meaning is the Omnipresent (puruṣa) and the Best (Uttamah)—the Absolute Reality.
names.simple_meaning: One who is Greater among the great

names.short_meaning: In direct meaning, of course, it means "He who shows the supreme humility."
names.commentary: In direct meaning, of course, it means "He who shows the supreme humility." But the term also means "One who humiliates those who are unrighteous." The Lord is one who leads well (Vi — Naya) the seekers steadily through the path of truth and righteousness.
names.simple_meaning: The one of supreme humility

names.short_meaning: The Victorious
names.commentary:
The Victorious. One who has conquered all the matter. It connotes that in order to experience the 'Self' we have to conquer all the lower matter-realms and their by-products. Realizing the Self, the seeker himself becomes the Self. At that time he has conquered all.

“ब्रह्मवित् ब्रह्मैव भवति।” (Brahmavit Brahmaiva Bhavati.)
names.simple_meaning: The Victorious

names.short_meaning: Of truthful resolution (saṅkalpa)
names.commentary: Of truthful resolution (saṅkalpa). The Lord is One, who in His perfection, has so completely integrated, that His resolve, His thoughts, feelings, words and actions are always truthful. There would be no compromise in them, and as such, every resolve of His becomes fruitful: "Heavens might fall down, the earth might tumble down, the Himalayas might be crushed, the ocean might become dry, but My word uttered shall never be in vain." (Purāṇa).
names.simple_meaning: Of truthful resolution (saṅkalpa)

names.short_meaning: It is a name of Lord Kṛṣṇa since He was born in the Dasaarha race (Yādava-kula)
names.commentary: It is a name of Lord Kṛṣṇa since He was born in the Dasaarha race (Yādava-kula). It can also mean "One who is fully competent to receive all devoted offerings made in the ritualistic sacrifices."
names.simple_meaning: Kṛṣṇa of the Dāśārha lineage

names.short_meaning: The Lord of the Sātvata-people
names.commentary: The Lord of the Sātvata-people. Those who are followers of the Tantra named sātvata—scriptures essentially sāttvika in nature— are called Saatvatas, and their Lord is Śrī Nārāyaṇa. The essential path of the Saatvatas is single-pointed meditation upon the form of Lord Viṣṇu with utter devotion.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of the Sātvata-people

names.short_meaning: One who remains as the limited-ego (jīvaḥ), who in its sense of separateness comes to experience the endless joys and sorrows in the fields of life
names.commentary:
One who remains as the limited-ego (jīvaḥ), who in its sense of separateness comes to experience the endless joys and sorrows in the fields of life. One who functions as the Experiencer-of-the — Field (Kshetrajna), as described in the Bhāgavata Gītā.

“क्षेत्रज्ञं चापि मां विद्धि सर्वक्षेत्रेषु भारत।” — Gītā XIII-2.
names.simple_meaning: One who remains as the limited-ego (jīvaḥ), who in its sense of separateness comes to experience the endless joys and sorrows in the fields of life

names.short_meaning: The Witness of modesty
names.commentary: The Witness of modesty. He is the one Consciousness that illumines the very sense of humility in His devotee's heart. It can also mean that as Pure Consciousness, He is one without a second, and, therefore, from His state of Universal Oneness He sees nothing other than Himself everywhere. In this Absolute Nature He does not see the world of finitude constituted of the ego and its deluded devilry.
names.simple_meaning: The Witness of modesty

names.short_meaning: One who gives liberation
names.commentary: One who gives liberation. To those who are trying to free themselves from the imperfections of the matter-conditionings, and who are struggling hard to end their delusions, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, being the very Goal, ultimately gives complete liberation for all devotees who reach Him in the true spirit of total surrender.
names.simple_meaning: One who gives liberation
