names.short_meaning: Of immeasurable Prowess or One whose step (Vikramah) is immeasurable (Amita)
names.commentary: Of immeasurable Prowess or One whose step (Vikramah) is immeasurable (Amita). The Lord in his Vamana-incarnation measured the three worlds by His three steps, and, therefore, He gained the title of 'Trivikramaha'. Since the Lord's steps are so vast, they are, indeed, immeasurable—"Amita"-Vikramah.
names.simple_meaning: Of immeasurable Prowess or One whose step (Vikramah) is immeasurable (Amita)

names.short_meaning: The direct meaning of the word is "ocean"
names.commentary:
The direct meaning of the word is "ocean" and the Lord Himself in the Bhāgavata Gītā has declared, "Of the lakes I am the ocean". According to the Taittirīya Braahmana: "These are the four Ambhas: viz. the Devas, Men, Manes and the Asuras." Therefore, the term Ambhonidhih should mean "One who is the substratum for all the four types of creatures.

“सरसामस्मि सागरः।” — Gītā X-24.

Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 2-3-8.
names.simple_meaning: The ocean

names.short_meaning: The Infinite Self
names.commentary: The Infinite Self. He is undefeated by time, space, or substance, and, therefore, in His own unconditioned nature He is the Infinite One Self. Or it can also mean One who manifests Himself as the endless varieties of entities constituting the universe. Ananta also means "end-less" and, therefore, the Endless Self, which means the paramātman, the Supreme Self.
names.simple_meaning: The Infinite Self

names.short_meaning: One who rests on the great ocean
names.commentary: One who rests on the great ocean. According to the description of Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Lord Nārāyaṇa reclines upon the Aadisesha in the Milky-ocean of Vaikuntha. It can also mean, "One who remains on a fig-leaf, upon the waters of the deluge, when all names and forms have been dissolved into the unmanifest.
names.simple_meaning: One who rests on the great ocean

names.short_meaning: The Death
names.commentary: The Death. As Time, He is the One who brings about constant changes in the world, without which no evolution or creative development is ever possible.
names.simple_meaning: The Death

names.short_meaning: Unborn
names.commentary: Unborn. As the changeless and deathless Reality, He has neither birth nor any decay. 'Unborn' in philosophy means undying; therefore, Eternal, Changeless. "Born (ज) to Lord Viṣṇu" (अ) is yet another meaning, and according to this interpretation, the term can suggest "Pradyumna," son of Viṣṇu, who is considered to be in our Purāṇa an Incarnation of the Lord of Love.
names.simple_meaning: Unborn

names.short_meaning: “One who deserves the highest worship."
names.commentary: “One who deserves the highest worship." Arhaa means 'poojaa': 'worship'.
names.simple_meaning: “One who deserves the highest worship."

names.short_meaning: Ever-rooted in the nature of His own Self
names.commentary: Ever-rooted in the nature of His own Self. One who is the Uncaused Cause, the God.
names.simple_meaning: Ever-rooted in the nature of His own Self

names.short_meaning: One who has conquered all his enemies both within and without
names.commentary: One who has conquered all his enemies both within and without. Within, He has conquered all enemies such as desires, hope, etc., and externally, has conquered enemies like Ravana, Hiraṇyakaśipu and others.
names.simple_meaning: One who has conquered all his enemies both within and without

names.short_meaning: 'Ever-blissful'
names.commentary: 'Ever-blissful'. One who is constantly enjoying His own Eternal, Blissful nature. The term indicates 'Viṣṇu' because Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the One that causes bliss in the heart of those who meditate upon Him.
names.simple_meaning: 'Ever-blissful'

names.short_meaning: A mass of Pure Bliss
names.commentary:
A mass of Pure Bliss. Bliss is His pure nature. The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad says: "Of this happiness, all other beings enjoy only a part."

“एतस्यैवानन्दस्यान्यानि भूतानि मात्रामुपजीवन्ति।” — Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad IV-3-32.
names.simple_meaning: A mass of Pure Bliss

names.short_meaning: "One who makes others blissful."
names.commentary: "One who makes others blissful." Since the Lord is the very source of the happiness of the devotees who reach the divine plane of Pure Consciousness, it is in Him they get themselves intoxicated with the endless drunkenness of this unceasing Bliss.
names.simple_meaning: "One who makes others blissful."

names.short_meaning: One who is freed from all limited worldly pleasures
names.commentary:
One who is freed from all limited worldly pleasures. Worldly pleasures come through contact with the objects of the sense-organs. The term means One who has no contact with the world of senses, as He dwells in transcendence of all the equipments of pleasure—the body, mind and intellect. Chāndogya Upaniṣad says, "That which is immensity is felicity; there is no felicity in littleness."

“यो वै भूमा तदमृतमथ यदल्पं तन्मर्त्यम्।” — Chāndogya Upaniṣad VII-24-1.

“यो वै भूमा तत्सुखं नाल्पे सुखमस्ति।” — Chāndogya Upaniṣad VII-23-1.
names.simple_meaning: One who is freed from all limited worldly pleasures

names.short_meaning: One who has in Himself all the true dharmas
names.commentary:
One who has in Himself all the true dharmas. Kindness, non-injury, charity etc. are considered as the noble dharmas. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is One in whom we find all these dharmas to the maximum. In short, He is the embodiment of Yoga (Yogesvara). It also means that One who is rich in the experience of the Supreme Self; for, the Upaniṣad says: "This alone is the Supreme dharma which is to experience the Self through yoga".

“अयं हि परमो धर्मः यद्योगेनात्मदर्शनम्।”
names.simple_meaning: One who has in Himself all the true dharmas

names.short_meaning: One who has taken the three steps
names.commentary:
'One who has taken the three steps". One who has, in three steps, conquered the three worlds in his Vamana-incarnation. The spiritual seeker has only to take three steps to reach the Centre of the Self in himself. Once he has stepped across the fields of-experiences in the waking, dream and deep-sleep conditions, he has reached the Infinite Consciousness, the Atman. The very term 'Tri' in Sanskrit means 'the three-worlds.' "The greatest men of reflection have declared the three fields-of-experiences (Loka) by the simple term 'Tri,''-(Harivaṃśa).

“त्रिरित्येव त्रयो लोकाः कीर्तिता मनीषिसत्तमैः।” — Harivaṃśa 3-88-51.
names.simple_meaning: One who has taken the three steps

names.short_meaning: - One who has manifested as the teacher Kapila, the great sage
names.commentary:
- One who has manifested as the teacher Kapila, the great sage. "ṛṣi", the sage, is one who has mastered a portion of the Veda, and one who has mastered the entire Vedas is called "maharṣi" in the Hindu tradition. The preceptor Kapila, who is a great master of the entire Vedic literature, is the propounder of the Saankhya philosophy. The glory of Kapilaachaarya is endorsed by Lord Kṛṣṇa Himself in the Gītā when He declares, "Of the perfected-ones, I am sage Kapila."

“सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः।”
ocr_notes: Scan locus corrected from [146] to [146, 147] by complete-text replay against the PDF page OCR.
names.simple_meaning: - One who has manifested as the teacher Kapila, the great sage

names.short_meaning: The created and the knower of the creation
names.commentary:
The created and the knower of the creation. kṛtam means "the universe that has been created." Jna means "the knower of all the objects." The Supreme Self is the material cause for the "knower" ego (Jna), and the effects constitute the world of things and beings (kṛtam). He who is the very substratum for both cause and effect is the Absolute Self, the Lord. He is unconditioned by the outer matter vestures such as body etc. and thus Lord Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the Absolute Reality. Nowadays, this word (Kritajna) has come to mean "gratitude" or "thanks-giving".

It is a cheap application of this deep meaning: To express to my benefactor that "I have known (Ina) what he had done (kṛtam) to help me" is thanksgiving, and hence, this usage is today very popular in our vernacular.
names.simple_meaning: The created and the knower of the creation

names.short_meaning: The Lord of the Earth, Śrī Nārāyaṇa
names.commentary: The Lord of the Earth, Śrī Nārāyaṇa. The Preserver Viṣṇu as the husband of the inert matter, Earth, is a concept at once immensely beautiful and deep, philosophic and poetic.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of the Earth, Śrī Nārāyaṇa

names.short_meaning: “The One who has taken the three steps."
names.commentary: “The One who has taken the three steps." This indicates, the Vamana-incarnation, and how He measured, in just three steps, the entire universe. The jeeva, the limited ego, meaning the seeker, has also to take three steps forward, to reach across the delusion of the three worlds of sleep, dream and waking. The meditator can measure these three "worlds" in three steps and arrive at his own original Real Nature in his inner mystic experience.
names.simple_meaning: “The One who has taken the three steps."

names.short_meaning: The Lord of the three steps—the three steps are waking, dream and deep-sleep
names.commentary: “The Lord of the three steps'—the 'three steps' are waking, dream and deep-sleep. One who is the Witness of the 'three steps' is the Self. It can also mean that One who assumes, in His play, the three qualities of Sattva, Rajas and Tamas-and yet, Himself, is not affected by any one of them.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of the three steps—the three steps are waking, dream and deep-sleep

names.short_meaning: "The Great — Horned."
names.commentary: "The Great — Horned." The term indicates how the Lord in the Fish-incarnation tied the ship to his great horn and sported in the waters of the deluge.
names.simple_meaning: "The Great — Horned."

names.short_meaning: He is the destroyer of the "creation."
names.commentary:
He is the destroyer of the "creation." He is the Creator, in our subjective life, of the inactive (taamasa) and positive (saattvic and raajasa) vāsanās— the sins and the merits. When the merits are more, the Lord provides a heaven for them to exist and when the sins are more, they move into the lower wombs, where sin-vāsanās, too, get exhausted. An individual seeker when he exhausts all the above vāsanās, rises to the realm of the Self and gets totally identified with the Self. Therefore, Śrī Nārāyaṇa is that State Divine, wherein all created vāsanās (kṛta) get destroyed (Anta).

Thus, the end (Anta) of the vāsanās (kṛta) is called "total liberation" (Kritaantam). He who is the giver of the 'krita', Himself is the giver of "total liberation" (Kritaanta-krit)… We find it also interpreted to mean that the Lord is one who has destroyed (Krindanam) Lord Death (Kritaanta) himself. One who is the destroyer 'Kritaanta', in this sense we can take this term as meaning the Lord who has taken the form of Rudra, the Destroyer — Lord Siva.
names.simple_meaning: He is the destroyer of the "creation."

names.short_meaning: One who had manifested as the Great Boar
names.commentary: One who had manifested as the Great Boar. In order to heave up the world from the slush that formed naturally when the waters of the deluge receded. This is the third of the Lord's incarnations.
names.simple_meaning: One who had manifested as the Great Boar

names.short_meaning: One who is to be known (Vid) through the declarations of the Vedānta (Go)
names.commentary: One who is to be known (Vid) through the declarations of the Vedānta (Go). In Viṣṇu Tilaka we read: ‘‘गोभिरेव यतो वेद्यो गोविन्द: समुदाहृत: ।’’ Here, "Gobhih" means the statements and declarations of the Upaniṣads.
names.simple_meaning: The one known through the declarations of the Veda

names.short_meaning: He who has a charming army
names.commentary: He who has a charming army. The army of Viṣṇu is called as His Ganas. They are mainly constituted of the great sages and hence, their compelling enchantment.
names.simple_meaning: He who has a charming army

names.short_meaning: The bright-as-gold armlets
names.commentary: The bright-as-gold armlets. Armlets are ornaments worn on the upper arm covering the shoulder and the top portion of the arm.
names.simple_meaning: The bright-as-gold armlets

names.short_meaning: The mysterious; the Profound
names.commentary: The mysterious; the Profound. Due to the profound nature of the Truth even in the Upaniṣads the essential theme is mysteriously secretive. Therefore, the entire Upanishadic literature is called as “ ture." Viṣṇu is to be realised in the secret chambers of the heart, so He is called as the Supreme "Secret" (Guhya).
names.simple_meaning: The mysterious; the Profound

names.short_meaning: “The Unfathomable.”
names.commentary: “The Unfathomable.” Even the Upaniṣads declare that He is unknown. The limited human intellect cannot apprehend or visualise, or plumb the depth of, or unravel the mystery of His Wisdom, Power, Str or Purity.
names.simple_meaning: “The Unfathomable.”

names.short_meaning: He is impenetrable; Imponderable
names.commentary:
He is impenetrable; Imponderable. We cannot dash into the domain of His Nature Divine. Through surrender alone can we reach the realm of the Self.

“न कर्मणा न प्रजया धनेन त्यागेनैके अमृतत्वमानशुः।” “Not by work, nor by birth, nor by wealth, but by renunciation alone is Immortality attained.” — Kaivalyopaniṣad 1-3.
names.simple_meaning: He is impenetrable; Imponderable

names.short_meaning: The Well-concealed
names.commentary:
The Well-concealed. He is not easily revealed by words. Nor can the sense organs ever recognise Him. All the Upaniṣads repeatedly declare that the Self being the very "subject," the instruments of the body, mind and intellect can never apprehend Him. He can only be apprehended by a steady mind that has been purified by continuous meditation. "Being the hidden nature of all beings he is not manifested."

"When the understanding becomes calm and refined, then in meditation one realises Him, the Absolute." —Mundaka, Ch. III-1-8.

"This Atman is hidden in all beings and does not shine forth." —Katha, Ch. I-iii-12.

“यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते अप्राप्य मनसा सह।” “Whence all speech turns back with the mind without reaching It.” — Taittirīya Upaniṣad II, Brahmānandavallī 4.
names.simple_meaning: The Well-concealed

names.short_meaning: One who is the bearer of the Discus and the Mace
names.commentary:
One who is the bearer of the Discus and the Mace. His Chakra is called Sudarśana: His Gadaa is called Kaumodakī. The ancient Acharyas have declared that the Discus represents the Mind and the Mace represents the Intellect,

“मनस्तत्त्वात्मकं चक्रं बुद्धितत्त्वात्मिकां गदाम्। धारयन् लोकरक्षार्थमुक्तश्चक्रगदाधरः॥” “Holding the discus, the principle of mind, and the mace, the principle of intellect, to protect the universe, He is called Chakragadādharaḥ.”
names.simple_meaning: One who is the bearer of the Discus and the Mace

names.short_meaning: One who is the Creator of the whole universe, the Supreme who is expressing Himself for the apparent function of creating the world of plurality
names.commentary: One who is the Creator of the whole universe, the Supreme who is expressing Himself for the apparent function of creating the world of plurality. The Infinite Truth functioning through the Total — Mind is the Creator — Hiranyagarbha. According to Amarakosha, 'Creator' is called as sraṣṭā (स्रष्टा), Prajaapatih (प्रजापति:) or vedhāḥ (वेधाः).
names.simple_meaning: One who is the Creator of the whole universe, the Supreme who is expressing Himself for the apparent function of creating the world of plurality

names.short_meaning: It is commented upon by some, as one who is beautiful, who has well proportioned limbs
names.commentary:
It is commented upon by some, as one who is beautiful, who has well proportioned limbs. This meaning emphasises the glory and beauty of the form of the enchanting Viṣṇu. The same term can also be interpreted as "Self-instrumental." For the projection of the pluralistic phenomenal world, He has no instrument other than Himself.

The Lord not only creates everything from Himself but He, Himself, is the instrumental cause for the world. We have already indicated earlier that in the making of anything, three causes must come into play, the "material-cause" (mud), the "instrumental-cause" (the pot-maker's wheel) and the "efficient-cause" (the intelligent pot-maker). In the case of the creation of the universe all these three causes are intrinsically the Lord alone. Thus, He is the material, from which He creates the world by Himself. This idea is expressed here when the compelling beauty of the Lord's form is being indicated by the precious term "Self-instrumental"
names.simple_meaning: The beautiful one whose limbs are perfectly proportioned

names.short_meaning: One who is vanquished by none—unconquered—and therefore, the unconquerable in any of His incarnations
names.commentary: One who is vanquished by none—unconquered—and therefore, the unconquerable in any of His incarnations. We never meet Him as vanquished in any of his confrontations with mighty evil.
names.simple_meaning: One who is vanquished by none—unconquered—and therefore, the unconquerable in any of His incarnations

names.short_meaning: One who incarnated in the Yādava tribe as the son of Vasudeva and Devakī
names.commentary: One who incarnated in the Yādava tribe as the son of Vasudeva and Devakī. It is commented upon as 'one who served the Hindu Spiritual World in the form of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipaayana' which is the full name of Vyasa, the author of the Purāṇas. However, Kṛṣṇa also means 'The Dark'; the one great Infinite Consciousness that plays in us constantly, because of which we are aware of our experiences, and yet, never can we directly apprehend this Source of All — Life within ourselves. The Kṛṣṇa is the "unknown factor" that expresses through us—whose manifestations are all our physical, mental and intellectual capabilities. He is, therefore, called as the 'Unknown', the 'Dark'-Kṛṣṇa.
names.simple_meaning: One who incarnated in the Yādava tribe as the son of Vasudeva and Devakī

names.short_meaning: "The Firm."
names.commentary: "The Firm." One who is firm in His convictions, judgements, love and mercy. It is in this sense that the Bhakti Marga describes the Lord often as 'A-dṛḍhaḥ', especially when a sinner prostrates before Him; meaning that in full repentance were a criminal to surrender himself to the Lord's Feet, the Infinite Justice even wavers and becomes anxious to help the sinner out of his mistaken notions and his consequent ugly actions. The Lord is ever vigilant to re-establish such a one in his own wisdom, which is his real nature.
names.simple_meaning: "The Firm."

names.short_meaning: During the great dissolution of the entire universe of names and forms, He, being the one who merges the entire plurality into His own essence—He is called 'Sankarshanah.'
names.commentary: During the great dissolution of the entire universe of names and forms, He, being the one who merges the entire plurality into His own essence—He is called 'Sankarshanah.' When an individual sleeps, his entire world of experiences get absorbed into himself and they all remain in seed condition in the 'Causal-body' as mere vāsanās. One who never falls away from His own essential nature is called 'Achyutah'-one who knows no fall (Chyutih). The one expression used here for the Lord is the combination of both these terms. The Lord Nārāyaṇa who absorbs the whole world into Himself at the time of the deluge. and He who never falls away from His own Real Nature.
names.simple_meaning: The one who draws all into himself yet never falls

names.short_meaning: Since, in the evening, the sun reaches the western horizon (Varuna — Dik), the sun is called varuṇaḥ
names.commentary:
Since, in the evening, the sun reaches the western horizon (Varuna — Dik), the sun is called varuṇaḥ. Also after his day's functioning in the world, in the dusk he gathers his scorching rays unto himself and disappears.

Like the setting sun, the Lord withdraws all the pluralistic world unto Himself. The Eternal Reality, functioning through the sun as the sun's energy and light, is described in the Upaniṣads as the 'Golden One', and hence the appropriateness of using this term varuṇaḥ for Nārāyaṇa. The designation Soorya — Nārāyaṇa is very familiar to the students of Purāṇa.
names.simple_meaning: The evening sun at the western horizon

names.short_meaning: The son of Varunah is called vāruṇaḥ
names.commentary:
The son of Varunah is called vāruṇaḥ. Both Vasishtha and Agastya are traditionally considered as sons of Varunah. Therefore, the term indicates the Lord, who manifested himself as Vasishtha or Agastya. Where-ever there is an explosive expression of any spectacular glory of stupendous achievement, "understand them all as coming out of my glory," says Kṛṣṇa in the Bhagavad Gītā. The term can also be read in some manuscripts as AVaarunah—meaning, according to some commentators, "one whose nature is never subject to veiling."

“यद्यद्विभूतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमदूर्जितमेव वा। तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोंऽशसम्भवम्॥” — Gītā X-41.
names.simple_meaning: The son of Varuṇa

names.short_meaning: The saṃsāra — Vriksha—the Tree of Life
names.commentary:
In the Upaniṣads the world emerging out of the Supreme Brahman is described metaphorically as a 'Tree'; in the Kaṭhopaniṣad and in the Gītā, we read of the saṃsāra-vṛkṣa—the Tree of Life—exhaustively described. In the Purāṇas, again we find, in more than 3 or 4 places, exhaustive descriptions of the world manifested from the Lord as a 'Tree.'

“ऊर्ध्वमूलमधःशाखमश्वत्थं प्राहुरव्ययम्।” — Gītā XV-1.

“ऊर्ध्वमूलोऽवाक्शाख एषोऽश्वत्थः सनातनः।” — Kaṭhopaniṣad II-VI-1.
names.simple_meaning: The saṃsāra — Vriksha—the Tree of Life

names.short_meaning: One who has eyes (Aksha) as beautiful as the lotus flowers (Pushkara); the descriptive epithet: 'Lotus-eyed.'
names.commentary: One who has eyes (Aksha) as beautiful as the lotus flowers (Pushkara); the descriptive epithet: 'Lotus-eyed.' The Sanskrit term 'Pushkara' also means the Universal — Space, thus, it also has the interpretation, "one who is ever pervading all space."
names.simple_meaning: One who has eyes (Aksha) as beautiful as the lotus flowers (Pushkara); the descriptive epithet: 'Lotus-eyed.'

names.short_meaning: “One who has a great mind."
names.commentary: “One who has a great mind." Nārāyaṇa as the Lord (Īśvara) is the Supreme Consciousness functioning through the Total — Mind, and He, with His Mind, creates, sustains and destroys, fulfilling the great game of Samsar, continuously.
names.simple_meaning: “One who has a great mind."

names.short_meaning: One who has all the Six Great Glories—Wealth, Power, dharma, Fame, Character, Knowledge and Dispassion—is called bhagavān
names.commentary:
The word 'Bhaga', according to the Great Viṣṇu Purāṇa means, “One who has all the Six Great Glories—Wealth, Power, dharma, Fame, Character, Knowledge and Dispassion—is called 'bhagavān'.” Again, Viṣṇu Purāṇa says: “He is named bhagavān who knows (a) the beginning and the end, (b) the arrival and the departure of beings, and also (c) vidyā and Avidyaa.” One who has all these Six Glories in Himself alone is Bhagavān and these great mighty powers automatically come to Him, because His equipment is the Total-mind.

“ऐश्वर्यस्य समग्रस्य धर्मस्य यशसः श्रियः। ज्ञानवैराग्ययोश्चैव षण्णां भग इतीरणा॥” — Viṣṇu Purāṇa 6-5-74.

“उत्पत्तिं प्रलयं चैव भूतानामागतिं गतिम्। वेत्ति विद्यामविद्यां च स वाच्यो भगवानिति॥” — Viṣṇu Purāṇa 6-5-78.
names.simple_meaning: The possessor of wealth, power, dharma, fame, character, knowledge, and detachment

names.short_meaning: One who destroys, during the deluge, the Six Glories just mentioned
names.commentary: One who destroys, during the deluge, the Six Glories just mentioned. At this time, the Lord absorbs everything unto Himself, and in this sense the term, "destroyer of all these great glories" (bhagahā) means only a destruction as in the case, say, of Napoleon who, while sleeping, absorbed unto himself all his glories. When thus the Total-mind rests from its self-willed projections, the world of plurality appears to have been absorbed by the Lord unto Himself.
names.simple_meaning: One who destroys, during the deluge, the Six Glories just mentioned

names.short_meaning: "The one who gives delight."
names.commentary: "The one who gives delight." The Lord is Himself Absolute Bliss, and those devotees who move towards Him in pure surrender, come to share His divine nature of All — Bliss. There is a version wherein we read this term as 'Nandee' (नन्दी). Here, too, there is no difference in meaning: Also this term indicates: "Son of Nandagopaala"- Lord Kṛṣṇa—Who was nurtured and tended by Yasodaa and Nandagopaala throughout His childhood.
names.simple_meaning: "The one who gives delight."

names.short_meaning: One who wears always a garland of leaves and flowers named Vaijayantī
names.commentary: One who wears always a garland of leaves and flowers named Vaijayantī. Vaishnavas declare this to represent the subtle aspect of the very five elements themselves, (bhūta-tanmaatraas).
names.simple_meaning: One who wears always a garland of leaves and flowers named Vaijayantī

names.short_meaning: “One who has the plough as His weapon."
names.commentary: “One who has the plough as His weapon." He is the brother of Lord Kṛṣṇa, Balabhadra, who is considered as the eighth Incarnation of Lord Viṣṇu. Even today in our country the farmers repeat Balarama's name while ploughing for a successful cultivation and profitable harvest.
names.simple_meaning: “One who has the plough as His weapon."

names.short_meaning: One who was born as the son of Aditi and Kasyapa as Vāmana, who begged of Emperor Bali three steps of ground and got all the three worlds
names.commentary: One who was born as the son of Aditi and Kasyapa as Vāmana, who begged of Emperor Bali three steps of ground and got all the three worlds.
names.simple_meaning: The son of Aditi

names.short_meaning: "The Supreme who is the resplendence in the Sun."
names.commentary:
"The Supreme who is the resplendence in the Sun." The Atman expressing as the glorious light and energy in the Sun is meditated upon as Lord Viṣṇu. "One must meditate upon Viṣṇu who is adorned fully, holding in His hands the Conch and the Discus, sitting in Padmaasana, enveloped in golden hue, in the centre of the orb of the Sun." The Deity residing in the disc of the Sun is Nārāyaṇa Himself. "Aat"—'from Viṣṇu'; "ityah"—'to be obtained'. From Viṣṇu, salvation is to be obtained and so He is called as Āditya. This interpretation gives us an insight into the meaning of the word Sun, in Sanskrit-'Āditya': "One from whom all creatures have to receive"! The great-grand-giver is the Sun.

ध्येयः सदा सवितृमण्डलमध्यवर्ती नारायणः सरसिजासनसन्निविष्टः। केयूरवान् मकरकुण्डलवान् किरीटी हारी हिरण्मयवपुर्धृतशङ्खचक्रः॥

“One must meditate upon Viṣṇu who is adorned fully, holding in His hands the Conch and the Discus, sitting in Padmaasana, enveloped in golden hue, in the centre of the orb of the Sun.”
names.simple_meaning: "The Supreme who is the resplendence in the Sun."

names.short_meaning: One who calmly endures the pairs-of-opposites
names.commentary: One who calmly endures the pairs-of-opposites. One who is above them, and thus is never influenced by these experiences of the physical and mental realms.
names.simple_meaning: One who calmly endures the pairs-of-opposites

names.short_meaning: The ultimate refuge for all devotees; the best (Highest) destination and at once the noblest path
names.commentary: The ultimate refuge for all devotees; the best (Highest) destination and at once the noblest path. Lord Nārāyaṇa represents the Supreme Brahman, the final state of liberation, and the path to reach. It is also worship of, and meditation upon, Lord Nārāyaṇa. "Gati" (गति) means both the goal and the path. In short, One who is Himself the very essence of spiritual liberation.
names.simple_meaning: The ultimate refuge for all devotees; the best (Highest) destination and at once the noblest path

names.short_meaning: One who has His glorious bow-called "Śārṅga."
names.commentary: One who has His glorious bow—called “Śārṅga.” According to some, it represents the sense organs and their activities.
names.simple_meaning: The bearer of the splendid bow Śārṅga

names.short_meaning: One who has the axe-weapon—called "Parasu."
names.commentary:
One who has the axe-weapon—called "Parasu." The Lord used this weapon in His Incarnation as Parasuraama, the son of Jamadagni. It is endowed with terrible prowess in cutting down the unholy enemies of the nobler life and so it is called as the "Khanda — Parasu."

As such it means 'one who wields the invincible Parasu,'
names.simple_meaning: The bearer of the battle-axe

names.short_meaning: "The one who is merciless towards the unrighteous."
names.commentary: "The one who is merciless towards the unrighteous." Up to a point the Lord is All-mercy— but when He finds that no other method can save the individual, like a surgeon at the operation theatre. He appears to be relentless-merciless.
names.simple_meaning: "The one who is merciless towards the unrighteous."

names.short_meaning: One who lavishly gives wealth asked for by His devotees
names.commentary: One who lavishly gives wealth asked for by His devotees. According to Vvasa, Lord Viṣṇu gives to his true devotees the wealth of the śāstra knowledge—the deeper and clearer understanding of the Science of Reality.
names.simple_meaning: One who lavishly gives wealth asked for by His devotees

names.short_meaning: "The Sky-reaching."
names.commentary: "The Sky-reaching." The Lord who revealed His Universal Form to Ariuna in the Bhagavad Gītā.
names.simple_meaning: "The Sky-reaching."

names.short_meaning: When considered as one word it means: "One who creates many omniscient men of wisdom."
names.commentary:
When considered as one word it means: "One who creates many omniscient men of wisdom." One who encourages the spread of knowledge and thus turns out many men of wisdom and clearer understanding of life and the world. Or taken as two words its interpretation can mean: "One who is Omniscient and Vyasa." This would mean, "The Lord who has expressed Himself as Śrī Veda Vyasa." Vyasa is the poet-philosopher who codified, compiled and edited the Vedas and published them in four volumes—Rig Veda, with its 21 branches; Yajur Veda, with its 101 branches: Sāma Veda, with its 1000 branches and the Atharvana Veda, with its 9 branches (or Saakhaas). He is the one who gave us the 18 Purāṇas and the Brahmasootras.

Hence he is called: "The Omniscient Vvasa."
names.simple_meaning: The all-seeing Vyāsa who arranged the Vedas

names.short_meaning: One who is a master of all knowledge (vidyās) and who is unborn through a mother's womb
names.commentary: One who is a master of all knowledge (vidyās) and who is unborn through a mother's womb.
names.simple_meaning: One who is a master of all knowledge (vidyās) and who is unborn through a mother's womb

names.short_meaning: "One who has been glorified by the three Sāmans."
names.commentary: "One who has been glorified by the three Sāmans." 'Sāma' means divine songs—hence, Veda. The one who has been praised by the singers of the Sāma — Veda, those called as the Devas, the Vratas and the Sagmans
names.simple_meaning: "One who has been glorified by the three Sāmans."

names.short_meaning: "The singer of the Sāman songs."
names.commentary: "The singer of the Sāman songs." One who performs the actions prescribed in the Sāma Veda and who invokes the Lord is called, in Vedic terminology. the 'Udgaataa'.
names.simple_meaning: "The singer of the Sāman songs."

names.short_meaning: The Lord is the sāma Veda
names.commentary:
The Lord is the sāma Veda. This is to indicate the sacredness of the very Book. Lord Kṛṣṇa has confessed in the Gītā: "Of Vedas I am the sāma Veda."

"वेदानां सामवेदोऽस्मि।" (Vedaanaam Saamavedosmi)—Gītā X-22.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord is the sāma Veda

names.short_meaning: The Lord is of the very nature of "Ever-liberated, Ever-free."
names.commentary: The Lord is of the very nature of "Ever-liberated, Ever-free." There is no trace of imperfection and sorrow in Him whose nature is, All — Bliss.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord is of the very nature of "Ever-liberated, Ever-free."

names.short_meaning: ‘bheṣajaṃ’ means ‘medicine.'
names.commentary: ‘bheṣajaṃ’ means ‘medicine.' Hence, He who is the very specific cure for the disease of Samsar (change, becoming).
names.simple_meaning: The medicine for worldly suffering

names.short_meaning: One who is the 'Physician,' who is the 'cure' for the disease of Samsar
names.commentary: One who is the 'Physician,' who is the 'cure' for the disease of Samsar. Or it can also mean that the Lord manifested during the "churning of the Milky Ocean" as the Deity of Medicine, holding the pot of Amrita in His hand - The Lord Dhanvantari. In Indian systems of Medicines. He is considered as the presiding Deity of the Medical Sciences. Viṣṇu manifested as this Lord of Doctors, whereupon this name for Him: "Doctor" (bhiṣak).
names.simple_meaning: One who is the 'Physician,' who is the 'cure' for the disease of Samsar

names.short_meaning: Lord is the institutor of the fourth stage of life (Aasrama) called 'saṃnyāsa' which is meant for those who walk the path of total renunciation
names.commentary: Lord is the institutor of the fourth stage of life (Aasrama) called 'saṃnyāsa' which is meant for those who walk the path of total renunciation. The One who, in His Infinite Grace, gives the needed qualifications unavoidable for saṃnyāsa.
names.simple_meaning: The institutor of renunciation

names.short_meaning: "The Calm."
names.commentary:
"The Calm." One who exists without the mind running out into the passions of the sense-organs. In saṃnyāsa. He teaches the life of calmness and quietude and in the accumulated inner peace, the final experience is gained. The Smriti prescribes the duties of the four stages as: "The duty of the 'Brahmachari' is service; for the 'Householder', charity: for the 'Forest-dweller' is the duty of restraint, and for the 'Samnyaasin' 'Calmness'. saṃnyāsa without Sama is inconceivable and this 'Calmness' is His nature.

“यतीनां प्रशमो धर्मो नियमो वनवासिनाम्। दानमेव गृहस्थानां शुश्रूषा ब्रह्मचारिणाम्॥” — Smṛti.
names.simple_meaning: "The Calm."

names.short_meaning: One who is quiet within, as in Him the sense-organs are perfectly controlled
names.commentary:
One who is quiet within, as in Him the sense-organs are perfectly controlled. The Upaniṣads glorify the Supreme State as actionless (निष्कियं), partless (निष्कलं), peaceful (शान्तं). This is a declaration from Svetaasvatara Upaniṣad.

“निष्कलं निष्क्रियं शान्तं निरवद्यं निरञ्जनम्।” — Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad VI-19.
names.simple_meaning: One who is quiet within, as in Him the sense-organs are perfectly controlled

names.short_meaning: The Abode of all beings, not only while living, but during the Pralaya (deluge)
names.commentary: The Abode of all beings, not only while living, but during the Pralaya (deluge). During this Cosmic dissolution, the entire living creatures merge back into their vāsanās, (seed-form), and remain in Him. Therefore, He is called, "The Abode of the Universe."
names.simple_meaning: The Abode of all beings, not only while living, but during the Pralaya (deluge)

names.short_meaning: "One whose very nature is Peace."
names.commentary: "One whose very nature is Peace." Agitations are caused by desires and the consequent temptations to strive for, acquire and indulge in them. In the All — Full, there is no desire, hence He need not seek His fulfilment among the perishable objects of the universe, and so He is Peace.
names.simple_meaning: "One whose very nature is Peace."

names.short_meaning: The Supreme Goal is Nārāyaṇa
names.commentary:
The Supreme Goal is Nārāyaṇa. After reaching Him there is no return. In short. the term indicates that Nārāyaṇa is the way to the Supreme Liberation (mokṣa).

"यद्गत्वा न निवर्तन्ते तद्धाम परमं मम।" (Yadgatvaa na nivartante Tat-dhaama paramam mama.) "To which having gone they return not; that is My Supreme Abode." —Gītā XV-6.
names.simple_meaning: The Supreme Goal is Nārāyaṇa

names.short_meaning: One who has the most beautiful form
names.commentary: One who has the most beautiful form. That one who is enchanting, most handsome.
names.simple_meaning: One who has the most beautiful form

names.short_meaning: Nārāyaṇa dispenses that Peace which puts an end to likes and dislikes (rāga — dveṣa)
names.commentary: Nārāyaṇa dispenses that Peace which puts an end to likes and dislikes (rāga — dveṣa). He is the Ope who cleanses the mind of His devotees and gives to each the inner Peace and Joy.
names.simple_meaning: Nārāyaṇa dispenses that Peace which puts an end to likes and dislikes (rāga — dveṣa)

names.short_meaning: "The Creator of all beings."
names.commentary: "The Creator of all beings." In the beginning, He has created all from Himself as the Great Five Elements: (Viranchi).
names.simple_meaning: "The Creator of all beings."

names.short_meaning: The reveller in the Earth
names.commentary: The reveller in the Earth. The term 'Ķu' (कु) means Earth. Therefore, the term means "He who delights in the Earth."
names.simple_meaning: The reveller in the Earth

names.short_meaning: He who reclines in the waters (Kuvala)
names.commentary: He who reclines in the waters (Kuvala). Waters surround the earth, thus it is called as Kuvala. The term can also mean the 'Crawler'-meaning Serpent. In this sense it indicates—"Sarpa — Saaye": "One who reclines upon the Great Sesha"—the Divine "Sesha — Saaye."
names.simple_meaning: He who reclines in the waters (Kuvala)

names.short_meaning: One who does the Cow-welfare-work, always
names.commentary:
One who does the Cow-welfare-work, always. Śrī Kṛṣṇa, through many incidents, helps to develop and conserve the sacred animal, Cow, for, the very existence of Bharat's dispensation depends upon the Cow; the agriculture being essentially Cow-centred. 'Go' also means Earth. Thus: "One who saved the world" from the materialists and their designs of excesses and imperfect vision.

One who protects against the irresponsible havoc, for example, of Ravana and others; all inimical to the genius of the natural Bhaarateeya Samskriti. "तस्मान्मच्छरणं गोष्ठं मन्नाथं मत्परिग्रहम् ।

गोपाये स्वात्मयोगेन सोऽयं मे व्रत आहितः ॥" (Tasmaat-mat-saranam goshtham mannaatham matparigraham Gopaaye svaatmayogena soyam me vrata aahitah. "As their sole protector it is my vow to guard the abode of cattle taken refuge in me, through my power of yoga."—Bhaagavatam.
names.simple_meaning: One who does the Cow-welfare-work, always

names.short_meaning: "The husband of the Earth."
names.commentary: "The husband of the Earth." Or, One who is the Lord protecting all those who are weary of their samsaaric life of passions and desires. Such ones, exhausted by grazing in the pastures of dissipation and enervated from the world of happenings, are comparable to cows. Hence, Nārāyaṇa is called here as the "Lord of the Cows",—'Gopaala.' 'Go' also may be interpreted as 'sense-organs'. In this way the term suggests "Lord of the Sense — Organs," Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Self
names.simple_meaning: "The husband of the Earth."

names.short_meaning: The root Gup has two meanings: to protect; to veil
names.commentary: The root 'Gup' (गुप) has two meanings: to protect; to veil. Thus 'goptā' can imply "One who protects the universe" or "One who, by His māyā, veils the glory of the Divine Self within."
names.simple_meaning: The protector who also veils himself

names.short_meaning: One whose eyes rain fulfilment of all desires of His devotees
names.commentary: One whose eyes rain fulfilment of all desires of His devotees. He sees the unexpressed desires of His devotees and fulfils them easily. Or it can be taken that Śrī Nārāyaṇa is "One whose eyes are dharma Itself"; meaning, One who sees righteousness clearly and continuously. If one wants to see clearly righteousness, he must cultivate and develop the Nārāyaṇa vision.
names.simple_meaning: One whose eyes rain fulfilment of all desires of His devotees

names.short_meaning: Viṣṇu delights in dharma
names.commentary: Viṣṇu delights in dharma. ‘vṛṣa’ means ‘dharma,’ so the term can be dissolved as "One who delights in dharma" (वृष: प्रियो यस्य सः). Or it can signify, "One who is beloved of the virtuous, the Good."
names.simple_meaning: Viṣṇu delights in dharma

names.short_meaning: "One who never knows retreat."
names.commentary: "One who never knows retreat." During the clashes between the Good (Devas) and the Bad (Asuras), Nārāyaṇa never retreats. He is One Who never turns back from dharma; for He is its friend and protector.
names.simple_meaning: "One who never knows retreat."

names.short_meaning: One who is fully restrained from all sense indulgences
names.commentary: One who is fully restrained from all sense indulgences. So long as the equipments of our experiences—the Body, Mind and Intellect—are roaming about in their pleasures—among objects, emotions and thoughts—our attention is dissipated and is not available for the contemplation of the Higher, the Self. Nārāyaṇa is the Atman in all, and to reach Him we have to retire from the fields of our indulgences. Hence, He is indicated as the "Restrained — Self."
names.simple_meaning: One who is fully restrained from all sense indulgences

names.short_meaning: The One who absorbs unto Himself the entire universe of multiplicity during the dissolution—the "Involver."
names.commentary: The One who absorbs unto Himself the entire universe of multiplicity during the dissolution—the "Involver." Nārāyaṇa presides over not only the evolution but also is the controller at the involution. In some readings, we find this term as "Asamksheptaa"—meaning "One who never abandons His devotees."
names.simple_meaning: The One who absorbs unto Himself the entire universe of multiplicity during the dissolution—the "Involver."

names.short_meaning: "The doer of Good"; One who protects and guides the devotees
names.commentary:
"The doer of Good"; One who protects and guides the devotees. "kṣema" signifies protecting what has been gained, and it includes "Yoga" also, meaning "acquiring things not yet gained." In Gītā, Lord Kṛṣṇa promises that "I shall govern both your 'Yoga' and 'kṣema' when you are a true devotee."

“तेषां नित्याभियुक्तानां योगक्षेमं वहाम्यहम्।” — Gītā IX-22.
names.simple_meaning: "The doer of Good"; One who protects and guides the devotees

names.short_meaning: Lord Nārāyaṇa is adored here as śivaḥ and, at the same time, all Vaishnavites repeat Viṣṇusahasranāma
names.commentary:
Lord Nārāyaṇa is adored here as śivaḥ and, at the same time, all Vaishnavites repeat Viṣṇusahasranāma. Human prejudices have no logic or reason. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is Siva (auspiciousness) and there is no difference between the two. "I am the dweller of Vaikuntha, Viṣṇu.

Between us there is no difference," so says Lord Siva Himself. Viṣṇu is the "Purifier" (Siva), as His names, when chanted, and His form-divine, when meditated upon, become a means of quietening the mind and sharpening our perceptions of the subtler and the transcendental.

“वैकुण्ठोऽहमहं विष्णुर्नावयोरस्ति वै भिदा।”
names.simple_meaning: Lord Nārāyaṇa is adored here as śivaḥ and, at the same time, all Vaishnavites repeat Viṣṇusahasranāma

names.short_meaning: One who has the mark
names.commentary:
One who has the mark, Sreevatsa, upon His divine and sacred chest.

The great Rishies once wanted to know who is great among the Trinity. Bhrigu who was deputed for this, and who failed to assess Brahmaa and Siva as the greatest, went to Vaikuntha. Seeing Viṣṇu in His Yoga Nidraa, he deliberately kicked Him on the chest. Waking up suddenly, the Lord regretted that he had been asleep on Bhrigu’s arrival and apologetically began massaging the Sage’s foot, hoping that his holy soft foot which could destroy the sins of the seekers had not been hurt. Since by the touch of the divine foot His sins are destroyed, Bhagavān says, He will ever bear the mark of the sage’s foot as SREE on His chest.

—Sreemad Bhagavatam, 10th Skandhu.
names.simple_meaning: One who has the mark

names.short_meaning: The Abode of Śrī; the dwelling place of Mother Lakṣmī
names.commentary: The Abode of Śrī; the dwelling place of Mother Lakṣmī. This term is dissolved as श्री वसत्यस्मिन्निति श्रीवासः “Śrī”—all glory and riches—ever dwell in His bosom of love and beauty.
names.simple_meaning: The Abode of Śrī; the dwelling place of Mother Lakṣmī

names.short_meaning: The Lord of Goddess Lakṣmī
names.commentary:
The Lord of Goddess Lakṣmī. During the great churning of the Ocean of Milk, holding a lotus in hand, there rose Lakṣmī from it, and She chose, among all gods, Lord Viṣṇu as Her Beloved Husband. Hence Nārāyaṇa is Śrī — Patih, the Lord of Śrī. The Svetasvatara Upaniṣad says: "The Supreme śakti of Him is declared to be various." Śrī represents the Energy (parā śakti) in the universe.

Lord Nārāyaṇa is the One Vital Truth that functions through the parā śakti and gives Her the dynamism to act and to accomplish.

“परास्य शक्तिर्विविधैव श्रूयते।” — Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad VI-8.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of Goddess Lakṣmī

names.short_meaning: The best among those who have glory-in-life, (Śrī), is Nārāyaṇa
names.commentary:
The best among those who have glory-in-life, (Śrī), is Nārāyaṇa. Taittirīya Braahmana says, "The Ric, Yajus and Sāman are the imperishable wealth of the wise", so Śrī has been interpreted here to mean the Vedas, Lord Nārāyaṇa is the One who is the Best among those who know the 'Books'; He being the very Infinite Reality that is the one theme of all the Vedas.

Also Varah (बर:) can mean "One Who blesses" and thus the term under discussion yields the meaning, "Viṣṇu, Who is the Lord That blesses all great students of the Vedas."

Taittirīya Brāhmaṇa 1-2-1.
names.simple_meaning: The best among those who have glory-in-life, (Śrī), is Nārāyaṇa

names.short_meaning: One who gives Śrī to all His sincere and dedicated devotees
names.commentary: One who gives Śrī to all His sincere and dedicated devotees. Nārāyaṇa provides wealth for all His ardent devotees. He is the River of Knowledge and Joy for all devoted hearts which are surrendered to Him.
names.simple_meaning: One who gives Śrī to all His sincere and dedicated devotees

names.short_meaning: The Lord of the Goddess of Wealth, Śrī—Mahalakshmi
names.commentary: The Lord of the Goddess of Wealth, Śrī—Mahalakshmi. Her wealth is 'the ability to nourish.' Thus She gives to the striving devotee, the mighty and noble virtues, his inner wealth.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of the Goddess of Wealth, Śrī—Mahalakshmi

names.short_meaning: One who dwells and manifests in the good people
names.commentary: One who dwells and manifests in the good people. Here the word Śrī is to be understood as "those who have Śrī in them." The One Who abides in purified hearts—wherein the passions and lusts have been removed and peace, joy, devotion and understanding have arrived. In such people the Self comes to shine all by Itself.
names.simple_meaning: One who dwells and manifests in the good people

names.short_meaning: One Who is the treasure-house (Nidhih) of Śrī
names.commentary: One Who is the treasure-house (Nidhih) of Śrī. Viṣṇu, being the All — Full and Perfect. all glories draw themselves from Him alone, Even Śrī — māyā —can play Her games only when She draws Her vitality from Nārāyaṇa, the Self.
names.simple_meaning: One Who is the treasure-house (Nidhih) of Śrī

names.short_meaning: "One Who is a Distributor of Śrī."
names.commentary: "One Who is a Distributor of Śrī." Viṣṇu provides each, according to his merit, the wealth, both inner and outer. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the Law behind actions and so He is the Dispenser of the fruitsof-actions (कर्मफलदाता).
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is a Distributor of Śrī."

names.short_meaning: Lord always carries Śrī in His bosom
names.commentary: Lord always carries Śrī in His bosom. In short, Atman, the Self, is never divorced from Its omnipotence and All — Fullness.
names.simple_meaning: Lord always carries Śrī in His bosom

names.short_meaning: One Who confers Śrī upon His devotees
names.commentary:
One Who confers Śrī upon His devotees who remember Him continuously, reflect upon His nature and meditate upon His Glories.

श्रियं करोति इति श्रीकरः (Śriyaṃ karoti iti Śrīkaraḥ)—“One Who bestows Auspiciousness.”
names.simple_meaning: One Who confers Śrī upon His devotees

names.short_meaning: Nārāyaṇa is mokṣa—Liberation
names.commentary: Nārāyaṇa is mokṣa—Liberation. He is the Way and the Goal. He gives to His devotees the total liberation from all their physical passions, emotional agitations and intellectual restlessnesses.
names.simple_meaning: Nārāyaṇa is mokṣa—Liberation

names.short_meaning: One Who possesses all Glories, Riches, Capacities and Beauties
names.commentary: One Who possesses all Glories, Riches, Capacities and Beauties. He Who is the owner of all Śrī: the abode of all Its Splendour.
names.simple_meaning: One Who possesses all Glories, Riches, Capacities and Beauties

names.short_meaning: The Shelter for the three worlds
names.commentary: The Shelter for the three worlds. The Substratum (आश्रय:) for the three worlds-of-experiences (waking, dream and deep-sleep). If the Self, the Consciousness, were not in us, no experience would ever be ours. Nārāyaṇa is this "objectless awareness."
names.simple_meaning: The Shelter for the three worlds

names.short_meaning: Brilliantly "Beautiful — Eyed" is Viṣṇu
names.commentary:
Brilliantly "Beautiful — Eyed" is Viṣṇu.

शोमने पुण्डरीकाभे अक्षिणी अस्य इति स्वक्षः। (Sobhane pundareekaabhe akshinee asya iti svakshah.) His eyes are compared to the petals of the lotus flower which is supremely beautiful and symbolic of knowledge. His eyes are beautiful with the brilliancy of knowledge.
names.simple_meaning: Brilliantly "Beautiful — Eyed" is Viṣṇu

names.short_meaning: "Beautiful — Limbed."
names.commentary: "Beautiful — Limbed." Most handsome form, captivating the hearts of all His loving devotees.
names.simple_meaning: "Beautiful — Limbed."

names.short_meaning: One Who divides Himself into the infinite jīvas, manifesting through the different equipments and experiences in all of them
names.commentary: One Who divides Himself into the infinite jīvas, manifesting through the different equipments and experiences in all of them. "Of infinite varieties of Joys": gained through the individual equipments from each one's appointed field of things and beings.
names.simple_meaning: One Who divides Himself into the infinite jīvas, manifesting through the different equipments and experiences in all of them

names.short_meaning: “Ínfinite Bliss” is the nature of Viṣṇu as the Supreme Self
names.commentary: “Ínfinite Bliss” is the nature of Viṣṇu as the Supreme Self. Thus by this term, nandiḥ, He is called.
names.simple_meaning: “Ínfinite Bliss” is the nature of Viṣṇu as the Supreme Self

names.short_meaning: The Lord of the luminaries in the Cosmos is Nārāyaṇa
names.commentary:
The Lord of the luminaries in the Cosmos is Nārāyaṇa. He, as the Self, gives light to all brilliant things in life. The Sun, itself, receives its light borrowed from the Infinite, Ever — Effulgent Self.

Kaṭhopaniṣad describing the Self as the Light of Consciousness declares, "When He shines all else shines after Him."

"तमेव भान्तमनभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति ।" (Tameva bhaantamanubhaati sarvam tasya bhaasaa sarvamidam vibhaati.) "When He shines, everything shines after him; by His light, all these shine."

-Katha II-V-15.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord of the luminaries in the Cosmos is Nārāyaṇa

names.short_meaning: One Who has conquered the sense-organs
names.commentary: One Who has conquered the sense-organs. That devotee who is no more a slave to his sense-organs comes to experience the necessary mental quiet with which Nārāyaṇa, the Self, can be apprehended.
names.simple_meaning: One Who has conquered the sense-organs

names.short_meaning: One Who has come to live under the command of the Higher Self or One Who is ever available for devotees to command in love
names.commentary:
One Who has come to live under the command of the Higher Self or One Who is ever available for devotees to command in love. Some read this as "A-Vidheya — Atmaa"—in which case it declares that Nārāyaṇa is "One Who is of Unfathomable Nature — Divine."

One Who obeys none, but all obey His Will is "A-vidheyātmā."
names.simple_meaning: One Who has come to live under the command of the Higher Self or One Who is ever available for devotees to command in love

names.short_meaning: Of Pure Fame is Nārāyaṇa
names.commentary: Of Pure Fame is Nārāyaṇa. He is the husband of Śrī and therefore He is famous.
names.simple_meaning: Of Pure Fame is Nārāyaṇa

names.short_meaning: One, whose doubts are ever at rest, or solved
names.commentary:
One, whose doubts are ever at rest, or solved. Doubts regarding the Supreme can be only so long as we try to experience and comprehend Him with our Intellect. He is the very subjective vitality in the Intellect. So, on transcending the Intellect, the seeker can "become" the Self in a non-mediate experience, intimate and immediate. Once having become the Self, there cannot be any spiritual doubts. Therefore Nārāyaṇa, the Self, is known as "The One in Whom all doubts are resolved." In Gītā, Arjuna admits that all his doubts were cleared.

“स्थितोऽस्मि गतसन्देहः करिष्ये वचनं तव।” “I am firm; my doubts are gone. I will do according to your word.” — Gītā XVIII-73.
names.simple_meaning: One, whose doubts are ever at rest, or solved

names.short_meaning: “The Great Transcendent.”He is the Infinite beyond all finitude, beyond all limitations and change, and therefore, beyond decay
names.commentary: “The Great Transcendent.” He is the Infinite beyond all finitude, beyond all limitations and change, and therefore, beyond decay. Transcending all equipments of our experiences, as the Self in all, Śrī Nārāyaṇa revels as the Immutable Transcendental Reality, the sole substratum for the entire universe of forms and actions.
names.simple_meaning: “The Great Transcendent.”He is the Infinite beyond all finitude, beyond all limitations and change, and therefore, beyond decay

names.short_meaning: "One Who has eyes everywhere."
names.commentary:
"One Who has eyes everywhere." Gītā declares Truth, the Pure Consciousness, as "Hands and legs everywhere, eyes-face-mouth everywhere." Viṣṇu, as the Consciousness, is the One Self That sees through all eyes in the world, hence He, through all eyes, sees everywhere at all times. If He is not, the eyes are blind; when He is the indweller, the eyes then see—therefore.

all eyes are only His.

“सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्।” — Gītā XIII-14.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has eyes everywhere."

names.short_meaning: "One Who has none to lord over Him."
names.commentary:
"One Who has none to lord over Him." The Supreme Lord is He. Mahanarayana upanishad says, "None rules over Him."

न विद्यते अस्य ईश इति अनीशः (Na vidyate asya īśa iti Anīśaḥ).

“न तस्येशः कश्चन।” — Nārāyaṇopaniṣad 1.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has none to lord over Him."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is ever Eternal and Stable"-never changing, thus permanent (Eternal) and ever-the-same (Stable)
names.commentary: "One Who is ever Eternal and Stable"-never changing, thus permanent (Eternal) and ever-the-same (Stable). The body changes, the mind modifies, the intellect grows into new dimensions—but the Consciousness that illumines them all with Its Light of Knowledge is ever-the-same (स्थिर:) through childhood, through youth, in middle years and old-age. It is the Changeless throughout, hence Eternal (शाइवत:) and ever-the-same without any change (स्थिर:).
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is ever Eternal and Stable"-never changing, thus permanent (Eternal) and ever-the-same (Stable)

names.short_meaning: "Resting on the Earth" is the word-meaning of this term, so it may signify One Who rested on the shores of the ocean, on His Way to Lankareferring to Śrī Ramachandraji
names.commentary:
"Resting on the Earth" is the word-meaning of this term, so it may signify One Who rested on the shores of the ocean, on His Way to Lanka—referring to Śrī Ramachandraji. Or, one who slept (on) the Earth—meaning the Lord is Bhoo — Pati, the Husband of the Mother Earth. Or, its intention may also be: "One in whom the world rests" at the time of dissolution.

भूः शेते अस्मिन् इति भूशयः (Bhūḥ śete asmin iti Bhūśayaḥ).
names.simple_meaning: Rāma resting upon the earth beside the ocean

names.short_meaning: One Who adorns the world: physically with the infinite beauties of His Creation
names.commentary:
"One Who adorns the world": physically with the infinite beauties of His Creation; emotionally He gives love and other finer instincts, and intellectually He is the One behind all great, noble and beautiful thoughts which have enriched human life, history and culture.

Lord Nārāyaṇa, in His various Incarnations, has also glorified the world.
names.simple_meaning: One Who adorns the world: physically with the infinite beauties of His Creation

names.short_meaning: One Who is the Pure “BE”-ness or Existence
names.commentary:
One Who is the Pure “BE”-ness (सत्तामात्र:) or Existence. “Bhooti” also means Glories (Aisvarya), so He is One Who is the treasure-house of all Glories.

“विभूतिभूतिरैश्वर्ये।” — Amara Kośa.
names.simple_meaning: One Who is the Pure “BE”-ness or Existence

names.short_meaning: Nārāyaṇa is sorrow-less; griefless
names.commentary: Nārāyaṇa is sorrow-less; griefless. He is the Self, transcending all matter vestures. At the body-mind-intellect level there are agitations and so there are sorrows. He is beyond them all, so He, as the Absolute Reality, is indicated as All — Blissful. Disturbances of sorrow or grief can never molest His nature of Infinite Bliss—ever contented, ever desire-less.
names.simple_meaning: Nārāyaṇa is sorrow-less; griefless

names.short_meaning: The destroyer of all sorrows for His devotees
names.commentary:
The destroyer of all sorrows for His devotees. One Who lifts the suffering ego-sense out of its meaningless identification with the changing, pain-breeding, equipments and gives it the true wisdom of Its Divine Nature. To those who truly worship "To them I shall be, err long, a Saviour from the Ocean of Samsar", promises Lord Kṛṣṇa in the Bhāgavata Gītā.

“तेषामहं समुद्धर्ता मृत्युसंसारसागरात्। भवामि न चिरात्पार्थ मय्यावेशितचेतसाम्॥” — Gītā XII-7.
names.simple_meaning: The destroyer of all sorrows for His devotees

names.short_meaning: “The Effulgent.”
names.commentary:
“The Effulgent.” As Pure Consciousness, Nārāyaṇa is the Source of all Light.

“ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परमुच्यते।” — Gītā XIII-17.

The Kaṭhopaniṣad confirms this when it declares, “There, neither the sun nor the moon, nor the stars nor the lightning, has any effulgence; how then can this Fire-light illumine It? By Its Light alone, all else in the world is illumined.”

“न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्युतो भान्ति कुतोऽयमग्निः। तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति॥” — Kaṭhopaniṣad II-5-15.
names.simple_meaning: “The Effulgent.”

names.short_meaning: One who is constantly worshipped by His devotees
names.commentary: One who is constantly worshipped by His devotees. Even Brahmaaii (The Creator) and Siva (The Destroyer) are worshipping Śrī Nārāyaṇa (The Preserver). Hence this term, "The Worshipped" for Lord Viṣṇu
names.simple_meaning: One who is constantly worshipped by His devotees

names.short_meaning: “The pot.”
names.commentary: “The pot.” The Lord, the Self, is called as “the pot” because just as things are contained within a pot, so the whole universe rests within Him, the "Container" and "Sustainer." Everything and every happening is within Him alone.
names.simple_meaning: “The pot.”

names.short_meaning: "One Who has the purest Soul."
names.commentary:
"One Who has the purest Soul." When the Self is cleansed of all passions and thought agitations, in that uncontaminated purity It is realised. Therefore, the Lord, the Self, is called the Pure Atman, completely bereft of all equipments and their passions, all disturbances from desire. One Who is beyond the "Three guṇas."

Trigunaateetah, meaning one who transcends all the vāsanās that generate the three moods constituting the entire phenomenon. Maavaa.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has the purest Soul."

names.short_meaning: "The Great Purifier."
names.commentary:
"The Great Purifier." The One, meditating upon Whom all vāsanās get exhausted and the personality purified from these desires, becomes free of all its accustomed, existent agitations. He Who is the very Source of Purity; Who lends purity even to the sacred-places.

By remembering Him, the human heart becomes cleansed of its sins, immaculately swept of all consequent feelings of restlessness.
names.simple_meaning: "The Great Purifier."

names.short_meaning: -Of the four manifestations (vyūhas) of Viṣṇu, the Aniruddha manifestation is indicated here
names.commentary: Of the four manifestations (vyūhas) of Viṣṇu, the Aniruddha manifestation is indicated here. The four vyūhas are: (1) Vaasudevah (वासुदेवः); (2) Samkarshanah (संकर्षणः); (3) Pradyumnah (प्रद्युम्नः); and (4) Aniruddhaḥ (अनिरुद्धः). The term can also mean “He Who is invincible by any of His enemies.”
names.simple_meaning: -Of the four manifestations (vyūhas) of Viṣṇu, the Aniruddha manifestation is indicated here

names.short_meaning: One Who is never challenged by any enemies and Who has no enemies to even threaten Him
names.commentary:
One Who is never challenged by any enemies and Who has no enemies to even threaten Him. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is without enemies; in His loving Presence they are vanguished.

न विद्यते प्रतिरथः—अप्रतिरथः (Na vidyate pratirathaḥ—Apratirathaḥ).
names.simple_meaning: One Who is never challenged by any enemies and Who has no enemies to even threaten Him

names.short_meaning: "Very Rich."
names.commentary: "Very Rich." Lord is Lakṣmī — Pati and, in His benevolence, He gives riches and mighty glory to His devotees. pradyumnaḥ can also be the third of His four manifestations as Vvoohas.
names.simple_meaning: "Very Rich."

names.short_meaning: Of immeasurable Prowess is Śrī Nārāyaṇa
names.commentary: Of immeasurable Prowess is Śrī Nārāyaṇa. The Self, the Supreme, is Omnipotent and none can stand against Him. It can also mean, "One Who has un-measurable steps" exhibited in His Divine performance in His Vamana Incarnation.
names.simple_meaning: Of immeasurable Prowess is Śrī Nārāyaṇa

names.short_meaning: The slayer of the Asura, kālanemi
names.commentary: The slayer of the Asura, kālanemi. "kāla" means 'Time.' The Self is the 'destroyer of time' as It is beyond the intellect and 'time' is but a concept of the intellect only.
names.simple_meaning: The slayer of the Asura, kālanemi

names.short_meaning: "The Heroic Victor."
names.commentary: "The Heroic Victor." One Who is ever victorious.
names.simple_meaning: "The Heroic Victor."

names.short_meaning: Born in the Soorasena-clan, in Jagannaath—which, in the Purāṇas, is called the Utkala country
names.commentary: Born in the Soorasena-clan, in Jagannaath—which, in the Purāṇas, is called the Utkala country. Also, Sauri can indicate the One who has invincible prowess always.
names.simple_meaning: Kṛṣṇa of the Śūrasena clan

names.short_meaning: “The Lord of the valiant.”
names.commentary: “The Lord of the valiant.” Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the fountain-head of irresistible might. He is invoked by the victorious, and is the Source of strength from which even Indra and others draw their vigour.
names.simple_meaning: “The Lord of the valiant.”

names.short_meaning: "The Reality, the Self of the three worlds."
names.commentary: "The Reality, the Self of the three worlds." The 'three-worlds' are the three 'fields of, experiences': the waking, the dream and the deep-sleep. As the Pure Consciousness, in the Light of which the waker-dreamer-sleeper comes to experience all the 'three-worlds,' the Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa is called "The Atman of the three-worlds."
names.simple_meaning: "The Reality, the Self of the three worlds."

names.short_meaning: "The Lord of the three-worlds."
names.commentary: "The Lord of the three-worlds." Lord is One in Whose presence all activities take place; in Whose absence all activities cease. He is called the Lord, the Great Proprietor. When life, the Self, manifests in a body, all experiences take place; when life is extinct, all activities cease. Hence Lord Nārāyaṇa is the Self, the spark of Existence in all creatures
names.simple_meaning: "The Lord of the three-worlds."

names.short_meaning: Generally it is meant to describe Lord Kṛṣṇa as "One Who has long hairs."
names.commentary:
Generally it is meant to describe Lord Kṛṣṇa as "One Who has long hairs." But Kesas are the rays of the Lord that illumine the Sun, Moon and such other effulgent things of the Cosmos. "The rays of Mine that illumine (the Sun, etc.) are called Kesas. Therefore, the wise Brahmins call Me, Kesava.” Also ‘Ka’ means Brahmaa, the Creator and 'Eesa' means Siva, the Destroyer. Both of them have sprung from Viṣṇu, the Preserver, hence He is called keśavaḥ.

Mahābhārata, Śānti Parva 342-49.
names.simple_meaning: The long-haired Kṛṣṇa

names.short_meaning: One Who destroyed the Asura called Kesi
names.commentary: One Who destroyed the Asura called Kesi
names.simple_meaning: The slayer of the demon Keśī

names.short_meaning: The Lord is called "The Destroyer."
names.commentary: The Lord is called "The Destroyer." He it is Who destroys the false values and the inner conflicts created by man in his own life and in his consequent discordant contact with the world around him. These confusions and sorrows created by man, for man in life, due to his own ignorance of his own divine nature, is called saṃsāra. Lord Nārāyaṇa is the Destroyer of this Samsara-sorrows in His devotees.
names.simple_meaning: The destroyer who removes sorrow and sin

names.short_meaning: “The Beloved Lord.”
names.commentary:
“The Beloved Lord.” One who is a seeker must necessarily get charmed by the Glory of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, and by the influence of this captivating love He is to be worshipped. Thus One Who is to be loved and worshipped by the seekers who strive for the four “aspirations-in-life”—Purushaarthas. There is also this meaning for the term: “The One Who is Pradyumnah”—since Pradyumna-form is an incarnation of kāma (Love).

काम्यते इति कामः—स देवः कामदेवः।
(Kaamyate iti kaamah—sa devah kaamadevah.)
names.simple_meaning: “The Beloved Lord.”

names.short_meaning: "The Fulfiller of Desires of all His true devotees."
names.commentary: "The Fulfiller of Desires of all His true devotees." Those who in their sincere attitude and love for Him alone are surrendered unto Him, their hearts' inner longings are satisfied by Him. The same idea finds similar but varied interpretation in that kāmapālaḥ can imply "One Who had taken the incarnation of Balarama," for Balarama is called as the "Wielder-of-the-plough" (Hala-ayudhah) or as kāmapālaḥ. Thus it can also mean "Protector (Paalah) of His devotees" (kāma, meaning the 'Desired Ones').
names.simple_meaning: "The Fulfiller of Desires of all His true devotees."

names.short_meaning: One who has fulfilled all His desires
names.commentary: One who has fulfilled all His desires. Desire is an expression of an inherent sense of incompleteness—and this insufficiency unto oneself is called ignorance of the Self. The non-apprehension of Reality gives rise to endless misapprehensions of the same. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the Self, the Reality, and so all non-apprehensions must end in Him, then no desires can ever remain in Him demanding fulfilment. He is "One of fulfilled desires"… Some commentators give just the opposite explanation, since the term kāmī in Sanskrit can also mean "One who has desires." Here it would mean that Lord Viṣṇu is the Supreme Reality who "desired to create" the world of plurality. The Upaniṣads roar: "He desired" (Sah akaamayata). The creative urge in the Supreme is that which expressed as the apparent illusion of a playful creation of multiplicity and the endless varieties in them.
names.simple_meaning: One who has fulfilled all His desires

names.short_meaning: “Of Enchanting — Form;” “Supremely — Handsome;” the “Beauty of Beauty itself.”
names.commentary: “Of Enchanting — Form;” “Supremely — Handsome;” the “Beauty of Beauty itself.” In all His Incarnations we find Him described as extremely charming with His Grace and Beauty. In Sanskrit the term Kah (कः) means the Creator, Brahmājī. In this sense, therefore, Ka-antah can suggest “One Who destroys even the Creator during the dissolution.”
names.simple_meaning: “Of Enchanting — Form;” “Supremely — Handsome;” the “Beauty of Beauty itself.”

names.short_meaning: The author of the Scriptures (Āgamas)
names.commentary:
The author of the Scriptures (Āgamas). Sruti and Smriti form the Āgamas. Or in perfect harmony with the preceding term where Lord is termed as the destroyer of even the Creator at the time of deluge, some commentators have again interpreted this term as “The One Who is the inaugurator of the kṛta — Yuga.”

This means the Lord is One into Whom the world dissolves and from Whom the world rises up again.

“योगो ज्ञानं तथा सांख्यं विद्याः शिल्पादि कर्म च। वेदाः शास्त्राणि विज्ञानमेतत्सर्वं जनार्दनात्॥” — Vyāsa.
(Yogo jnaanam tathaa saamkhyam vidyaah silpaadi karma cha; Vedaah saastraani vijnaanametat sarvam janaardanaat.)
“Yoga, Knowledge Divine, Sāṅkhya philosophy, science, sculpture and such other arts, Vedas, śāstras, Spiritual wisdom—all these came from Śrī Janaardana.”
names.simple_meaning: The author of the Scriptures (Āgamas)

names.short_meaning: “Of Indescribable Form;” “Of Indefinable Nature.”
names.commentary: “Of Indescribable Form;” “Of Indefinable Nature.” Since the Lord transcends the Elements and is the very cause for the three guṇas— as the pure Self, expressing Itself through the body, mind and intellect of man—it becomes impossible to describe or define His Form.
names.simple_meaning: “Of Indescribable Form;” “Of Indefinable Nature.”

names.short_meaning: "All — Pervading."
names.commentary:
“All — Pervading.” One Who pervades the entire Visvam. In His Visvaroopa — Form in Gītā XI we have from Arjuna a description of the dazzling wonderment of Him as “All-pervading.”

“द्यावापृथिव्योरिदमन्तरं हि व्याप्तं त्वयैकेन दिशश्च सर्वाः।” — Gītā XI-20.
(Dyaavaaprithivyoridamantaram hi Vyaaptam tvayaikena disascha sarvaah.)
“By Thee alone is filled the earth, the outer space and the inner space. It is Thee who fills all directions everywhere”—Arjuna describes his experience of the All-pervading, unbelievably Glorious Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "All — Pervading."

names.short_meaning: "The Valiant;" "The Courageous— the One of heroic exploits."
names.commentary: “The Valiant;” “The Courageous—the One of heroic exploits.” The root ‘Vi’ (वी) often means creation, radiance, existence, involution or motion. One who has all these powers is called vīraḥ.
names.simple_meaning: "The Valiant;" "The Courageous— the One of heroic exploits."

names.short_meaning: "Infinite; Endless."
names.commentary: "Infinite; Endless." That which is unconditioned by Time — Space — Substance is 'Infinite.' None can discover the end of such a Truth. Conditioned things will all have an end—a change from one condition to another. The Infinite is totally unconditioned, so unlimited, and naturally, therefore, changeless. Hence Nārāyaṇa is Infinite.
names.simple_meaning: "Infinite; Endless."

names.short_meaning: One Who had gained through his conquest and his prowess vast wealth for the enrichment of his country
names.commentary:
One Who had gained through his conquest and his prowess vast wealth for the enrichment of his country. From his various campaigns, Arjuna had brought great wealth to the land. In Gītā, Lord Kṛṣṇa says: “I am Dhananjaya, among the sons of Pandu.”

“पाण्डवानां धनञ्जयः।” — Gītā X-37.
(Paandavaanaam Dhananjayah.)
names.simple_meaning: One Who had gained through his conquest and his prowess vast wealth for the enrichment of his country

names.short_meaning: One Who is a great friend of Brahman
names.commentary: One Who is a great friend of Brahman. The term Brahman includes in its connotation the śāstra, Tapas, Vedas, Truth, Knowledge, etc. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is a protector and friend of all these. Here Brahman means jīva—a friend of all individuals.
names.simple_meaning: One Who is a great friend of Brahman

names.short_meaning: The One Who performs the Brahman—meaning the one who lives in Truth, who abides in Tapas, etc
names.commentary: The One Who performs the Brahman—meaning the one who lives in Truth, who abides in Tapas, etc. He is the author of Brahman as enumerated in the explanation of the preceding term.
names.simple_meaning: The one who brings forth and lives in sacred knowledge

names.short_meaning: "Creator."
names.commentary: "Creator." As the total Creative-power (क्रिया शक्ति), it is Nārāyaṇa Who functions as Creator through Brahmājī.
names.simple_meaning: "Creator."

names.short_meaning: "The Biggest, the Vastest, the All- Pervading."
names.commentary:
“The Biggest, the Vastest, the All — Pervading.” Upaniṣads thunderingly declare the Brahman to be “Existence—Knowledge—Infinite.” The Knowledge which lifts all false perceptions of differences, pure in all its aspects, ever beyond the grasp of the senses, and that which can be experienced only in one's own Self, is called Brahman.

बृहत्त्वात् ब्रह्म।
(Brimhatvaat Brahma.)

“सत्यं ज्ञानमनन्तं ब्रह्म।” — Taittirīya Upaniṣad II-1.
(Satyam Jnaanamanantam Brahma.)

“आत्मसंवेद्यं तज्ज्ञानं ब्रह्मसंज्ञितम्।” — Viṣṇu Purāṇa 6-7-53.
(Aatmasamvedyam taj-jnaanam Brahmasamjnitam.)
names.simple_meaning: "The Biggest, the Vastest, the All- Pervading."

names.short_meaning: “One Who increases the Brahman."
names.commentary: “One Who increases the Brahman." Here, of course, the term Brahman means "Austerities, Vedas, Truth, Knowledge." These are increased in one who has earned the Grace of Śrī Nārāyaṇa through total surrender and constant devotion.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who increases the Brahman."

names.short_meaning: "One Who knows Brahman."
names.commentary:
“One Who knows Brahman.” The meaning here is one who has intuited the Vedas and their full commentaries. In Gītā (XV) we listen to the Lord declaring that: “I alone am the Author of the Vedas and the Knower of the Vedas.” Brahman alone can “know” Brahman just as the “dreamer” can never survive to know the “waker.” The knower-of-the-waker is the “Waker” alone.

Similarly, the individualised ego conditioned by the equipments of Body, Mind and Intellect experiences the Brahman only when it has transcended the entanglements of matter—and then the ego is no more a jīva but “becomes Brahman.” Thus the Higher is experienced only by the Higher. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the Brahman—and, therefore, He alone is the Knower of Brahman.

“वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम्।” — Gītā XV-15.
(Vedaantakrid vedavideva chaaham.)
names.simple_meaning: "One Who knows Brahman."

names.short_meaning: One who has realised that the pluralistic world is a mere superimposition upon the Brahman caused by an error of judgement, and who experiences the Supreme Consciousness of the One Reality is a brāhmaṇaḥ
names.commentary:
One who has realised that the pluralistic world is a mere superimposition upon the Brahman caused by an error of judgement, and who experiences the Supreme Consciousness of the One Reality is a brāhmaṇaḥ. His duty is to convey this knowledge to others with a pure missionary zeal and a higher proselytising enthusiasm. By mere accident of birth one does not become a brāhmaṇaḥ. Visvamitra and others through their Tapas and Divine Experience had reached the status of Brahmin-hood, so we read in the Purāṇas. Nārāyaṇa manifests as such mighty men of realisation, serving their generations through their teachings.

“ब्रह्मज्ञानी तु ब्राह्मणः।”
(Brahmajnaanee tu brāhmaṇaḥ.)
names.simple_meaning: The knower of Brahman who sees unity beneath plurality

names.short_meaning: "One Who is with Brahma."
names.commentary: "One Who is with Brahma." The term Brahma meaning as before—"Austerities, Vedas, Truth and Knowledge-divine."
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is with Brahma."

names.short_meaning: One Who lives ever in Brahman, and so "knows" the nature of the Brahman
names.commentary: One Who lives ever in Brahman, and so "knows" the nature of the Brahman. He, the Lord, being the very Brahman, no one knows His nature as He Himself can. The "waker" alone knows the waking—the "dreamer" and "sleeper" can never realise and experience the waking-state until they "become" the "waker."
names.simple_meaning: One Who lives ever in Brahman, and so "knows" the nature of the Brahman

names.short_meaning: One Who is the beloved of and One Who is the lover of true men of full realisation, the brāhmaṇas
names.commentary: One Who is the beloved of and One Who is the lover of true men of full realisation, the brāhmaṇas. Not the caste, but the men of supreme experience-divine. The Lord is dear to them, and they too are dear to Him.
names.simple_meaning: One Who is the beloved of and One Who is the lover of true men of full realisation, the brāhmaṇas

names.short_meaning: "Of Great — Step."
names.commentary: "Of Great — Step." Directly we are reminded of the Vamana — Incarnation when the Lord measured the three worlds by His three steps. It also indicates the root meaning of the term, Viṣṇu-"The one who has the long stride—meaning, "All-pervading." Since He is All-pervading, He reaches everywhere earlier than all others.
names.simple_meaning: "Of Great — Step."

names.short_meaning: “One Who performs great deeds."
names.commentary: “One Who performs great deeds." The creation, the dissolution, the protection and the spread of the Knowledge-of — Truth, all these are indeed great undertakings. He alone performs them, through Maha — Purushas who have surrendered themselves unto Him-those who, in total surrender, have indeed become one with the Lord in love and being.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who performs great deeds."

names.short_meaning: “Of Great Resplendence."
names.commentary:
“Of Great Resplendence." The Upaniṣads glorify Him in that even the Sun. Moon, the stars and fire have no light of their own. By Him they shine, the Giver of Light to all. In the Gītā, the Lord insists that "The Supreme is the Light of all lights, beyond all darkness" and again He asserts, "Understand that Light in the Sun by which the whole world is illumined, and that Light in the Moon and in the fire to be My own Light."

Here the Light of Consciousness, the Self, is indicated.

“न तत्र सूर्यो भाति न चन्द्रतारकं नेमा विद्यतो भान्ति कृतोऽयमग्निः।

तमेव भान्तमनभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वं मिदं विभाति ।" (Na tatra sooryo bhaati na chandrataarakam nemaa vidyuto bhaanti kutoayamagnih; Tameva bhaantamanubhaati sarvam tasya bhaasaa sarvamidam vibhaati.) --- Mundaka: II-2-10.

"ज्योतिषामपि तज्ज्योतिस्तमसः परम्च्यते।" (Jyotishaamapi taj-jyotistamasah paramuchyate.) —Gītā XIII—17.

''यदादित्यगतं तेजो जगद्भासयतेऽखिलम । यच्चन्द्रमसि यच्चाग्नौ तत्तेजो विद्धि मामकम ॥" (Yadaadityagatam tejo jagadbhaasayate-akhilam; Yat-chandramasi yat-chaagnau tat-tejo viddhi maamakam.) -Gītā XV-12.
names.simple_meaning: “Of Great Resplendence."

names.short_meaning: "The Great Serpent."
names.commentary:
