"The Great Serpent." Uraga means serpent. In Gītā, Bhagavān says "अनन्तश्चास्मि नागानाम'' (Among the nagas, the many-hooded serpents, I am Ananta.) Ananta is the five-headed Great Serpent also called Sesha, upon which the Lord Viṣṇu reclines. Again in Gītā the Lord says "सर्पाणामस्मि वास्किः" (Among the serpents I am Vaasuki). Mythologically, this is the serpent adorning Lord Siva's ring finger. Though so small as to become a ring for the Lord, it was this Vaasuki who offered himself as the great rope in churning the milky ocean. This paradox reminds us of the Upanishadic declaration "अणोरणीयान महतो महीयान" (Smaller than the smallest and greater than the greatest).

उरमा गच्छति इति उरगः। 'Urasaa gacchati iti uragah.) "One who crawls on his belly is Uraga,"
names.simple_meaning: "The Great Serpent."

names.short_meaning: "The Great Sacrifice."
names.commentary:
"The Great Sacrifice." The Supreme cannot be experienced without the greatest sacrifice, the total sacrifice of the Ego, the jīva — Bhaava. The Great Sacrifice indicates traditionally the Asvamedha yāga. Therefore, some commentators explain this term "as one who is of the very form of Asvamedha yāga."

One of the great sacrifices. It is performed by mighty kings wherein an enormous amount of wealth is distributed. One hundred such Yagas is said to qualify one for the status of Devendra. It declares the sovereignty and prowess of the sacrificer king.
names.simple_meaning: "The Great Sacrifice."

names.short_meaning: “One Who had performed Great yajñas.”
names.commentary: “One Who had performed Great yajñas.” In the Rama — Incarnation, He had performed Asvamedha-yāga. He is the One, by Whose Grace, all "Sacrifices" are fulfilled successfully. One who performs sacrifice properly and faithfully is called Yajvaa.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who had performed Great yajñas.”

names.short_meaning: “The Great yajña.”
names.commentary:
“The Great yajña.” In Bhāgavata Gītā, the Lord in describing His Immanence in the world says to Arjuna: "I am among the yajñas, the Japa-yajña." Lord Nārāyaṇa Himself is the greatest yajña—therefore, in devotion approach Him and gain His Grace. The Japa yajña is glorified by the Lord as the greatest sacrifice because it is both the essential means of all other yajñas and transcends them all as an end in itself, by maintaining a constant stream of the same divine thoughts in the mind.

" यज्ञानां जपयज्ञोऽस्मि ।" - Gītā X-25. (Yajnaanaam japayajnosmi.)
names.simple_meaning: “The Great yajña.”

names.short_meaning: “The Great Offering.”
names.commentary:
“The Great Offering.” The yajña is He; the very things offered to the sacred fire, the Havis, are also He. Gītā tells us, "We offer to Brahman that which is Brahman, in the fire which is Brahman, and the act of offering is also Brahman."

"ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हिवर्ब्रह्माग्नी ब्रह्मणा हतम ।" (Brahmaarpanam Brahma havir Brahmaagnau Brahmanaa hutan.) -Gītā IV-24
names.simple_meaning: “The Great Offering.”

names.short_meaning: One Who is the object of all praise
names.commentary: "One Who is the object of all praise"-meaning, One Who deserves all our praise but One Who has none to praise. He is praised by all and He praises none. The jīva invokes Him: the Self, the Atman, never invokes the ignorant jīva.
ocr_notes: Scan locus corrected from [177] to [177, 178] by complete-text replay against the PDF page OCR.
names.simple_meaning: One Who is the object of all praise

names.short_meaning: One Who is invoked through the loving chants of the devoted hearts
names.commentary:
One Who is invoked through the loving chants of the devoted hearts. When a devoted seeker melts away in singing the praise of the Lord, his physical, mental and intellectual preoccupations with objects, emotions and thoughts silently roll away from him. In such quiet moments, in their intense love for the Lord, such seekers come to dwell upon the Nature of the Lord, the Self.

In these moments they rise above their present nature and explode into the realms of experiences of the Higher State of Divine Consciousness—Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: One Who is invoked through the loving chants of the devoted hearts

names.short_meaning: "The Hymn."
names.commentary: "The Hymn." A glorious hymn, that describes the Lord's Divine Nature, itself is He, as the words lift the singer into the experience of the Supreme Nature of Truth. It is infallible if the singer of the Hymn has full devotion and ardent aspiration to realise Him. "Naama" and "Naamee" are one and the same in experience.
names.simple_meaning: "The Hymn."

names.short_meaning: "The act of praise."
names.commentary: "The act of praise." The very noble, divine "act of invoking the Lord" is by His Grace alone.
names.simple_meaning: "The act of praise."

names.short_meaning: "One who adores or praises."
names.commentary:
"One who adores or praises." The true devotee, singing the divine hymns is also of the Nature of Supreme peace, love, beauty, goodness—the divine qualities attributed to the Lord in whom he dissolves through his songful identification. Such a devotee in this at-one-ment with Him. the Lord praises again and again as "He is the one dear to Me. "

‘‘स मे प्रिय:।’’ -Gītā XII-14.
names.simple_meaning: "One who adores or praises."

names.short_meaning: "Lover of Battles."
names.commentary: "Lover of Battles." Hence we see Śrī Nārāyaṇa ever carrying His mace and discus in order to destroy the vulgar and thus protect the decent. Here "battle" is the constant struggle for evolution.
names.simple_meaning: "Lover of Battles."

names.short_meaning: "The Full."
names.commentary:
"The Full." The Infinite is ever the same. Though things are apparently emerging out of It, still the Supreme remains irreducible and without a change. Lord Nārāyaṇa is Ever — Full with His own glories and powers; One who is full with all the wealth, inner and outer, the Supreme Lakṣmī-pati.

“पूर्णस्य पूर्णमादाय पूर्णमेवावशिष्यते ।” (Poornasya poornamaadaaya poornamevaavasishyate.) "When from the Full, the Full is removed, still the Full remains ever — Full."
names.simple_meaning: "The Full."

names.short_meaning: "The Fulfiller."
names.commentary: "The Fulfiller." Lord Hari fulfils, surely, all the desires and demands of His true devotees.
names.simple_meaning: "The Fulfiller."

names.short_meaning: "The truly — Holy."
names.commentary: "The truly — Holy." When the devotee's heart is filled with remembrance of the glorious Form Divine and Infinite Nature Supreme of the Lord Viṣṇu. He then, in that very moment, removes all sin from His devotee's heart. The Lord is Auspiciousness itself, so where He is invoked, all inauspiciousness must immediately retire.
names.simple_meaning: "The truly — Holy."

names.short_meaning: "Of Holy — Fame."
names.commentary: "Of Holy — Fame." He is gloriously renowned as the Holy One. Whoever glorifies him becomes himself holy. All the unholy animal passions in the devotee are routed and beaten back when his heart is wholly in tune with the Lord's Glory and Form.
names.simple_meaning: "Of Holy — Fame."

names.short_meaning: One who has neither the mental or physical diseases
names.commentary: One who has neither the mental or physical diseases. Of pure unstained divine essence is His Nature. He is not involved in Karmas, thus the resultant of the Karmas which visit us in terms of mental restlessness or physical pangs, never touch Him.
names.simple_meaning: One who has neither the mental or physical diseases

names.short_meaning: Fleet as the mind is the Lord's movement
names.commentary:
Fleet as the mind is the Lord's movement. He is anxious to run and reach the devotee to remove his suffering and ignorance. All — Pervading is the Lord, thus He is faster than all those who run after Him—the sense organs or the mind can only move in Him—and wherever they reach, the Supreme, He, in the form of Existence (सत्), is already there.

“अनेजदेकं मनसो जवीयो नैनद्देवा आप्नुवन् पूर्वमर्षत् । तद्धावतोऽन्यानत्येति तिष्ठत् तस्मिन्नपो मातरिश्वा दधाति ॥” (Anejadekam manaso javeeyo nainaddevaa aapnuvan poorvamarshat; Tat-dhaavato-anyaanatyeti tishthat-tasminnapo maatarisvaa dadhaati.) "The Self is motionless, one, swifter than the mind. The Devas could not overtake; It ran before them. Sitting, It goes faster than those who run after It. By It Maatarisvan supports the activity of all living beings (the Element Water)." —Īśāvāsya Upaniṣad.
names.simple_meaning: Fleet as the mind is the Lord's movement

names.short_meaning: "The Teacher of the Teerthas," The term, Teerthas, means vidyās
names.commentary: "The Teacher of the Teerthas," The term, Teerthas, means vidyās. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the author of the vidyās or auxiliary Sciences. Therefore, "One Who is the most ancient Teacher of all vidyās and Tantras."
names.simple_meaning: The teacher who opens the sacred fords of knowledge

names.short_meaning: “He Whose Essence is Golden.”
names.commentary: “He Whose Essence is Golden.” In the beginning of Creation were the primeval waters. Into this One Ocean the Lord dropped His Essence and it became a Golden Egg from which Brahmaa, the Creator, first arose. Thus Lord, as the womb of all Creation, is mentioned in the Purāṇas as "Hiranyagarbha," the Golden Womb.
names.simple_meaning: “He Whose Essence is Golden.”

names.short_meaning: "The Free — Giver of Wealth."
names.commentary: "The Free — Giver of Wealth." In this context, Vasu means "Worldly — Wealth"— money, property, grains, possessions, progeny. Lord Viṣṇu who nourishes and maintains all beings with the wealth of His consort, Śrī Lakṣmī, distributes and patronises His devotees very liberally.
names.simple_meaning: "The Free — Giver of Wealth."

names.short_meaning: Again, the same term as we read above, but here it means "The Giver of Salvation."
names.commentary: Again, the same term as we read above, but here it means "The Giver of Salvation." Liberation (mokṣa) is the greatest wealth—whom He chooses, mokṣa is gained by him alone.
names.simple_meaning: The giver of liberation

names.short_meaning: “The son of Vasudeva,”Lord Kṛṣṇa
names.commentary:
“The son of Vasudeva,”Lord Kṛṣṇa. Or “One Who is Vāsu and Deva.” “Vāsu” means "One who dwells in all creatures as their ego-centric individuality (jīva-roopa)." 'Deva' means "One Who revels."

Therefore, this name for Lord Kṛṣṇa has the appropriate meaning: "One Who revels in every living creature as the jīva-entity in each."

‘‘ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानां हृद्देशेऽर्जुन तिष्ठति ।

भ्रामयन्सर्वभतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥" (Īśvaraḥ sarvabhootaanaam hriddese Arjuna tisthati: Bhraamayan sarvabhootaani yantraaroodhaani maayayaa.) "The Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings, by His illusive power, to revolve as if mounted on a machine.' -Gītā Ch. XVIII-61.
names.simple_meaning: “The son of Vasudeva,”Lord Kṛṣṇa

names.short_meaning: "The Refuge for all."
names.commentary:
"The Refuge for all." The One Who dwells within, veiled behind māyā, the mind. The mind projects this play of things, beings, emotions and thoughts. The world is the shadow-show round the Pure Consciousness, Lord declares in Gītā: "I am the beginning, the middle and also the end of all beings." Thus He alone is the Refuge, for there is no other existence. "All have emerged out from Me, exist in Me and must come back to Me.

‘‘अहमात्मा गडाकेश सर्वभताशयस्थितः।

अहमादिश्च मध्यं च भृतानामन्त एच च ॥" (Aham-aatmaa gudaakesa sarvabhootaasayasthitah Ahamaadischa madhyam cha bhootaanaamanta eva cha.) -Gītā Ch. X-20.
names.simple_meaning: "The Refuge for all."

names.short_meaning: One Who is attentive to, and, therefore, concerned with every object and being in this world: "Omnipresent."
names.commentary: One Who is attentive to, and, therefore, concerned with every object and being in this world: "Omnipresent."
names.simple_meaning: One Who is attentive to, and, therefore, concerned with every object and being in this world: "Omnipresent."

names.short_meaning: "The Oblation."
names.commentary:
"The Oblation." That which we offer unto Him is also permeated by Him-there is nothing other than He, Himself, the same everywhere, in all places, at all times. In Gītā, Lord insists that the "oblations" are nothing but Brahman."

‘‘ब्रह्मार्पणं ब्रह्म हिवर्षे ह्याग्नी ब्रह्मणा हतम ॥’’ (Brahmaarpanam Brahma havirbrahmaagnau Brahmanaa hutam.) -Gītā Ch. IV-24.
names.simple_meaning: "The Oblation."

names.short_meaning: "The goal of good and noble seekers."
names.commentary:
"The goal of good and noble seekers." Lord Nārāyaṇa is the Spiritual Goal to be reached. "The Good" here means those who know the existence of Brahman, for the Upaniṣad says: "If a person knows 'Brahman exists,' then the wise call him 'good."

"अस्ति ब्रह्मोति चेद्वेद सन्तमेनं ततो विद्:।" (Asti Brahmeti chedveda santamenam tato viduh.) -Taittirīya II-6.
names.simple_meaning: "The goal of good and noble seekers."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is full of Good Actions."
names.commentary: "One Who is full of Good Actions." Lord Hari is the One Who maintains the rhythm of creation and the logic of its preservation. Even through His destructive activities, there is creation only for the sake of the individual and for the good of the world. All His actions are totally in harmony for the establishment of Peace (शान्त).
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is full of Good Actions."

names.short_meaning: The Lord is the One without a second
names.commentary:
The Lord is the "One without a second," and, therefore, remains ever the same, without any differences of genus, species or in Itself.

"एकमेवाद्वितीयम।" (Ekamevaadviteeyam) — Chhandogyopanishad 6-2-1.

‘‘सजातीय विजातीय स्वगतभेदरहित वस्तु।’’ (Sajaateeya vijaateeya svagatabhedarahita vastu.) sattā is Infinite vastu.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord is the One without a second

names.short_meaning: "One Who has Rich Glories."
names.commentary: "One Who has Rich Glories." The term 'Glories' (भूति) means wealth, power, happiness (ऐश्वर्यं). Or "One Who has taken different kinds of Incarnations," exhibiting in all of them the glories of the Supreme. So immeasurable are the Lord's Glories that even all these splendours scarcely reveal His Divine Might. Him, whom even the Devas know not; only the yogīs in meditation come to perceive His Eternal Glory.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has Rich Glories."

names.short_meaning: The Supreme Goal for the "Good" who pursue the path of Truth
names.commentary: The Supreme Goal for the "Good" who pursue the path of Truth. Here the "Good" means those who are the Knowers of Brahman.
names.simple_meaning: The Supreme Goal for the "Good" who pursue the path of Truth

names.short_meaning: "One Who has heroic and valiant armies."
names.commentary: "One Who has heroic and valiant armies." The Incarnations as Rama and Kṛṣṇa are indicated here in whose armies there were valiant people like Hanumaan and Lakshmana, Arjuna, Bhīma and others.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has heroic and valiant armies."

names.short_meaning: “The Best among the Yadava clan.”
names.commentary: “The Best among the Yadava clan.” The Glory of the Yadavas—Lord Kṛṣṇa, Who was an Incarnation of Śrī Hari.
names.simple_meaning: “The Best among the Yadava clan.”

names.short_meaning: "The Abode of the Good."
names.commentary:
"The Abode of the Good." The great souls of realisation come to live in Him, the Self: drowned in God — Consciousness, they beam out from that Abode their divinity all around. Bhagavān in Gītā says: "My devotee thus knowing (realising the Truth, the jneyam, seated in the heart of all) enters into My Being."

"मद्भक्त एतद्विज्ञाय मद्भावायोपपद्यते।" (Madbhakta etadviinaaya madbhaayaayopapadyate. —Gītā XIII-18.
names.simple_meaning: "The Abode of the Good."

names.short_meaning: One Who is attended by the righteous Yaamunas—meaning Gopas who live on the Yamuna banks
names.commentary:
One Who is attended by the righteous Yaamunas—meaning Gopas who live on the Yamuna banks. In a metaphysical sense, these Gopas are not the keepers of 'cows,' but the keepers of the sacred milk of Knowledge — Upaniṣads.

‘‘तारुण्यारम्यरम्यं परमसुखरसस्वादरोमाञ्चिताङ्गै- रावीतं नारदाद्यैविलसदूपनिषत्सुन्दरीमण्डलैश्च ॥” (I behold) the form of a divine boy, attractive with the advent of adolescence and surrounded by Narada and others with their limbs covered with hairs standing on end at the taste of the Bliss Supreme, and by that bevy of charming maidens of the form of shining Upaniṣads.

-- Narayaneeyam—Desaka 100-1.
names.simple_meaning: The one attended by the righteous people of the Yamunā

names.short_meaning: "The very dwelling place of the Great Elements."
names.commentary:
"The very dwelling place of the Great Elements." "Since the Beings (Elements) dwell in You, You are called 'Bhootaavaasa,'" so says Harivaṃśa. bhagavān Himself says in the Gītā: "I am the Source of all Creation." Therefore He is also called the 'Bhootayoni.'

"वसन्ति त्वयि भतानि भतावासस्ततो भवान।" (Vasanti tvayi bhootaani bhootaavaasastato bhavaan.) -- Harivaṃśa, 279-52.

‘‘अहं सर्वस्य प्रभवः।’’ (Aham sarvasya prabhavah.) -Gītā, X-8.
names.simple_meaning: "The very dwelling place of the Great Elements."

names.short_meaning: One Who envelops the world with His māyā-powers of veiling and agitations
names.commentary:
One Who envelops the world with His māyā-powers of veiling (आवरण) and agitations (विक्षेप). The Lord discloses: "I pervade the whole world with My Glory, as the Sun with its rays." 1

“छादयामि जगद् विश्वं भूत्या सूर्य इवांश्भिः।” (Chhaadayaami jagad visvam bhootyaa soorya ivaamsubhih.) -Mahabharat, Santiparva 342-41.
names.simple_meaning: One Who envelops the world with His māyā-powers of veiling and agitations

names.short_meaning: "The Abode of all Life — Energies."
names.commentary: "The Abode of all Life — Energies." One Who is the very Substratum for the life and existence of all creatures. He is the Self, the Life in all of us—therefore, He is the very support for the prāṇa in each living creature.
names.simple_meaning: "The Abode of all Life — Energies."

names.short_meaning: “One Who is of Unlimited Wealth, Power and Glory.”
names.commentary:
“One Who is of Unlimited Wealth, Power and Glory.” There is no boundary for His Glories-there is no limit for His Greatness, as He is, by His Nature, beyond all Naama-roopaadi and All — Pervasive. 'Of My Divine Glories there is no end', Bhagavān Himself reveals to Arjuna.

‘‘नान्तोऽस्ति मम दिव्यानां विभूतीनां परंतप।’’ (Naantosti mama divyaanaam vibhooteenaam paramtapa.)—Gītā X-40.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is of Unlimited Wealth, Power and Glory.”

names.short_meaning: -"The Destroyer of pride in evil-minded people."
names.commentary: -"The Destroyer of pride in evil-minded people." Easily He curbed the pride of Indra and others by lifting the mountain and protecting the cows of the Yamuna banks.
names.simple_meaning: -"The Destroyer of pride in evil-minded people."

names.short_meaning: “One Who gives pride to the righteous,”—meaning, One Who creates in the Good an anxious urge to be the best among the righteous and virtuous
names.commentary: “One Who gives pride to the righteous,”—meaning, One Who creates in the Good an anxious urge to be the best among the righteous and virtuous. This pride is their protection from compromising in even a small way in any act. This is a positive 'pride' of the higher order. There is also a reading of A-darpadah when the meaning would be: "One Who never allows His devotees to become proud." In this way, devotees who totally surrender unto Him all their virtues, acting on purely as His agents, are freed by Him from the bondage of spiritual pride. For such pride, resulting from a preponderance of Sattva guna and sense of doership, would make them vain-glorious of their goodness.
names.simple_meaning: The one who grants dignity to the righteous

names.short_meaning: One Who is ever drunk with the Infinite Bliss of His own essential nature as sat-cit-ānanda
names.commentary: One Who is ever drunk with the Infinite Bliss of His own essential nature as sat-cit-ānanda.
names.simple_meaning: One Who is ever drunk with the Infinite Bliss of His own essential nature as sat-cit-ānanda

names.short_meaning: The object of contemplation which is indeed very difficult to attain:—the One Who is realised by yogīs through arduous processes of intense, single-pointed contemplation
names.commentary:
The object of contemplation which is indeed very difficult to attain:—the One Who is realised by yogīs through arduous processes of intense, single-pointed contemplation. Lord Kṛṣṇa in the Bhagavad Gītā admits: "Greater is their trouble whose minds are set on the Unmanifest; for the goal, the Unmanifested, is very hard for the embodied to reach."

दुर्धरः अथ अपराजितः। (Durdharah atha aparaajitah.)

‘‘क्लेशोऽधिकतरस्तेषामव्यक्तासक्तचेतसाम।’’ (Kleso-adhikatarasteshaamavyaktaasaktachetasaam.) -Gītā XII-5.
names.simple_meaning: The one difficult to hold in contemplation

names.short_meaning: “The Unvanquished.”
names.commentary:
“The Unvanquished.” “Never — Conquered” is the Glory of the Self, for, conquering is of 'objects'; the 'Subject' can never be conquered. This, being the Reality in all, the senses, mind, etc., including the faculties (Devas) can never reach or conquer Him. Even when the mighty senses and the terrible Asuras fight against It, still these overwhelming powers of desires and passions can never vanquish the Self, the divine Nārāyaṇa.

“नैनद्देवा आप्नुवन्।” (Nainat Devaa Aapnuvan.) -Īśāvāsyopaniṣad IV.

"The Devas could not overtake It."
names.simple_meaning: “The Unvanquished.”

names.short_meaning: “Of the Form of the entire Universe."
names.commentary: “Of the Form of the entire Universe." Lord is the total—created, so His Form is called Visvaroopa. The total-gross-form of the Universe together represents His gross — Form — Divine.
names.simple_meaning: “Of the Form of the entire Universe."

names.short_meaning: The Great — Form- Divine of the Lord as He reclines upon the Sesha couch as the very support for the Creator to bring into existence the Universe of forms and plurality
names.commentary: The Great — Form- Divine of the Lord as He reclines upon the Sesha couch as the very support for the Creator to bring into existence the Universe of forms and plurality. The entire Universe and the Creator of the Universe are but an aspect of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Self.
names.simple_meaning: The great cosmic form supporting creation

names.short_meaning: “Of the Resplendent Form.”
names.commentary:
“Of the Resplendent Form.” As Consciousness, He is ever bright and fully effulgent, illumining all experiences at all times. Sanjaya reports: "If the splendour of a thousand Suns were to blaze out at once in the sky, that would be like the splendour of that Mighty Being."

"दिवि सूर्यसहस्रस्य भवेद्यगपद्रिथता।" (Divi sooryasahasrasya bhavedyugapadutthitaa.) —Gītā XI-12.
names.simple_meaning: “Of the Resplendent Form.”

names.short_meaning: “Having no Form.”
names.commentary:
“Having no Form.” Though He is described above as Deepta-moorti: “of the Resplendent Form"; Mahaa-moorti: "of Great Form"; Visva-moorti: "of the Universal — Form"—He has, in reality, "No — Form"; A-moortimaan. He pervades all, but nothing limits Him. The limited alone has a form—the Unlimited, like 'Space', has no form. The Infinite Brahman being so subtle, "Subtler than the subtlest," Śrī Nārāyaṇa as the Self-in-all, allows everything to remain in Him, but He is not conditioned by any one of them, ever.

“सूक्ष्मात् च तत् सूक्ष्मतरम्।” (Sookshmaat cha tat sookshmataram.) —Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad III-I-7.
names.simple_meaning: “Having no Form.”

names.short_meaning: "Multi — Formed": One Who Himself has become the world of varieties of Forms -Who has Himself taken the various Incarnations in order to help the world of beings to evolve quicker and fuller
names.commentary: "Multi — Formed": One Who Himself has become the world of varieties of Forms -Who has Himself taken the various Incarnations in order to help the world of beings to evolve quicker and fuller.
names.simple_meaning: The one of many forms and incarnations

names.short_meaning: "Unmanifest."
names.commentary:
"Unmanifest." Things are called manifest when they can be perceived by the sense-organs. As the Self, the Consciousness in us, Śrī Hari is the very faculty of seeing, hearing, smelling, tasting and touching in the five sense-organs. He being, thus, the very subject, He cannot at the same time be the object of the sense-organs.

Hence. He cannot be defined or described.
names.simple_meaning: "Unmanifest."

names.short_meaning: "Of Myriad — Forms": even though Consciousness, like Light, has no form of its own, all thought and the thought-projected world of infinite forms are all illumined by the Supreme
names.commentary: "Of Myriad — Forms": even though Consciousness, like Light, has no form of its own, all thought and the thought-projected world of infinite forms are all illumined by the Supreme. Therefore, the Self, functioning through the fluctuations of the restless mind "creates" the illusion of forms—all those forms as His, just as all dreamforms are created by the waker's mind only.
names.simple_meaning: The one of myriad forms

names.short_meaning: "Many — Faced": because He is of the Universal — Form, all faces are His only
names.commentary:
"Many — Faced": because He is of the Universal — Form, all faces are His only. "Hands and feet everywhere, with heads and mouths everywhere, His ears everywhere, stands (The Lord), enveloping all"

“सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत्सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्। सर्वतः श्रुतिमल्लोके सर्वमावृत्य तिष्ठति॥” (Sarvatah paanipaadam tat sarvatoakshisiromukham; Sarvatah srutimalloke sarvamaavritya tishthati.) —Gītā XIII-14.
names.simple_meaning: "Many — Faced": because He is of the Universal — Form, all faces are His only

names.short_meaning: The One
names.commentary:
"The One. The One-without-a second." As the Infinite is without any of the three distinctions, He, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Brahman, can only be the One without any otherness.

“एकमेवाद्वितीयम्।” -Chhandogyopanishad 6-2-1. (Ekamevaadviteeyam.)

They are: (1) without distinctions of Genus (सजातीय भेद); (2) without distinctions of Species (विजातीय भेद); and (3) without any distinction within Itself (स्वगत भेद).
names.simple_meaning: The One

names.short_meaning: "The Many."
names.commentary:
"The Many." One Who, though the One, yet plays in the bosom of all the living creatures. Just as we are one entity, but our thoughts are many, the Supreme Consciousness, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, though One, His reflections as 'jīvas' play in all mind-intellect-equipments.

Because He is thus seen to be manifested in the world of plurality, He is "Not One." Again, "The One" is a definition, a quality. The Lord is Indefinable, quality-less (unqualified).

Hence after making the student grasp that He is "The One," where the pluralities are all merged, the teacher is immediately pointing out that He is "Not even One." For, to conceive "The One" is to conceive the Truth with our intellect—He is to be experienced on transcending the intellect. "The One" has a meaning only with reference to the many. "The One" is a relative statement. To show that the Infinite is to be "experienced" by the "becoming" and not by "knowing," the teacher has negated "Not even One." Sruti says "The Lord sports with many forms by His māyā."

‘‘इन्द्रो मायाभिः पुरुह्प ईयते।’’ (Indro maayaabhih pururoopa eeyate.)—Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2-5-19.
names.simple_meaning: "The Many."

names.short_meaning: "He Who is of the nature of the Sava—Sacrifice."
names.commentary: "He Who is of the nature of the Sava—Sacrifice." The sacrifice in which the Soma juice is squeezed out is called Sava.
names.simple_meaning: "He Who is of the nature of the Sava—Sacrifice."

names.short_meaning: “Happiness.”
names.commentary: “Happiness.” One Who is of the Nature of Bliss. Since He transcends the body-mind-intellect-equipments, which are the seats of sorrow, in Him there can be only Bliss. Or kaḥ (कः) means a question: He Who is ever a "question without an answer" to the human intellect—He who can be experienced only on transcending the intellect and not apprehended through intellection.
names.simple_meaning: “Happiness.”

names.short_meaning: "What."
names.commentary: "What." Since the Lord is the final Goal to be reached. He is the One Who is to be enquired into or diligently sought through constant questioning upon What is His Nature. Also because the Truth is realised through this process of enquiry and discrimination—the final Goal of all "What" enquiring—the Lord, is termed here as "What," (kim).
names.simple_meaning: "What."

names.short_meaning: “Which.”
names.commentary:
“Which.” The pronoun “yat” means “that which is self-existent.” Hence in the Upaniṣads we find the usage of this term frequently. It may also be noted that the pronoun "Which" (yat) denotes an already existing object. Thus the Self-existence of the Supreme Reality, independent of the existence and non-existence of things in the world is indicated when Lord Śrī Hari is termed as "Which."

"यतो वा इमानि भृतानि जायन्ते।" (Yato vaa imaani bhootaani jaayante.) —Taittirīya Up. 3-1. "That from 'Which' all these living creatures are born;" or again

‘‘यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते अप्राप्य मनसा सह।’’ (Yato vaacho nivartante apraapya manasaa saha.) -Taittirīya Upaniṣad 2-9-1.

"That from 'Which' words retire, along with the mind, unable to reach."
names.simple_meaning: “Which.”

names.short_meaning: "That."
names.commentary:
"That." The Supreme is indicated by this term in all the Upanishadic literature, and one of the mahāvākya is "That Thou Art" (तत्त्वमित). Here "That" means the Truth that is not comprehended now, but is to be apprehended through listening to the Teacher (Sravana), reflections upon what you have heard (Manana) and meditation (Nididhyaasana). In Gītā, Bhagavān says: "Om tat Sat" are the three designations of Brahman. Or again, the term tat can mean "That which expands all the world of plurality."

ॐ तत्सदिति निर्देशो ब्रह्मणस्त्रिविधःस्मतः।" (Om tatsaditi nirdeso brahmanastrividhah smritah.) "'Om Tat Sat' this has been declared to be the triple designation of Brahman.' -Gītā VII-23.

तनोतीति तत (Tanoteeti tat.) "That which fans out the manifold world of plurality is 'Tat'; for तन विस्तारे करणे च (Tanu vistaare karane cha.)
names.simple_meaning: "That."

names.short_meaning: "The Unequalled State of Perfection: The Supreme State of Truth."
names.commentary:
"The Unequalled State of Perfection: The Supreme State of Truth." Lord Viṣṇu is the Way (पद) and the Goal (पद) and the very pilgrimage (पद) "He than Whom there is no Higher."

"अनुत्तमां गतिम्।" (Anuttamaam gatim.) —Gītā VII-18.
names.simple_meaning: "The Unequalled State of Perfection: The Supreme State of Truth."

names.short_meaning: "Friend of the World."
names.commentary: "Friend of the World." Everyone is inextricably bound to Him in His Love Infinite, and He is the Father to all. Since there is no well-wisher or friend dearer than one's own Father, He is the One unfailing sure Friend of the world of beings and things. The Lord serves for the uplift of the world whenever the creatures come to suffer sorrows created by their own immoral negative ways.
names.simple_meaning: "Friend of the World."

names.short_meaning: One Who is the Lord of the World
names.commentary: “One Who is the "Lord" of the World," or "One Who is 'solicited' by the world of beings for the fulfilment of all their desires and needs. Or it also means, "One Who 'adds glory' to the world. There are also interpretations for the term 'Naath' (नाथ) which express "shines, praised by or loved by": in all these different meanings, Śrī Hari is described as the Lord of the World Lokanaatha.
names.simple_meaning: One Who is the Lord of the World

names.short_meaning: “One Who was born in the family of Madhu."
names.commentary: “One Who was born in the family of Madhu." The Vaisaakha-month is called Maadhavamonth because the Lord is the Spirit of Beauty behind the Spring and its regal lush.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who was born in the family of Madhu."

names.short_meaning: “One Whose Love for the devotees knows no bounds.”
names.commentary: “One Whose Love for the devotees knows no bounds.” He is ever merciful and endlessly kind towards His devotees.
names.simple_meaning: “One Whose Love for the devotees knows no bounds.”

names.short_meaning: “Golden Coloured” is Śrī Nārāyaṇa for He is, in the devotee, the pure Self; and in all, He is the very All — Illumining Pure Awareness
names.commentary:
“Golden Coloured” is Śrī Nārāyaṇa for He is, in the devotee, the pure Self; and in all, He is the very All — Illumining Pure Awareness. Mundaka Upaniṣad declares: "When the Seer sees Him of Golden-hue."Upon witnessing the Self — Effulgent (Golden) Being, the seer's realization is completely transforming, and "then that wise one, shaking off all deeds of merits and demerits, becomes stainless, and attains the supreme State of Equipoise."

"यदा पश्यः पश्यते रुक्मवर्णम्।" (Yadaa pasyah pasyate rukmavarnam.) —Mundaka, V-3.
names.simple_meaning: The golden-coloured one

names.short_meaning: “One who has limbs of Gold.”
names.commentary:
“One who has limbs of Gold.” The description of the Lord functioning through the orb of the Sun is well-known: Hiranmaya-"of pure-golden-form." Sruti mentions it: "This Golden Person seen in the disc of the Sun"… This same Upaniṣad insists further that "Mind is Brahman" and the "Sun is Brahman." Lord Hari, as the Infinite Brahman, plays in the Sun (Soorya — Nārāyaṇa)— thus the term is most appropriate.

‘‘य एषोऽन्तरादित्ये हिरण्मयः पुरुषो दश्यते ।’’ (Ya esho-antaraaditye hiranmayah purusho drisyate.) Chāndogya, 1-6-6.

"मनो ब्रह्मेत्युपासीत।" (Mano Brahmetyupaaseeta.) -Chāndogya, 3-18-19.

“आदित्यो ब्रह्मोत्यादेश:।” (Aadityo Brahmetyaadesah.) — Chāndogya, 8-10-1.
names.simple_meaning: “One who has limbs of Gold.”

names.short_meaning: "With beautiful limbs."
names.commentary: "With beautiful limbs." Also, Vara can take the meaning "lovable," therefore, Śrī Nārāyaṇa is described here as "One whose form (limbs) is supremely "lovable" to the yogi-of-devotion."
names.simple_meaning: "With beautiful limbs."

names.short_meaning: This is made up of two terms, "Joy-giving" (Chandana) and "armlets" (Angada)
names.commentary:
This is made up of two terms, "Joy-giving" (Chandana) and "armlets" (Angada). Thus the phrase means "One Who has attractive armlets." It can also be used as describing "One Who is smeared with the sandal."

Angada (armlet) are ornaments of defence worn on the upper arm to protect the shoulders from enemy swords.
names.simple_meaning: This is made up of two terms, "Joy-giving" (Chandana) and "armlets" (Angada)

names.short_meaning: "The destroyer of the valiant heroes"—in order to uphold righteousness, Lord Hari takes His Incarnations and destroys the intrepid and daring Asuras in battle
names.commentary: "The destroyer of the valiant heroes"—in order to uphold righteousness, Lord Hari takes His Incarnations and destroys the intrepid and daring Asuras in battle. Again, it may be interpreted as One Who destroys the powerful and mighty forces of likes and dislikes—Dvandva -pairs of opposites, the hosts of our own negativities in our hearts.
names.simple_meaning: "The destroyer of the valiant heroes"—in order to uphold righteousness, Lord Hari takes His Incarnations and destroys the intrepid and daring Asuras in battle

names.short_meaning: “Unequalled.”
names.commentary:
“Unequalled.” Arjuna, in Bhagavad Gītā, estimates his experience of the Lord’s Cosmic Form and says: “None there exists who is equal to You; how can there be then another superior to You in the t

न विद्यते समो यस्य सः विषमः ।

(Na vidyate samo yasya sah vishamah.)

"न त्वत्समोऽस्त्यभ्यधिकः कृतोऽन्यः।" (Na tvatsamo-astyabhyadhikah kuto-anyah.) -Gītā XI-43.
names.simple_meaning: “Unequalled.”

names.short_meaning: “The Void.”
names.commentary:
“The Void.” Here Void means the total absence of (a) the equipments-of-experiences—the body-mind-intellect; (b) the fields-of-experiences—the objectsemotions-thoughts; (c) the experiencer-attitudes—the perceiver-feeler-thinker personality. In Brahman, the Pure Consciousness, all these three (a, b and c) are totally absent as the devotee of Hari transcends them all. So the Lord, in His Infinite Nature, is 'without attributes;' seemingly then, He is the "Void." This is not "non-existence" of the Buddhists.

This is Pure Existence without the object-emotion-thought world—the Self. Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: “The Void.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who has no need for any good wishes from any one.”
names.commentary: “One Who has no need for any good wishes from any one.” The Infinite Lord, perfect and transcendental, has no need for any of the objects of the world to make Him complete since the state of incompleteness is indeed the springboard for all desires to gush forth. It can also mean one who has eaten away the ghee stolen from the cow-herds' store-rooms in Brindavan.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who has no need for any good wishes from any one.”

names.short_meaning: "The non-moving."
names.commentary:
"The non-moving." Either it can signify One Who never falls and therefore does not move away from His own Infinite nature, or it may mean that since the Lord is All — Pervading, He cannot move as there is no place where, at any time, He is not. He is Ever — Present everywhere.

“नित्यः सर्वगतः स्थाणरचलोऽयं सनातनः।” (Nityah sarvagatah sthaanurachalo-ayam sanātanaḥ.) "It is eternal, all-pervading, stable, immovable and ancient."

-Gītā II-24.
names.simple_meaning: "The non-moving."

names.short_meaning: "Moving."
names.commentary: "Moving." By the juxtaposition of these two opposite qualities, we are reminded that the apparent world of plurality that constitutes the realm of change is also nothing other than the immovable Atman interpreted through our personal equipments of experiences. Unconditioned by the body, mind and intellect, the Lord in His Infinitude is motionless, but as conditioned by the vehicles He apparently seems to move. We have already explained this relationship earlier. It is something like a traveller, though himself sleeping, is able to travel all the night since he is conditioned by the vehicle which carries him.
names.simple_meaning: "Moving."

names.short_meaning: “One who has no false vanity."
names.commentary: “One who has no false vanity." Since He knows His own real divine nature. He has no false identifications with the equipments of not — Self such as the flesh, the emotions or the thoughts.
names.simple_meaning: “One who has no false vanity."

names.short_meaning: "One who gives, or causes, by His māyā the false identification with the body."
names.commentary:
"One who gives, or causes, by His māyā the false identification with the body." The Sanskrit term 'maana' can also mean 'honour,' and therefore, 'maanadah' can mean One who honours all His true devotees.

The root 'da' in Sanskrit means 'blasting', and therefore, the same term can also mean one who blasts all false notions from the bosom of his devotees
names.simple_meaning: "One who gives, or causes, by His māyā the false identification with the body."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is to be honoured."
names.commentary:
"One Who is to be honoured." He is the most worshipful as He is the very material Cause for the world of plurality. Bhagavān Śaṅkara says: "If he, who has realised the Supreme, is so blessed and to be honoured in this world," how much more worshipful is the Lord who is the very substratum and support of the whole universe and by Whom all are blessed and inspired to gain their experiences in the world of things and beings!

‘‘धन्यः स मान्यो भुवि ।’’ (Dhanyah sa maanyo bhuvi.) — Vivekachoodaamani — 425.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is to be honoured."

names.short_meaning: “Lord of the Universe.”
names.commentary: “Lord of the Universe.” Here the word ‘loka’ in Sanskrit means ‘field-of-experience.' The One Who is the Controller, Director, Who is the Lord and Governor of all fields-of-experiences of all living creatures, at all times, everywhere, is the Consciousness that illumines matter. Therefore, the term Loka-svaamee is extremely appropriate.
names.simple_meaning: “Lord of the Universe.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who is the support of all the three worlds.”
names.commentary: “One Who is the support of all the three worlds.” Apart from the usual concept of the three worlds: heaven, earth and hell, there is a deeper import of the term 'loka'. It should mean the three fields of experience constituted of waking, dream and deep sleep. Atman, the Self, as Consciousness, is the One that supports all these three states inasmuch as, without this kindling support of life in the bosom, it would be impossible for us to have any experience.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is the support of all the three worlds.”

names.short_meaning: “One who has Pure Intelligence.”
names.commentary: “One who has Pure Intelligence.” In fact, the term may denote a special power in the human intellect which is the capacity to remember and repeat what has been once experienced before. As such, the term indicates that the very nature of the Self is not a knowledge newly gained, but it is only a remembrance of the seeker's own real nature, which the seeker in his earlier confusion had forgotten. So long as we have not invoked this great power of memory of our real nature, we shall continue to grope in our sorrows created by our misconception. On realising the Self, it is not that we gain anything new, but we re-discover our own essential Self. Naturally, therefore, with reference to our present forgetfulness, the ultimate goal is indicated by the pregnant term 'Divine Memory Power.'
names.simple_meaning: “One who has Pure Intelligence.”

names.short_meaning: “Born out of sacrifices.”
names.commentary:
“Born out of sacrifices.” ‘Medha’ means sacrifices like Asvamedha yajña. In such a sincere and great ritual, He is invoked and in His Pure Presence there in the sacrifice, we can say He is born. The Gītā meaning of 'sacrifices' (yajña) is "a co-operative endeavour wherein we offer our capacity into a field of chosen work invoking in it the unmanifested Lord Who pours forth His blessings in terms of profit." In this sense, when all the personality layers are offered in an act of total surrender, the spiritual experience of the Self is born. To the student of Vedānta, the term is rich in its suggestiveness.

“तस्मात्सर्वगतं ब्रह्म नित्यं यज्ञे प्रतिष्ठितम् ।” (Tasmaatsarvagatam Brahma nityam yajne pratishthitam.) —Gītā III-15.
names.simple_meaning: “Born out of sacrifices.”

names.short_meaning: “Fortunate.”
names.commentary: “Fortunate.” As He has no objects yet to be fulfilled, or any of His wishes not already fulfilled. He is indeed one who is utterly fulfilled. The state of the Self is an eternal state of total contentment.
names.simple_meaning: “Fortunate.”

names.short_meaning: “One whose intelligence never fails."
names.commentary: “One whose intelligence never fails." He is the supreme Power of Discrimination, never deluded by the finite world of appearances, but is, in all circumstances, ever rooted in the Truth that He alone is the world of multiplicity.
names.simple_meaning: “One whose intelligence never fails."

names.short_meaning: "The sole support of the earth."
names.commentary:
"The sole support of the earth." The earth here stands for matter; and the very essence from which matter has come to express itself, both in its gross and subtle forms, is the Self, Nārāyaṇa, and therefore, He is considered as the very substratum for the play of matter (earth). Geographically, the earth is supported by water.

Water is supported by the atmospheric air and the atmospheric air by the space. The daring enquirer may still continue the question and investigate into the source of space. We know that the space is a concept which we experience in our intellect.

All experiences of the intellect are established in Consciousness and, therefore, the ultimate support for the entire 'world' is the Supreme Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "The sole support of the earth."

names.short_meaning: "One Who showers Radiance."
names.commentary: "One Who showers Radiance." In the outer cosmos the Sun gives out heat and light. and because of this, rain and cultivation are possible—not directly because of the Sun, but due to the sum-total-result of an endless chain of cause-effect links. In the same way, He Who by His mere presence illumines the experiences of all living creatures with His Light, is Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Self.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who showers Radiance."

names.short_meaning: The term 'Dyuti' indicates the glow of beauty and strength in a form; thus the term means "One Who bears an Effulgent Form."
names.commentary: The term 'Dyuti' indicates the glow of beauty and strength in a form; thus the term means "One Who bears an Effulgent Form." The expression also discloses that the seat of Pure Consciousness is described as "the Bearer of Radiance" for it is in the light of the Atman that creatures become aware of all their perceptions, emotions and thoughts.
names.simple_meaning: The bearer of radiance

names.short_meaning: - "The best among those who wield weapons."
names.commentary:
"The best among those who wield weapons." Since Śrī Nārāyaṇa is described in the Purāṇas as wielding the Discus (Sudarśana), it, being the greatest of all weapons, justifies this term. Also, the Lord never uses His weapon of annihilation indiscriminately-for He is ever supremely just. It is also significant that all destructions in nature are always 'constructive destructions', therefore the Lord's Discus is itself called "the auspicious vision" (Su-darsana). In the maturity of one's evolution when one becomes fit for one's own inner unfoldment, slowly, but irresistibly the seeker can ever detect a secret hand that diligently cuts off all his connections with the outer world, and compels him to lean more and more on the higher.

Our Puranic literature is replete with instances, and, without exception, in all of them Śrī Nārāyaṇa is described as using His weapon to destroy the devilish—and to give him mokṣa!

-"the Auspicious Vision": Su-darsana. Others, when they employ their weapons on destruction, the result invariably ends in a sad 'destructive destruction', and, therefore, to invoke Him as "the best among those who wield weapons" is most significant for a seeker.
names.simple_meaning: - "The best among those who wield weapons."

names.short_meaning: One Who is the sole receiver of all the worship of every devotee, irrespective of his creed or race, or his location in the world, at all times
names.commentary:
One Who is the sole receiver of all the worship of every devotee, irrespective of his creed or race, or his location in the world, at all times. The devotee may invoke the spiritual presence in various institutions, using different symbols, believing in his own creed and scripture, but, whoever he be, when he comes to transcend his vehicles of perception, feeling and thinking, the experience of the Self (God) should be universally one and the same—as God is All — Pervading and Changeless. This great factor-transcendental is the Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, and therefore, He is the ultimate, sole Receiver of all prayers that rise consciously or unconsciously in every heart, be it from a plant, an animal or a man.

The term 'pragrahaḥ' is used in Sanskrit to mean the reins with which horses are controlled and their movements regulated. In this sense when we reflect, the metaphor of the chariot in the Upaniṣad suddenly comes in front of us. In this famous scriptural metaphor, mind is the rein by which the steeds of the sense-organs are controlled and regulated. Here Lord Śrī Nārāyaṇa Himself is invoked as 'pragrahaḥ' because when the mind has turned in devotion to His feet, the devotee need not strive to control his sense-organs, but the Lord's own glory shall imperceptibly do the job for His beloved seeker. Therefore, a truly devoted heart in its utter surrender, calls the Lord "as the very controller of his sense-organs."

Kaṭhopaniṣad—Section III—3, 4.
names.simple_meaning: One Who is the sole receiver of all the worship of every devotee, irrespective of his creed or race, or his location in the world, at all times

names.short_meaning: “The killer.”
names.commentary: “The killer.” An uninitiated student may get shocked when he finds that the Lord is invoked as a murderer! But it is true. The only difference is that He is only the destroyer of the ego—just as a doctor is a 'murderer' of diseases; just as the sun is the destroyer of the night; as summer is the annihilator of winter. Similarly, the Lord is the destroyer of ego and ego-centric limitations in the devotee. In Sanskrit this word also indicates "One Who absorbs the devotee unto Himself." Once an individual withdraws himself even a wee bit from his total pre-occupation with the world and turns his attention to the spiritual centre in himself, the Lord fascinates and enchants the seeker's attention more and more to His own Infinite Glory, and ultimately "absorbs" (Ni-grahah) the individual totally into the state of Pure — Consciousness.
names.simple_meaning: “The killer.”

names.short_meaning: "One Who is ever engaged in fulfilling the devotee's desires."
names.commentary: "One Who is ever engaged in fulfilling the devotee's desires." Desire arises in the human mind due to a sense of imperfection in oneself. In the absolute sense of bliss and peace, which is the true nature of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, there cannot arise any desire and, therefore, He is described as "the fulfiller of all desires."
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is ever engaged in fulfilling the devotee's desires."

names.short_meaning: “One Who has many (na-eka=Naika) horns.”
names.commentary: “One Who has many (na-eka=Naika) horns.” To a modern student it would look fantastic and even foolish should one worship his Lord, the God, as One with many horns. This mental shock can even stun him when he understands also that his Lord has three legs: "Chatvaarah Sringaah Trayo Asya Paadaah," says the Maha Upaniṣad. If the literal translation shocks the student, the very jolt prods him to a more vigorous enquiry. The four horns mean the four States of Consciousness—the waking, dream, deep-sleep and the fourth plane of consciousness, the Pure Awareness. The three feet (pāda) indicate the three states of consciousness in which we now revel in our gross, subtle and causal bodies respectively.
names.simple_meaning: The many-horned one

names.short_meaning: "The elder brother of Gada."
names.commentary: "The elder brother of Gada." Lord Kṛṣṇa had a younger brother whose name was Gada. The term Gada has also the meaning in Sanskrit of 'mantra.' Mantras are chanted and therefore Gada can indicate 'mantra,—'Gadyate iti gadah.' A commentator insists that Ni-gada means mantra, but the prefix Ni gets dropped, so Gada means mantra. Naturally, "Gadaagraja" would mean One who manifests or is invoked through mantras.
names.simple_meaning: "The elder brother of Gada."

names.short_meaning: "Four — Formed."
names.commentary: "Four — Formed." The Lord, the Infinite is considered as having four forms—meaning that He, in His manifestations in the world, takes these four forms. The Purāṇas have declared that the incarnations of the Lord in the various Yugas were of different colours: white in kṛta Yuga, red in Tretaa Yuga, yellow in Dvaapara Yuga and dark (black) in the Kali Yuga. But according to Vedānta, the Lord, the Self, has four distinct expressions in the subjective life of each individual: the Waker, the Dreamer, the Deep-sleeper and the Pure Self. In the microcosm these are called as Visva, Taijasa, Prajna and Tureeya, and in the macrocosm, the Lord's complete expression, in the total gross, subtle and causal bodies, is called as virāṭ, Hiranyagarbha, Eesvaraand, beyond all bodies as the Eternal paramātman.
names.simple_meaning: "Four — Formed."

names.short_meaning: Lord Nārāyaṇa is represented as having four hands
names.commentary: Lord Nārāyaṇa is represented as having four hands. These represent the four factors that together constitute the inner equipments in man— mind (Manas); intellect (Buddhi); thought flow towards objects (Chitta) and ego (ahaṅkāra). These are the four agents by which all the physical activities are controlled, regulated and constantly commanded from within the body.
names.simple_meaning: Lord Nārāyaṇa is represented as having four hands

names.short_meaning: One Who expresses Himself as the dynamic centre in the four vyūhas
names.commentary:
"One Who expresses Himself as the dynamic centre in the four vyūhas. A "vyūha" is a whirlpool of activities made by a large number of imperfected forms, commanded by a pivotal person who remains in the centre of the whirlpool—just as a battalion functions under the orders of its commander. It is shown in this analogy that the Lord, the central Source of all activities, is manifest as the universal Force which blesses every engagement and contact of a living man with his outer world. In the Aitareya Upaniṣad, the four vyūhas (or persons) are mentioned: the person in the body, the person in the Chhandas (Vedic mantra), the person in the Vedas and the Great Person.

‘‘ईश्वरः सर्वभृतानां हृद्देशेऽर्ज्न तिष्ठति। भ्रामयन्सर्वभृतानि यन्त्रारूढानि मायया ॥’’ (Īśvaraḥ sarvabhootaanaam hrid-desearjuna tishthati; Bhraamayan sarvabhootaani yantraaroodhaani maayayaa.) The Lord dwells in the hearts of all beings, O Arjuna, causing all beings, by His illusive power, to revolve as if mounted on a machine."

-Gītā XVIII-61. ‘‘शरीरपूरुषञ्छन्दःपूरुषो वेदपूरुषो महापूरुषः ।’’ (Sareerapurushaschhandahpurusho vedapurusho mahaapurushah.) -Aitareya Upaniṣad 3-2-8.
names.simple_meaning: One Who expresses Himself as the dynamic centre in the four vyūhas

names.short_meaning: "The ultimate goal of all the four."
names.commentary: "The ultimate goal of all the four." Though their means and purposes appear divergent, Śrī Nārāyaṇa alone is the inevitable goal of all activities of the four types (Varnas) of men: Thinkers (brāhmaṇas), Rulers and Leaders (Kshatriyas), Men of Commerce (Vaisyas) and Workers (Soodras). The Lord, also, is the consummate goal to be achieved by the four stages (Aasramas) of life: the Age of Study (Brahmacharya), the Householder (Grihastha), the Retirement (Vaanaprastha) and the Stage of Renunciation (saṃnyāsa).
names.simple_meaning: "The ultimate goal of all the four."

names.short_meaning: The clear-minded
names.commentary: There is also a reading as Chatvaraatmaa (चत्वरात्मा). In the former reading, the definition suggests "the clear-minded"—meaning the Lord is one who is completely free from desires, passions, vanities, in short, free from all maladies of ego in His essential Nature. In the latter term, the meaning signifies that Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the one Infinite Effulgence which expresses Itself as the four aspects of our inner equipment (Antahkarana Chatushtava).
names.simple_meaning: The clear-minded

names.short_meaning: "The Source of the four."
names.commentary:
"The Source of the four." One Who is the Source for the four types (Varna), for the four stages-of-life (Aasrama) and the four human aspirations (purushaartha). The human aspirations as codified by the sanātana dharma are again four in number. Righteousness (dharma), Wealth (Artha), Pleasure (kāma) and Spiritual Liberation (mokṣa). Lord Kṛṣṇa reveals in the Bhagavad Gītā: "All the four types in creation have come from Me."

‘‘चातूर्वण्यं मया सप्टं…।’’ (Chaaturvarnyam māyayā srishtam…) "The fourfold caste has been created by Me according to the differentiation of guṇa and Karma…?

Gītā IV-13.
ocr_notes: Scan locus corrected from [198] to [198, 199] by complete-text replay against the PDF page OCR.
names.simple_meaning: "The Source of the four."

names.short_meaning: "Knower of all the four Vedas."
names.commentary:
"Knower of all the four Vedas." The Lord is the very theme discussed and expounded in the four vedas. The student of the vedas when he realises the Lord, then only he fulfils his study of them. In this sense of the term, Bhagavān proclaims in the Fifteenth Chapter of Gītā: "I am verily that which has to be known in all the Vedas: I am indeed the author of the Vedas and the "knower" of the Vedas am I."

''वेदान्तकृद्वेदविदेव चाहम।'' (Vedaantakridvedavideva chaaham.) - -Gītā XV-15.
names.simple_meaning: "Knower of all the four Vedas."

names.short_meaning: "The one-footed."
names.commentary:
"The one-footed." The term 'pāda' in Sanskrit has two meanings: a 'part' and a 'foot." The Lord, in Bhagavad Gītā, uses the first meaning to describe His mighty Glory: "The whole universe is supported by one part of Myself." There is a reference in the Taittirīya Aaranyaka which clarifies the latter meaning: "All beings are His foot." The significance here is the same as in Gītā—wherein even the totality of all universes cannot be compared to Him, the Infinite Absolute Existence.

''विष्टभ्याहमिदं क्रत्स्नमेकांशेन स्थितो जगत।'' (Vishtabhyaahamidam kritsnamekaamsena sthito jagat.) Gītā X-42.
names.simple_meaning: "The one-footed."

names.short_meaning: “The efficient turner” -of the wheel-of-life
names.commentary: “The efficient turner” -of the wheel-of-life. 'Aavarta' is to turn. The wheel-of-life-and-death, the samsar, is constantly being churned by the Law, which is none other than the Lord. The Law and the Law — Giver are one and the same in this universe—Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: “The efficient turner” -of the wheel-of-life

names.short_meaning: “One whose mind is turned away from all sense indulgences."
names.commentary:
“One whose mind is turned away from all sense indulgences." The famous 'two birds' of the Mundaka Upaniṣad strike a simile here. "Two birds bound one to the other in close friendship, perch on the selfsame tree. One of them eats the fruits of the tree with relish, while the other looks on without eating." The latter is the anivṛttātmā. Some commentators have taken the word as 'A-nivrittaatmaa' in which case the meaning would be: "One who never turns away from anything, but enters into everything," as the very Self is every thing and every being—that Supreme One, Lord Nārāyaṇa.

Mundaka Upaniṣad III-I-1.
names.simple_meaning: “One whose mind is turned away from all sense indulgences."

names.short_meaning: "The Invincible"—One who cannot be conquered by anyone else
names.commentary: "The Invincible"—One who cannot be conquered by anyone else. Even though, in the majority of us, there is a preponderance of the lower urges, in the patient grinding of time, the evolutionary goal ultimately wins and irresistibly pushes each one of us towards the altar of the Self. Battles may be lost but the war in the end is won by the Lord of our heart.
names.simple_meaning: "The Invincible"—One who cannot be conquered by anyone else

names.short_meaning: “One Who is difficult to be disobeyed.”
names.commentary:
“One Who is difficult to be disobeyed.” This term declares a truth which is proven upon observation of this scientifically precise world where no object or being dares to disobey the Lord, the Cosmos. The ṛṣi in Kaṭhopaniṣad says "through fear of Him the Fire burns, through fear of Him shines the Sun, through fear of Him functions Indra, Vaayu, Lord of the Wind, and Death itself is the fifth"—as though He is behind each one with uplifted thunderbolt. The term 'Atikramah' means 'going beyond', therefore the term, as it stands, indicates "a state beyond which no one can go"-meaning Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the final and the absolute destination of all evolution. He is the transcendental Reality and other than He there is no more a beyond to be achieved.

‘‘भयादस्याग्निस्तपति भयात्तपति सुर्यः। भयादिन्द्रश्च वायुश्च मृत्युर्धावति पञ्चमः।" (Bhayaadasyaagnistapati bhayaattapati sooryah; Bhayaadindrascha vaayuscha mrityurdhaavati panchamah.) -Kaṭhopaniṣad II-3-3.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is difficult to be disobeyed.”

names.short_meaning: "One Who is obtained with consummate effort."
names.commentary: "One Who is obtained with consummate effort." The final destination of all evolution is He, the spiritual perfection. Therefore, He is only gained after millenniums of slow evolutions, from the insignificant unicellular existence to the status of man, and the fulfilment of man's evolved, rational life is the state of Godhood. The reward for all the slow and steady efforts of evolution is bestowed when an organism reaches the height of the rational human being; and, thereafter, through selfless, dedicated service, deep and individual devotion, and sincere and serious study of the scriptures, man learns to remove his mind from all his worldly pre-occupations and brings himself to finally realise his divine Godhood. Indeed, the state of Nārāyaṇa — Consciousness is an experience that is to be obtained with consummate effort.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is obtained with consummate effort."

names.short_meaning: “One Who is realised with great difficulty.”
names.commentary:
“One Who is realised with great difficulty.” In Bhagavata there is a statement that the Lord is easily obtained (A-dur-gamah). For those who have not already developed extreme meditative abilities in their devoted hearts, the processes of self development, when studied from a book or heard from a teacher, the immediate reaction in the bosom of such students will be that it is very difficult.

But as he marches forward in his saadhanaa he gains the further guidance and inspiration to 'go-forward.' More bounteous aspects on him beam and the 'kindly light' leads him safely to the goal through all obstacles. A candle or torch can at best light up only ten or fifteen yards in front of a traveller. It can never illumine the whole path of one or two miles at a stretch.

He has to start and proceed as far as he can see and as he marches ahead the forward stretches will be illumined.

‘‘दुर्गं पथस्तत्कवयो वदन्ति।’’ (Durgam pathastatkavayo vadanti.) —Kaṭhopaniṣad 1-3-14.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is realised with great difficulty.”

names.short_meaning: "Not easy to storm into."
names.commentary:
"Not easy to storm into." The term is used in Sanskrit to indicate a fortress; therefore the suggestion is that the essence of the Lord, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, is fortressed around by the matter vestures and their objects of fascination. Attracted by them, our attention is always distracted towards the joy contents in them. This seducing power of the matter vestures is itself the mighty māyā, which only very rare, courageous and blessed ones are able to cross over.Bhagavān Himself says: "Mama māyā Duratyavaa… " The Upaniṣads say that the Truth, Nārāyaṇa, cannot be perceived by the senses, imagined by the mind or thought of by the intellect. These being the only source of our knowing, it seems almost impossible to realise the Truth. It is only an all-out suicidal attack that enables some rare ones to storm the fort and reach the Goal. Hence to an extrovert man, the seat of Consciousness apparently seems to be impenetrably fortified.

The direct meaning here indicates the great Lord seated in our heart Who is "not easily realised."

‘‘दैवी ह्येषा गुणमयी मम माया द्रत्यया । मामेव ये प्रपद्यन्ते मायामेतां तरन्ति ते ॥" (Daivee hyeshaa gunamayee mama māyā duratyayaa; Maameva ye prapadyante maayaametaam taranti te.) -Gītā VII-14.

‘‘यतो वाचो निवर्तन्ते अप्राप्य मनसा सह।’’ (Yato vaacho nivartante apraapya manasaa sah.) "He who knows the Bliss of Brahman, from which all words return without reaching It, together with the mind, is no more afraid of anything."

-Taittireeva Upaniṣad II-9-1.
names.simple_meaning: "Not easy to storm into."

names.short_meaning: “Not casy to lodge”— within the heart steadily for even great seekers who are diligent in their consistent pursuit
names.commentary:
“Not easy to lodge”— within the heart steadily for even great seekers who are diligent in their consistent pursuit. To withdraw the mind from the objects of pleasure and to steadily contemplate upon the great Seat of Life is not an easy accomplishment. Therefore, even yogins, in their persevering meditation, find it not easy to contemplate steadily upon Śrī Nārāyaṇa, hence this name.

"This Yoga of equanimity, taught by Thee, O slayer of Madhu, I see not its enduring continuity, because of the restlessness (of the mind)," cries Arjuna in the Gītā. Bhagavān also adds in the same Chaptert that the meditation should be "As a lamp placed in a windless place does not flicker."

‘‘योऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मध्सूदन। एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात स्थिति स्थिराम ॥' (Yo ayam yogastvayaa proktah saamyena madhusoodana; Etasyaaham na pasyaami chanchalatvaat sthitim sthiraam.) -Gītā VI-33.

‘‘यथा दीपो निवातस्थो ने ज्ञते सोपमा स्मृता। योगिनो यतचित्तस्य युञ्जतो योगमात्मनः ।।’’ (Yathaa deepo nivaatastho nengate sopamaa smritaa; Yogino yatachittasya yunjato yogamaatmanah.) -Gītā VI-19.
names.simple_meaning: “Not casy to lodge”— within the heart steadily for even great seekers who are diligent in their consistent pursuit

names.short_meaning: "One Who is the slayer of the devilish Asuras."
names.commentary: "One Who is the slayer of the devilish Asuras." Even in those among us who are not steadily good, the Lord, when invoked, out of His compassion, destroys the devilishness and redeems our personality from its sad consequences. The asuric tendencies are in the bosom of every seeker and devoted invocation of the Lord in our bosom can cleanse the heart of all its negative tendencies. Therefore, it is indeed appropriate that He is significantly indicated as Duraarihaa '
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is the slayer of the devilish Asuras."

names.short_meaning: “One with enchanting limbs of perfect beauty.”
names.commentary: “One with enchanting limbs of perfect beauty.” The Beauty of all beauty is the Lord, and His captivating form and the rhythm of His shape are the theme of meditation for the devotees. In the Upaniṣads the Infinite Lord, the Self, is described as Peace — Auspiciousness — Beauty (Saantam — Sivam — Sundavam). Thus the devotees of the Lord, remembering the auspicious beauty of His sacred limbs, prostrate at His altar in their deep reverence and mounting joy of devotion.
names.simple_meaning: “One with enchanting limbs of perfect beauty.”

names.short_meaning: “One who has enquired into or understood the Essence behind the universe of names and forms."
names.commentary: “One who has enquired into or understood the Essence behind the universe of names and forms." Or, lokasāraṅgaḥ can mean the essence, or the source, of the world which is the great praṇava, 'OM.' So the term means the State of Supreme Consciousness that is gained or reached through the contemplation upon the significance of OM.
names.simple_meaning: “One who has enquired into or understood the Essence behind the universe of names and forms."

names.short_meaning: "Beautifully expanded."
names.commentary:
"Beautifully expanded." Just as the thread is drawn out in different counts from cotton which is later employed as the warp and woof in the creation of infinite varieties of cloth, so too, from the Nārāyaṇa — Consciousness, the endless variety of beings and things gets projected to constitute the enchanting tapestry of His mighty universe. As the thread is the substratum for all the various fabrics, the Nārāyaṇa is the beautiful thread, the substratum, for all this wonderful universe. The Lord Himself says: "There is nothing whatsoever higher than I, O Dhananjaya. All this is strung on Me, as clusters of gems on a string.

“मत्तः परतरं नान्यत किञ्चिदस्ति धनञ्जय।

मयि सर्वमिदं प्रोतं सूत्रे मणिगणा इव ।।" (Mattah parataram naanyat kinchidasti dhananjaya;Mayi sarvam idam protam sootre maniganaa iva.) -Gītā VII-7.
names.simple_meaning: "Beautifully expanded."

names.short_meaning: "One who sustains the continuity of the drive for the family."
names.commentary: "One who sustains the continuity of the drive for the family." The family is maintained by the virility of the members and this potency in the individual is an expression of vitality which Life imparts to the living organism. Thus, the grace of the Self is that which is manifested in the fertility of the seed (Ojas). Generally in India, among the Hindus, it is customary to attribute the continuity of the family to the Grace of Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "One who sustains the continuity of the drive for the family."

names.short_meaning: “One who always performs gloriously auspicious actions."
names.commentary: “One who always performs gloriously auspicious actions." The root 'Id' is used in the sense of Supreme Auspiciousness, Parama-aisvarya (परमैश्वर्य).
names.simple_meaning: “One who always performs gloriously auspicious actions."

names.short_meaning: "One Who accomplishes Great Activities."
names.commentary: "One Who accomplishes Great Activities." To create a cosmos so scientifically precise and perfect out of the five great elements, and to sustain them all with an iron hand of efficiency, all the time constantly presiding over the acts of destruction without which the world of change cannot be maintained, is, in itself, a colossal achievement of an Absolute Intelligence.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who accomplishes Great Activities."

names.short_meaning: "One Who has fulfilled all His activities."
names.commentary: "One Who has fulfilled all His activities." There is nothing more for Him to achieve. He is the Goal. He is the Destination. In His Eternal Perfection there is nothing more for Him yet to achieve. This sense of complete fulfilment is described in all the scriptures as the State of Blissful Perfection—the Self.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has fulfilled all His activities."

names.short_meaning: “One who is the author of the Vedas."
names.commentary:
“One who is the author of the Vedas." The vedic mantras are called Agamah. The mantras were revealed to the great ṛṣis during moments when they were not identified with the Body — Mind — Intellect and, therefore, they were not, at those inspired mo- ments, limited individual egos. Where the ego is thus ended, the Self alone comes to manifest. In this sense of the term, all scriptures have burst forth from prophets and seers when they transcended their limited existence to experience their oneness with the Eternal, Śrī Nārāyaṇa. In Bhagavad Gītā also, Lord Kṛṣṇa confesses, "I am the author of all the Vedas; I alone am the knower of the Veda."

“वेदैश्च सर्वेरहमेव वेद्यो वेदान्तक्रद्वेदविदेव चाहम ।” (Vedaischa sarvairahameva vedyo vedaantakrid vedavideva chaaham.) -Gītā XV-15.
names.simple_meaning: “One who is the author of the Vedas."

names.short_meaning: "The ultimate source"— the very spring of Creation
names.commentary:
"The ultimate source"— the very spring of Creation. In the Puranic view of the term, it may mean One Who has by His own free-will manifested Himself by Himself for the service of mankind, or, it may designate subjectively, the Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, as the one dynamic Witness in Whose Presence alone the vital activities of life gush forth into expression.

"सर्वयोनिष कौन्तेय मुर्तयः संभवन्ति याः। तासां ब्रह्म महद्योनिरहं बीजप्रदः पिता ॥" (Sarvayonishu kaunteya moortayah sambhavanti yaah; Taasaam brahma mahad yoniraham beejapradah pitaa.) "Whatever forms are produced, O Kaunteya, in any womb whatsoever, the Great Brahman is their womb, I the seed-giving Father."

-Gītā XIV-4.
names.simple_meaning: "The ultimate source"— the very spring of Creation

names.short_meaning: “Of unrivalled beauty.”
names.commentary:
“Of unrivalled beauty.” In almost all religions the Infinite Lord is described as one having the most enchanting beauty. When we experience beauty in the world, we are moved to consider its beauty either by the proportion or the symmetry, or the tender charm in the object of observation. Within the mind of the observer, there reflects for a moment the rhythmic grace in the proportion, the smooth peace in the symmetry, or the joy of ecstasy which ripples out from the object into the contemplative eye. In all these condi- tions, the observer's mind, sensitive to the aestheticism in him, quietens, and, it is at such moments of supreme inner satisfaction, the flashes of "beauty-experiences" flood the bosom.

Remember, beauty is not in the object nor is it in the mind. The enchanting occasion silences the mind that is now available for the aesthetic reaction which resultingly fills the observer—and this is nothing but the manifestation of That which is behind the mind, Śrī Nārāyaṇa. Hence, the Infinite Reality is glorified in the Upaniṣads as "Peace — Auspiciousness — Beauty" (Saantam — Sivam — Sundaram).
names.simple_meaning: “Of unrivalled beauty.”

names.short_meaning: “Of Great Mercy.”
names.commentary: “Of Great Mercy.” Whatever be the amount of vāsanās hoarded in our personality, due to our ego-centric, extroverted activities, once a devotee turns unto Him in total surrender, all the vāsanās are purified and he comes to move more and more towards Him—as though, in infinite mercy, He forgives all sins that a man might commit in his innocent ignorance (Avidvaa).
names.simple_meaning: “Of Great Mercy.”

names.short_meaning: "Of beautiful navel."
names.commentary:
"Of beautiful navel." Text books of Bhakti-cult advise devotees that they should meditate upon the Lord's navel-point, as a flashy, brilliant jewel (Ratna). This point of concentration is not without significance. The mystics of India long ago explored the percentage of human action that is grossly manifest at the physical level. Today also, psychologists confess that they have no other knowledge beyond the obvious fact that thoughts express themselves as actions. But deeply meditative mystic enquirers delved deeper to detect and chart the story of actions. In their adventurous explorations, they discovered that in seed form all thoughts are with the Infinite (Para) before manifestation.

From this womb they become manifest and an individual becomes dimly aware of thoughts in their embryo form-vague and still incompletely un-formed (Pasyantee). Thereafter, the thoughts get translated into expressions (Madhyamaa) and in their last full stage of manifestation they come to express themselves as actions in the outer world (Vaikharee).

In this chain of processes when thoughts become manifest for the thinker, it is said the seat of Pasyantee-stage is the navel region. This brilliant seat of nascent manifestation of all thoughts is indicated here as "the jewel of his navel." Generally, the intelligent student would readily jump to the conclusion that this truth is merely a poetic exaggeration, but there is a deep significance in it indeed.

This is perhaps the significance of the representation that from the navel of Viṣṇu rises the lotus on which sits the "Creator" of the Cosmos.

names.simple_meaning: "Of beautiful navel."

names.short_meaning: -"One Who has the most enchanting eyes."
names.commentary:
"One Who has the most enchanting eyes." The term indicates the beauty of the Lord's eyes for those devotees who turn to the Lord's form. To the deeper students of contemplation, the eyes are great not because of their form, colour or expression, but because of their ability to see constantly the infinite purpose and goal of the entire creation. Therefore, the term means "One who has the wisdom of the Self."

The Sruti says: "It is the eye of the eye" (चक्षुषश्चक्षुः) -Kenopaniṣad 1-2.
names.simple_meaning: -"One Who has the most enchanting eyes."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is in the form of the Sun."
names.commentary:
"One Who is in the form of the Sun." The Sun is worshipped as a Vedic deity, even by the Creator Himself-hence, the term suggests 'most worshipful.' The Sun—centre of the solar system—is the one source of light and energy illumining and nourishing everything. The Infinite Consciousness, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, is the Sun by Whose Splendour the experiences of all people are illumined, at all places and at all times. He, as the One Life, thrills all living creatures and presides over, in and through their nurture and nourishment.

Once He has left from therein, that body cannot be maintained -though we witness today the experiments of medical science to do so.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is in the form of the Sun."

names.short_meaning: "The giver of food."
names.commentary:
"The giver of food." The one Vital Force that ultimately sustains, supports and nourishes all living creatures in the Universe is the Supreme. and Its Nature is not really different from the Lord, Śrī Nārāyaṇa. In the Bhagavad Gītā the Lord describes Himself as manifesting through the sun as the sunlight which penetrates the earth to fertilise it. The fertility of the soil, in turn, becomes the plant on the surface into which the Lord transfuses the food value of the vegetable world by the essence of moonlight from the moon. Further, in the Upaniṣads, we find indicative declarations that offerings, given in the worship of Fire themselves come down as a reward in the form of rain and plenty for the society.Again, it is a law of life that each individual is supplied with the exact type of 'equipments for experiences' and each one also finds himself in the precise environmental circumstances for their expression according to the texture and type of vāsanās in him. Thus, in the larger sense, the entire world of 'emotions-feelings-and-thoughts' constitute the total food (Annam) for the experiences of the body, mind and intellect.

Gītā, XV-12, 13.
names.simple_meaning: "The giver of food."

names.short_meaning: "The horned one."
names.commentary: "The horned one." This is generally commented upon as reminiscent of the Lord's Incarnation as a Fish. It would have been happier had it been reminiscent of the Boar — Incarnation which Śrī Nārāyaṇa took to lift up the world from its slushy condition to the plane of dry-surfaced earth.
names.simple_meaning: "The horned one."

names.short_meaning: "The conqueror of all enemies."
names.commentary: "The conqueror of all enemies." No force could ever vanguish Him Who is 'the Source of all energy and strength'—the Almighty. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is acclaimed as the conqueror, because it is by His Grace and direct help that the gods always win against the 'diabolically bad' (the Asuras). In our bosom it is the grace of the mind and intellect, in attunement with the Self, that helps us to conquer our lower impulses, our endless desires for the sensuous—and our craving for the cruel pleasures of indulgence.
names.simple_meaning: "The conqueror of all enemies."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is at once Omniscient (Sarvavit) and victorious (jayī)."
names.commentary: "One Who is at once Omniscient (Sarvavit) and victorious (jayī)." The term, however, is not two words and, therefore, as a single expression, we can also understand it to mean, 'One who is victorious over all men of wisdom.' Prattlers of wisdom, however eloquent in their discussions, must become utterly silent in their moments of samādhi, in the presence of the Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is at once Omniscient (Sarvavit) and victorious (jayī)."

names.short_meaning: "With limbs radiant like gold."
names.commentary:
"With limbs radiant like gold." Chāndogya Upaniṣad declares: "He, having a golden body, even to the tip of his nails." The great name of the Lord in the Vedic literature is 'OM' which consists of the sounds 'A', 'U', and the bindu 'M.'
