‘‘आप्रणखात् सर्व एव सूवर्णः ।’’ (Aapranakhaat sarva eva suvarnah.) - Chāndogya Up. 1-6-6.

Which is otherwise called as the Anusvaara.
names.simple_meaning: "With limbs radiant like gold."

names.short_meaning: “One Who is ever unruffled."
names.commentary:
“One Who is ever unruffled." Ordinarily an individual gets disturbed, subjectively, by the presence of desires, anger, passions, etc., and objectively an average man is constantly stormed by the enchanting dance of beautiful sense-objects all around him. Lord, the Self, is a state of existence wherein neither the subjective disturbances of the mind, nor the objective persecutions of the sense-organs can ever reach to ruffle the quietude and peaceful grace of His perfection. In describing the state of the Sthitaprajna, Bhagavān says in the Gītā that such a one will be Akshobhya like the ocean: "He attains Peace into whom all desires enter as waters enter the ocean, which filled from all sides, remains unmoved; but not the 'desirer-of-desires."

''आपर्य माणमचलप्रतिष्ठं समद्रमापः प्रविशन्ति यद्वत । तद्वत कामा यं प्रविशन्ति सर्वे स शान्तिमाप्नोति न कामकामी ।।" (Aapooryamaanam achalapratishtham samudramaapah pravisanti yadvat; Tadvat kaamaa yam pravisanti sarve sa saantimaapnoti na kaamakaamee.) --Gītā II-70.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is ever unruffled."

names.short_meaning: “The very Lord of the Lord of Speech.”
names.commentary:
“The very Lord of the Lord of Speech.” In the Kenopaniṣad it has been made amply clear that it is not the instruments of actions and perceptions that act by themselves as they are all made up of inert matter. The immediate animation to the equipment is given by the 'inner instruments.' Therefore, for all the sense-organs, the mind-intellect-equipment is their immediate Lord. But these subtle instruments themselves get their dynamism to act only in the presence of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Consciousness. Therefore, it is most appropriate to invoke Him as the Lord of Lords in all living creatures.

The term Vaageesvara (Lord of Speech) is often used in the language to indicate poets, writers and orators. Therefore, the term can also be interpreted as 'the Lord from whose altar all ordinary speakers draw their powers. Theologically, some commentators have spun a meaning out of this term indicating that Śrī Nārāyaṇa, as the Absolute Reality, is the 'Lord' of even the Creator.

"यत् वाचा अनभ्यदितं येन वागभ्यद्यते ।" Kenopaniṣad 1-4.
names.simple_meaning: “The very Lord of the Lord of Speech.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who is like a great refreshing swimming pool.”
names.commentary: “One Who is like a great refreshing swimming pool.” In the hot summer season, plunging into the cool crystal waters of a pool holds the swimmer in a refreshing cool embrace on all sides. Similarly, the plane of Nārāyaṇa — Consciousness revives, refreshes and enthralls all meditators when they plunge into Its reviving quietude. The yogins often plunge into It from the springboard of their devotion, and after a time emerge out of It—cool, clean and refreshed. Śrī Nārāyaṇa is metaphorically addressed as the great (Mahaa) pond (Hradah).
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is like a great refreshing swimming pool.”

names.short_meaning: "The great chasm."
names.commentary:
"The great chasm." Here the 'chasm' means the Lord's māyā which He Himself describes, in the Bhagavad Gītā as "My māyā (non-apprehension and the consequent misapprehension) is very difficult to cross over." The industrious lexicographers enter here and additionally press out of this word garta the meaning, 'chariot,' and, therefore, the term can also mean that He is a 'mahaaratha' (Great Chariot).

‘‘मम माया दूरत्यया।’’ (Mama māyā duratyayaa.) —Gītā VII-14.
names.simple_meaning: "The great chasm."

names.short_meaning: "The Great Being."
names.commentary: "The Great Being." He is the Source from which even the Great Elements spring forth into existence and, therefore, in His Infinitude and Pervasiveness, Lord Nārāyaṇa is called 'mahābhūtaḥ.' The entire play of birth and death, of integration (sanghaata) and disintegration (vighauta) are taking place in Him Who is the mighty substratum and, therefore, it is very appropriate that the Lord, the God, is considered by the devotees as the "Great Being.'
names.simple_meaning: "The Great Being."

names.short_meaning: "The Great Abode."
names.commentary: "The Great Abode." "The Eternal Source from which everything springs forth and the Infinite substratum upon which the entire play of the finite is held in animated suspension." The term 'nidhi' means 'treasure' and, therefore, its indication here is that Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the richest treasure of all His devotees—to loot at will!
names.simple_meaning: "The Great Abode."

names.short_meaning: “One Who gladdens the earth,” or “one who gets gladdened by the earth.”
names.commentary: “One Who gladdens the earth,” or “one who gets gladdened by the earth.” Earth here should be understood as the entire cosmos ever so dynamic and scientifically precise. The world of plurality is Nārāyaṇa's joyous expression of His infinite potentialities. It is the fulfilment of the Omnipotent.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who gladdens the earth,” or “one who gets gladdened by the earth.”

names.short_meaning: The one who tore the earth in His Incarnation as the Boar in order to destroy the mighty tyrant, Hiraṇyākṣa
names.commentary:
"The one who tore the earth in His Incarnation as the Boar in order to destroy the mighty tyrant, Hiraṇyākṣa. It can also mean: Darah (one who wears); Kum (the earth). The term is further commented upon as "One who bestows rewards as beautiful as the Kunda flowers."

hiraṇya means 'gold' and Aksha means 'eye'—thus "One who has an eye for gold only" is Hiraṇyākṣa—a man of pure materialism and, therefore, a man of the sheer secular point-of-view.
names.simple_meaning: The one who tore the earth in His Incarnation as the Boar in order to destroy the mighty tyrant, Hiraṇyākṣa

names.short_meaning: Here we read it as 'Kunda flower.'
names.commentary: Here we read it as 'Kunda flower.' In this context the term means "One who is as comely and attractive as the kunda flowers." In Hariyamsa it is said that the Lord, as Parasuraama, in order to atone for the battles he had fought, gave (da) gifts of this earth (kum) to ṛṣi Kasyapa. 'Ku' also has the meaning of the "rulers of the earth," and 'da' means "slaying." In this way the term indicates the "one who had taken the Incarnation of Parasuraama to destroy the unreasonably vicious tyrants of the land."
names.simple_meaning: The one lovely as the white jasmine flower

names.short_meaning: "He who is similar to the rain-bearing clouds."
names.commentary:
"He who is similar to the rain-bearing clouds." Lord Kṛṣṇa has been described as being so gloriously hued. Again, agriculturists and all living creatures are extremely happy when they see these clouds—the harbingers of comfort and prosperity. To the devotees, the Lord is a total fulfilment, as the clouds are for the parched earth.

‘‘यज्ञाद्भवति पर्जन्यो यज्ञः कर्मसम्द्भवः। कर्म ब्रह्मोद्भवं विद्धि ब्रह्माक्षरसम्द्भवम्॥" (Yajnaad bhavati parjanyo yajnah karmasamudbhavah;Karma brahmodbhavam viddhi brahmaaksharasamudbhavam.) "… from rain food is produced; from sacrifice arises rain, and sacrifice is born of action. Know you that action comes from Brahma (the Creator) and Brahma comes from the Imperishable… —Gītā III-14, 15.
names.simple_meaning: "He who is similar to the rain-bearing clouds."

names.short_meaning: "One Who ever purifies."
names.commentary: "One Who ever purifies." The impurities of a personality are gathered when the mind and intellect, in a natural impulse of animal voluntuousness. rush towards the sense-objects with ego-centric passion. To retrieve the mind from the sense-objects and to peacefully let it settle in contemplation of the divine nature and the eternal glory of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Self, is to exhaust all the existing vāsanās, which are the personality-impurities within.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who ever purifies."

names.short_meaning: Like the atmospheric air the Lord is the life-giver everywhere, and also He is All-pervading
names.commentary: Like the atmospheric air the Lord is the life-giver everywhere, and also He is All-pervading. Nilah also means 'to slip'—into a condition of non-apprehension: thus, one who is ignorant (avidya). When the symbol of negation, 'a', is added to it, 'A-nilah' comes to indicate "One who slips not, but is ever of the nature of Consciousness." Hence it means "Omniscient."
names.simple_meaning: Like the atmospheric air the Lord is the life-giver everywhere, and also He is All-pervading

names.short_meaning: Since 'amrita' has both the meanings of 'nectar' and 'immortality,' the term is interpreted to mean "One whose desires are never fruitless," as well as "One whose greatest desire is for the State of Immortality."
names.commentary: Since 'amrita' has both the meanings of 'nectar' and 'immortality,' the term is interpreted to mean "One whose desires are never fruitless," as well as "One whose greatest desire is for the State of Immortality."
names.simple_meaning: The one whose aspiration is immortality

names.short_meaning: “He Whose Form is Immortal.”
names.commentary: “He Whose Form is Immortal.” He, the Eternal Reality, is unconditioned by time. This principle of Consciousness, functioning as the flame of life in every bosom, by Its mere presence has in Itself neither the physical, subtle nor causal bodies—which alone are the perishable. Transcending them all—unconditioned by time, and, therefore, never undergoing any of the natural modifications of mortality, Śrī Nārāyaṇa revels in His Absolute Glory.
names.simple_meaning: “He Whose Form is Immortal.”

names.short_meaning: "Omniscient."
names.commentary: "Omniscient." It is only when the light of Awareness illumines the happenings that living creatures can become conscious of their experiences. To know the outer and the inner world of happenings, they must be lighted up by the principle of Consciousness. This seat of Śrī Nārāyaṇa is, therefore, called the Pure Knowledgethe Principle, because of vihich all other knowledge is possible in every being.
names.simple_meaning: "Omniscient."

names.short_meaning: "One Who has His face turned everywhere"—just as the light in the sun, or the light of a lamp
names.commentary:
"One Who has His face turned everywhere"—just as the light in the sun, or the light of a lamp. In the Bhagavad Gītā He is described as having eyes, heads and faces on all sides.

"सर्वतः पाणिपादं तत् सर्वतोऽक्षिशिरोमुखम्।" (Sarvatah paanipaadam tat sarvatoakshisiromukham.) -Gītā XIII-14.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has His face turned everywhere"—just as the light in the sun, or the light of a lamp

names.short_meaning: “One Who is readily available” and, therefore, easily attainable for those who have true devotion and the heroism to put forth the right effort in unveiling Him from the miserable pits of matter
names.commentary:
“One Who is readily available” and, therefore, easily attainable for those who have true devotion and the heroism to put forth the right effort in unveiling Him from the miserable pits of matter. To the mind in contemplation, the Reality is self-evident; all saadhanaas are only to render the mind contemplative.

"अनन्यचेताः सततं यो मां स्मरति नित्यशः। तस्याहं सूलभः पार्थं नित्ययुक्तस्य योगिनः ॥" (Ananyachetaah satatam yo maam smarati nityasah;Tasyaaham sulabhah paartha nityayuktasya yoginah.)"I am easily attainable by that ever-steadfast Yogi who constantly remembers Me daily, not thinking of anything else, O Pa
names.simple_meaning: The one readily attained through true devotion

names.short_meaning: He Who has taken the most auspicious Forms—to destroy the evil and to protect the good
names.commentary: "He Who has taken the most auspicious Forms''—to destroy the evil and to protect the good is the motive behind all His manifestations. The seeker himself is one of the Lord's own manifestations; thus, every spiritual student will ultimately realise that to destroy the ego in himself and finally gain back the very state from which he apparently manifested is re-discovery of the Self.
names.simple_meaning: He Who has taken the most auspicious Forms—to destroy the evil and to protect the good

names.short_meaning: "One Who is Perfection"—not one who has attained perfection
names.commentary: "One Who is Perfection"—not one who has attained perfection. Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Absolute State of Perfection, can never, even when He is playing as the Incarnation, forget His real nature of Eternal, Unbroken, Unchanging Perfection.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is Perfection"—not one who has attained perfection

names.short_meaning: "One Who is ever victorious over His hosts of enemies."
names.commentary: "One Who is ever victorious over His hosts of enemies." In the bosom of man, his enemies are none other than consciousness of his body and the consequent passions of the flesh—both objective and subjective.The seeker feels that these urges in him constitute a very powerful team of belligerent forces, and against their concerted onslaught he feels helpless. But when such an alert seeker turns himself towards the Truth, the Lord Who is in his own heart, all obstacles whither away. It is natural then that Śrī Nārāyaṇa is invoked here as the "Supreme Conqueror of all Enemies."
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is ever victorious over His hosts of enemies."

names.short_meaning: “The Scorcher of enemies.”
names.commentary: “The Scorcher of enemies.” When the devotee offers himself at the altar of His Feet. He burns down all the negative tendencies polluting the devotee's heart.
names.simple_meaning: “The Scorcher of enemies.”

names.short_meaning: "The One Who, while controlling all beings, veils Himself behind this māyā."
names.commentary:
"The One Who, while controlling all beings, veils Himself behind this māyā." The Consciousness constantly functions within us, but due to the vāsanās, our attention is constantly distracted to the perception of objects outside and not to the Effulgent Being which is the core in us. At the same time Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Self, is the very Life which has made possible the entire manifestation of the world. Still, by His own playful inscrutability we recognize Him not. Interpreted in another sense, the term can also mean, "He Who is above all.' The nobler, the mightier power which controls and regulates any organised set of activities, when it is conceived by human intellect, it is always expressed as something higher or above. Therefore, the significance of this term must be clear to the students.

The individual Avidvaa in us.
names.simple_meaning: "The One Who, while controlling all beings, veils Himself behind this māyā."

names.short_meaning: “He Who is the Nourisher of all living creatures”—supplying each with its appropriate food
names.commentary: “He Who is the Nourisher of all living creatures”—supplying each with its appropriate food. The term also suggests: “one who transcends even Aakaasa, the subtlest of the manifested elements." Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Source out of which all creatures have emerged, He alone must also be the Great Cause from which even the subtlest element, Aakaasa, (space) has sprung forth. The cause is subtler than the effect, therefore, the essential principle, Nārāyaṇa, transcends even the concept of space.
names.simple_meaning: “He Who is the Nourisher of all living creatures”—supplying each with its appropriate food

names.short_meaning: In the Upaniṣad, (Kaṭhopaniṣad) and in the Bhagavad Gītā (Chapter XV), Lord Nārāyaṇa is indicated as the great "Tree of Life," the Asvattha
names.commentary:
In the Upaniṣad, (Kaṭhopaniṣad) and in the Bhagavad Gītā (Chapter XV), Lord Nārāyaṇa is indicated as the great "Tree of Life," the Asvattha. Ficus Religiosa is a perennial tree, seemingly relatively immortal, as compared with the quickly-perishing mankind that comes in waves, generation after generation, to play under its shade, to make love at its base, to grow old in its breeze. Even when they are dead, their bodies are carried in moonlit procession to the burial ground, where under the tree's dancing leaves, a play of light and shade splashes a wizardly pattern upon each lifeless face. The children of each departed one, in their turn, repeat the unending cycle of life under the shade of the same old tree whose nodding grimace mocks the procession of fleeting joys and sorrows. This tree has been chosen to represent the finite play of the Infinite and the Tree itself has been named: A-svattham meaning: "That which will not remain the same tomorrow."

श्वः = tomorrow; श्वत्थ = remaining tomorrow also; which will not remain the same tomorrow—finite.

Refer Gītā Chapter X-26—"अञ्चत्थः सर्ववक्षाणां…"
names.simple_meaning: The tree of life

names.short_meaning: The slayer of Cāṇūra, the great wrestler
names.commentary: "The slayer of Cāṇūra, the great wrestler. Andhra means "wrestler."
names.simple_meaning: The slayer of Cāṇūra, the great wrestler

names.short_meaning: “He Who in His Effulgence has thousands of rays."
names.commentary:
“He Who in His Effulgence has thousands of rays." The Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Pure Consciousness which illumines all experiences, is considered in our scriptures as the 'Light of all Lights,' and, in the Gītā's famous description of this mighty Effulgence of Reality we read: "If the Splendour of a thousand suns were to rise up together and at one and the same time blaze forth in the sky, that would be like the Splendour of the Mighty Being."

Gītā XI-12.
names.simple_meaning: “He Who in His Effulgence has thousands of rays."

names.short_meaning: “He Who expresses Himself as the ‘seven tongues’ (flame).”
names.commentary:
“He Who expresses Himself as the ‘seven tongues’ (flame).” ‘jihvā’ means tongue; here it is used as the ‘tongues-of-flame.’ These seven flames of different properties are enumerated in the Muṇḍakopaniṣad. It sets forth the idea that the Light of Consciousness beams out through seven points in the face of a living entity-two eyes, two ears, two nostrils and the mouth. As intelligent beings, powers of perception, metaphorically flame out through each one of them, illumining the world for us.

The one in our heart, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, Who totally manifests as the seven distinct tongues-of-flame is classified here by the scientific-poets, the ṛṣis, in the language of lyrical service as Sapta-jihvaah.
names.simple_meaning: “He Who expresses Himself as the ‘seven tongues’ (flame).”

names.short_meaning: “The Seven Effulgent flames.”
names.commentary: “The Seven Effulgent flames.” The earlier term invoked Him as the “Seven tongues-of-flame." Here the emphasis seems to be for the Effulgence in those flames.
names.simple_meaning: “The Seven Effulgent flames.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who has the vehicle of seven horses.”
names.commentary: “One Who has the vehicle of seven horses.” Lord Sun is described by the poet-seers of the Vedas as riding in a chariot drawn by seven horses, representing the seven days of the week.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who has the vehicle of seven horses.”

names.short_meaning: "One Who is formless."
names.commentary: "One Who is formless." 'Form' implies a thing that is limited by other factors. The All — Pervading cannot have a form—just as space has no particular form. All things having a form are perishable. Nārāyaṇa Who is Infinite and Eternal is thus ever Formless.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is formless."

names.short_meaning: One who is sinless or sorrowless
names.commentary:
The Sanskrit term Aghah (अघ:) means sin or sorrow. Therefore the term means one who is sinless or sorrowless. Lord Paramesvara, the Self, is Immaculate—untouched and uncontaminated by the vāsanās.

He is Eternal Bliss—beyond all traces of sorrow.
names.simple_meaning: One who is sinless or sorrowless

names.short_meaning: “One Who cannot be comprehended by man’s mind and intellect.”
names.commentary:
“One Who cannot be comprehended by man’s mind and intellect.” Not only the Lord is Formless, and consequently Imperceptible, but He is also unavailable as an object for our emotional experience, or for our intellectual appreciation. He is the Pure Consciousness in Whose Light all our perceptions, feelings and thoughts are illuminated. In Gītā, this "Nourisher of All" is compared with the changeless white screen upon which all the perishing scenes of life are focused.

‘‘सर्वस्य धातारमचिन्त्यरूपम्।’’ (Sarvasya dhaataaramachintyaroopam.) —Gītā VIII-9.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who cannot be comprehended by man’s mind and intellect.”

names.short_meaning: Lord is the “Giver of fear.”
names.commentary:
Lord is the “Giver of fear.” He is a terror to the evil-minded. In all His Incarnations, He gives fear to the evil-hearted, that they may ultimately be swayed to the path of dharma.

And thus gave अभयं to the virtuous. As He destroys the fear of the devotees, He is also called भयकृत = भयं कृन्तति इति ।
names.simple_meaning: Lord is the “Giver of fear.”

names.short_meaning: "Destroyer of all fear," is the Supreme Lord
names.commentary:
"Destroyer of all fear," is the Supreme Lord. The Upaniṣads repeatedly declare the State of Self — Knowledge to be the only state of absolute fearlessness. From a sense of otherness or plurality alone can fear spring forth. In the One Reality, where there is no other, how can there be fear? Śrī Nārāyaṇa alone is the only harbour from all fears.

“न बिभेति कृतश्चनेति।” (Na bibheti kutaschaneti.) -Taittirīya Up. II Valli-9.

“दितीयादै भयं भवति।” (Dviteeyaat vai bhayam bhavati.) —Bṛhadāraṇyaka Up. 1-42.
names.simple_meaning: "Destroyer of all fear," is the Supreme Lord

names.short_meaning: "The Subtlest; the All-pervading."
names.commentary:
"The Subtlest; the All-pervading." Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the subtle flame-of-life in our bosom, the Essence from which all life's activities spring forth. He is called as aṇuḥ because He is in the centre of even the Subtlest. Bhagavān Himself says: "I am seated in the heart of all—as the core or Essence in all."

“सर्वस्य चाहं हृदि सन्निविष्ट:।” (Sarvasya chaaham hridi sannivishtah.) —Gītā XV-15.
names.simple_meaning: "The Subtlest; the All-pervading."

names.short_meaning: At the same time He is Greator than the Greatest in dimension, He being the All-pervading
names.commentary:
At the same time He is Greater than the Greatest in dimension, He being the All-pervading. These two may seem paradoxical but the apparent contradiction dissolves into an illumining experience for the contemplative mind. The Upaniṣad daringly combines these two terms to give the students a vague comprehension of the All-pervading Infinitude of the Self.

“अणोरणीयान् महतो महीयान् आत्मास्य जन्तोर्निहितं गुहायाम् ।” (Anoraneeyaan mahato maheeyaan aatmaasya jantornihitam guhaayaam.) -Kaṭhopaniṣad I-ii-20.
names.simple_meaning: At the same time He is Greator than the Greatest in dimension, He being the All-pervading

names.short_meaning: "One Who is lean; subtle; delicate."
names.commentary: "One Who is lean; subtle; delicate." Again, this description will be opposed by the next following one, for herein is a deliberate use of contradictions. The ṛṣis made an art of effectively employing terms of contradiction in order to bring the incomprehensible within the cognition of the students of contemplation.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is lean; subtle; delicate."

names.short_meaning: “One Who is the fattest; the grossest; roughest.”
names.commentary: “One Who is the fattest; the grossest; roughest.” These two terms are indicating opposites. Here it is to be understood that the Lord, in His state as Pure Consciousness, is the subtlest, and He is the grossest in the form of the Universe (virāṭ).
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is the fattest; the grossest; roughest.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who supports”—maintains and expresses through the three guṇas
names.commentary: “One Who supports”—maintains and expresses through the three guṇas. Through Rajas He creates; through Sattva He preserves and through Tamas He annihilates. He, as Consciousness, expresses Himself through these three textures of vāsanās.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who supports”—maintains and expresses through the three guṇas

names.short_meaning: "Without-any-properties."
names.commentary:
"Without-any-properties." That which has property is matter—perishable, changeable, finite. The Imperishable, the Changeless, the Infinite is property-less; it is the Consciousness that illumines all properties (guṇas).

With the matter equipments, in His Incarnations He manifests as having 'form' (guṇa-bhrit), and in His Absolute Nature He is 'form-less'—the Non-dual Self.
names.simple_meaning: "Without-any-properties."

names.short_meaning: "The Great; the Glorious; the Mighty."
names.commentary: "The Great; the Glorious; the Mighty." "One Who is not conditioned by the five Elementsnor by Time and Space. Quite on the other hand, it is He Who is the very Existence in everything.
names.simple_meaning: "The Great; the Glorious; the Mighty."

names.short_meaning: None supports Him, but He supports all
names.commentary: None supports Him, but He supports all. Just as the cotton in cloth, gold in ornaments, mud in pots, He is the supporter of the entire universe. To the devotee who feels the Lord is far away from him, to contemplate upon Śrī Nārāyaṇa as his very own support will open his heart to the certainty and plenitude of faith.
names.simple_meaning: None supports Him, but He supports all

names.short_meaning: "Self-supported."
names.commentary:
"Self-supported." When from the previous term we hear that the Self is the ultimate support of the Universe, the question automatically rises in a rational intellect: 'what supports the Self?' The Lord is "supported" by nothing else other than His own Glory. In the Upaniṣad, in answer to a question where the Mighty One abides, the teacher declares, "He abides in His own Glory."

‘स भगवः कस्मिन प्रतिष्ठित इति स्वे महिम्नि।’’ (Sa Bhagavah kasmin pratishthita iti sve mahimni.) -Chāndogya Upaniṣad 7-24-1.
names.simple_meaning: "Self-supported."

names.short_meaning: “One Who has an Effulgent Face.”
names.commentary: “One Who has an Effulgent Face.” Because He gives to the Vedas their beauty and charm, He is conceived as brilliantly beautiful, enchantingly fascinating, hauntingly charming.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who has an Effulgent Face.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who has the most ancient ancestry.”
names.commentary:
“One Who has the most ancient ancestry.” The Infinite, the Cause for the Universe and Time itself, is indicated as the ‘Most Ancient’ (पुराणपुरुषः). The term can also mean the accommodation reserved during a yāga meeting where the invitees and guests may rest.

Generally built on the eastern courtyard of the house, this accommodation is called 'prāgvaṃśaḥ.' Since everything connected with a yajña or yāga is considered as sacred, the 'prāgvaṃśaḥ' has been used here as a name to indicate Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who has the most ancient ancestry.”

names.short_meaning: “He Who multiplies His family of descendents."
names.commentary: “He Who multiplies His family of descendents." The Lord's family is the whole Universe of things and beings. Or it can also imply just the opposite as the root Vardh ( वर्ष ) means 'the annihilator.' Nārāyaṇa is the sacred factor in us, to Whose Feet we turn in all love and undivided attention, in Whom the world of perceptions, emotions and thoughts merge as a dream merges into the mind of the waker.
names.simple_meaning: “He Who multiplies His family of descendents."

names.short_meaning: “One Who carries the load of the Universe.”
names.commentary: “One Who carries the load of the Universe.” This carrying is not as a man would carry a load—something other than himself. The Self Itself has become the world so here it means only that Nārāyaṇa is the very material Cause of the Universe.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who carries the load of the Universe.”

names.short_meaning: "One Who is glorified in the Vedas and other spiritual text books."
names.commentary:
"One Who is glorified in the Vedas and other spiritual text books." Nārāyaṇa-essence is the theme of all scriptures in the world.

‘‘वेदैश्च सर्वेरहमेव वेद्य:।” (Vedaischa sarvairahameva vedyah.) "In all scriptures I am the one theme to be known."

—Gītā XV-15.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is glorified in the Vedas and other spiritual text books."

names.short_meaning: “One Who can be realised through Yoga:" "One Who is the greatest yogī."
names.commentary:
“One Who can be realised through Yoga:" "One Who is the greatest yogī." The term Yoga is defined in the śāstra as 'stopping all thought-flow.' One who has no thought agitations—who has totally conquered the mind (māyā) and lives in His own Effulgent Self-nature is the greatest yogī.

‘'योगः चित्तवत्तिनिरोधः।'' (Yogah Chittavrittinirodhah.) -Yoga śāstra.
names.simple_meaning: The supreme yogī, realized through yoga

names.short_meaning: "The King of yogīs."
names.commentary:
"The King of yogīs." "One who realises the Self, becomes the Self," is an Upanishadic declaration. Therefore, Self alone is the perfect yogī and Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Self, is the King of all yogīs. The sense of agency-in-action and the sense of enjoyership-inexperience is the ego (jīva-bhaavanaa). To end this ego-personality is to rise to the awareness of the Universal Consciousness, the Self. Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Absolute Reality, alone can be free—entirely and fully—from any involvement while being ever in the midst of Samsar and its seething activities.

Hence He is glorified as the best among yogīs.

"स यो ह वै तत्परमं ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवति।" (Sa yo ha vai tatparamam brahma veda Brahmaiva bhavati.) -Muṇḍakopaniṣad III-ii-9.
names.simple_meaning: "The King of yogīs."

names.short_meaning: "One Who fulfils all desires of all true devotees."
names.commentary: "One Who fulfils all desires of all true devotees." Such devotees have no other desire but to reach, meet and merge in Him. In this way the term would also indicate that He destroys the chances of fulfilment of all unholy, sensuous and lusty desires in the faithless.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who fulfils all desires of all true devotees."

names.short_meaning: Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the harbour, the sequestered haven for all who are tossed about in the storms of life without and within
names.commentary: Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the harbour, the sequestered haven for all who are tossed about in the storms of life without and within. For each one, the source of all strains is attributable entirely to his functioning as a body-mind-intellect equipment. To remain as the Self-the essential real nature of man—is to experience the end of all stresses and strains. This state of Peace and Joy, of Quiet and Bliss is Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Lord of the heart.
names.simple_meaning: Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the harbour, the sequestered haven for all who are tossed about in the storms of life without and within

names.short_meaning: "One Who persecutes the worldly people"—who, driven by their hungers and passions, seek sense-gratifications
names.commentary:
"One Who persecutes the worldly people"—who, driven by their hungers and passions, seek sense-gratifications. By the very nature of the ephemeral sense-objects and the ever-changing instruments of experience in us, the life of gratifications can only yield exhausting fatigue and weary disappointments. This is the 'Law' and Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the 'Law — Giver.' The Law and the Law — Giver are but one in theology.

The sense organs, mind and intellect.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who persecutes the worldly people"—who, driven by their hungers and passions, seek sense-gratifications

names.short_meaning: “One Who destroys everything during the final deluge"—He Who prunes our agitations and shrinks our desire-prompted world-projections
names.commentary: “One Who destroys everything during the final deluge"—He Who prunes our agitations and shrinks our desire-prompted world-projections.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who destroys everything during the final deluge"—He Who prunes our agitations and shrinks our desire-prompted world-projections

names.short_meaning: "The Golden Leaf."
names.commentary:
"The Golden Leaf." In Bhagavad Gītā the world is pictured as the Asvattha tree and its leaves are declared to be the Vedas. The theme of the Vedas is none other than the Self, making the term extremely enchanting with its springs of suggestions.

"छन्दांसि यस्य पर्णानि यस्तं वेद स वेदवित्।" (Chhandaamsi yasya parnaani yastam veda sa vedavit.) -Gītā XV-1.
names.simple_meaning: "The Golden Leaf."

names.short_meaning: “The mover of the winds.”
names.commentary:
“The mover of the winds.” From fear of Him Fire burns, Sun and Moon function, earth rotates, the Wind moves… declares the Upaniṣad.

"भीषास्मादात: पवते।" (Bheeshaasmaat vaatah pavate.) -Taittirīya Upaniṣad II-viii — I.
names.simple_meaning: “The mover of the winds.”

names.short_meaning: "The wielder of the Bow."
names.commentary:
"The wielder of the Bow." In His Incarnation as Śrī Rama, He drew the great Bow as no one else ever could. Also in the Upaniṣad there is the famous metaphor of the Bow with which the arrow of the individuality is to be shot to strike and sink into the goal. The ṛṣi of the Muṇḍakopaniṣad explains that the 'Bow' is the OM (praṇava mantra). (The significance is clear.)

‘‘धनुर्गृहीत्वौपनिषदं महास्त्रं…’’ ‘‘प्रणवो धन:…’’ (Dhanurgriheetvaupanishadam mahaastram…) (Pranavo dhanuh…) "Having taken the bow furnished by the Upaniṣads, the great weapon—and fixed in it the arrow rendered pointed by constant meditation and having drawn it with the mind fixed on the Brahman, hit… at the mark — the Immortal Brahman."

-Muṇḍakopaniṣad II-ii-3 "The praṇava is the bow, the Atman is the arrow and the Brahman is said to be its mark. It should be hit by one who is self-collected and that which hits becomes like the arrow, one with the mark, i.e. Brahman.' -Muṇḍakopaniṣad II-ii-4.
names.simple_meaning: "The wielder of the Bow."

names.short_meaning: "One Who declared the Science of Archery."
names.commentary: "One Who declared the Science of Archery." The One Who propounded the unfailing technique of OM-meditation for realisation of the Self.
names.simple_meaning: The revealer of the science of archery

names.short_meaning: "One Who punishes the wicked."
names.commentary:
"One Who punishes the wicked." In Gītā, Bhagavān declares Himself to be the policeman of the Universe. The term can also mean the 'Sceptre'—the insignia of king-ship. Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the King of kings in the entire, limitless universe, holds the Sceptre of total royalty.

"दण्डो दमयतामस्मि।" (Dando Damavataamasmi) "Among punishers I am the Sceptre." -Gītā X-38
names.simple_meaning: "One Who punishes the wicked."

names.short_meaning: "The Controller."
names.commentary: "The Controller." One Who punishes the wicked, destroys the sinners and thus regulates and cultivates life in the universe, making it a garden for the blossoms of spiritual beauties.
names.simple_meaning: "The Controller."

names.short_meaning: That which is ultimately gained by the worldly punishments—the final experience of Beatitude in the Self
names.commentary: That which is ultimately gained by the worldly punishments—the final experience of Beatitude in the Self.
names.simple_meaning: That which is ultimately gained by the worldly punishments—the final experience of Beatitude in the Self

names.short_meaning: "The Invincible; One Who cannot be defeated."
names.commentary: "The Invincible; One Who cannot be defeated." The Self ultimately asserts within every bosom from wherein the spiritual values finally emerge victorious. The Self alone remains when all else has been destroyed.
names.simple_meaning: "The Invincible; One Who cannot be defeated."

names.short_meaning: "One Who carries the entire Universe."
names.commentary: "One Who carries the entire Universe." The One Who meets heroically all the enemical impulses of unspiritual lusts. He carries the entire Universe as its very material Cause: as mud in pots.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who carries the entire Universe."

names.short_meaning: “One Who has none above Him to control Him."
names.commentary: “One Who has none above Him to control Him." He is the One Who has appointed all other controllers of the phenomenal forces as the Sun, the Moon, Air and Waters.
names.simple_meaning: The supreme controller, controlled by none

names.short_meaning: "One Who is not under the laws of anyone else."
names.commentary: "One Who is not under the laws of anyone else." He is the Law and the only Law — Giver. It is His hand that governs the inscrutable and unrelenting laws of nature.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is not under the laws of anyone else."

names.short_meaning: "One Who knows no death."
names.commentary: "One Who knows no death." He is the Eternal: how can He know death?—the principle of death cannot act in Him. Within Time alone there is change or death. The Pure Consciousness is That which illumines the sense of time and so is beyond Time—beyond death.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who knows no death."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is full of exploits and courage."
names.commentary: "One Who is full of exploits and courage." Supremely adventurous, daring and heroic is Nārāyaṇa—as witnessed in all His actions during all His Incarnations.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is full of exploits and courage."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is full of sāttvika qualities."
names.commentary: "One Who is full of sāttvika qualities." Quietude, tranquillity, peace—these are some of the saattvic qualities. Sattva is the creative-pause of the mind before it launches out into a burst of creative thoughts and action. Full of inspiration and meditative-poise is the Total — Mind, Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is full of sāttvika qualities."

names.short_meaning: "Truth."
names.commentary:
"Truth." That which remains the same in the past, present and future is Truth. Self knows no change. It is ever in Its own Nature in all the three periods of Time.

त्रिकालाबाधितं वस्तु सत्यमिति । (Trikaalaabaadhitam vastu satyamiti.)
names.simple_meaning: "Truth."

names.short_meaning: “One Who is the very abode of Truth and Righteousness.”
names.commentary:
“One Who is the very abode of Truth and Righteousness.” Satyam (Truth) is 'truthfulness in thought, speech and action. dharma (Righteousness) is the injunctions regarding 'what is and what is not the duty to be fulfilled.

कर्तव्याकर्तव्यविधिरेव धर्म: । (Kartavyaakartavyavidhireva dharmah.)
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is the very abode of Truth and Righteousness.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who is faced by all seekers marching to the Infinite."
names.commentary: “One Who is faced by all seekers marching to the Infinite." Or it can mean, "One Who merges the entire world of plurality into Himself."
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is faced by all seekers marching to the Infinite."

names.short_meaning: "One Who deserves all our love."
names.commentary: "One Who deserves all our love." Priya also expands its meaning into: "things we are supremely fond of," therefore, the term, as it stands, may be read: "One Who deserves to be worshipped by His devotees with all that they are supremely fond of." As an expression of our devotion we do offer to the Lord that which we love the most in life.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who deserves all our love."

names.short_meaning: Nārāyaṇa is the One Who deserves to be worshipped by all devotees
names.commentary: Nārāyaṇa is the One Who deserves to be worshipped by all devotees. He, being our very own Self, is the treasure-source of all our devotion. Thus He does draw from us all our surrender, love and reverence.
names.simple_meaning: Nārāyaṇa is the One Who deserves to be worshipped by all devotees

names.short_meaning: “One Who is ever-obliging in fulfilling our wishes”—One Who is anxiously eager for the well-being of all devotees
names.commentary: “One Who is ever-obliging in fulfilling our wishes”—One Who is anxiously eager for the well-being of all devotees. But the term can also yield just the opposite meaning—"One Who destroys the wishes or disturbs the well-being of the wicked and the faithless."
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is ever-obliging in fulfilling our wishes”—One Who is anxiously eager for the well-being of all devotees

names.short_meaning: The sense of drunken joy that arises in one's bosom when one loves deeply and truly is called prīti
names.commentary: The sense of drunken joy that arises in one's bosom when one loves deeply and truly is called prīti. "One Who increases prīti in the devotee's heart" is Śrī Nārāyaṇa. The more He is contemplated upon, the more His glories are appreciated, thereby the more our prīti in Him increases.
names.simple_meaning: The one who increases love and joy

names.short_meaning: The term vihāyasa means pertaining to, depending on, the space—aerial
names.commentary: The term vihāyasa means pertaining to, depending on, the space—aerial. Gatih means one who moves. Therefore, in its totality, this name describes: "One Who travels in space—having the nature of the Sun, Soorya — Nārāyaṇa."
names.simple_meaning: The one whose path is the sky

names.short_meaning: "Effulgent with His own inherent Light."
names.commentary:
"Effulgent with His own inherent Light." The Lord as Consciousness is the 'Light of all lights.' "By Its Light all are brilliant: by Its Light all are illumined." Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the Self-effulgent Atman, the Self.

"ज्योतिषामि तज्ज्योतिः।" (Jyotishaamapi taj-jyotih.) --- Gītā XIII-18.

"तमेव भान्तमनुभाति सर्वं तस्य भासा सर्वमिदं विभाति।" (Tameva bhaantamanubhaati sarvam tasya bhaasaa sarvamidam vibhaati.) -Muṇḍakopaniṣad II-ii-10.
names.simple_meaning: "Effulgent with His own inherent Light."

names.short_meaning: The suffix ‘Su’ indicates Auspiciousness (sobhana): the term ‘Ruchi’ is Glory or Desire
names.commentary:
The suffix ‘Su’ indicates Auspiciousness (sobhana): the term ‘Ruchi’ is Glory or Desire. The Glory of Lord Nārāyaṇa is this world: it is His 'desire' (sankalpa) that manifests as the universe.

The Supreme Brahman, the Infinite Reality, functioning through the 'Total-vāsanās,' meaning the 'Total — Causal — Body' (māyā), is Lord, the Īśvara. So we are given the irrefutable scientific truth in the Sruti-declaration that the universe is the 'will' or 'desire' of Lord Nārāyaṇa.

‘‘सम्बिटकारणशरीराभिमानी परमात्मा ईश्वरः।’’ (Samashtikaaranasareeraabhimaanee paramātmā Īśvaraḥ.)
names.simple_meaning: The one of beautiful radiance and auspicious will

names.short_meaning: “One Who receives and enjoys all that is offered into the sacred fire during the Vedic Rituals—yajñas and yāgas.”
names.commentary: “One Who receives and enjoys all that is offered into the sacred fire during the Vedic Rituals—yajñas and yāgas.” The faithful may offer oblations invoking his own special Deity, but it is the One Lord, Nārāyaṇa Who receives them all, manifesting as the particular Deity invoked.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who receives and enjoys all that is offered into the sacred fire during the Vedic Rituals—yajñas and yāgas.”

names.short_meaning: "All-pervading."
names.commentary: "All-pervading." Lord Nārāyaṇa, the Self, is unconditioned by time or space for He is the Eternal, the Omnipresent. In His Absolute Nature, He is All-pervading as He is unlimited by any conditionings.
names.simple_meaning: "All-pervading."

names.short_meaning: “One Who absorbs the vapours (Rasa) from everything.”
names.commentary: “One Who absorbs the vapours (Rasa) from everything.” As the Soorya — Nārāyaṇa, Śrī Hari dries up everything in the universe.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who absorbs the vapours (Rasa) from everything.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who shines in different forms.”
names.commentary: “One Who shines in different forms.” Whatever form the devotee chooses for contemplation upon Him, the Lord manifests in that very Form for the sake and joy of the devotee. Additionally it may be interpreted as "One Who Himself manifests as the Sun and the Moon and all other resplendent spheres in the Consmos."
names.simple_meaning: “One Who shines in different forms.”

names.short_meaning: The term etymologically means the One Source from which all things have been born or out of which they have been delivered
names.commentary: The term etymologically means the One Source from which all things have been born or out of which they have been delivered. The Lord as the First Cause is the Womb of the Universe. On the surface of the world it is the Sun that nurtures and nourishes all living creatures. It must be noted that many of the Lord's names indicate or are associated with the Sun—as He is in us like the Sun in the Solar System: the Centre around which the entire system revolves and by Whose benign rays, as the 'Orb-of-all Energies', He is thrilling to life the infinitude of creatures.
names.simple_meaning: The sun, source of all brilliance

names.short_meaning: "The One Who brings forth, from Himself, the Universe of things and beings."
names.commentary:
"The One Who brings forth, from Himself, the Universe of things and beings." The Supreme Self functioning through the Sun is called savitā.

"प्रजानां तु प्रसवनात सवितेति निगद्यते।" (Prajaanaam tu prasavanaat saviteti nigadyate.)
names.simple_meaning: "The One Who brings forth, from Himself, the Universe of things and beings."

names.short_meaning: "One Whose Eyes are the Sun."
names.commentary:
"One Whose Eyes are the Sun." In the Upaniṣad and the Gītā, the virāṭ Form of the Lord (the Cosmic — Form) is described as having for His eyes the Sun and the Moon.

“अग्निमूँढी चक्षषी चन्द्रसूर्यो।” (Agnirmoorddhaa chakshushee chandrasooryau.) -Muṇḍakopaniṣad II-i-4
names.simple_meaning: "One Whose Eyes are the Sun."

names.short_meaning: "Endless."
names.commentary: "Endless." One Who is not conditioned by time and place is Self. In His All-pervading nature He is immortal, and thus Immutable.
names.simple_meaning: "Endless."

names.short_meaning: “One Who accepts the things devotedly poured as oblation into the sacred Fire.”
names.commentary:
“One Who accepts the things devotedly poured as oblation into the sacred Fire.” These oblations which may be in the name of any devataa, are all received by Nārāyaṇa in the form of that devataa because He is the One Infinite Self Who plays in and through all forms.

worldly and heavenly.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who accepts the things devotedly poured as oblation into the sacred Fire.”

names.short_meaning: The One Who enjoys the world of objects-emotions-thoughts
names.commentary:
The One Who enjoys the world of objects-emotions-thoughts, through the equipments of body-mind-intellect is none other than the Self expressing through these 'instruments-of-experiences' as the individuality-constituted of the perceiver-feeler-thinker-ego.

The term bhoktā also means "One Who Protects" (the Universe)—as He is the very material Cause for the entire world of names and forms.

“भज पालनाभ्यवहारयोः।” (Bhuj paalanaabhyavahaarayoh.) The root has both the meanings.
names.simple_meaning: The One Who enjoys the world of objects-emotions-thoughts

names.short_meaning: One Who gives the experience of Eternal Bliss to the devotees at their final spiritual destination-mokṣa
names.commentary: "One Who gives the experience of Eternal Bliss to the devotees at their final spiritual destination-mokṣa. As the term stands in the verse, some would read it-'A-sukha-da' in which case the nominative would mean: "One Who removes all the discomforts and pains of the devotees."
names.simple_meaning: One Who gives the experience of Eternal Bliss to the devotees at their final spiritual destination-mokṣa

names.short_meaning: Na—'not'; Eka—'once'; Ja -born.'
names.commentary: Na—'not'; Eka—'once'; Ja -born.' One Who is born not only once, but many times, in many Forms, to serve the devotees in His different Incarnations. In fact, all births are all His manifestations alone as He is the Spark-of — Existence in the Universe of inert matter. Through all equipments He alone is the One Consciousness that dances Its Infinite Glories.
names.simple_meaning: Na—'not'; Eka—'once'; Ja -born.'

names.short_meaning: "The One Who was First- Born."
names.commentary: "The One Who was First- Born." Naturally, everything came from Him alone; this Primordial First Cause is the concept of God. That from which everything comes, in which everything exists and into which all things can again finally merge--'That' is conceived as God.
names.simple_meaning: "The One Who was First- Born."

names.short_meaning: "One Who feels no disappointments"—Who has no chance to feel disappointment as He is ever the totally fulfilled
names.commentary:
"One Who feels no disappointments"—Who has no chance to feel disappointment as He is ever the totally fulfilled. The agonising disgust with things that comes to a bosom when a burning desire is unfulfilled is called Nirveda. One who has no Nirveda is called anirviṇṇaḥ. He, being "Ever-full" and "Perfect," has no desires yet unfulfilled or something yet to be fulfilled in the future. Bhagavān declares this in Gītā: "There is neither anything that I have not gained nor anything I have yet to gain."

‘‘नानवाप्तमवाप्तव्यम…।’’ (Naanavaaptamavaaptavyam…) -Gītā III-22.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who feels no disappointments"—Who has no chance to feel disappointment as He is ever the totally fulfilled

names.short_meaning: "One Who ever forgives the trespasses of all His devotees"—One Who is infinitely merciful and kind
names.commentary: "One Who ever forgives the trespasses of all His devotees"—One Who is infinitely merciful and kind.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who ever forgives the trespasses of all His devotees"—One Who is infinitely merciful and kind

names.short_meaning: The one sole substratum for the entire Universe of things and beings
names.commentary: The one sole substratum for the entire Universe of things and beings."
names.simple_meaning: The one sole substratum for the entire Universe of things and beings

names.short_meaning: "Wonder is He."
names.commentary:
"Wonder is He." The Gītā roars of this 'wonder,' and the Upaniṣads assert that He and the teacher who teaches of Him, and even the student who grasps Him are all 'wonders.' "Wonder" is an experience that comes to one whose mind and intellect are stunned by the overwhelming experience of any given moment. The experience has made the mind stagger, the intellect to halt—so that no feelings or thoughts emanate from them. That moment of realisation is a moment of total transcendence of the "inner-equipments,' so this term "Wonder" is often used in our scriptures to point out the condition within at the time of our Experience Infinite.

"आश्चर्यवत्पश्यति कश्चिदेनमाश्चर्यवद्वदति तथैव चान्य: ।

आश्चर्यवच्चैनमन्यः शृणोति श्रत्वाप्येनं वेद न चैव कश्चित ।" (Aascharyavatpasyati kaschidenamaascharyavadvadati tathaiva chaanvah: Aascharyavachchainamanyah srinoti srutvaapyenam veda na chaiva kaschit.) -Gītā II-29.

''श्रवणायापि वहभियों न लभ्यः श्रुष्वन्तोऽपि बहुवो यं न विद्युः। आश्चर्यो वक्ता कुशलोऽस्य लब्धाऽऽश्चर्यो ज्ञाता कुशलानशिष्ट: ॥" (Sravanaayaapi bahubhiryo na labhyah srinvantoapi bahavo yam na vidyuh; Aascharyo vaktaa kusalo-asya labdhaa-aascharyo inaataa kusalaanusishtah.) Kaṭhopaniṣad I-ii-7.
names.simple_meaning: "Wonder is He."

names.short_meaning: "The Beginningless and the Endless factor is He."
names.commentary: "The Beginningless and the Endless factor is He." Time cannot condition Him. He, the Consciousness, illumines the very concept of Time and Space. He was, is and shall ever be — He being Changeless, Immutable.
names.simple_meaning: "The Beginningless and the Endless factor is He."

names.short_meaning: "The most Ancient."
names.commentary: "The most Ancient." It is from Him that the very intellect springs forth and thereafter one of the concepts of the intellect is Time. Therefore, He is the most 'Ancient,' inasmuch as He was already there to be aware of even the first experience of the beginning of Time.
names.simple_meaning: "The most Ancient."

names.short_meaning: The Lord Himself, manifested as the great ṛṣi Kapila, propounded the Sāṅkhya philosophy
names.commentary:
The Lord Himself, manifested as the great ṛṣi Kapila, propounded the Sāṅkhya philosophy. In the Gītā, Bhagavān Śrī Kṛṣṇa declaring His own Glory, describes Himself: "I am Kapila among the great ones."

‘‘सिद्धानां कपिलो मुनिः।’’ (Siddhaanaam Kapilo munih.) -Gītā X-26.
names.simple_meaning: The Lord Himself, manifested as the great ṛṣi Kapila, propounded the Sāṅkhya philosophy

names.short_meaning: One Who drinks water
names.commentary:
"One Who drinks water" -- by one's rays. The Sun it is that dries up everything, evaporating the water-content contained on the surface of the earth.

कं जलं पिबतीति कपि:। (Kam jalam pibati iti kapiḥ.) "Kam" means water.
names.simple_meaning: One Who drinks water

names.short_meaning: "The One in Whom the entire Universe merges"—during the great deluge when the Total-mind—the Creator—rests
names.commentary:
"The One in Whom the entire Universe merges"—during the great deluge when the Total-mind—the Creator—rests. The Supreme Atman functioning through the Total-mind is the Creator, Brahmājī—each mind being ruled by its own vāsanās. The Total-vāsanās in the Universe (Causal — Body) is māyā and the Supreme Self expressing through māyā (the Total — Causal — Body) is Īśvara.

Therefore, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, as Īśvara, is the One into Whom the total world of experiences merges when the Total-mind rests during the 'pause' between two busy cycles of Creation and involvement in the projected world of thoughts-feelings-objects.

In the north this term is read as avyayaḥ (अव्यय:) where the meaning is clear: "Immutable": and needs no explanation.
names.simple_meaning: "The One in Whom the entire Universe merges"—during the great deluge when the Total-mind—the Creator—rests

names.short_meaning: "One Who gives Svasti to all His sincere devotees."
names.commentary: "One Who gives Svasti to all His sincere devotees." A true devotee is one who has discovered his fulfilment in seeking and gaining the Infinite Bliss that is Śrī Hari. Naturally, he comes to turn away from the realms of inauspiciousness. To the extent he is able to move into the Hari — Consciousness, he is to that degree in the Bliss — Experience. Therefore, the Lord is termed as the 'Giver-of — Auspiciousness.'
names.simple_meaning: "One Who gives Svasti to all His sincere devotees."

names.short_meaning: As in many earlier terms which were preceded by the suffix 'kṛt,' here also, it expands into two meanings: "One Who brings Auspiciousness" or "One who robs all Auspiciousness."
names.commentary: As in many earlier terms which were preceded by the suffix 'kṛt,' here also, it expands into two meanings: "One Who brings Auspiciousness" or "One who robs all Auspiciousness." To the seeker who is moving towards the Nārāyaṇa — Consciousness, his experience is of added joy and peace in life, but the one who seeks only sense-gratification and so moves away from the Reality, to him the experience is more and more sorrow, agitations, tears and tragedies—total inauspiciousness. The indeclinable (Avvava) Sanskrit word 'Svasti' means Auspiciousness.
names.simple_meaning: The maker and remover of auspicious conditions

names.short_meaning: "One Who is the Source of all Auspiciousness"—as He is Himself the Auspicious
names.commentary:
"One Who is the Source of all Auspiciousness"—as He is Himself the Auspicious. In essence His Nature is sat-cit-ānanda so there can be no cause for inauspiciousness therein. The individual functions within the powers of His avidvaa and so is under the infatuation of māyā, while the Lord rules over māyā and plays out through māyā.

‘‘ईश्वराधीना हि माया… अविद्याधीनः तू जीवः ।’’ (Eesvaraadheenaa hi māyā… Avidyaadheenah tu jīvaḥ.)
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is the Source of all Auspiciousness"—as He is Himself the Auspicious

names.short_meaning: "One Who constantly lives in His Experience a perpetual sense of holy Auspiciousness"-as it is His very nature-divine
names.commentary: "One Who constantly lives in His Experience a perpetual sense of holy Auspiciousness"-as it is His very nature-divine. It can also be interpreted as "One Who showers Grace and makes His devotees constantly experience Auspiciousness in their loving Narayanacentred hearts."
names.simple_meaning: "One Who constantly lives in His Experience a perpetual sense of holy Auspiciousness"-as it is His very nature-divine

names.short_meaning: Lord is ever engaged in smartly distributing Auspiciousness
names.commentary:
Lord is ever engaged in smartly distributing Auspiciousness. The word 'dakṣiṇā' has, apart from the meaning of 'gift,' also a meaning: "One Who is efficient and quick." Therefore, the term indicates that Śrī Nārāyaṇa quickly and efficiently will reach His sincere seekers to give them the experience of Auspiciousness which is the Lord's very nature.

क्षिप्रकाशी।

(Kshiprakaasee.)
names.simple_meaning: Lord is ever engaged in smartly distributing Auspiciousness

names.short_meaning: "One Who has none of the negative terrible urges and emotions."
names.commentary: "One Who has none of the negative terrible urges and emotions." The State of Perfection is a condition where the frailties of the mortal heart can never remain. The Lord is One in Whom the cruelties which rule the man of the world—likes, dislikes, hatredness, jealousy and his other imperfections—can never abide or even be contained.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has none of the negative terrible urges and emotions."

names.short_meaning: “One Who wears the famous ear-ring called the Makara — Kundala."
names.commentary:
“One Who wears the famous ear-ring called the Makara — Kundala." The term kuṇḍalī also signifies the 'Serpent'—hence the Kundalinee-śakti—the 'Serpent — Power'—the coiled mystic-glory lying now inert, uninvoked at the base of the back-bone in the deep pelvic region. Here the 'Serpent' may be taken as the thousand-tongued Ananta on whom Śrī Nārāyaṇa is described as ever reclining in His Yoga-rest.

In all religions, 'Serpent,' it seems, symbolises the 'mind.' In Hinduism it is true. Whether it is in Kṛṣṇa's dance on the Kaalivan — Serpent, or Siva wearing as ornaments the Serpents (Bhooshana), or Śrī Hari resting upon Ananta—the idea is always the conquest of the mind, the poisonous serpent.
names.simple_meaning: The wearer of makara earrings

names.short_meaning: “He Who wears ever His Discus called Su — Darsana (Auspicious Vision).”
names.commentary: “He Who wears ever His Discus called Su — Darsana (Auspicious Vision).” The Lord destroys with the Discus only the foul and the low in us and the individual naturally gains the Experience Divine, the Self.
names.simple_meaning: The bearer of the discus Sudarśana

names.short_meaning: “He Who is more daring than all others.”
names.commentary: “He Who is more daring than all others.” The term is also interpreted: “One Who travels by air,” as ‘Vi’ means Bird. Famous is the allegory that Lord Viṣṇu travels on the back of the white-necked Eagle.
names.simple_meaning: “He Who is more daring than all others.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who commands and administers with His Hand."
names.commentary: “One Who commands and administers with His Hand." His commands in the scriptures advise us firmly what is right to do and what are the destructive forces in each one of us. In case man decides to disobey His Laws, He severely punishes him on all such occasions. Disobedience of Laws is immediately followed by His loving curative punishment. It permits no exceptions; accepts no excuses; admits no circumstantial conditions.
names.source_heading_devanagari_ocr: ऊ जि त शा स नः
names.simple_meaning: “One Who commands and administers with His Hand."

names.short_meaning: "He Who transcends all words"—One Who is Indescribable
names.commentary: "He Who transcends all words"—One Who is Indescribable. The Vedas themselves are but indications 'pointing to Truth' and are not explaining, describing or even defining Truth. The Infinite and the Eternal Truth is beyond even the Vedas, beyond all that can be gained through even the highest faculties of the finite equipments (mind and intellect).
names.simple_meaning: "He Who transcends all words"—One Who is Indescribable

names.short_meaning: “One Who allows Himself to be invoked by the Vedic declarations.”
names.commentary: “One Who allows Himself to be invoked by the Vedic declarations.” If, however, the Upanishadic declarations are properly reflected and sincerely meditated upon, even though the Vedas have failed to define Truth, their contemplative implications can transport us into the realms of the Infinite Experience — Divine.
names.simple_meaning: The one who permits invocation through sacred sound

names.short_meaning: The term means winter, the cold season
names.commentary: The term means winter, the cold season. In India it is the cool season. Therefore, by suggestion, this name indicates that the Lord is the 'cool arbour' for those who are tortured by the heat of Samsar.
names.simple_meaning: The cool season that relieves burning heat

names.short_meaning: The word Sarvaree means 'night' or 'darkness'; therefore, the term defines the Lord as "One Who creates darkness."
names.commentary:
The word Sarvaree means 'night' or 'darkness'; therefore, the term defines the Lord as "One Who creates darkness." To the men of realisation, our world of sorrows and pains, of strains and stresses, of worries and anxieties is unknown—while to those who live in their ego-sense, to them the Real is unknown. The unknown means 'veiled in darkness.' The subtle meaning is clear now.

"या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुने: ॥ (Yaa nisaa sarvabhootaanaam tasyaam jaagarti samyamee; Yasyaam jaagrati bhootaani saa nisaa pasyato muneh.) "That which is night to all beings, in that the self-controlled man wakes; where all beings are awake, that is the night for the Sage (Muni) who sees."

--Gītā II-69.
names.simple_meaning: The maker of night and darkness

names.short_meaning: "Never-cruel."
names.commentary:
"Never-cruel." Cruelty comes from anger, and anger rises from 'desire'—craving or lust. Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Fulfilled and the All — Full, cannot have 'desire' from which could come anger—thus, naturally, never any cruelty. Generally this term is interpreted as "One Who is of the form of the Yādava, Śrī Akroora." Akroora was a great devotee of the Lord upon whom were bestowed many divine powers. "Wherever, there is any special glory in anyone. know that to be a manifestation of a part of my Splendour." sings Lord in Bhagavad Gītā. Thus the term is interpreted as the Lord Whose one ray of glory was the Kamsa-employee.

the Yādava — Akroora.

"यद्यद्विभृतिमत्सत्त्वं श्रीमद्जितमेव वा । तत्तदेवावगच्छ त्वं मम तेजोऽशसंभवम ।।" (Yadyadvibhootimatsattvam sreemadoorjitameva vaa; Tattadevaavagaccha tvam mama tejomsasambhavam.) --- Gītā X-41
names.simple_meaning: "Never-cruel."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is supremely soft."
names.commentary: "One Who is supremely soft." In His Infinite Kindness and Mercy, His Heart-divine is ever flowing out in love and tenderness towards His devotees when they call out for help ardently and lift themselves from their body-consciousness and ego-centric life of sense-pursuits.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is supremely soft."

names.short_meaning: This term stands for the quality of 'promptitude.'
names.commentary: This term stands for the quality of 'promptitude.' In army training, the Sanskrit command Daksha is equal to "attention alertness, vigilance and utter preparedness to act immediately with supreme urgency." All these are implied in that pose of "Attention." The Lord is 'Daksha' in serving the world and in rushing to His sincere devotees. Omnipotent and divinely Efficient in His Infinite Smartness to reach and help all, at all times, everywhere, under every circumstance is echoed in the charming suggestions of this chosen term in the Sahasranāma of Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Self in All
names.simple_meaning: The prompt and capable one

names.short_meaning: “One Who is most liberal.”
names.commentary:
“One Who is most liberal.” The term ‘Dakshina’ is popularly used for the ‘gift’ presented to the priests after a ritual as their fee. This giving must be done in a spirit of large-hearted, liberal charity—so that very large-heartedness of mind (Daakshinya) itself is the Lord, as it is the opposite of selfishness and attachment to the wealth which one possesses. "One Who has Infinite Kindness and Charity towards all good people and One Who is thus ever-ready to liberally give away His endless Benevolence" is Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Dakshina.

दाक्षिण्य भाव: ।

(Daakshinya bhāvaḥ.) The attitude of large-heartedness and the ability to be supremely liberal in giving away whatever one has for others is Daakshinya.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is most liberal.”

names.short_meaning: "One Who has the greatest amount of patience with the sinners and for-giveness for their sins."
names.commentary:
"One Who has the greatest amount of patience with the sinners and for-giveness for their sins." Śrī Nārāyaṇa is more patient than even the Earth which is generally pointed to as an example of highest patience (Kshamaa). He exhibits supreme patience with the evil-minded, with the tyrant, the foul and the fiendish.

Hiraṇyākṣa, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Ravana and others of this type were given many fair opportunities to realise for themselves the folly of their baser attitudes to existing things and their immoral ways of life. It is only when no other method of treatment could cure them that the Lord destroyed them in His infinite kindness.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has the greatest amount of patience with the sinners and for-giveness for their sins."

names.short_meaning: “One Who has the greatest Wisdom."
names.commentary: “One Who has the greatest Wisdom." There are wise men in the world-each one also may be a master in his own subject. The Lord, the very Consciousness illumining all bosoms simultaneously everywhere, is the One Knowledge Absolute, the Knower of all knowledge of all wise men. Omniscient — Infinite Truth is Śrī Nārāyaṇa as He is Pure Knowledge by the Light of which all 'Knowledge' is known.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who has the greatest Wisdom."

names.short_meaning: "One Who has lost all fears."
names.commentary: "One Who has lost all fears." Fear can come only from the sense of 'other.' In Advaita Reality, there cannot be any fear as He is the "Onewit tout-a-second." The state of Nārāyaṇa — Consciousness is declared in all scriptures to be 'Abhava'—the Fearless State.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who has lost all fears."

names.short_meaning: One Whose Glory when heard and sung causes merits to grow in the bosom of that devotee
names.commentary:
“One Whose Glory when ‘heard’ (sravana) and ‘sung’ (keertana) causes merits (punya) to grow in the bosom of that devotee. This statement of fact is never investigated deeply by students so they generally understand its superficial and obvious meaning only.

By 'hearing'—with attention—to the stories of the Lord— we must get ourselves involved in the 'listening' and thereafter we must reflect upon the glories of the Lord (Bhāgavata guṇa) and thus expose ourselves to those recreative thoughts. Not only is it sufficient thus that we imbibe the qualities spiritual, but we must learn to get ourselves committed to the life of Godcentred activities. This is called true keertana—singing His Glories. It is not to be a mere noisy chanting of hymns, a mere muttering of mantras; we must teach ourselves to allow Him to express through us. Our physical activities, mental feelings and intellectual thoughts must all shine forth the awareness of His Divine Presence that is in us at every moment, everywhere. The life of such a devotee will itself become, in its dynamic beauty, love and devoted tenderness, a constant worship (poojaa), a continuous (akhanda) hymn chanted (keertana) in praise of the Lord-of-the-heart.
names.simple_meaning: One Whose Glory when heard and sung causes merits to grow in the bosom of that devotee

names.short_meaning: “One Who lifts us out of the ocean-of-change.”
names.commentary:
“One Who lifts us out of the ocean-of-change.” We, by identifying through our body-mind-intellect, with the changing whirls of matter around us, assume to ourselves the changes and these provide us, in their totality, the horrible sorrow of the mortal finitude. On lifting our attention from the giddy changes in these whirls of finite matter, when we fix it upon Him, the one Consciousness that illumines all changes in all living creatures, we get uplifted into a state of Immortality—Changeless, Blissful, Supremely Satisfying. Hence, Śrī Nārāyaṇa is called as the 'Up-lifter,' the 'Saviour.' The 'Taara-mantra' lifts us from the cesspool of sense living into the serener climes of the lit-up peaks of peace and perfection.

तारयति इति तारः।

(Taarayati iti Taarah.) 'Taara is that which saves, uplifts, regulates, revives, etc."
names.simple_meaning: “One Who lifts us out of the ocean-of-change.”

names.short_meaning: ‘Kriti’ means actions; 'Dush-kriti' means bad actions
names.commentary: ‘Kriti’ means actions; 'Dush-kriti' means bad actions. When actions are undertaken. prompted by sensuous desires, they leave impressions (vāsanās) and these always have a tendency to make us repeat similar actions. When one turns the mind towards Nārāyaṇa, the Self, he is emptied of his existing vāsanās, so Lord is indicated as the 'destroyer (Haa) of the sins.'
names.simple_meaning: The destroyer of evil deeds

names.short_meaning: "Supremely Pure."
names.commentary: "Supremely Pure." One Who purifies the heart of His devotee—removing all his sense-hunting vāsanās of indulgence. Śrī Nārāyaṇa guides the pure-hearted to the portals of the final goal, the Higher Consciousness.
names.simple_meaning: "Supremely Pure."

names.short_meaning: "One Who destroys all 'bad dreams'."
names.commentary:
"One Who destroys all 'bad dreams'." The worst dream is the samsar. Perception of plurality is the horrible dream of terrible pangs, consuming fears and drowning sorrows. Dreams are explosions of the suppressions stored away in the subconscious. A real devotee exists in utter surrender unto the Lord. When his life is ever-centred in Nārāyaṇa-smarana, in such total and humble dedication he has no chance of earning these suppressions.

Since his sub-conscious mind is not loaded with half-digested thoughts and unexpressed intentions, repressed desires and suppressed motives, immoral passions and covetous inclinations, he has no fearful dreams in his daily sleep. Ultimately each seeker will rise above his little ego and its hungers and enter into the plane of Nārāyaṇa — Consciousness
names.simple_meaning: "One Who destroys all 'bad dreams'."

names.short_meaning: "One Who ends the passage from womb-to-womb—the wheel of birth and death."
names.commentary: "One Who ends the passage from womb-to-womb—the wheel of birth and death." 'Veera' means diversified ways, or one who functions in innumerable fields in countless ways.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who ends the passage from womb-to-womb—the wheel of birth and death."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is the Protector of the Universe."
names.commentary:
"One Who is the Protector of the Universe." Among the Trinity, Viṣṇu is the Protector. the Sustainer of all the created. "For the protection of the good, the destruction of the wicked and the establishment of righteousness, He takes different Incarnations."

"परित्राणाय साधनां विनाशाय च दृष्कृताम् । धर्मसंस्थापनार्थाय संभवामि युगे युगे ॥" (Paritraanaaya saadhoonaam vinaasaaya cha dushkritaam; Dharmasamsthaapanaarthaaya sambhayaami yuge yuge.) -Gītā IV-8.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is the Protector of the Universe."

names.short_meaning: This term, used in the plural number, indicates "the good people."
names.commentary: This term, used in the plural number, indicates "the good people." They are considered as "good" who have moral virtues, ethical values, spiritual purity and scriptural knowledge. By using the plural form here, the import is that the holy beauty of Śrī Nārāyaṇa is found expressed in the glory of such a company of good and saintly men.
names.simple_meaning: The one present as the good and saintly

names.short_meaning: "The Life — Spark in all living creatures."
names.commentary:
"The Life — Spark in all living creatures." The Flame-of — Existence that warms an organism to life is the presiding Consciousness Supreme, the Self. This Self is Nārāyaṇa. "Permeating the earth I support all beings by (My) energy; and having become the juicy Moon I nourish all herbs"—is the declaration of Bhagavān.

‘‘गामाविश्य च भूतानि धारयाम्यहमोजसा । पष्णामि चौषधी: सर्वाः सोमो भृत्वा रसात्मकः ॥" (Gaamaavisya cha bhootaani dhaarayaamyahamojasaa; Pushnaami chaushadheeh sarvaah somo bhootvaa rasaatmakah.) --- Gītā XV-13.
names.simple_meaning: "The Life — Spark in all living creatures."

names.short_meaning: In all places, in all creatures, He dwells
names.commentary: In all places, in all creatures, He dwells. He is the final Factor — Divine beyond which there is nothing, and upon which all else depends.
names.simple_meaning: In all places, in all creatures, He dwells

names.short_meaning: "One of Infinite Forms."
names.commentary: "One of Infinite Forms." The endless variety of forms constituting the world of objects are all projections in Him. They are in their essence nothing but Himself. Just as the entire spread-of-objects in a dream is nothing but the creation of one single mind of the waker, and it is seen as many only in the dream-plane-of — Consciousness, so, too, the world of objects-emotions-and-thoughts are all discovered as the One Self when the spiritual seeker re-awakens himself to the Nārāyaṇa — Consciousness.
names.simple_meaning: "One of Infinite Forms."

names.short_meaning: “One Who is full of Infinite Glories,” or, “One Who is full of Incomparable Powers."
names.commentary:
“One Who is full of Infinite Glories,” or, “One Who is full of Incomparable Powers." The main three 'powers' which the Lord expresses in the world are the 'Desire-power' (Icchaa-sakti), 'Action-power' (Kriyaa-sakti) and 'Knowledge-power' (jñāna-sakti).

These are expressions of His Glory at our physical, mental and intellectual levels. These three manifestations of His 'powers' and their continuous interplay, together weave the fabric of the total dynamic expressions of life in the world. The Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the one spring-board for all these vibrant aspects of life—He, the Omniscient, is called "One of Infinite Forms."

At the physical level we express His Kriyaa-sakti; at our mental plane, His Icchaa-sakti, and in our intellectual functions we experience His jñāna-sakti.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is full of Infinite Glories,” or, “One Who is full of Incomparable Powers."

names.short_meaning: “One Who has conquered anger" (manyuh)
names.commentary:
“One Who has conquered anger" (manyuh). It cannot be repeated too often, thus the significance is again given in this term, that anger is one of the most overpowering enemies within us—"One Who has conquered anger" is One Who is established in His own Purity.

Earlier, the technique of anger was explained that when a desire is unfulfilled, anger rises in a man's heart towards the obstacle between him and his desire. The Self is All-full (Paripoorna); It cannot feel any need, want or desire. The Self, then, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, is ever without the low and ruinous passion called 'anger.'
names.simple_meaning: “One Who has conquered anger" (manyuh)

names.short_meaning: “One Who destroys or removes all fears in samsaric life.”
names.commentary: “One Who destroys or removes all fears in samsaric life.” Naturally, Lord Nārāyaṇa is the one sure harbour wherein the boats of life, tossed mercilessly on the high-seas of passions, can find their calm of peace and total security.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who destroys or removes all fears in samsaric life.”

names.short_meaning: One Who deals squarely with all
names.commentary: 'One Who deals squarely with all." The term caturaśraḥ means a geometrical square of equal sides. Śrī Nārāyaṇa distributes the results of actions equally to all: each one can get only the exact reward of his own previous actions. Thus, Nārāyaṇa bestows justly and squarely upon all.
names.simple_meaning: One Who deals squarely with all

names.short_meaning: "One Who, in His Real Nature, is too deep to be fathomed by the frail instrument of our mind."
names.commentary:
"One Who, in His Real Nature, is too deep to be fathomed by the frail instrument of our mind." Depth here indicates profoundness—the Supreme Essence pervading the Universe is unfathomably profound in Its significance and glory.

“निम्नं गभीरं गम्भीरम्।” (Nimnam, Gabheeram, Gambheeram.) All are synonyms according to the Amarakosa.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who, in His Real Nature, is too deep to be fathomed by the frail instrument of our mind."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is unique in His giving."
names.commentary: "One Who is unique in His giving." He is divinely liberal, magnificently benevolent in fulfilling the earnest desires of all His true devotees.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is unique in His giving."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is unique in His Commanding — Power."
names.commentary: "One Who is unique in His Commanding — Power." One Who orders even the phenomenal powers, the deities and gods.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is unique in His Commanding — Power."

names.short_meaning: "One Who advises and gives knowledge."
names.commentary: "One Who advises and gives knowledge." It is the Self Who is the Author of the Vedas, nay, the very theme and essence of the Vedas. Lord Nārāyaṇa, in the form of the Sruti-texts, gives to man the knowledge of the Self.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who advises and gives knowledge."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is the First Cause" -and Who is Himself the Uncaused
names.commentary: "One Who is the First Cause" -and Who is Himself the Uncaused. The Eternal, the Beginningless is Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is the First Cause" -and Who is Himself the Uncaused

names.short_meaning: “The very substratum or support for the Earth.”
names.commentary: “The very substratum or support for the Earth.” Since Earth revolves in Space, we can say that He Who is both Earth and the Space in which the Universe exists and revolves is the Supreme, Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: “The very substratum or support for the Earth.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who is the wealth, the richness or glory of the Universe.”
names.commentary:
“One Who is the wealth, the richness or glory of the Universe.” If Self were not, then all would have been inert, unborn, dead. As the One Life everywhere, as Pure Existence, all the glories of this dynamic Universe are in Him and from Him alone.

There is a reading wherein the terms 942 and 943 are coupled, in which case their combined meaning would be: "One Who is the glory in the Universe and in the interspace everywhere."

As "भूभवोलक्ष्मी:।" (Bhoorbhuvolakshmeeh.)
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is the wealth, the richness or glory of the Universe.”

names.short_meaning: "One Who moves through various ways which are all divinely glorious."
