names.commentary: "One Who moves through various ways which are all divinely glorious." Or, One Who exhibits in all His Incarnations the inimitable splendour of valour in His actions and achievements
names.simple_meaning: "One Who moves through various ways which are all divinely glorious."

names.short_meaning: “One Who wears resplendent shoulder-caps”—a kind of ornament used by ancient Indian kings to protect their upper arms and shoulders from their enemies' slashing swords
names.commentary: “One Who wears resplendent shoulder-caps”—a kind of ornament used by ancient Indian kings to protect their upper arms and shoulders from their enemies' slashing swords.
names.simple_meaning: The wearer of radiant armlets

names.short_meaning: "He Who delivers all living creatures."
names.commentary:
"He Who delivers all living creatures." Lord Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the great Father of all living beings as all the universe comes from Him alone. He alone was before all creation; from Him alone everything has risen; in Him everything exists, is nurtured and nourished by His Glory. Thus, as the very progenitor of the universe, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Self, is the only Jagat-Īśvara (Lord of the Universe).

"पितासि लोकस्य चराचरस्य…।" (Pitaasi Lokasya Charaacharasya.) 'Thou art the Father of the world, movable and immovable…" -Gītā XI-43.
names.simple_meaning: "He Who delivers all living creatures."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is the sole Cause of birth for all living creatures in the Universe."
names.commentary: "One Who is the sole Cause of birth for all living creatures in the Universe." The immediate cause is, of course, the vāsanās of each being, but the real and ultimate Cause is the Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is the sole Cause of birth for all living creatures in the Universe."

names.short_meaning: “One Whose form is terrible and frightening to the sinners."
names.commentary:
“One Whose form is terrible and frightening to the sinners." "Oh, Glorious Sir, seeing your wonderful but awesome form, the whole world is shuddering with fear," cried Arjuna upon beholding the Cosmic Form of the Lord. He adds: "Having seen Thy Immeasurable Form… the worlds are terrified, and so am I." Again, "On seeing Thee touching the sky… my heart is stricken with dread and I find no courage nor peace, O Viṣṇu."

“दृष्ट्वाद्भुतं रूपमुग्रं तवेदं लोकत्रयं प्रव्यथितं महात्मन्।” (Drishtvaadbhutam roopamugram tavedam lokatrayam pravyathitam mahaatman.) —Gītā XI-20.

“रूपं महत्ते बहुवक्त्रनेत्रं महाबाहो बहुबाहूरुपादम्; बहूदरं बहुदंष्ट्राकरालं दृष्ट्वा लोकाः प्रव्यथितास्तथाहम्।” (Roopam mahatte bahuvaktranetram mahaabaaho bahubaahoorupaadam; Bahoodaram bahudamshtraakaraalam drishtvaa lokaah pravyathitaastathaaham.) —Gītā XI-23.

“नभःस्पृशं दीप्तमनेकवर्णं व्यात्ताननं दीप्तविशालनेत्रम्; दृष्ट्वा हि त्वां प्रव्यथितान्तरात्मा धृतिं न विन्दामि शमं च विष्णो।” (Nabhahsprisam deeptamanekavarnam vyaattaananam deeptavisaalanetram; Drishtvaa hi tvaam pravyathitaantaraatmaa dhritim na vindaami samam cha Vishno.) —Gītā XI-24.
names.simple_meaning: “One Whose form is terrible and frightening to the sinners."

names.short_meaning: “One Whose prowess is irresistible and fearful to His enemies."
names.commentary: “One Whose prowess is irresistible and fearful to His enemies."
names.simple_meaning: “One Whose prowess is irresistible and fearful to His enemies."

names.short_meaning: “One Who is the fundamental sustainer"—the support for all that exists
names.commentary: “One Who is the fundamental sustainer"—the support for all that exists. All things and all beings are supported by the Earth which itself rests upon the Lord, its substratum. It is upon the Lord, the Self, that each mind projects the entire world of names and forms.
names.source_heading_devanagari_ocr: आ घा र नि ल यः
names.simple_meaning: “One Who is the fundamental sustainer"—the support for all that exists

names.short_meaning: “Above Whom there is no other to control or to command”—One Who is the Supreme Controller of all
names.commentary: “Above Whom there is no other to control or to command”—One Who is the Supreme Controller of all. He is the Law; the eternal Truth is that the Law and the Law — Giver are one and the same.
names.simple_meaning: The unsurpassed supreme controller

names.short_meaning: "He Who shines like an opening flower."
names.commentary: "He Who shines like an opening flower." The bud opens and manifests into the bloom; the flower was unmanifest in the bud. Since the Lord at the time of the deluge existed as the Total Unmanifest, and thereafter, at the maturity of the vāsanās, opens up as the manifest world of things and beings. He came to be indicated by this term.
names.simple_meaning: "He Who shines like an opening flower."

names.short_meaning: "Ever — Awakened"—He Who knows no sleep
names.commentary: "Ever — Awakened"—He Who knows no sleep. Sleep means 'non-apprehension.' This 'non-apprehension' of Reality is called 'Avidyaa' (nescience) which produces our 'mis-apprehension' of I and mine, and the world of pains and shocks. Since Nārāyaṇa is the Self, He is 'Ever-available' and is never asleep to His Eternal — Divine — Nature.
names.simple_meaning: "Ever — Awakened"—He Who knows no sleep

names.short_meaning: "One Who is on the top of everything"—One Who ever goes high, for He is the highest Truth, the Summit of evolution
names.commentary:
"One Who is on the top of everything"—One Who ever goes high, for He is the highest Truth, the Summit of evolution. "One Who goes higher and higher is called "Oordhyagah."

ऊर्घ्वं गच्छति इति ऊर्घ्वं ग: । (Oordhvam gacchati iti Oordhvagah.)
names.simple_meaning: The exalted one

names.short_meaning: “One Who walks the path of truth”—a path which others implicitly follow to reach the Truth Infinite
names.commentary:
“One Who walks the path of truth”—a path which others implicitly follow to reach the Truth Infinite. "Whatever an adored one does, other people will implicitly follow," warns Kṛṣṇa in Bhagavad Gītā. Lord is the "Standard of Perfection" and all devotees place Him as the Ideal—trying to imitate, in their own lives, His Absolute Goodness, Absolute Love and Absolute Peace.

"यद्यदाचरित श्रेष्ठस्तत्तदेवेतरो जन: ।" (Yadyadaacharati sreshthah tat-tadevetaro janah.)
names.simple_meaning: “One Who walks the path of truth”—a path which others implicitly follow to reach the Truth Infinite

names.short_meaning: "One Who gives 'prāṇa' to all."
names.commentary: "One Who gives 'prāṇa' to all." The term 'prāṇa' in our śāstras means the physiological functions, the manifestations of Life in man. Therefore, Nārāyaṇa, the Self, is the Vital Source from which all sense organs, mind and intellect borrow their power of perception, capacities of feeling and their faculties of thinking and understanding.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who gives 'prāṇa' to all."

names.short_meaning: "oṃkāra is praṇava."
names.commentary:
"oṃkāra is praṇava." The Infinite Reality is indicated by 'OM' in the Vedas. 'OM' is the manifesting sound of the Supreme Self. Therefore, Śrī Nārāyaṇa is called 'praṇavaḥ': meaning He is of the 'nature of oṃkāra.'

ॐकारस्वरूपो हि नारायणः। ("OM"-kaarasvaroopo hi Naaraayanah.)
names.simple_meaning: "oṃkāra is praṇava."

names.short_meaning: “The Supreme Manager of the Universe.”
names.commentary: “The Supreme Manager of the Universe.” The root ‘Pana’ means “to transact.” By giving the exact rewards for all actions, Lord both orders and justly manages all activities of each individual and directly supervises the interactions between individuals and things constituting this scientifically precise universe.
names.simple_meaning: “The Supreme Manager of the Universe.”

names.short_meaning: “He Whose very form is the Vedas"—which are the only 'proof' for the Eternal Reality
names.commentary:
“He Whose very form is the Vedas"—which are the only 'proof' for the Eternal Reality. Or, we may read it: He Who is the Pure Infinite Consciousness (Prajnaanam) as we have it in the great Commandment, "Consciousness is the Infinite Reality."

"प्रज्ञानं ब्रह्म।" (Prajnaanam Brahma.)
names.simple_meaning: “He Whose very form is the Vedas"—which are the only 'proof' for the Eternal Reality

names.short_meaning: “He in Whom all ‘prāṇas’ stand established.”
names.commentary: “He in Whom all ‘prāṇas’ stand established.” He Who is the very substratum— vital foundation—for all 'activities' manifested in a living organism.
names.simple_meaning: “He in Whom all ‘prāṇas’ stand established.”

names.short_meaning: "He Who rules over all 'Pragnas' "-Śrī Hari is the One Who causes everyone to eat
names.commentary: "He Who rules over all 'Pragnas' "-Śrī Hari is the One Who causes everyone to eat. digest, feel energised, act, achieve the fruits thereof, grow old and die. In all these 'activities,' the great One — Commanding, Factor — Divine. Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Self, presides in silent detachment, and by His Presence He initiates and maintains all these activities in all living creatures upon the earth's surface.
names.simple_meaning: "He Who rules over all 'Pragnas' "-Śrī Hari is the One Who causes everyone to eat

names.short_meaning: "He Who maintains the life-breath in all living creatures."
names.commentary: "He Who maintains the life-breath in all living creatures." This interpretation is not a happy one as this meaning has just come in the preceding, endearing term. In love, of course, there is no rule that the lover should not repeat the same loving words to address his Beloved. But, we can find yet a new depth of suggestion if we understand this term to mean "One Who is the very life-giving divine-touch in every breath."
names.simple_meaning: "He Who maintains the life-breath in all living creatures."

names.short_meaning: "The Reality"—That which is Eternal, the Essence
names.commentary:
"The Reality"—That which is Eternal, the Essence. "That which one gains in subjective realisation is the Self," Śrī Nārāyaṇa.

“तत् त्वम् इति विज्ञानमेव तत्त्वम्।” (Tat tvam iti vijnaanameva tattvam.)
names.simple_meaning: "The Reality"—That which is Eternal, the Essence

names.short_meaning: "One Who has realised fully the Reality"—meaning the original essential nature of the Self
names.commentary:
"One Who has realised fully the Reality"—meaning the original essential nature of the Self. On realising the Self, the individual becomes the Self and, therefore, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, that very Self, is the One Who has realised fully the Reality which is His Own Nature Divine.

“स यो ह वै तत् परमं ब्रह्म वेद ब्रह्मैव भवति।” (Sa yo ha vai tat paramam Brahma veda Brahmaiva bhavati.) —Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad III-ii-9.
names.simple_meaning: The knower of reality as it truly is

names.short_meaning: "The Advaita Reality"— Nārāyaṇa is the One Self, the Oversoul, Who expresses Himself as the individualities of the infinite entities in the universe
names.commentary: "The Advaita Reality"— Nārāyaṇa is the One Self, the Oversoul, Who expresses Himself as the individualities of the infinite entities in the universe.
names.simple_meaning: The one Self

names.short_meaning: “One Who knows no change or modifications in Himself."
names.commentary:
“One Who knows no change or modifications in Himself." Every finite object in the world undergoes constant 'change' and each of them is extremely painful. They are birth, growth, decay, disease and death. One who has none of these is the Infinite and the Eternal, the Changeless Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa, Ever-the — Same Supreme. Gītā thunders the nature of the Self to be “ever-birthless and never-dying,” and once It has existed, Self never becomes non-existent.

“न जायते म्रियते वा कदाचित् नायं भूत्वा भविता वा न भूयः। अजो नित्यः शाश्वतोऽयं पुराणो न हन्यते हन्यमाने शरीरे।” (Na jaayate mriyate vaa kadaachit naayam bhootvaa bhavitaa vaa na bhooyah; ajo nityah saasvato-ayam puraano na hanyate hanyamaane sareere.) “He is not born, nor does He ever die; after having been He again ceases not to be; unborn, eternal, changeless and ancient he is not killed when the body is killed.” —Gītā II-20.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who knows no change or modifications in Himself."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is the Sap in the Tree-of — Life existing in all this Universe of the higher-world, our-world and the lower-world."
names.commentary: "One Who is the Sap in the Tree-of — Life existing in all this Universe of the higher-world, our-world and the lower-world." The famous Vedic terms bhūḥ Bhuvah and Svah connote the three worlds (lokas). The word 'Loka' in Sanskrit means 'a field of experience.' Therefore, in fact, these three terms, called Vyaahritees, subjectively represent all our experiences in the waking, dream and deep-sleep states of consciousness. Vvaahritees are mantras by which the Lord performs His constant Yaina to nurture and nourish the Universe. So, this epithet has been given to Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Infinite Self, the glorious Essence (Sap) that pervades the entire Tree-of — Life-flowing out to even embrace all experiences in all planes of Consciousness, everywhere, in everything at all times.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is the Sap in the Tree-of — Life existing in all this Universe of the higher-world, our-world and the lower-world."

names.short_meaning: "One Who helps all to crossover"—the Eternal Boat-man, to Whom, if the devotees can surrender in unswerving faith and true devotion
names.commentary:
"One Who helps all to crossover"—the Eternal Boat-man, to Whom, if the devotees can surrender in unswerving faith and true devotion, He will surely row them across the "Ocean of Samsar;" That One is tāraḥ.

Through exclusive, devoted meditation, alert with understanding, the individuality in each of us wakes up to the higher plane—and there in that Be-attitude to experience the Self. the Eternal Brahman-Śrī Hari.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who helps all to crossover"—the Eternal Boat-man, to Whom, if the devotees can surrender in unswerving faith and true devotion

names.short_meaning: "He Who is the Father of All"- Who is the Eternal Father of the entire Universe
names.commentary: "He Who is the Father of All"- Who is the Eternal Father of the entire Universe.
names.simple_meaning: "He Who is the Father of All"- Who is the Eternal Father of the entire Universe

names.short_meaning: “He Who is the Father of even the ‘Father of all Beings,’ the Creator, Brahmājī, of the Trinity."
names.commentary: “He Who is the Father of even the ‘Father of all Beings,’ the Creator, Brahmājī, of the Trinity." The Creator Himself rose from the Absolute Self. Creator is known in our scriptural language as Pitaamaha -the Father.
names.simple_meaning: “He Who is the Father of even the ‘Father of all Beings,’ the Creator, Brahmājī, of the Trinity."

names.short_meaning: “One Whose very nature is yajña.”
names.commentary: “One Whose very nature is yajña.” The term yajña means “work undertaken with a pure spirit of total dedication in complete co-operation with others, and for the well-being of all creatures and for the welfare of the world." Wherever there is such a co-operative endeavour with total selflessness, there is Śrī Nārāyaṇa in action through His creatures.
names.simple_meaning: “One Whose very nature is yajña.”

names.short_meaning: “The Lord of all yajñas.”
names.commentary:
“The Lord of all yajñas.” I am the ‘Enjoyer’ in all self-dedicated, co-operative endeavours (yajña). These are the joyous words of the Lord Who Himself declares: "The 'Enjoyer' and the 'Lord' in all yajñas am I."

“अहं हि सर्वयज्ञानां भोक्ता च प्रभुरेव च।” (Aham hi sarvayajnaanaam bhoktaa cha prabhureva cha.) —Gītā IX-24.
names.simple_meaning: “The Lord of all yajñas.”

names.short_meaning: The One Who performs yajña according to the strict prescriptions laid down in the Vedas
names.commentary:
"The One Who performs yajña according to the strict prescriptions laid down in the Vedas"- The One Who maintains in all His divine actions the true yajña spirit,

Refer commentary on 972 for the meaning of yajña. This is the meaning in which “yajña” is employed in Gītā Chapter III also.
names.simple_meaning: The One Who performs yajña according to the strict prescriptions laid down in the Vedas

names.short_meaning: “One Whose limbs are the ‘things’ employed in yajña.”
names.commentary:
“One Whose limbs are the ‘things’ employed in yajña.” In Harivaṃśa we are told that these 'things' are the very aspects of Lord Śrī Nārāyaṇa.

Used in yajñas and yāgas, such as Vedam and Yoopam.
names.simple_meaning: “One Whose limbs are the ‘things’ employed in yajña.”

names.short_meaning: “One Who fulfils yajñas in complete and exact accord with the Vedic instructions."
names.commentary: “One Who fulfils yajñas in complete and exact accord with the Vedic instructions."
names.simple_meaning: “One Who fulfils yajñas in complete and exact accord with the Vedic instructions."

names.short_meaning: "The Ruler of the yajñas"— the One Who helps us to conclude successfully all our 'good, dedicated, selfless acts of service to others'—Yainas
names.commentary: "The Ruler of the yajñas"— the One Who helps us to conclude successfully all our 'good, dedicated, selfless acts of service to others'—Yainas.
names.simple_meaning: The ruler of yajñas

names.short_meaning: “One Who performs yajña."
names.commentary:
“One Who performs yajña." The same term can also mean One Who destroys the yajñas. The term yajña connotes all noble and divine actions of service and love undertaken in a pure sense of God-dedication, selflessness and joy. Lord issued forth the Creation as an act of yajña, and in the end He must also undertake the total dissolution of this very yajña. Sometimes this is interpreted as "One Who 'performs' the yajñas of the good people and One Who 'destroys' the yajñas of the evil-minded folk."

“सहयजाः प्रजाः सृष्ट्वा पुरोवाच प्रजापितः ।

अनेन प्रसविष्यध्वमेष वोऽस्त्विष्टकामधक ॥" (Sahayajnaah prajaah srishtvaa purovaacha prajaapatih; Anena prasavishyadhyamesha vo-astvishtakaamadhuk.) "Prajaapati (the Creator), having in the beginning (of creation) created mankind together with sacrifices, said: "By this shall you propagate; let this be the milch-cow of your desires—Kaamadhuk (the cow which yields all desired objects)."

-Gītā III-10.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who performs yajña."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is the constant 'Enjoyer' of the perpetual yajñas."
names.commentary: "One Who is the constant 'Enjoyer' of the perpetual yajñas." In all yajñas, because every act is Nārāyaṇa-centred—God-dedicated—to Him alone is the attribute of being the only single 'Enjoyer.'
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is the constant 'Enjoyer' of the perpetual yajñas."

names.short_meaning: One receiver of all that is offered
names.commentary: All that is offered into the sacred Fire during a yajña, though with an invocation to any of the deities, in tender devotion and joy, goes to Him alone, the "One receiver of all that is offered," for all deities are but Nārāyaṇa in different forms.
names.simple_meaning: One receiver of all that is offered

names.short_meaning: “One Who fulfils all yajñas."
names.commentary: “One Who fulfils all yajñas." It is by His Grace alone all noble endeavours, undertaken in an honest and true sincerity, gain spectacular success.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who fulfils all yajñas."

names.short_meaning: “One Who performs the last, concluding act in all yajñas."
names.commentary:
“One Who performs the last, concluding act in all yajñas." The final item in a yajña is the "total-offering" (Poorna — Aahuti) when Śrī Nārāyaṇa is reverently and earnestly invoked. Without this prayer-ritual, yajña is never complete. Śrī Hari, therefore, is of the form of Poorna — Aahuti-in the sense that when 'total' surrender of all vehicles and their actions is accomplished, the transcendental experience of the Self, Nārāyaṇa alone, comes to manifest in all His divine Splendour.

Some commentators have, however, taken the meaning of the yajña-anta—not as "the last item in yajña" but as 'anta,' the 'fruit' of the yajña by which they bestow the meaning that Nārāyaṇa is the "One Who gives away the 'fruits' for all Hari-dedicated, selfless acts of love and service."
names.simple_meaning: “One Who performs the last, concluding act in all yajñas."

names.short_meaning: "Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the most profound truth to be realised in all yajñas."
names.commentary:
"Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the most profound truth to be realised in all yajñas." The Self is the most noble truth to be sought through 'offering' all the 'Dravya' (objects) into the "Consciousness" (Fire) in the "body" (kunda). This kind of subjective-yajña is called in the Gītā as "Knowledge — yajña." This is also called in the Vedas as Brahma — yajña.

(ज्ञान यज्ञ ) — (jñāna yajña) — The fire of newly kindled knowledge whereinto we offer all false values and our immoral tendencies for burning into the Effulgent Self, the Divine.
names.simple_meaning: "Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the most profound truth to be realised in all yajñas."

names.short_meaning: “One Who has Himself become the 'food' "-sense-objects which are the 'food' consumed by the sense-organs
names.commentary: “One Who has Himself become the 'food' "-sense-objects which are the 'food' consumed by the sense-organs. As a verb it can be used as One Who "Eats" the whole Universe at the time of the great dissolution. At that time, He is the One in Whom the world remains absorbed in Pralaya, just as our individual world each day gets dissolved in our sleep. The One in Whom alone the world of names and forms can remain in their 'seed-form,' is Śrī Nārāyaṇa, the Self.
names.simple_meaning: “One Who has Himself become the 'food' "-sense-objects which are the 'food' consumed by the sense-organs

names.short_meaning: "One Who eats the 'food."
names.commentary: "One Who eats the 'food'." Not only the objective world is the projection on Nārāyaṇa. but the subjective-enjoyer—the individuality, the ego, that experiences—is also Nārāyaṇa. The Self, functioning through the "equipments" is the Jeevaatman, the individuality in each of us who "experiences." Thus the Self is both 'food' (Annam) and 'eater-of-food' (annādaḥ) just as our own waking-mind becomes the "experiencer" and the "experienced" in our dream-world.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who eats the 'food."

names.short_meaning: “One Who is Himself the 'material Cause' (Upaadaana kāraṇa) for Himself:" the Self-born, the Uncaused Cause
names.commentary:
“One Who is Himself the 'material Cause' (Upaadaana kāraṇa) for Himself:" the Self-born, the Uncaused Cause.

Both 985 and 986.
names.simple_meaning: Self-born

names.short_meaning: “One Who, as the Lord of the Universe, has no other ‘Instrumental Cause’ (nimitta-kāraṇa) in projecting Himself."
names.commentary: “One Who, as the Lord of the Universe, has no other ‘Instrumental Cause’ (nimitta-kāraṇa) in projecting Himself." Three causes are necessary in all 'creation' in the pluralistic world: the 'Material cause' (mud), the 'Instrumental cause' (wheel), and the 'Efficient cause' (the potmaker). In Śrī Nārāyaṇa's self-projection, as in the dream, that all these three causes are He, Himself, is shown in these terms.
names.simple_meaning: Self-born

names.short_meaning: "The One Who dug through the earth"—cutting through the denseness of the gross to reach, apprehend and kill the subtle Hiraṇyākṣa, the terrible and the monstrous who had tried to destroy the spiritual values in the world
names.commentary:
"The One Who dug through the earth"—cutting through the denseness of the gross to reach, apprehend and kill the subtle Hiraṇyākṣa, the terrible and the monstrous who had tried to destroy the spiritual values in the world. The Self has to reach us to destroy the ego in us and give us the 'liberation' from our evil adherence to the body-mind-intellect.

Ego=The jīva; hiraṇya=Gold: Aksha=Eye; therefore, 'the eye for gold,' meaning a mere view of the enjoyments of the objects through the senses—Hiraṇyākṣa, Hari alone can totally kill him.
names.simple_meaning: The Boar who dug through the earth to destroy Hiraṇyākṣa

names.short_meaning: "One Who sings the Sāma-songs."
names.commentary: "One Who sings the Sāma-songs."
names.simple_meaning: "One Who sings the Sāma-songs."

names.short_meaning: "He Who appeared as born to Devakī in His Incarnation as Kṛṣṇa."
names.commentary: "He Who appeared as born to Devakī in His Incarnation as Kṛṣṇa." And since Devakī could only, from afar, see, watch and enjoy the pranks and play of her blessed child in Gokula, Kṛṣṇa is called as the "Joy of Devakī" (Devakī-nandana).
names.simple_meaning: "He Who appeared as born to Devakī in His Incarnation as Kṛṣṇa."

names.short_meaning: "One Who creates."
names.commentary: "One Who creates." Even the Creator can perform His job only by drawing His abilities and capacities from the Infinite Self, Śrī Nārāyaṇa.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who creates."

names.short_meaning: "One Who is the Lord of the Earth."
names.commentary: "One Who is the Lord of the Earth." Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the husband of Mother Earth. He is Her Protector, Her nurturer and nourisher. Here, Earth may stand for all that is gross—the entire māyā—and Nārāyaṇa is the Lakshmee — Pati.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who is the Lord of the Earth."

names.short_meaning: Meditating upon Whom, all vāsanās (sins) are liquidated
names.commentary:
Meditating upon Whom, all vāsanās (sins) are liquidated. When an individual, surrendering in love to Him, acts and fulfils his duties, all his existing vāsanās are destroyed and no new ones are created— this is the very root in the theory of Karma Yoga in the Vedas.

Through meditation upon the Self, all sins are dissolved and totally removed.
names.simple_meaning: Meditating upon Whom, all vāsanās (sins) are liquidated

names.short_meaning: One Who has the divine conch named Pāñcajanya
names.commentary: “One Who has the divine conch named “Pāñcajanya.” The word meaning of this term pāñca-janya is “that which is born of the five” (sense organs), so it stands for the mind. Mind being the seat of ego, the śāstras declare that the conch in the divine hand of Śrī Nārāyaṇa is the ego-factor (ahaṅkāra — Tattva) in our personality.
names.simple_meaning: One Who has the divine conch named Pāñcajanya

names.short_meaning: The Lord's sword is called Nandaka
names.commentary: The Lord's sword is called Nandaka. Therefore, this term indicates One Who holds and wields the Nandaka-sword. The words Nanda-kam mean "that which brings bliss." The śāstras sing that this divine sword in the sacred hands of Lord Hari represents the Knowledge — Spiritual (vidyā — Tattva), with which a seeker can destroy all his "ignorance" of the Self in him.
names.simple_meaning: The bearer of the sword Nandaka

names.short_meaning: “One Who carries the Discus called Sudarśana.”
names.commentary: “One Who carries the Discus called Sudarśana.” The term Su — Darsana means “that which gives the auspicious vision." The śāstras attribute to this Discus — Divine the representation of the human mind.
names.simple_meaning: The bearer of the discus Sudarśana

names.short_meaning: “One Who aims His unerring Bow called Śārṅga.”
names.commentary: “One Who aims His unerring Bow called Śārṅga.” This bow of Nārāyaṇa is glorified in our texts as representing the Ego, as the 'apex' of all the sense organs, ahaṅkāra — Tattva. In this concluding Stanza, the instruments of Blessing in Śrī Nārāyaṇa's hands are remembered with reverence and devotion.
names.simple_meaning: The wielder of the bow Śārṅga

names.short_meaning: "One who holds His divine Club (Mace) celebrated as Kaumodakī-which generates and spreads beauty and joy."
names.commentary: "One who holds His divine Club (Mace) celebrated as Kaumodakī-which generates and spreads beauty and joy." This Mace is described as representing the intellect in man (Buddhi — Tattya).
names.simple_meaning: The mace-bearer

names.short_meaning: The traditional meaning is, of course, "One Who has the 'wheel of the chariot' as His weapon."
names.commentary:
The traditional meaning is, of course, "One Who has the 'wheel of the chariot' as His weapon." This means the Discus which already has been mentioned in this very Stanza as cakrī. But, there are others who would like to interpret this term in other ways.

In a glorification — Hymn or devotional — Chant, repetition is no sin; in fact, it should be quite natural.
names.simple_meaning: The one whose hand holds the chariot wheel

names.short_meaning: "One Who cannot be exasperated by anyone, by any act or acts, however blasphemous they may be."
names.commentary:
"One Who cannot be exasperated by anyone, by any act or acts, however blasphemous they may be." One Whose peace and calm cannot be stormed out by any happening in his outer world: Ever-peaceful.

The term suggests Infinite patience, love and kindness towards man and his frailties.
names.simple_meaning: "One Who cannot be exasperated by anyone, by any act or acts, however blasphemous they may be."

names.short_meaning: “He Who has all implements for all kinds of assault and fight."
names.commentary: “He Who has all implements for all kinds of assault and fight." No enemy can surprise Him, the 'conqueror of all.' One Who has weapons to meet any missile, however powerful.
names.simple_meaning: “He Who has all implements for all kinds of assault and fight."
